# dsh-mv-cli · world.execute(me); screening room

English · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@ljwei-stak/dsh-mv-cli)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ljwei-stak/dsh-mv-cli) · [![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/alice-marx/dsh-mv-cli) · [Releases](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-cli/releases) · [创意工坊 / workshop](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-workshop)

**MV 放映室** is a DeepSeek Harness Desktop plugin (`@ljwei-stak/dsh-mv-cli`, profile entry id `dsh-mv`, current version **0.12.1**) that plays ASCII / terminal-styled, pixel 2D, WebGL2 3D and local rendered **music videos** on a `<canvas>` in the workbench. Script scenes use **your own audio** as the clock; local videos use their own media clock.

Supports DSH **0.2.1-rc.2** and **0.2.0-rc.1 / rc.2**. If an older plugin version is disabled because of a protocol mismatch, update the plugin and restart Harness.

## DSH plugin listing

**One-line value:** Adds an MV 放映室 sidebar for creating and playing music videos synced to your own audio or video, with lyrics and ASCII, Canvas2D, and WebGL2 scenes.

**Primary category (one of the directory's 11 categories):** Entertainment (music and media).

**Install command (npm, pinned):**
```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @ljwei-stak/dsh-mv-cli@0.12.1
```
The same package can be installed from **DeepSeek Harness Desktop → Plugins → Add plugin** by entering `@ljwei-stak/dsh-mv-cli@0.12.1`.

**Compatibility:** DSH protocol `0.2.1-rc.2` and `0.2.0-rc.1` / `0.2.0-rc.2`; Host Node.js `>=20`. WebGL scenes need Chromium Worker OffscreenCanvas and WebGL2; unsupported clients fall back to the generic renderer. Local video decoding depends on Chromium codecs.

**Configuration files:** The root `package.json` identifies the npm package and declares `dsh.bundle.patch`; `cordis.patch.yml` registers the `dsh-mv` plugin row, whose module exports `apply(ctx)` from `.dsh-plugin/index.mjs`. Each MV pack uses `mv.json`, with `mv.schema.json` for validation and editor completion. Runtime settings are managed in the DSH plugin configuration page (`canvasFontSize`, `ffmpegPath`, `lrclib`, `enginePython`, `uvPath`, `hfEndpoint`, `httpProxy`, `workshopMirror`, `workshopDir`, `agentTools`); the panel also stores local preferences in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-mv\settings.json`.

**Permissions and external services:** The Host reads user-selected pack/media paths and writes packs and settings under user-selected folders or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-mv`, subject to normal OS file permissions. `ffmpeg` runs only after confirmation. Optional lyric-engine setup downloads Python packages and speech models. Optional LRCLIB lookup sends only title, artist, album, and duration (no audio or filename) and can be disabled. Workshop browsing/install downloads from GitHub or the configured HTTPS mirror. AI pack creation opens a Harness Agent session for the local workspace; file access and model-provider handling follow the active Harness configuration and approval flow.

**License:** Plugin/npm code is MIT. Repository presets, workshop packs, artwork, lyrics, fonts, and other third-party materials may have separate terms; see [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md), and [License and credits](#license-and-credits).

**Screenshots:** See [Screenshots](#screenshots), including the [library](docs/screenshots/library-list.png), [workshop](docs/screenshots/workshop.png), and [scene packs](docs/screenshots/ports.png). These are standalone client UI previews from `tools/ui-preview` with a mock Host and placeholder demo packs/lyrics; they show UI states, not end-to-end verification against a live DSH Host.

**0.12.0 Manim / local video support:** `canvas.renderer: "video"` and `video.file` display the original MP4/M4V/MOV/WebM/MKV frames, with embedded sound or a separate local soundtrack, independent `audio.offset`, seek/pause/replay, volume/mute, fullscreen, PNG snapshots and optional lyric overlay. Run `npx --yes --package @ljwei-stak/dsh-mv-cli@0.12.0 dsh-mv-import-video "D:/MV/manim-for-world-execute-me" --out "D:/MV-packs/manim"`, then import the generated folder. Render the [upstream Manim project](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/manim-for-world-execute-me) first: its original animation and baked captions remain intact. See the [Manim import guide](docs/MANIM_VIDEO.zh.md) for the 5.16-second title card and soundtrack/lyric timing. Plugin and workshop releases contain no movies or song recordings.

**0.11.0 workshop discovery:** combined type/licence/tag/lyrics/compatibility/installation-update filters, clear filters, stable update/title sorting, native keyboard actions and narrow-panel layouts. No workshop account or Harness login integration. Shared statistics and anonymous voting are not deployed: default UI hides unavailable community metrics/rankings/trophy filters and all vote actions. Optional read-only data contracts remain available for a future trusted source; no fabricated popularity. See the [released scope and integration note](docs/WORKSHOP_COMMUNITY.zh.md).

**0.9.8 workshop downloads:** fixes the HTTP CONNECT proxy path, adds bounded retries for transient download failures and supports a trusted HTTPS fallback mirror. TLS verification, commit-pinned files, size/SHA-256 checks and scene isolation remain enforced. See [Workshop network and mirrors](#workshop-network-and-mirrors-098).

**0.10.0:** default direct-HTTPS fallback to the [official Huawei static mirror](https://www.jianweilimarx.top/dsh-mv-workshop/main/index.json), offline script fonts, silent negative-time introductions and larger bounded bitmap packs. [Nyankomint's adaptation](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-workshop/tree/main/packs/world-execute-me-nyankomint) preserves 87 shots, 8 original silhouettes, 129 captions, 34 offline OFL faces and a five-second warning; only music is user-provided. This work is Canvas2D with WebGL2 post-processing, not geometric 3D. Rapid flashes remain: read its warning; QA is not PSE certification.

Script bitmap options: `canvas.fonts` is a local descriptor list `{family,file,weight:"400",style:"normal",unicodeRange?,licenseFile}` (64 faces, 2 MiB each, 12 MiB total, 30-second initialization). FontFace APIs/buffers remain private to the supervisor. `canvas.preroll` is 0–30 seconds at negative song time; audio, shots and captions still use zero. Optional WebGL-only `canvas.context` accepts boolean `antialias`, `depth`, `premultipliedAlpha`, `preserveDrawingBuffer` and enum `powerPreference`; omitted options preserve existing defaults. Bitmap workshop limits: 160 files/32 MiB, declared non-cover images 2 MiB; other single-file caps are unchanged. Fonts need separate OFL provenance, full licences and attribution; Windows fonts do not ship. Attributed author prompts/methods are included in the downloadable template's [TEACHING_REFERENCES.md](template/TEACHING_REFERENCES.md), as reference material, not instructions executed by scenes.

**0.9.7 heavy 3D startup:** optional `warmup(info, gl)` runs once, after
`prepare()`, on the final output size and before playback, so one-off GPU work
(shader compilation, render-target allocation) is paid on the panel's own
20-second deadline instead of stalling the first visible frame. The stall
watchdog is now graded: the first 10 seconds of playback get an 8-second stall
window and are not charged to the slow-frame quota, then the unchanged 1500 ms
limit and 45-frame quota apply, so a scene that stalls mid-song is still
stopped. `setup()` is 5 seconds and `prepare()` 300 seconds in total (10 s per
step, 512 steps). Existing scene APIs remain compatible; the graded deadlines
also apply to scenes without `warmup()`. A frame keeps the deadline assigned
when requested, including when it crosses the initial 10-second boundary.

**0.9.6 heavy 3D preparation:** optional `function* prepare(info, gl)` prewarms
resources/shaders before playback, with progress, cancellation, a 10-second
step deadline, 120-second total deadline and 512-step limit. Music waits for
preparation. Frame limits and blocked network/font/storage APIs are unchanged.
FrostNova's realtime 3D workshop adaptation uses this lifecycle; its AGPL
source, original word/Chinese captions and OFL resources are published separately.

**0.9.4 complete packs:** only music is user-provided. Licensed lyrics, translations, cue/word timing, spectrum data and declared visual resources download together and load automatically. Update Three / Wallpaper to **1.1.0**, Polytech Tree to **1.2.0**. Song-text terms are separate from code MIT; the Mili fan packs are non-commercial under [Mili's official guidelines](https://projectmili.com/copyright-guidelines). The npm plugin itself still includes no song or lyric data. Older timing-only packs remain supported.

**0.9.5 dsh PV resource support:** complete dsh PV pack 1.1.0 adds 98 captions, remade geometry, 1,658 raster samples and 14 atlas pages. Space Mono Bold / Anton Regular travel with their own OFL notices. The new dancer is an AI-assisted remake from the user-provided character reference, **not a recovery of unpublished original-film or MMD frames**. Consolas, Microsoft YaHei and Segoe UI Symbol use locally installed system fonts only; Windows font files and per-glyph bitmap fonts are not bundled. New assets require 0.9.5; legacy packs stay compatible.

> **Unofficial fan work.** The plugin ships **no** audio, video, lyric text or fonts; you bring your own files and they never leave your computer. The song and lyrics belong to Mili. Since **0.9.0** the plugin itself contains no MV at all and is **MIT** licensed: the two world.execute(me) MVs are one-click installs from 创意工坊, each with its own licence and a link to its original — the ASCII scenes from [yym8224961/world.execute-me-ascii](https://github.com/yym8224961/world.execute-me-ascii) (Bilibili: 野生大K, **used with the author's permission**) and the dsh PV from [MisakaZentai/world-execute-me-dsh-pv](https://github.com/MisakaZentai/world-execute-me-dsh-pv) (MIT data + **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** whale-girl art). See [License and credits](#license-and-credits).

![Library list view (Harness skin, light)](docs/screenshots/library-list.png)

## Features

- **Canvas MV player**: every frame is drawn on a canvas and synced to your audio or video file (MP3, M4A/AAC, FLAC, Ogg/Opus, WAV, the audio track of MP4/WebM/MKV …; ffmpeg can convert the rest). Lyrics from LRC / SRT / VTT, optional `spectrum.json`, keyboard control, fullscreen, per-file audio sync offsets.
- **world.execute(me) in 创意工坊** (were built-in presets until 0.8.x; one click from the empty library):
  - [**world.execute(me);**](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-workshop/tree/main/packs/world-execute-me): the five-chapter ASCII MV — original [yym8224961/world.execute-me-ascii](https://github.com/yym8224961/world.execute-me-ascii).
  - [**world.execute(me); dsh PV**](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-workshop/tree/main/packs/world-execute-me-dsh-pv): a real-time port of the "world.execute(me) through the eyes of 大肥鱼" PV (97 shots, 10 chapters, DeepSeek window, whale-girl art, per-word lyric timing matched to your own LRC) — original [MisakaZentai/world-execute-me-dsh-pv](https://github.com/MisakaZentai/world-execute-me-dsh-pv).
- **MV packs** (`mv.json`): play any song with the generic spectrum + lyrics renderer or your own sandboxed scene script; start from a template with prompts and examples.
- **用 AI 制作新 MV**: pick a song; the plugin builds a pack and hands it to a Harness agent session that writes the timing and the scene script, checked with the plugin's agent tools.
- **Automatic lyric timing**: LRCLIB lookup (optional) + a local faster-whisper / Demucs engine, word alignment with per-line confidence and section detection, then a **calibration editor** on the waveform.
- **创意工坊 (workshop)**: browse, install, update and publish community MV packs from [Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-workshop](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-workshop) (sha256-checked, no song audio; licensed captions and visual/data resources may be included).
- **Three skins** (Harness 原生 / 现代音乐应用 / 终端 · 黑客), each with 跟随 / 浅色 / 深色.
- **Library**: compact **list** (default) or cover **grid**, up to 50 recent packs, and a **collapsible** library header that shrinks to the song now playing.

Screenshots are captured from the standalone client UI preview in `tools/ui-preview`, which uses a mock Host plus placeholder demo packs and lyrics. They demonstrate rendered UI states and are not end-to-end verification against a live DSH Host.

## Install

Requires DeepSeek Harness Desktop with plugin support and Node ≥ 20 on the Host (bundled with Harness). No native dependencies.

**From npm (recommended):** run `dsh plugin --profile web add @ljwei-stak/dsh-mv-cli@0.12.1` for a web profile, or in **DeepSeek Harness Desktop → Plugins → Add plugin**, enter `@ljwei-stak/dsh-mv-cli@0.12.1`, then install and enable it.

**From a GitHub Release archive:** download `ljwei-stak-dsh-mv-cli-<version>.tgz` and its `.sha256` from [Releases](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-cli/releases). Check it in PowerShell with `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath <path-to-tgz>` and compare with the `.sha256` file, then enter the archive's absolute path in **Plugins → Add plugin**.

After installing either way:

1. **Fully quit Harness (including the tray icon) and start it again.** The Host only loads new plugin code after a full restart. If the panel shows a "后台版本与界面不一致" banner, the restart was incomplete.
2. The left sidebar shows **MV 放映室** below the built-in entries. Click it to open the panel in the main area. The plugin details page (Plugins → dsh-mv-cli) also has an **打开 MV 放映室** button.
3. The library starts empty: click **一键安装** next to world.execute(me); or the dsh PV (or **打开创意工坊** to browse), then pick your own copy of the song.

### Upgrading from 0.8.x

0.9.0 removes the built-in presets. If one was selected, the panel says it has moved to 创意工坊 and offers **从创意工坊安装**; after installing, the audio, lyrics and spectrum you had chosen for it are reused automatically. Your other packs and settings are unchanged. (0.8.x clients cannot install the dsh PV workshop pack — it exceeds their 4 MB pack limit — but they still have the built-in preset.)

## The panel at a glance

The panel reads top to bottom like a music player:

1. **曲库 (library)**: your MV packs (imported, AI-made or from the workshop; when empty, a 创意工坊 call-to-action with one-click installs of the two world.execute(me) packs), plus **创意工坊**, **用 AI 制作新 MV**, **导入 MV 包** and **新建（模板）**. **列表 / 网格** switches between the compact list (default) and cover cards; the chevron before 曲库 collapses the library to its header, the count and the row of the song now playing (remembered on this computer; the sidebar / tab 曲库 entry expands it again).
2. **正在播放 (now playing)**: title, artist, pack type and a **▶ 播放** button; tiles for audio, lyrics and spectrum.
3. **Stage**: the canvas plus a player bar (play/pause, seek, time, chapter, volume, audio sync, keyboard shortcuts, fullscreen), and the **歌词校准** editor below it.
4. **设置 (settings)**, collapsed by default: font size, subtitle offset.
5. **外观** and **ⓘ** at the top right: skin picker; about, credits and legal notice.

## Skins (外观)

**外观** picks one of three skins: **Harness 原生** (default, follows the Harness theme; Fluent cards), **现代音乐应用** (left sidebar navigation, cover grid, blurred-cover hero, page-wide bottom player bar; dark by default) or **终端 / 黑客** (tmux-style tab bar and status line, monospace + CRT scanlines; dark by default, light = paper terminal). Switching never interrupts playback. Each skin remembers its own 跟随 / 浅色 / 深色 setting in local storage. Only the look changes; every feature works the same in all three.

## MV packs: play any song

An **MV pack** is a folder with an `mv.json` manifest. It names your audio, lyrics and optional spectrum files (paths relative to the folder), and says how to draw the song:
- with the built-in **generic** canvas renderer (spectrum bars, title, current and next lyric, progress), which works for any song;
- with the **dsh-pv** renderer (`canvas.renderer: "dsh-pv"`), which replays the dsh PV from data files named in `canvas.assets` (used by the dsh PV workshop pack; only meaningful for that song);
- with a **scene script** (`canvas.renderer: "script"`, `canvas.script: "scenes.js"`): your own `render(t, cols, rows, ctx)` in plain JavaScript, run sandboxed in a Web Worker with a time limit per frame (falls back to generic on errors). The template README documents the API;
  - **Pixel scenes (0.9.1) / WebGL 2D and 3D scenes (0.9.2)**: add `"output": "pixels"` or `"output": "webgl"` (optionally `"size": [1920, 1080]`, 160×90 – 1920×1080, default 1280×720) to `canvas` and define `paint(g|gl, t, w, h, ctx)` instead of `render`:
    - `pixels`: `g` is a 2D context of an `OffscreenCanvas` in the same sandbox (no WebGL, fonts, network or DOM), 100 ms per frame. Needs plugin 0.9.1+.
    - `webgl`: `setup(info, gl)` and `paint(gl, t, w, h, ctx)` receive the sandbox-owned WebGL2 context. Bundled Three.js uses `new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas: info.canvas, context: gl })`; `info.canvas` is a minimal canvas facade, not a DOM element. Network, storage, DOM, timers, nested workers and WASM remain blocked. Use absolute `t` for seeking, not an independent animation loop. Scene cap: 2 MiB (text/pixels: 256 KiB); bitmap frame budget: 100 ms. Needs plugin 0.9.2+ and Chromium with Worker OffscreenCanvas/WebGL2; otherwise playback falls back to generic with a reason.
    Files named in `canvas.assets` arrive in `setup(info)` as `info.assets` (JSON parsed, shards merged; PNG / WebP as ImageBitmap, usable by pixels or WebGL textures). Pixel scene packs need plugin 0.9.1; webgl packs need 0.9.2 (recorded as `requires` in the workshop index). Node/CI checks use a recording context, not a real GPU; validate shaders and images separately in a browser.

In the panel's **曲库** (library):

1. **新建（模板）**: choose a folder. The plugin creates `dsh-mv-pack-template` there and never overwrites existing files. The folder contains `mv.json`, `mv.schema.json` (completion and validation in VS Code), README.md / README.zh.md, a placeholder `lyrics.example.lrc`, and `examples/` (`scenes.example.js`, seven scene modules and a full example pack). **下载模板 zip** in the import dialog gives the same files as a zip.
2. Put your own audio (any [supported format](#audio-formats)) and lyrics in the folder, and edit `mv.json`.
3. **导入 MV 包** → **选择文件夹…**, or paste the path of the folder or of `mv.json`. Importing only reads the manifest.
   - Recently used packs (up to 50) are remembered on this computer and appear in the library (× on a row or card removes it).
   - The last active pack is reopened next time.
4. **▶ 播放** plays the pack: the audio is streamed from the Host in chunks, and lyrics/spectrum are loaded with it.

Minimal `mv.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./mv.schema.json",
  "format": "dsh-mv-pack",
  "version": 1,
  "title": "My Song",
  "artist": "Someone",
  "audio": { "file": "song.mp3", "offset": 0 },
  "lyrics": { "file": "lyrics.lrc" },
  "canvas": { "renderer": "generic" }
}
```

Fields:
- `format`, `version`, `title` are required. Optional fields: `artist`, `album`, `credits[]`, `notice`, `duration`, `audio {file, offset}`, `lyrics {file, offset}` (LRC/SRT/VTT/lyrics.json), `spectrum {file}`, `canvas {renderer: generic | script | dsh-pv, script, fontSize, bpm, beatOffset, assets}`. `canvas.assets` maps names to relative `.json` / `.webp` / `.png` files (or lists of JSON shards merged in order) that a renderer reads through the Host. A legacy `terminal` section is ignored with a warning; `renderer: "world-execute-me"` (0.8.x) falls back to generic with a hint to install the workshop pack.
- Unknown fields are errors; use `x-…` for your own data.
- Relative paths must not contain `..`.

## Make a new MV with AI

**曲库 → 用 AI 制作新 MV** turns any song you have into an MV pack, with a Harness agent writing the lyric timing, `mv.json` and an ASCII scene script.

1. Click the **用 AI 制作新 MV** card. In the dialog:
   - **选择音频…**: any audio or video file Chromium can decode (see [Audio formats](#audio-formats)). The detected format is shown next to it.
   - **歌名** (pre-filled from the file name) and optionally **歌手**.
   - **歌词** (optional): paste them or **从文件读取…**. Timed LRC is best; plain text works too (the agent estimates the timing).
   - **风格说明** (optional): what you would like to see, e.g. "rainy cyberpunk night, code rain in the chorus".
   - **保存位置**: defaults to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-mv\packs`; a new sub-folder named after the song is created there and nothing is overwritten.
2. **创建 MV 包**: the panel decodes the audio locally, computes `spectrum.json` (48 bands, 20 fps), and the Host creates the folder: a copy of your audio as `audio.<ext>`, `spectrum.json`, your lyrics (`lyrics.lrc` / `lyrics.txt`), a working `mv.json` (generic renderer), `scenes.js` (an example scene), `mv.schema.json`, README and `AGENT.md` (the task description and the scene API for the agent). The pack immediately appears in the library and already plays with the generic renderer. Your original file is never modified and nothing is uploaded.
3. **在新会话中交给 AI**: the plugin adds the folder as a Harness workspace, opens a new agent session there titled `MV：<song>` and queues the task (you can edit the prompt first). The agent reads `AGENT.md`, aligns the lyrics, writes `scenes.js` and the final `mv.json`, and checks its work with the plugin's agent tools **`mv_pack_validate`** (schema, files, lyric timing, scene script run in a sandbox) and **`mv_pack_preview_frame`** (renders one frame as text). Harness may ask you to approve file writes; the session uses your model quota.
   - If your Harness build does not expose the session API to plugins, the dialog shows **复制提示词** instead (and **打开新会话** when a blank session can be opened): create a session on the pack folder yourself and paste the prompt.
4. When the agent is done, click the pack's card in the library to reload it and press **▶ 播放**. If the scene script fails in the panel (error, too slow, hangs), the panel says so and falls back to the generic renderer.

Safety: the plugin never runs external programs for this flow, scene scripts run sandboxed (Web Worker in the panel; `node:vm` with time limits and no `require`/`process` for the agent tools), and the agent tools are read-only. The tools can be turned off with the `agentTools` setting.

## MV template: prompts and examples (0.7.0)

**下载模板** and every pack made with **用 AI 制作新 MV** now contain material that helps an AI (or you) write a good MV instead of a bare example:

- `prompts/zh/` and `prompts/en/`: `01-creative-brief.md` (overall concept from song, lyrics and sections), `02-storyboard.md` (per-section storyboard), `03-scene-script-guide.md` (scene API, frame budget, sandbox limits, ASCII / layout techniques, sync to lyrics, word timings, spectrum and beat), `04-qa-checklist.md` (self-check before finishing) and `05-iteration.md` (prompts for revision rounds). `AGENT.md` and the 在新会话中交给 AI prompt walk the agent through them in that order.
- `examples/`: seven small, commented scene modules adapted from [world-execute-me-dsh-pv](https://github.com/MisakaZentai/world-execute-me-dsh-pv) (MIT, © 2026 MisakaZentai; see `examples/NOTICE.md`): `chat-window`, `heartbeat`, `ops-ticker`, `token-bar`, `execution-split`, `whale-fall` (silhouette drawn in code, **no artwork**) and `post-effects`. Each one runs in the sandboxed script renderer as is.
- `examples/rich-pack/`: a complete multi-section pack (120 s, 6 sections, transitions, karaoke word highlight, spectrum ring, beat pulses, glitch chorus, whale-fall ending) with **placeholder lyrics and no audio**: add your own audio to try it.
- New scene `ctx` fields: `ctx.section` / `ctx.sections` (from `x-dsh-mv-ai.sections`), `ctx.beat` (from `canvas.bpm` / `canvas.beatOffset`), and `ctx.lyric.words` / `word` / `progress` (enhanced LRC `<mm:ss.xx>` word stamps or `timing.json`).

## 创意工坊 (MV workshop, 0.7.0)

A community gallery of MV packs that lives in the public GitHub repository [Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-workshop](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-mv-workshop); there is no server of our own. Each pack is a folder `packs/<id>/` (`mv.json`, scenes, `cover.png`/`.webp`, README, optional `lyrics.timing.json`). GitHub Actions validates every pull request (schema, size limits, no song audio; separately licensed lyric tracks, licence field, static sandbox checks, scenes run at sample times) and, after a merge, regenerates `index.json` with each file's sha256.

**Install and play**

1. **曲库 → 创意工坊**: browse covers, search by title / artist / author / tag, filter by licence or renderer, or show only installed packs. Cards and details show the **原作** (original work) link when a pack sets `x-dsh-mv-workshop.source`. Click a card for details (licence, duration, files with sha256, GitHub source).
2. **安装到曲库**: the panel downloads the files from GitHub (or the configured fallback mirror) at the commit named in the index, checks size and sha256, validates the pack again and stores it in `<install folder>\<id>` (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-mv\workshop`, changeable since 0.9.1, see below). Cards show **有更新** when the index has a newer version (**更新到 …**); **卸载** removes the folder.
3. Play it with **your own** music. Declared pack lyrics, translations and spectrum load automatically. Old timing-only packs may still need a local lyric file. Music choices are remembered per pack; a new complete pack takes priority over stale cached lyrics, while deliberate overrides are remembered for that same pack version. Duration and optional audio fingerprint checks remain local. `lyrics.timing.json` can retime matching user-provided lyric lines by hashes.

**Install location (0.9.1)**: the bottom of the 创意工坊 page shows where packs are installed (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-mv\workshop`), with **打开文件夹**, **更改…** and **恢复默认**. Type a full path on any drive, e.g. `F:\MV\workshop` (or a `\\server\share` path); the Host checks it, creates it and tests that it can write there before switching, and explains why when it cannot. Then choose **移动到新位置** — each pack is copied, verified against the sha256 recorded at install and only then deleted from the old folder (progress and failures are shown; a failed pack stays where it was) — or **留在原处**: packs left in the old folder stay in the library and keep working, and can be moved later from the same place. Library entries follow moved packs. The setting is stored by the Host in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-mv\settings.json`; the plugin config field `workshopDir` sets the default folder (the panel's choice wins).

![Install location](docs/screenshots/install-dir.png)

### Workshop network and mirrors (0.9.8)

Set these fields in **Harness → Plugins → dsh-mv-cli → configuration**, then fully restart Harness so the Host reloads them:

- `httpProxy`: an HTTP CONNECT proxy URL such as `http://127.0.0.1:7897`. The default empty string inherits `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` (including lowercase variants); `NO_PROXY` is checked against the actual destination host and port. Only `http://` proxies are supported; HTTPS/SOCKS proxy URLs fail with an explanation, rather than silently switching to direct access. The plugin does not change your system proxy. This setting also applies to LRCLIB.
- `workshopMirror`: the HTTPS raw-file prefix of a **trusted, available** workshop mirror, without a branch, commit, query, credentials or fragment. Since 0.10.0 the default (also for an absent field) is `https://www.jianweilimarx.top/dsh-mv-workshop`. An explicitly saved empty string still disables fallback; older configurations saved as empty must restore the default or enter this URL. The plugin appends `main/index.json` for the index and `<commit>/packs/<id>/<file>` for files. Gitee is not the default: its content restrictions remain unresolved.

The Huawei mirror's existing seven packs and independent Corresponding Source were anonymously verified without any proxy: all 137 files, 40,317,815 bytes, matching SHA-256. A dedicated unprivileged pull service checks the fixed official GitHub repository every 15 minutes; files are immutable and the catalogue changes last. Failed syncs preserve the previous index. It serves only public static files, not uploads or arbitrary proxy URLs; it does not modify OpenClaw. Bandwidth/certificate/service availability is not guaranteed. Operator tools: [tools/workshop-static](tools/workshop-static).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH Remote

A single DSH bundle for pairing with another DSH over a trusted LAN or VPN and controlling its workspaces and sessions from a native **Remote DSH** panel.

The repository root **is** the plugin package. Do not look for a nested package directory.

## Install

Install the repository root as one bundle:

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle target: /absolute/path/to/dsh-remote
```

If the Plugins-page installer accepts local folders, select the repository root directly. It contains `package.json` with `dsh.bundle.patch` and `cordis.patch.yml`.

After installation, refresh the DSH page once. A **Remote DSH** icon appears in the sidebar.

## What it provides

- **Remote DSH panel** — a sidebar icon and dedicated main panel:
  - **This computer**: enable/disable remote access, choose the LAN/VPN interface and stable port, generate a pairing code, list paired devices, and revoke them.
  - **Remote computers**: pair a host, browse its workspaces and sessions, create/rename/delete/reorder workspaces, and create/rename/reorder/pin/archive/open sessions.
- **Host services** — persistent pairing, device-token authentication, remote workspace/session state and actions, remote directory browsing, and one-time browser sessions for opening the full remote DSH or a specific session in a new tab.

## Pair two machines

On the **home** DSH:

1. Open **Remote DSH → This computer**.
2. Enable **Allow remote access**, choose the reachable LAN/VPN interface and a stable port, then **Apply**.
3. Click **Pair a new computer** and copy the address plus pairing code.

On the **laptop** DSH:

1. Open **Remote DSH → Remote computers**.
2. Enter a name, the home address, and the pairing code, then **Pair**.
3. Select the paired computer to control its workspaces and sessions.

Do not copy `$DSH_HOME/remote-dsh/` between machines. Pairing creates the device record on the home DSH and stores the token on the laptop.

## Security

- Remote DSH uses plain HTTP on the LAN/VPN. Use only a trusted network.
- Paired devices are owner-level: they can control every exposed workspace and session, and opening the full remote UI gives the same access as a local browser.
- The host stores only SHA-256 device-token hashes; the laptop stores the token in the DSH credential store. The device token is never sent to the browser.
- Revoke a paired device in the home’s **This computer** tab when it is no longer needed. Revocation closes browser sessions created by that device.
- Remote-DSH routes reject requests that arrive through a one-time browser bridge, so a remote browser cannot create new pairings or change remote-access settings.

## Requirements

- DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` or a compatible build providing the workspace, session, session-query, connection, and web-server services.
- Both machines reachable over the same LAN or an existing VPN.
- The remote-access port and the DSH process allowed through the home firewall.

## Layout

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host entry and browser-facing Fetch routes. |
| `remote-host.js` | Remote access service, pairing/device records, state/actions, directory browsing, browser-session manager. |
| `browser-bridge.js` | Internal one-time authenticated reverse proxy for browser sessions. |
| `client.js` | The Remote DSH browser panel and remote-session auto-open. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Loader bundle patch. |
| `test/` | Smoke tests for the browser bridge, pairing/proxy, and state/action handling. |

## Verification

```bash
node test/browser-bridge-smoke.mjs
node test/remote-smoke.mjs
node test/remote-service-smoke.mjs
```

# @argszero/dsh-activation-doctor

Writes the activation report the harness already composes and never files.

When a plugin fails to activate — most often because a tool or prompt-section
name it registers is already taken — the fiber that threw is unloaded **whole**:
every tool and every prompt section that plugin contributed disappears, while the
marketplace still shows it installed and enabled. This plugin sweeps the loader's
entries after the tree settles, awaits each fiber to recover the original error
and stack, and files a private report where an operator will find it.

It is a **detector, not a repairer**. It does not revive the failed plugin, does
not change registration semantics, does not touch the marketplace row, and cannot
move the desktop shell's stderr. A plugin whose tool name collides still fails;
the difference is that you can now find out which two plugins, which name, and
from where.

## The problem

The reported incident
([#9308](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/9308)) is the
clean form of it. A third-party plugin registered a tool whose name was already
taken. `NamedEntries.insert` threw before any insertion, the error left the
plugin body, and the fiber unloaded — taking with it every tool and every prompt
section that plugin had contributed. The operator's search for a log found **zero
hits**.

Zero hits is the expected result, and the reason is structural rather than a bug
in logging. Three facts, each read from the shipped source:

1. **The failure *is* logged, into a sink nobody can read.** `Fiber._reload()`
   catches the plugin body's throw, calls `this.ctx.logger.error(reason)`, records
   the error, and unloads the fiber (`vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts`). Neither
   shipped profile mounts a logger sink.
2. **Startup only *fails* for core entry ids.** `auditStartupEntries` marks an
   entry required only when its id is in the built-in set or it is the bootstrap
   include (`packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts`). A third-party id can never be
   in that set, so a third-party failure takes the `warn` branch: one line goes to
   `process.stderr`, and the rest of the application starts normally.
3. **The durable report is written only on that fatal path.**
   `reportStartupFailure` has exactly one caller — the `StartupError` handler in
   `apps/cli/src/bin.ts` — so `$DSH_HOME/logs/startup-*.log` is never created for a
   third-party-only failure. In the desktop build the stderr line is drained into a
   64 KiB in-memory buffer (`apps/desktop/src/host-process.ts`) that is attached to
   an error message only on **exit**.

So the missing piece is not a fix to the loader, the registry or the audit policy
— it is a **sink**. The state a report needs is already public: the loader exposes
its entries (`ctx.loader.entries()`), every entry carries its fiber, and
`fiber.await()` rethrows the original activation error with its stack.

## The stage before the entries

An entry that failed is still an entry. It has an id, a name and a fiber, which is
why it can be reported at all. The strictly larger loss is the one shape the entry
sweep cannot see: a **bundle the profile names and the process did not start from**.

A bundle is composed *before* any entry exists. When the launcher skips one —
the bundle is not installed, a peer is missing, the name is misspelled — it
contributes **no entries at all**: no fiber, no `internal/status` event, nothing to
await. The process starts, every remaining entry activates perfectly, and the
application runs with a smaller composition than its own configuration declares.
That is
[#9451](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/9451): for such
a profile, `dsh` and `--dump-config` both exit `0`, and the launcher prints the
skip reason once to stderr and carries on.

The doctor reports this too. It diffs the profile manifest's declared bundles
against the launcher's own `ctx.profileContext.startedBundles`, and for each name
that did not contribute it recovers the launcher's skip reason from
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot`'s `loadProfileDirectory(...).skippedBundles` — read as
a package at runtime, so **this plugin still declares no dependency on it**. Where
the launcher is unreachable the finding stands and the report says the reason is
unavailable, naming why.

| `profileBundles` header line | meaning |
|------------------------------|---------|
| `2 declared, 2 started` | every declared bundle contributed |
| `2 declared, 1 started, 1 did not start` | one name in the manifest contributed nothing |
| `the declaration could not be read — …` | the manifest was missing or malformed. **Not** the same as "names no bundles" |

A third-party entry failure takes the `warn` branch of `auditStartupEntries`, so
nothing can turn a partial composition into an exit status from outside the
launcher — the report is where an operator can see it.

## The stage before the composition

There is one more way to lose a plugin, and both stages above are blind to it: the
package is **installed and never selected**. It is not in
`ctx.profileContext.startedBundles` (it contributed no layer) and it is not in
`dsh.profile.bundles` either (nothing ever added it there), so the two agree, the
composition looks healthy, and the plugin is simply absent from the process. The
entry sweep has nothing to report because there is no entry, and the composition
diff has nothing to report because both of its sides are consistent.

That is [#9261](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/9261):
`dsh plugin add` installs through the package manager and reconciles afterwards, so
a run the CLI never finishes leaves the package in `dependencies` and in
`pnpm-lock.yaml` with `dsh.profile.bundles` untouched. `pnpm install` run by hand, a
profile edited by a script, an interrupted or killed install — all reach the same
state, and nothing in the running application can report it, because the only
artifact of the loss is a list the package is missing from.

The doctor reads those two lists off the same manifest parse and reports the
difference:

| `profileBundles` header line | meaning |
|------------------------------|---------|
| `1 declared, 1 started, 1 installed but never selected` | a dependency declares `dsh.bundle` and is not in the bundle list |
| `coverage: 2 of 11 dependencies could not be inspected` | how much of the dependency set this arm actually read |

The qualifier is what keeps this from being noise. **Most dependencies are not
bundles** — a profile's `dependencies` and its `dsh.profile.bundles` are different
lists on purpose — so the bundle claim is read from each package's own manifest, the
way the harness's own `bundleManifest` reads it: a dependency is a bundle when its
`dsh.bundle.patch` is defined. A dependency declaring none is inspected and passed
over; a dependency whose `dsh.bundle.patch` exists but is neither a file path nor a
list of them is reported too, because app-boot throws while loading that declaration
and the profile loses the package either way.

Each dependency is resolved from disk the way the loader resolves a bundle — the
**installation anchor first, then the profile** — so an in-box package is never
mistaken for the profile-local copy, and only `package.json` files are read: no
third-party module is imported to describe one. Dependencies this arm cannot resolve,
or whose manifest it cannot read, are listed as **coverage**, never as findings: an
incomplete audit must not read as a broken installation.

Two things are deliberately not checked. The reverse direction — a name in
`dsh.profile.bundles` that is not a dependency — is the normal shape of a healthy
profile, since every shipped bundle comes from the installation rather than the
profile. And a bundle that *is* selected but cannot be loaded is the arm above: the
launcher reports it in `skippedBundles`.

## The rows the launcher switched off

The entry sweep classifies a `disabled` entry as a decision. That is wrong for
exactly one class of row. Before the Loader is handed a profile's entry list,
`prepareProfileEntries` runs a compatibility preflight over it and refuses a row by
setting `disabled: true` on a clone of the list. Three consequences follow, and each
one is why this arm exists:

- **On the only surface a plugin can read, a refusal and a decision are the same
  value.** There is no second flag, no annotation, and no record of what the
  declaration said before the preflight touched it.
- **The reason is one stderr line**, written at composition time, before any plugin
  owns a logger. In the desktop build it drains into the 64 KiB buffer that is
  attached to an error message only on *exit*, so while the application is running
  the reason exists nowhere an operator can look.
- **The line it does print is often misleading.** Any throw from reading the row's
  manifest is rewritten as *"its declared dsh requirements cannot be validated"*,
  which describes a version-range question. The case in
  [#10203](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/10203) is a
  `--patch` row with **no `name` field at all**: `manifestOf` opens with
  `name.startsWith('cordis:')`, so `undefined` throws `Cannot read properties of
  undefined (reading 'startsWith')`, the catch rewrites it, and `deny()` switches
  the row off. The patch file looks correct, and `--dump-config` renders the patch
  layer without ever calling the preflight, so it looks correct there too.

The doctor censuses the switched-off entries and separates the two:

| `switchedOff` header line | meaning |
|---------------------------|---------|
| `2 entries, 0 refused by the launcher's preflight; rule: the launcher's own` | both switch-offs are yours |
| `1 entry, 1 refused by the launcher's preflight; rule: not needed` | the row no manifest could ever be read for |
| `1 entry, 0 refused …, 1 could not be recomputed; rule: unavailable — …` | coverage, not a finding: this census could not classify the row |

For a row with no `name` the verdict needs no dependency at all — the declaration
is structurally unreadable, and the row could not mount enabled or not. Every other
row's verdict is the launcher's own `evaluatePluginCompatibility`, run against the
manifest the row names with the profile's `compatibility.json` exemptions applied,
so a granted exemption is never reported as a refusal.

That verdict is worded as *"the preflight refuses this row"* and not as *"the
preflight denied this row"*, deliberately: the preflight skips a row that is already
`disabled`, so a row you switched off by hand is never one it touched, and no
surface is left that says which of the two happened. What the report can say is
what the rule makes of the declaration — and for a row that is switched off *and*
incompatible, the sentence that helps is the one saying re-enabling it will not
work either.

Two limits are stated rather than hidden. The preflight rewrites clones in place
and keeps no copy of the original declaration, so this is **recompute-only**: it
cannot diff the patch row against the Loader's entry. And a row whose manifest
cannot be resolved from the same anchors the Loader uses is listed as **coverage**,
never as "the operator did it" — an audit that cannot answer must not answer
"healthy".

## Install

**In the application (the Desktop shell, and the Web UI).** Desktop's profile is
the application's own and cannot be managed from a terminal: `dsh --profile
desktop` and `dsh plugin --profile desktop …` are both refused before they run
(`apps/cli/src/args.ts`, `rejectElectronProfile` — the `plugin` subcommand skips
the refusal only for Desktop's own installed carrier). Install it where that
profile *is* managed: open the sidebar's **Plugins** page, choose **Add plugin**,
and give the package name.

```
@argszero/dsh-activation-doctor
```

The Host reads the spec, installs it, and offers **Enable now**; the same page
switches the plugin off later without uninstalling it (which is what keeps the
report file readable after the incident).

**In a profile the launcher manages (web, tui, any custom profile).**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add @argszero/dsh-activation-doctor
```

That command forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory, so `npm install
@argszero/dsh-activation-doctor` run there is equivalent — a profile is an
ordinary package with its own `package.json`.

Then mount it, or apply the bundled patch, which mounts it and changes nothing
else:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: activation-doctor
      name: '@argszero/dsh-activation-doctor'
      inject:
        - loader
```

## What it does

- **Sweeps after the tree settles.** An entry that has not finished importing has
  no fiber yet, and reading that as an import failure is exactly the wrong answer
  this plugin exists to prevent. The sweep waits for the loader's pending task
  count to reach zero, then classifies every entry — including nested subtrees.
- **Classifies four ways, behaviourally.** `await fiber.await()` is the primary
  question, because cordis declares fiber states as a `const enum` and a `const
  enum` is **erased at emit time**: `import { FiberState } from
  '@deepseek-ai/cordis'` evaluates to `undefined`, so `fiber.state ===
  FiberState.FAILED` is `false` for a failure. The numeric state is read only
  *after* a successful settle, to separate `active` from `pending`, and a state it
  does not recognise is reported as `unknown` with its raw value rather than
  guessed into a category:

  | outcome | meaning |
  |---------|---------|
  | `disabled` | switched off in the profile or patch. A decision, not a finding |
  | `import-failed` | the module could not be imported, so no fiber exists |
  | `failed` | the fiber threw; the original error and stack are reported |
  | `active` | running |
  | `pending` | waiting for a service; the missing service names are reported |
  | `unknown` | a settled state with no name, reported with its numeric value |

- **Files a private report.** `<home>/logs/activation-<timestamp>-<uuid>.log`,
  directory mode `0700`, file mode `0600`, created with `wx` so an existing path
  is an error rather than an overwrite. **Those modes are POSIX only**: Windows has
  no permission bits, Node drops the `mode` argument there, and access is decided by
  whatever ACL the log directory inherits. On Windows the `wx` exclusivity still
  holds, but "private" is not something this plugin establishes or can assert. `<home>` is `$DSH_HOME` when it is set to
  a non-blank value, and `~/.dsh` otherwise — the same directory the harness's own
  startup report uses. The first line warns that raw diagnostics may contain
  configuration or credential values.

  **Before pasting a report into a public thread, read its header.** It records
  `timestamp`, `phase`, `settled`, `dshVersion`, `profile`, `nodeVersion`,
  `platform` and `execPath` — the last three name the machine and the exact Node
  binary, which is more about you than about the bug. The entries below the header
  quote a failing plugin's own error text verbatim, and that text is whatever the
  plugin chose to say, so it may carry a path or a value from your configuration.
- **Prints one line** per finding, plus the report path, to stderr — the same
  channel the harness already uses for third-party activation failures.
- **Keeps watching.** A failure that appears later — a hot reload, a profile patch
  re-application, a plugin mounted after startup — is reported too. `internal/status`
  fires for every fiber in the process, including fibers owned by other contexts,
  which is what makes a post-startup failure observable at all.
- **Answers `activation_status` on demand.** "Which of my plugins is actually
  running" is a question you ask *after* the process is up, usually while looking
  at a session in which a tool you expect is missing. The answer comes from the
  same sweep as the report, so the two can never disagree.
- **Audits the profile composition as well.** A bundle the launcher skipped
  contributes no entries, so the sweep above cannot see it. See
  [the stage before the entries](#the-stage-before-the-entries).
- **Reports installed packages the profile never selected.** The one loss both
  stages above agree on, because a package that never entered
  `dsh.profile.bundles` is missing from each list they read. See
  [the stage before the composition](#the-stage-before-the-composition).
- **Separates "you switched it off" from "the launcher refused it".** A denial is
  `disabled: true`, the same value your own decision produces, and its reason is
  one stderr line written before any plugin could read it. See
  [the rows the launcher switched off](#the-rows-the-launcher-switched-off).

## Configuration

| key | default | meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` installs nothing at all |
| `log` | `'summary'` | `'off'` writes the file and says nothing on the terminal |
| `report` | `true` | write the durable file |
| `reportDir` | `$DSH_HOME/logs` | where reports are written; a leading `~` is expanded |
| `includePending` | `true` | list entries waiting for a service |
| `composition` | `true` | audit the profile's declared bundles against what this process started from |
| `installed` | `true` | report installed dependencies that declare a bundle and were never selected |
| `denial` | `true` | separate the entries the launcher's preflight refused from the ones you switched off |
| `watch` | `true` | re-report failures that appear after the first sweep |
| `tool` | `true` | register the `activation_status` tool |
| `maxEntries` | `50` | inclusive bound on the entries listed |
| `errorChars` | `4000` | inclusive bound on one entry's rendered error |
| `maxLiveReports` | `5` | cap on post-startup reports per process |
| `debounceMs` | `50` | quiet period before a sweep |
| `maxSettleTries` | `400` | sweeps that may pass while the loader still has pending tasks |

Every value is read defensively: a configuration file is authored by hand, and a
diagnostic that throws on a typo is a diagnostic that loses the failure it was
mounted to report.

There is deliberately **no `Config` schema export**. Cordis validates a plugin's
config through `runtime.Config['~standard'].validate(config)` whenever the runtime
carries a `Config` at all, and a plain defaults object has no `~standard` —
exporting one throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'validate')`
out of `Fiber._reload`, taking the plugin down before it can report on anybody.
A schema would satisfy that check at the price of a `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`
peer; the knobs above are normalized in code instead, so the defaults are the same
with or without a schema, and one fewer dependency is one fewer range to keep
admitted across the release lines.

## What it is not

- **It does not repair anything.** The failed plugin stays failed, its entry stays
  enabled, and nothing it contributed comes back.
- **It cannot move the desktop shell's stderr.** The 64 KiB ring buffer is in
  `apps/desktop/src/host-process.ts`; a plugin can write more to stderr, not
  redirect what is already there. The report file is the answer to that.
- **It is not a policy change.** Registration semantics, the marketplace row and
  the startup-audit required-id set are all untouched. Switching a denied row back
  on does not make it run: the report says so, and changes nothing.
- **It cannot tell a denied row from an identical row you switched off.** The
  preflight rewrites clones in place and keeps no copy of the original declaration,
  so the census recomputes the launcher's verdict from what the entry still carries
  and cannot diff it against the patch row that produced it.
- **It does not re-import a module to explain an `import-failed` entry.** The
  obvious way to recover that reason is to import the entry's specifier again and
  catch the throw — but that re-executes third-party module code inside the
  doctor's own context, for a plugin the harness has already decided not to load,
  and it would contradict the promise above that the doctor never touches the
  plugin that failed. A resolve-only probe (`import.meta.resolve`,
  `createRequire(...).resolve`) executes nothing, but it has to resolve from the
  entry's own base URL, and no public surface the doctor reads exposes it — so the
  probe would answer about the doctor's location instead and be wrong for exactly
  the relative specifiers it was meant to explain. The entry is reported by id and
  name, and the harness's own import error is not replaced by a guess.
- **`reportDir` has no access to a launcher-configured home.** The harness's own
  `resolveDshHome` honours an explicit configured path supplied by the launcher; a
  plugin mounted from a patch cannot see that value. If you configure a non-default
  home, set `reportDir` explicitly.

## Supported lines

The peer ranges admit the harness lines this package was measured against:

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` `0.1.7-rc.2`, `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.2`
- `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `4.0.4` and `4.0.5-alpha.1`

`node scripts/probe-lines.mjs` copies this package into a scratch tree per line,
pins the whole line, installs, builds and runs the suite — the range is a claim
nobody ran until that passes.

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm test                       # tsc, then node --test on the real loader
npm run test:inject            # mutate each distinction; every arm must be caught
npm run test:probe-lines       # install and test each supported line
```

`npm test` mounts a real cordis context, the real loader, the real
`SystemPrompt`, the real `ToolRuntime` and real fixture modules on disk. The
incident is reproduced rather than simulated: two fixtures register the same tool
name, the second one's registration throws out of its body, and the whole plugin
goes down with that fiber. A control arm mounts everything **except** the doctor,
so "the report names the failure" is never confounded with "the failure happened
at all".

## License

MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @argszero/dsh-recursive-delete-guard

A Cordis plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) that refuses a **recursive delete whose operand is a filesystem root** rather than a directory.

It exists because of one incident, [discussion #10569](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/10569): a cleanup meant to remove one project subdirectory instead removed the root of `C:` — 48 user files, much of `Program Files` — in 120 seconds, under `danger-full-access` with `approval: never`.

## What actually happened

The command was written as

```powershell
$d = 'C:/Users/<user>/Documents/AI/Moveit/pvkit/projects/v4_wall_full/out/film_blur_frames'
if (Test-Path $d) { cmd /c "rd /s /q \"$d\"" }
```

`\"` is a `cmd.exe` escape. It is not a PowerShell escape — PowerShell escapes with a backtick — so the string ends at that quote and the delete verb is handed `\`, the root of the current drive.

Measured on PowerShell 7.6.7 with a stand-in `cmd` that prints its argv:

| command | argv the delete verb sees |
|---|---|
| `cmd /c "rd /s /q \"$d\""` | `[1] = rd /s /q \`  `[2] = <the path>\` |
| `cmd /c "rd /s /q `"$d`""` | `[1] = rd /s /q "<the path>"` |

The reporter's stderr corroborates it independently: every path it lists is anchored at the drive root (`\PROGRA~2`, `\$RECYCLE.BIN`, `\pagefile.sys`). Nothing in the harness checked the target, because `danger-full-access` means exactly that.

## What this plugin does

Before a tool call is dispatched, it reads the command string, splits it **in the dialect of the shell that would run it**, follows `cmd /c` and `sh -c` wrappers inside it, and denies the call when a recursive delete's operand is one of:

- a filesystem root — `/`, `\`, `//`, `\\`
- a drive root — `C:\`, `C:/`, `C:/*`, `C:\*`
- a bare drive letter — `C:` (the current directory on that drive)
- a separator relative to the current drive's root — `\Users\x` (Windows only)
- a path that normalizes to the directory the command started in — `.`, `..`, `a/..`
- nothing at all — `rm -rf`, `Remove-Item -Recurse`

Everything else passes through untouched.

```
Recursive delete refused: "rd" would receive "the operand "\" is a filesystem root".
A shell does not always hand a delete program the path the command text appears to name. …
```

## What it does not do

- **It is not a sandbox.** A recursive delete aimed at a real subdirectory is allowed, including one outside the workspace: you chose `danger-full-access`, and a plugin that quietly narrowed it would be a different product with a different consent story.
- **It does not build a blocklist of destructive programs.** The set is explicit and small — `rm -r`, `rd|rmdir /s`, `del|erase /s`, `deltree`, and PowerShell's `Remove-Item` with its aliases. `find -delete`, `git clean -fdx`, `shred`, and a language runtime's own delete are out of scope by design.
- **It cannot see an expansion.** `rm -rf "$OUT"` is allowed, because the operand is a variable and the guard does not evaluate one. The reported command *is* caught, because the operand that reaches `rd` is a literal `\` in the command text — but a guard that guessed at variable values would refuse working commands.
- **It fails open.** A command it cannot split confidently — an unterminated quote — is allowed, not guessed at.
- **It is not the upstream fix.** The report's items 1, 2 and 4 belong to the core: validate a destructive target before running it, require confirmation for destructive commands, and make the timeout kill the *process tree*. This plugin is a floor under the worst case.

## Install

```sh
npm i github:argszero/dsh-recursive-delete-guard
```

then mount it through its bundle patch like any other DSH plugin:

```yaml
# cordis.yml
plugins:
  '@argszero/dsh-recursive-delete-guard': {}
```

## Configuration

```yaml
plugins:
  '@argszero/dsh-recursive-delete-guard':
    mode: deny      # deny (default) | off
    tools:          # shell tools whose `command` argument is read
      - bash
      - pwsh
```

`mode: off` mounts nothing at all. An unknown `mode`, a non-array `tools`, or a `tools` entry that is not a string throws at mount time — a guard that silently defaulted would report protection it does not provide.

## Verification

```sh
node --test test/*.spec.mjs      # 136 tests
node scripts/inject-defects.mjs  # 30 mutation arms, every one CAUGHT
node scripts/mount-smoke.mjs     # real cordis dispatch, deny and allow both observed
```

The suite pins the measured argv above, so a tokenizer change that stopped reproducing it would fail rather than quietly start agreeing with itself.

## License

MIT.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-agent-progress

给 **DeepSeek Harness** 网页端加一条常驻的任务进度条：当前对话在干什么、走到第几步、还剩多少，一眼可见；其他对话里的任务也会自动出现在列表里。

- 一条扁平进度条，没有卡通元素、没有悬浮球、没有表情
- 没有任务时显示「无任务」，不消失
- 百分比来自真实数据（todo 清单、`done/total`、任务自己发布的进度、会话历史步数与耗时），不是来回滑动的加载动画
- 后台命令、子代理这类脱离回合运行的任务也会出现，含其他对话里的
- 可拖动、可展开，展开后每项任务各有一条自己的进度
- 只读本地文件与宿主任务注册表，不写宿主状态、不依赖任何第三方包

---

## 为什么

DSH 的一个回合可能跑很久：装依赖、下模型、批量处理文件。网页端原本只在会话里滚动输出，切到别的对话就完全不知道刚才那个任务走到哪了。这个插件补的就是这块：一条一直在右上角（可拖动）的进度条，加上「所有对话的任务」聚合视图。

## 特性

| 能力 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 常驻 | 无任务时显示「无任务 · 空闲」，不会整条消失 |
| 真实百分比 | 优先用 `done/total`；有 todo 清单时用完成数；否则用该会话历史平均步数/耗时推算，封顶 99%，完成才到 100% |
| 跨会话聚合 | 任何对话正在跑的回合都会被自动发现，显示标题、项目目录、`第 N 轮 · 第 M 步`、已用与剩余 |
| 后台任务 | 接入宿主 `ctx.jobs` 事件流：后台命令、子代理、长任务一注册就出现，结束时显示完成/失败，跨会话同样可见 |
| 总进度 | 折叠时显示的是**所有在跑任务的加权总进度**（按 `total` 加权，无边界的任务各算 1 份），不再只挑其中一条 |
| 拖动 | 按住卡片拖动，位置存 `localStorage`，刷新后保持 |
| 展开 | 折叠时一行**总进度**；展开后每项任务一条进度、状态点、阶段/速度/耗时 |
| 五色克制 | 只用 `#21467A #C71F2D #D45814 #DBA972 #f4f5f7`，无阴影、无渐变、无半透明 |
| 零依赖 | 宿主侧只读 `fs`，网页侧只用 React 与宿主已注入的服务 |

## 安装

### 方式一：插件市场

在 DSH 网页端的「插件市场 → 已安装」里安装并启用 `dsh-agent-progress`。启用后刷新页面即可。

### 方式二：直接从 GitHub 装（尚未发布 npm 时）

本包是零依赖的纯 JS 插件，可以直接从 tag 的源码包安装，不需要先发 npm：

```bash
pnpm add "https://github.com/Autodog875/dsh-agent-progress/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.1.tar.gz" --dir <DSH_HOME>/profiles/desktop
```

装完用插件市场的开关把它启用（市场会负责写 `bundles` 并热加载），刷新页面即可。

> 这种方式市场里搜不到，更新时要把 URL 里的版本号一起改掉。

### 方式三：本地 link（开发用）

```bash
pnpm add "link:D:/path/to/dsh-agent-progress" --dir <DSH_HOME>/profiles/desktop
```

然后在插件市场里把 `dsh-agent-progress` 打开（市场会把它写进 profile 的 `bundles`）。

> 手改 `package.json` 的 `bundles` 会被插件市场的状态（`.dsh-market/state.json`）反推覆盖，请走市场开关。

## 使用

网页端会自动显示进度。需要让某个任务显示精确百分比时，用附带的 CLI 写一条记录：

```bash
# 开始一个 500 个文件的任务
node bin/ap.mjs set --key download --label "下载视频" --total 500 --done 0 --unit 个

# 推进（可反复调用，只需给变化的部分）
node bin/ap.mjs set --key download --done 137 --speed 3.2 --eta 120

# 结束 / 失败
node bin/ap.mjs done --key download
node bin/ap.mjs fail --key download --note "sha256 mismatch"

# 长任务保活（每 5 秒续一次心跳，直到超时）
node bin/ap.mjs hold --key download --seconds 600

# 清掉已结束的记录
node bin/ap.mjs clear

# 看记录目录
node bin/ap.mjs dir
```

记录写在 `<DSH_HOME>/agent-progress/<sessionId>/<key>.json`，默认同时镜像到所有会话目录，所以每个对话都能看到同一条进度（`--local` 只写当前会话）。

字段：

```json
{
  "key": "download",
  "label": "下载视频",
  "status": "running",
  "done": 137,
  "total": 500,
  "unit": "个",
  "speed": 3.2,
  "eta": 120,
  "phase": "加密校验",
  "note": "",
  "startedAt": 1792572000000,
  "updatedAt": 1792572060000
}
```

`status` 取 `running` / `done` / `failed`。`running` 的记录 15 秒没有心跳会被判定为中断；结束的记录保留 60 秒（界面再留 6 秒）。

## 百分比是怎么算的

按优先级：

1. 记录里给了 `total > 0` → `done / total`。
2. 会话有 todo 清单 → 已完成条数 / 总条数。
3. 后台任务自己发布了进度行（`7/10 files`、`42%`）→ 直接采用。
4. 都没有 → 用**该会话自己的历史**当分母：
   - 时间维度：`本轮已用 ÷ 平均每轮耗时`
   - 步数维度：`当前步数 ÷ 平均每轮步数`
   - 取两者较大值，夹在 1%–99% 之间；回合结束时由宿主状态变化自动消失。
   后台任务没有上面任何数据时，用 `已用时间` 做单调上升的估算，封顶 95%，只有真正结束才到 100%。

所以进度条随任务真实推进而增长，不会空转；但也请注意第 4 种是**估算**，不是精确值。

## 工作原理

```
网页端 (lib/client.js)
  └─ 注册槽位 conversation.session.header.actions
      └─ 每 0.8s（有任务）/ 4s（空闲）调用
          connection.rpc.call('/api', 'agentProgress/state', { request: { sessionId, global: true } })

宿主侧 (lib/index.js)  AgentProgressService
  ├─ 读 <DSH_HOME>/agent-progress/<sessionId>/*.json      ← 显式记录（ap.mjs 写）
  ├─ 订阅 ctx.jobs.events（进程级，所有会话）
  │     registered / progress / settled → 后台任务行（含归属会话、完成/失败）
  └─ 扫 <DSH_HOME>/storages/session_projcache/sessions/*.json
        sessionStats.openStep 非空 + 文件 2 分钟内被改写 = 该会话正在工作
        → 生成一行（标题、项目、轮/步、估算百分比）
```

`cordis.patch.yml` 把服务以 `agent-progress` 这个名字插入 profile 的插件图：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: agent-progress
      name: 'dsh-agent-progress'
```

## 目录结构

```
lib/index.js        宿主侧服务：读记录、订阅任务事件流、扫会话、合并去重
lib/client.js       网页侧组件：进度条、拖动、展开、轮询
bin/ap.mjs          CLI：写/推进/结束记录
cordis.patch.yml    插件图补丁
test/preflight.mjs  客户端冒烟测试（桩 React + 桩模块加载器）
test/state-check.mjs 宿主侧 state() 合并逻辑测试
test/jobs-check.mjs 后台任务行测试（桩 ctx.jobs 事件流）
test/demo*.mjs      演示用：造几条假任务
```

## 开发

```bash
node test/preflight.mjs     # 11 项客户端检查
node test/state-check.mjs   # 宿主侧合并/单位/foreign 检查
node test/jobs-check.mjs    # 后台任务行：百分比解析、跨会话归属、结算状态
```

改完客户端代码后，让宿主重建补丁：

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<GUI 端口>/dsh-market/toggle \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"dsh-agent-progress","enabled":false}'
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<GUI 端口>/dsh-market/toggle \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"dsh-agent-progress","enabled":true}'
```

## 兼容性

- DSH 0.2.x（桌面端 / 网页端），`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client.platform: web`
- peer：`@deepseek-ai/cordis ^4.0.1`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol`
- Node.js ≥ 20（CLI 用）

## 已知边界

- 折叠时的「总进度」是加权平均：同时跑多个任务、中途又新来一个 0% 的任务时，数字可能短暂回退，这是平均的固有行为；新任务出现的前 2 秒不参与加权，避免数字瞬间塌陷。
- 后台任务靠宿主任务注册表（`ctx.jobs`）的事件流发现：插件加载**之后**注册的任务必然可见；加载前就在跑的，会在第一次轮询时用 `jobs.list(sessionId)` 补种。任务注册表是进程内的，重启后自然清空。
- 没有 todo、没有 `total`、任务也没发布进度的，百分比是估算值。
- 只读本机 `<DSH_HOME>` 下的进度与投影文件，不联网、不上报。诊断文件 `<DSH_HOME>/agent-progress/.host-status.json` 只记录本插件自己的状态。

## 更新日志

### v0.1.2

- 折叠时显示**总进度**：所有在跑任务按 `total` 加权平均（没有 `total` 的各算 1 份），文案变成「总进度 · N 个任务」，右侧给 `xx% · ✓完成数 · ✗失败数`。
- 失败项不参与平均，只进计数；新任务前 2 秒不参与，避免数字瞬间回退。
- 只有一个任务时行为不变，仍显示它的标题与进度。
- `test/preflight.mjs` 增加 6 项聚合断言（单任务等价、按量加权、失败不拉低、新任务淡入、全为瞬时任务）。

### v0.1.1

- 修复：后台任务在跑时错误显示「无任务」。宿主侧现在订阅 `ctx.jobs.events`，注册、进度、结算都会变成进度条里的一行，跨会话可见。
- 后台任务有自报进度（`7/10`、`42%`）时用真实百分比；没有时按已用时间给出单调上升、封顶 95% 的估算。
- 新增 `test/jobs-check.mjs`。

### v0.1.0

首个版本：常驻进度条、跨会话聚合、确定百分比、拖动与展开、五色配色、CLI 写记录。

## License

MIT

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# 抖音专家 (douyin-expert)

把 Qoder 上 5 个抖音 / 多平台 / 海外插件的全部能力，去重整合成 **一个 DeepSeek Harness 宿主插件**：
22 个技能、37 个可执行脚本，装好后自动出现在 DSH 技能目录里。

| 来源插件 | 版本 | 贡献技能 |
|---|---|---|
| 抖音爆款内容制造机 | 1.0.0 | 8 个（去重后 6 个独立） |
| 抖音内容灵感专家 | 1.0.0 | 8 个（去重后 4 个独立） |
| 抖音增长黑客 | 1.0.0 | 8 个（去重后 4 个独立） |
| 多平台AI信息源 | 1.0.1 | 6 个 |
| 海外内容创作专家 | 1.0.1 | 3 个（**已改为开源实现**） |

---

## 装了什么

去重后 **22 个技能**（原 33 个技能目录，11 个重名已按「文件最全」原则合并）：

### 抖音核心（13 个）

| 技能 | 干什么 | 需要 Key |
|---|---|---|
| `douyin-daily-hot` | 每日最热作品榜，单日点赞 TOP50 | 是 |
| `douyin-hot-trend` | 实时热榜，每小时更新，支持近 7/30 天 | 是 |
| `douyin-content-surge` | 每日点赞飙升榜 TOP50 | 是 |
| `douyin-weekly-surge` | 七日点赞飙升榜 TOP50 | 是 |
| `douyin-search` | 关键词搜索爆款作品，支持日期范围 | 是 |
| `douyin-works-crawler` | 输入账号名/ID，输出近期作品列表 | 是 |
| `douyin-top-account` | 日/周/月最具影响力账号榜 | 是 |
| `douyin-rise-ranking` | 涨粉账号推荐，日/周/月榜 27 分类 | 是 |
| `douyin-similar-account` | 相似账号推荐，对标分析 | 是 |
| `douyin-account-diagnosis` | 一键诊断账号健康度，四维度打分 | 是 |
| `douyin-video-downloader` | 本人作品下载备份到本地 | 是 |
| `douyin-ai-feed` | 每日扫描抖音 AI 作品，生成 HTML 日报 | 是 |
| `douyin-prohibited-word` | 违禁词检测 + 替换建议 + 改写稿 | 是 |

### 多平台 AI 信息源（5 个）

| 技能 | 平台 |
|---|---|
| `bili-ai-feed` | B 站 |
| `gzh-ai-feed` | 微信公众号 |
| `ks-ai-feed` | 快手 |
| `wechat-channels-ai-feed` | 视频号 |
| `xiaohongshu-ai-feed` | 小红书 |

每个都是「每日扫描 AI 相关内容 → 按互动量筛选 → 聚类 → 生成 HTML 日报」。

### 写作（1 个，纯本地）

| 技能 | 干什么 |
|---|---|
| `multi-copywrite-alchemy` | 复刻蒸馏写作：分析一位作者的多篇文章，还原其思维与文风，生成写作分身 |

**不联网、不需要 Key**，正文引用的四份 markdown 框架（七维分析、写作公式、人格模板、核心工作流）直接读。

### 海外情报（3 个，**已改为开源实现**）

| 技能 | 数据源 | 需要什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `youtube-digest` | yt-dlp 直连 YouTube | 装 `yt-dlp` |
| `twitter-work-search` | X 官方 API v2 / 网页 GraphQL | `X_BEARER_TOKEN` 或 `X_AUTH_TOKEN`+`X_CT0` |
| `overseas-trending-search` | YouTube/TikTok 走 yt-dlp，X 走官方接口 | 同上 |

> **这三个原版依赖 `DATA_API_BASE` 付费转售服务**，本插件把它们全部改成了开源实现：
> - YouTube / TikTok → [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp)（Unlicense，19 万星）
> - X → 官方 API v2（用户自带 Bearer）或网页 GraphQL（用户自带 cookie）
>
> **不再需要 `DATA_API_KEY` / `DATA_API_BASE`。**

---

## 装法

```powershell
cd C:\AI\插件1021\douyin-expert

# 基础安装（22 个技能全部注册）
.\install.ps1

# 顺带装海外技能依赖（yt-dlp）
.\install.ps1 -WithOverseasDeps
```

然后**重启 DeepSeek Harness**。重启后技能目录里会出现 22 个技能。

`install.ps1` 做的事（每步都有备份，`*.dyexbak-<时间戳>`）：

1. `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/` 下建目录联接指向本仓库（改代码即时生效）
2. `profile/package.json` 的 `dependencies` 加 `"douyin-expert": "file:C:/AI/插件1021/douyin-expert"`
3. 同文件 `dsh.profile.bundles` 数组末尾追加 `"douyin-expert"`
4. `cordis.patch.yml` 兜底补一行 `insert`
5. （可选）用 DSH 运行时 Python 装 `yt-dlp`

卸载：

```powershell
.\uninstall.ps1                        # 移除改动 + 删 junction
.\uninstall.ps1 -Restore 20261021-131500   # 或直接还原某次备份
```

---

## 凭据配置

### 抖音 / 多平台类（18 个技能）

需要两个环境变量：

```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("REDFOX_API_BASE", "https://redfox.hk", "User")
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("REDFOX_API_KEY", "ak_xxxxxxxx", "User")
```

Key 申请：<https://redfox.hk/settings/api-keys?source=qoder>（新用户赠免费积分）

设完**重启 DSH**。

> `REDFOX_API_BASE` 现在**有内置默认值 `https://redfox.hk`**（本插件已给 21 处脚本打补丁），
> 所以只设 Key 也能跑。但显式设置更保险，将来换上游时不用改代码。

### 海外类（3 个技能）

见 [`CONNECTORS.md`](./CONNECTORS.md)。要点：

- **YouTube**：`python -m pip install -U yt-dlp`，装完就能用
- **X**：必须配 `X_BEARER_TOKEN` 或 `X_AUTH_TOKEN`+`X_CT0`（X 已关闭未登录搜索）
- **TikTok**：仅支持「视频链接」和「@用户名」，关键词搜索不可用（需要 msTag/X-Bogus 签名）

---

## Python 运行时（重要）

本机 PATH 上的 `python` / `python3` 是 **Microsoft Store 重定向存根**，跑任何脚本都会直接 exit 49。
不要用它。

插件里的脚本一律走 DSH 自带的真 Python（3.12.14）：

```
C:\Users\11781\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\python\python.exe
```

这个路径已经写进每个技能的正文末尾「运行时」区块，模型加载技能时会读到，不会误用系统 python。

调用形态：

```powershell
& "C:\Users\11781\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\python\python.exe" scripts\douyin_daily_hot.py --type 美食
```

脚本输出中文，需 `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`，否则控制台是乱码（不影响输出内容本身）。

已装依赖：`requests` / `beautifulsoup4` / `python-docx` / `yt-dlp`。

---

## 结构

```
douyin-expert/
├── package.json          # DSH 插件清单，dsh.bundle.patch 指向 cordis.patch.yml
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle 层：insert 宿主插件
├── lib/index.js          # 宿主逻辑：注册 22 个技能的 provider，按类型注入运行时块
├── assets/
│   ├── douyin-daily-hot/{SKILL.md, README.md, README.en.md, scripts/, references/}
│   ├── ... 共 22 个技能目录
│   └── overseas-trending-search/scripts/sources/{x,tiktok,youtube}_source.py   # 开源实现
├── locale/{zh,en}.json
├── CONNECTORS.md         # 凭据与依赖说明（三类技能分别讲）
├── install.ps1 / uninstall.ps1
├── scripts/selftest.mjs  # 不依赖 DSH 进程的自检
└── .github/workflows/selftest.yml
```

`lib/index.js` 用 `ctx.skills.registerProvider()` 注册一个 provider：

- `list()` 返回 22 个候选
- `get()` 读 `assets/<name>/SKILL.md`，**按技能类型追加不同的运行时区块**：
  - 18 个 redfox 类 → 注入 `REDFOX_API_BASE` / `REDFOX_API_KEY` 说明
  - 1 个本地类 → 声明不联网、无需 Key
  - 3 个海外类 → 声明开源实现、yt-dlp 装法、X 凭据要求
- `resourceBase` 指向技能自己的目录，所以 `references/`、`scripts/` 里的相对路径能正常解析

---

## 海外技能的开源改造说明

原版三个技能都是 `POST {DATA_API_BASE}/...` 的 HTTP 客户端，要求用户自建付费数据服务。
本次改造的实际情况（都实测过）：

| 能力 | 原方案 | 现方案 | 实测结果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| YouTube 搜索 | `POST /youtube/searchVideo` | `yt-dlp ytsearchN:关键词` | ✅ 15 条真实数据，按播放量排序 |
| YouTube 字幕 | `POST /youtube/transcript` | `yt-dlp --write-auto-subs` + json3 解析 | ✅ 248 段带时间戳，zh 429 时自动降级 en |
| TikTok 视频详情 | `POST /tiktok/ability/awemeDetail` | `yt-dlp` 单 URL | ✅ 播放/点赞/评论/时间全有 |
| TikTok 用户作品 | `POST /tiktok/ability/userAwemeList` | `yt-dlp tiktokuser:<secUid>` | ✅ 10 条 |
| TikTok 关键词搜索 | `POST /tiktok/ability/searchVideo` | ❌ 无开源替代 | 明确报不可用（需 msToken/X-Bogus 签名） |
| X 搜索 | `POST /x/search` | 官方 API v2 / 网页 GraphQL | ✅ 有凭据时可用；无凭据明确报错 |

**关键取舍**：拿不到的数据（YouTube 点赞数、TikTok 关键词搜索、无凭据时的 X）一律
**如实标记为不可用或 0**，绝不估算、不伪造。这是这些技能正文里反复强调的纪律。

框架替换：

| 原实现 | 现实现 | 许可证 |
|---|---|---|
| 付费转售 API（无内置基址） | [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) | Unlicense（公共领域） |
| — | X 官方 API v2（用户自带 Bearer） | X 服务条款 |

### 为什么不用 snscrape / Nitter

调研阶段实测过，全部不可行：

| 方案 | 实测结果 |
|---|---|
| `snscrape` 0.7.0 | `AttributeError: 'FileFinder' object has no attribute 'find_module'` — 与 Python 3.12 不兼容 |
| Nitter 公共实例（11 个） | 全部离线 / SSL 失败 / 403 / 451 / 无内容 |
| X guest token | `403 Forbidden` — X 已关闭匿名 API |
| `TikTokApi`（davidteather） | 需要 playwright + chromium（197MB），且搜索仍受签名限制 |

结论：X 走官方凭据是唯一可靠路径，YouTube/TikTok 走 yt-dlp 是最优解。

---

## 自检

不启动 DSH 也能验：

```powershell
node scripts/selftest.mjs

# 本机验收（要求 python 路径真实存在）
$env:REQUIRE_PYTHON="1"; node scripts/selftest.mjs
```

覆盖：插件名 / inject / apply 是否注册 provider / **技能数 22** / **22 个名字与预期逐一比对** /
无重复 / description 与 content 非空 / **运行时块按技能类型正确注入**（redfox 类必须有
`REDFOX_API_KEY`，本地类必须声明不联网，海外类必须声明开源实现且不得把 `DATA_API_KEY` 当必需项）/
python 路径存在 / resourceBase 是真实目录 / 元数据可 JSON 序列化。

当前结果：**PASS — 6/6**。

---

## 已知边界

1. **无 redfox Key 时，18 个抖音/多平台技能只返回鉴权错误**。这是设计行为，不是 bug。
2. **YouTube 搜索结果的点赞数为 0** —— yt-dlp 列表接口不提供该项，如实显示不估算。
   要真实点赞数请用 `youtube-digest` 取单视频详情。
3. **TikTok 关键词搜索不可用** —— 平台签名限制，仅支持链接与 @用户名。
4. **X 无凭据时不可用** —— 平台限制。
5. **YouTube 字幕可能 429** —— 请求过频触发限流，脚本会自动降级到下一个语言或提示等待。
6. 需要境外网络访问 YouTube / X / TikTok，可能需要代理。
