evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-open-in-browser

A community DSH plugin that opens a Sidebar file in the **system default browser**
instead of the in-app preview.

Two entry points ship in one plugin:

| Seat | Where it shows | What it needs from the Host |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sidebar.right.tab.document.unpreviewable` | "Cannot preview this file" empty state | the file's Host path (`absolutePath`) |
| `sidebar.right.tab.menu.item` | Right-click menu of a Sidebar **tab chip** | only the tab's `contentId` (`dsh-resource://file/session/…`) |

There is deliberately **no** `sidebar.right.tab.document.actions` seat. When the
preview renders a file, the header already carries the preview's own controls, and a
second "open in browser" button next to them earns nothing; the tab-chip menu is one
right-click away and works for every tab. That menu seat is also what makes the
plugin useful for a tab whose preview **fails**: the built-in preview only renders
the document seats once its Host metadata read succeeds, so a tab showing an error
(for example `HTTP 405` from a third-party previewer) has no `absolutePath`. The tab
menu still has the tab's resource address, which is enough to resolve, verify, and
open the file.

## Install

The package ships prebuilt artifacts (`dist/`), so installing needs no build step
and no runtime dependency.

**From npm** (after the first publish):

1. Open DSH → **插件 → 添加插件**.
2. Enter the package name `dsh-plugin-open-in-browser`.
3. Fully quit and reopen DSH so the new Host half and client artifact load.

The same target works from the plugin tooling:

```
plugin_manager  action=install_bundle  target=dsh-plugin-open-in-browser
```

**From a local checkout or a GitHub clone** (the clone already contains `dist/`):

```
plugin_manager  action=install_bundle  target=<absolute path to the checkout>
```

**Requirements**: the DSH desktop app (the Host must be able to launch a native
application); Node ≥ 20 only when building from source. A remote/SSH deployment has
no desktop browser to launch, so the control reports that instead of failing
silently.

After any install, update, or rebuild, fully quit and reopen DSH: the client bundle
is cached by the module loader.

## Why

The built-in preview renders HTML inside a sandboxed `iframe` (`srcDoc`/blob). Pages
that depend on `fetch`, modules, absolute paths, service workers, or a real origin
show up blank — and files the preview cannot render at all show an empty state. The
fastest escape hatch is the OS: hand the file to the default browser, which resolves
relative assets and origin-dependent APIs normally.

## How opening works

The browser half posts to one exact Host route registered by this plugin's Host half:

```http
POST /dsh-plugin-open-in-browser/open
content-type: application/json

{ "path": "C:\\Users\\me\\project\\preview.html" }
{ "address": "dsh-resource://file/session/<sessionId>/pages/preview.html" }
```

`address` is the form a tab menu can produce: the Host resolves the Session's
workspace root (`sessions.get(sessionId).header.cwd`), joins the relative path,
then verifies the result (below). The reply is
`{ ok: true, mode: "browser" | "association", path }`; failures are
`{ ok: false, code }` with a 4xx/5xx status.

The Host half then resolves the user's **actual default browser** instead of relying
on the OS file association:

1. `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Associations\UrlAssociations\https|http\UserChoice`
   → `ProgId` → `HKCR\<ProgId>\shell\open\command` → executable;
2. well-known install paths (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox, Vivaldi, Opera);
3. fallback: the OS association (`explorer.exe <file-uri>` on Windows, `open` on
   macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux).

This matters for images, PDFs, and other previewable files: the shipped
`session.openWorkspacePath` Remote follows the OS association (a `.png` opens the
Photos app on Windows), while this plugin promises a browser. If the Host route is
unavailable (older Host half, deployment without it), the browser half degrades to
that Remote so the control still does something useful.

> The Remote request schema is `{ path, action?: 'reveal', application?: string }`.
> There is no `intent` field — omitting `action`/`application` *is* "open with the
> default application".

## Relationship to DSH's shipped `open-in-app`

DSH already ships `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-open-in-app` +
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-open-in-app`, which register the document-preview seats
(`…document.actions` and `…document.unpreviewable`) with an "Open in app" menu
(editors, Git GUIs, terminals). This plugin is not a replacement: it is a
single-purpose shortcut for "just open it in the browser", including files that
plugin's own preview cannot render, and it adds the tab-chip menu.

## Layout

```
src/security.ts   path-safety layer: absolute-path check, traversal/UNC/device
                  rejection, extension whitelist, workspace containment, symlink
                  escape detection via an injected realpath, and the
                  dsh-resource://file/… address parser
src/browser.ts    Host-side default-browser resolver: registry UserChoice → ProgId →
                  command, well-known install paths, detached launch with a
                  watch window
src/index.ts      Host half: registers the one route, resolves address → workspace
                  path, validates, launches
src/client.ts     browser half: two slot registrations + route/Remote adapter
locale/en.json    meta.title / meta.description
locale/zh.json    same in Chinese
cordis.patch.yml  Loader insert row
scripts/*.mjs     tsc-driven builds (no bundler); the client build wraps the
                  compiled module in the DSH module-loader factory
tests/*.test.mjs  node:test suites: safety layer, browser resolver, Host route
                  contract, and the built client bundle
```

### Why no `src/main/`, `src/preload/`, `src/renderer/`?

Those are the layers of an **Electron application**. A DSH plugin is a Cordis
bundle, not an Electron app: it never reaches the Electron main process and DSH
exposes no preload/`contextBridge` bridge to plugins. The equivalent split is:

| Electron app layer | This plugin |
| --- | --- |
| main process (Node) | `src/index.ts` + `src/browser.ts` — the Host half, running inside DSH's Host process |
| preload / contextBridge | the Host route `POST /dsh-plugin-open-in-browser/open` (with DSH's `session.openWorkspacePath` Remote as the fallback) |
| renderer injection | `src/client.ts` — the browser artifact loaded through `window.__ModuleLoader__` |

`security.ts` is shared by both halves on purpose: the browser half validates
before calling, and the Host validates again before launching. Splitting it into
a "main" copy would let the two gates drift apart.

## Build

Requires Node ≥ 20 (verified on Node 24) and no runtime dependency.

```bash
npm install       # typescript + @types/node only
npm run build     # dist/index.js + dist/browser.js (host) + dist/client.js (browser)
npm run typecheck # host and client configs
npm test          # builds, then runs all four node:test suites
```

`npm run build` is the only step DSH needs: the package's `files` and `exports`
point at `dist/`.

## Local test steps

1. **Build and unit-test**

   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm test
   ```

   Expected: `dist/index.js`, `dist/browser.js`, and `dist/client.js` exist; all
   `node:test` cases pass (currently 78). The suites cover the pure safety layer and
   address grammar, the Windows registry/path resolution and launch-plan ordering
   (with injected process facts), the HTTP contract of the Host route (405/415/403/
   400 paths and the Origin fence), and the built client bundle executed in a bare VM
   (loader id, two registrations, route-first behavior with Remote fallback, and the
   refusal paths).

2. **Install into the current profile** (from an absolute package directory):

   ```
   plugin_manager  action=install_bundle  target=E:\Ai\DSHprojects\plug-in\open-in-browser
   ```

   A profile that already had this package installed must be restarted before the new
   artifact is loaded. When the profile links the workspace directory (as the local
   development setup does), rebuilding is enough; only the restart is required.

3. **Smoke-test in the GUI**

   - Open a session, open the Files tab, click a file the preview renders (an `.html`
     page, a `.png`) → the preview header carries **no** extra browser button; the
     file is meant to be read in place.
   - **Right-click the tab chip** and choose **Open in browser** → the tab's file is
     handed to the system default browser (not the OS file association), for any file
     type on the whitelist — an image opens in the browser instead of Photos.
   - Click a tab whose preview fails (for example a third-party previewer showing
     `HTTP 405`) → the same right-click item resolves the tab's resource address and
     opens the file.
   - In a remote/SSH deployment (`canOpenWorkspacePath()` false and no Host route) the
     document controls stay hidden and the menu item reports that the Host route is
     unavailable.
   - Refusals surface as short inline text, never as a crash: a path with `..`, a
     non-whitelisted extension, a foreign `Origin`, or a path the Host cannot map is
     reported.

4. **Uninstall**

   ```
   plugin_manager  action=set_plugin  target=dsh-plugin-open-in-browser  enabled=false
   ```

## Security notes

- The route is fenced on three layers: the Host web server's own authentication, a
  same-origin `Origin` check (`dsh-app://app` or the serving `Host`; absent `Origin`
  is a local client such as curl), and a bounded JSON body (`16 KiB`,
  `content-type: application/json` required). It can only ever open a **file** path
  that passes validation, never accept a command.
- The browser half validates before calling: the path must be absolute, must not
  contain `.`/`..`, UNC or device-namespace paths, control characters, or reserved
  device names, and its extension must be on the browser-safe whitelist.
- Address-based requests are resolved against the Session's live `header.cwd`, then
  passed through the same gate **and** an injected `realpath`; a symlink that leaves
  the workspace is rejected (`symlink-escape`), as is an unknown Session
  (`session-unavailable`) rather than guessing a root.
- Containment against a workspace root is only possible where a root is known; on the
  document seats the slot only supplies the absolute path, so the Host mapping check
  of the Remote (and of the preview itself) remains the authoritative fence there.

## Limitations

- No file-tree right-click menu. The slot catalog exposes no file-node context-menu
  slot (only `sidebar.right.tab.files.actions`, a toolbar that receives the displayed
  workspace directory), and the shipped Files tree has no context menu of its own.
  Adding one would require shipping a replacement file tree (what
  `dsh-better-sidebar` does).
- The empty-state button only appears once the preview has metadata for the file
  (`absolutePath`); a tab whose preview fails is covered by the tab-chip menu seat.
- The preview header has no button at all by design (see above); if you want one back,
  re-register `sidebar.right.tab.document.actions` in `src/client.ts`.
- A profile restart is required after rebuilding, because the client artifact is
  cached by the module loader.
- The whitelist is deliberately small; extend `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS` if you want
  more types opened externally.

## Security

The plugin adds a process-launch capability, so it ships with a written threat
model: the single Host route, the fences around it, the path gate, and what is
explicitly out of scope. See [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md).

To report a vulnerability, use GitHub's private advisory form (Security tab) rather
than a public issue.

## Releasing

Repository: <https://github.com/haoqiya138-source/dsh-plugin-open-in-browser>.
The package is published to npm as `dsh-plugin-open-in-browser`.

Release checklist:

1. `npm test` (rebuilds `dist/` and runs all 78 cases) and `npm run typecheck`.
2. `npm version <patch|minor|major>` — bumps `package.json`, commits and creates the tag.
3. `git push origin main --follow-tags` — the tag triggers
   `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which rebuilds, tests, publishes with
   [npm provenance](https://docs.npmjs.com/generating-provenance-statements) and
   creates the GitHub release.

CI publishing needs a one-time setup: create an npm **automation** token
(<https://www.npmjs.com/settings/~/tokens>) and add it as the repository secret
`NPM_TOKEN` (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions). Until that secret
exists, the release workflow skips `npm publish`, still creates the GitHub
release, and the package can be published manually with `npm login` +
`npm publish --access public`.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the typecheck and all 78 test cases on Linux
and Windows for Node 20 and 22. The release workflow rebuilds `dist/` before
publishing, so the tarball always matches the tagged source.

## License

whole dark logo](https://hol.org/brand/Logo_Whole_Dark.png) | **Stop risky AI actions before they compromise your machine.** HOL Guard is a local-first security layer for AI agents, tools, plugins, skills, MCP servers, and package installs.

[Install HOL Guard](https://hol.org/guard/activate)
[Read the documentation](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/blob/main/docs/guard/get-started.md)
[PyPI Package (`hol-guard`)](https://pypi.org/project/hol-guard/)
[Report an Issue](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/issues) | | :--- | :--- | HOL Guard reviews agent actions before they run: shell commands, file access, package installs, and MCP tool calls. It detects secret exposure, destructive operations, prompt injection, and supply-chain risks, then allows, blocks, or requests approval according to your policy. Run it locally without an account. Use the CLI and local dashboard to manage protection, resolve approvals, and inspect decision history. Optional [Guard Cloud](docs/guard/local-vs-cloud.md) adds shared history, team policy, and fleet management. [Get started](#install-hol-guard) · [Supported agents](#supported-ai-agents) · [Plugin scanner](#plugin-scanner) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Contribute an extension](#contribute-a-new-extension) · [Contribute an adapter](docs/guard/adapter-contributions.md) · [Development](#development) ## Install HOL Guard Requires Python 3.10 or newer and [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io/stable/installation/). ```bash pipx install hol-guard hol-guard init ``` The first-run wizard discovers supported agents and walks you through protection setup. It asks before each setup change, including opening the dashboard, installing agent integrations, and connecting optional cloud services. Check your installation: ```bash hol-guard --version hol-guard status ``` To update an existing installation: ```bash hol-guard update ``` For manual setup, see the [installation guide](docs/guard/get-started.md). Annotated release notes with upgrade context live at [hol.org/guard/releases](https://hol.org/guard/releases); raw releases and prereleases are on the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/releases). ## What HOL Guard Protects | Surface | Protection | | :--- | :--- | | **Shell commands and file access** | Reviews destructive operations, sensitive file access, credential exposure, and suspicious outbound commands. | | **Package installs** | Evaluates supported package-manager operations against supply-chain intelligence before installation. | | **Plugins, skills, and agent configuration** | Inventories local artifacts and reviews new or changed tools before launch. | | **MCP servers and tools** | Inspects server configuration and reviews tool calls through supported hooks and managed proxies. | | **Prompts and tool results** | Screens supported events for prompt injection and sensitive content. | | **Approvals and evidence** | Routes decisions to native prompts or the approval center, and records local receipts for review. | Guard connects through native agent hooks, managed MCP proxies, and launch integrations. Coverage depends on the events each agent exposes; the [support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) documents enforcement, approval delivery, and failure behavior per integration. ## Supported AI Agents Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI, Grok, Hermes, Kimi Code, Pi, oh-my-pi, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Antigravity, ZCode, and Devin. [Paseo](docs/guard/paseo.md) is supported through these native provider integrations, with per-provider coverage. For example, to set up Codex explicitly: ```bash hol-guard install codex hol-guard run codex --dry-run hol-guard run codex ``` The dry run records the current artifact state before launch. For Codex, Guard installs native pre-tool hooks and refuses a managed launch if those hooks are missing or disabled. [Agent support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/guard/troubleshooting.md) ## Everyday Use | Task | Command | | :--- | :--- | | Check protection status | `hol-guard status` | | Diagnose an agent integration | `hol-guard doctor codex` | | Inspect changes before launch | `hol-guard diff codex` | | Review pending approvals | `hol-guard approvals` | | Approve or deny a request | `hol-guard approvals approve ` / `hol-guard approvals deny ` | | Read decision history | `hol-guard receipts` | | List tracked artifacts | `hol-guard inventory` | | Export an AI bill of materials | `hol-guard abom --format json` | | Scan workspace dependencies | `hol-guard supply-chain scan` | | Connect optional cloud sync | `hol-guard connect` | ### Understand a paused command Inspect the command's classification and matching rules: ```bash hol-guard command test 'rm -rf ./build' hol-guard command explain 'git clean -ndx' hol-guard command extensions command.git --json ``` `command test` and `command explain` inspect the command without executing it or creating an approval. Use `hol-guard approvals` to resolve a pending request and `hol-guard receipts` to review the recorded decision. The [Extension directory](docs/guard/extensions/README.md) lists command coverage generated from the Rust-compiled catalog. External contributions require explicit opt-in; required core protections remain enabled. To add coverage, follow the [Extension contribution guide](docs/guard/extensions/contributing.md). ### Check a package ```bash hol-guard supply-chain sync hol-guard supply-chain scan hol-guard supply-chain explain minimist@1.2.5 --ecosystem npm ``` The package verdict includes the available advisory evidence and ecosystem coverage. See the [get-started guide](docs/guard/get-started.md) for package-manager interception and the [remediation guide](docs/guard/remediation.md) for handling false positives. ## Plugin Scanner This repository also ships `plugin-scanner`, a CLI for maintainers who want security and quality checks before publishing agent plugins, skills, and MCP integrations. ```bash pipx install plugin-scanner plugin-scanner scan . plugin-scanner lint . plugin-scanner verify . ``` | Command | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | | `scan` | Security findings and a quality report across detected package surfaces. | | `lint` | Rule-level authoring feedback. | | `verify` | Install-surface and runtime readiness checks. | | `submit` | A submission artifact for one plugin package. | | `doctor` | Component diagnostics and troubleshooting bundles. | The scanner detects Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, and OpenCode package formats. Use `plugin-scanner --list-ecosystems` to list them or `--ecosystem` to select one. At a Codex marketplace root, it discovers local plugin entries automatically. Checks cover manifests, secrets, MCP transport and command configuration, approval defaults, skills, dependency lockfiles, and GitHub Actions permissions. Optional Cisco integrations add skill and MCP analysis. Reports support text, JSON, Markdown, and SARIF. ```bash plugin-scanner scan . --format sarif --output plugin-scanner.sarif plugin-scanner scan . --fail-on-severity high ``` Quality grades use the checks applicable to each package. Trust scoring has separate provenance and weights; see the [skill](docs/trust/skill-trust-local.md), [MCP](docs/trust/mcp-trust-draft.md), and [plugin](docs/trust/plugin-trust-draft.md) scoring references. ### GitHub Actions Add the scanner to a plugin repository: ```yaml name: Plugin security on: [push, pull_request] permissions: contents: read jobs: scan: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6 - uses: hashgraph-online/ai-plugin-scanner-action@fdb49f9d85321a2ced2933301b395dd3c1ce9c8f # v1.2.631 with: plugin_dir: "." min_score: 80 fail_on_severity: high ``` See the [action documentation](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/ai-plugin-scanner-action) for SARIF uploads, submission workflows, and machine-readable outputs. The action source is maintained in [`action/`](action/). ### Optional Cisco analysis The baseline packages work without Cisco dependencies. To add Cisco skill scanning, use Python 3.11 through 3.14 and install the extra in an isolated environment: ```bash pipx install 'plugin-scanner[cisco]' ``` For Cisco MCP analysis, use the repository's [Docker image](Dockerfile) or the `cisco-mcp` dependency group: ```bash uv sync --extra dev --extra cisco --group cisco-mcp --python 3.13 uv run plugin-scanner scan . --cisco-skill-scan on --cisco-mcp-scan on ``` The published `cisco` extra provides skill scanning; the separate `cisco-mcp` group supplies the MCP scanner. Dependency versions and Python constraints are maintained in [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml). ## Ecosystem Support | Ecosystem | Detection surfaces | | :--- | :--- | | Codex | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `marketplace.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | | Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | | DeepSeek Harness | `package.json` with `dsh.bundle`, declared patches, and Cordis `apply(ctx)` exports, or `dsh.bundle.mode` set to `"patch"` for patch-only bundles | | Gemini CLI | `gemini-extension.json`, `commands/**/*.toml` | | Kimi Code | `kimi.plugin.json`, `.kimi-plugin/plugin.json`, declared skills, agents, commands, prompts, and MCP servers | | OpenCode | `opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc`, `.opencode/commands`, `.opencode/plugins` | Use `--ecosystem auto` to detect supported packages in a repository, or select an ecosystem explicitly: ```bash plugin-scanner scan ./plugins-repo --ecosystem claude plugin-scanner scan ./dsh-plugin --ecosystem deepseek-harness ``` ## What The Scanner Checks | Category | Coverage | | :--- | :--- | | Manifest validation | Required fields, versions, declared paths, interface metadata, links, and assets. | | Security | Hardcoded secrets, unsafe MCP commands and transports, and risky approval defaults. | | Operational security | GitHub Actions permissions and pinned dependencies, privileged checkout patterns, Dependabot, and lockfiles. | | Plugin packaging | README and license files, skill frontmatter, ignore rules, and accidentally committed environment files. | | Marketplace | Manifest validity, local package discovery, and safe source paths. | | Skill and MCP analysis | Analyzer availability, findings, and analyzability from optional Cisco integrations. | | Code quality | Dynamic code execution and shell-injection patterns. | ## How Trust Scoring Works Plugin Scanner reports a quality grade alongside trust provenance. Quality scores are normalized across applicable checks, so optional surfaces do not inflate a package's grade. Skill trust uses the HCS-28 baseline adapter IDs, weights, and denominator rules. MCP and Codex plugin trust use explicit adapters, weights, and contribution modes documented in the local specifications: - [Skill Trust Local Draft](docs/trust/skill-trust-local.md) - [MCP Trust Draft](docs/trust/mcp-trust-draft.md) - [Codex Plugin Trust Draft](docs/trust/plugin-trust-draft.md) ## CLI Usage ```bash # Structured security report plugin-scanner scan ./my-plugin --format json --profile public-marketplace # Inspect authoring rules plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --list-rules plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --explain README_MISSING # Apply supported mechanical fixes plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --fix --profile strict-security # Verify package readiness; --online permits live probes plugin-scanner verify ./my-plugin --format json plugin-scanner verify ./my-plugin --online --format text # Generate a submission artifact for one plugin plugin-scanner submit ./my-plugin --profile public-marketplace --attest dist/plugin-quality.json # Collect component diagnostics plugin-scanner doctor ./my-plugin --component mcp --bundle dist/doctor.zip ``` For a repository marketplace, `scan`, `lint`, `verify`, and `doctor` can target the root. `submit` targets one plugin package. ## Codex Spec Alignment The scanner recognizes Codex plugin manifests, interface metadata, declared assets, and marketplace packages: - Local manifest paths use `./` prefixes; `lint --fix` preserves or adds them. - `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is the preferred marketplace location, with root `marketplace.json` supported for compatibility. - Interface validation checks declared links and assets without requiring an undocumented `type` field. - `verify --online` checks HTTP remote reachability. Stdio server execution is skipped for manual review. See the [Codex plugin documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins) and [Model Context Protocol specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) for upstream formats. ## Config + Baseline Example Configure the scanner in `.plugin-scanner.toml`: ```toml [scanner] profile = "public-marketplace" baseline_file = "baseline.txt" ignore_paths = ["tests/*", "fixtures/*"] [rules] disabled = ["README_MISSING"] severity_overrides = { CODEXIGNORE_MISSING = "low" } ``` The GitHub Action requires `trust_repository_policy: true` before repository-owned configuration and baselines can change its verdict. Enable that option only for policy you intend the workflow to trust. ## Report Formats | Format | Use | | :--- | :--- | | `text` | Terminal summaries with category totals and findings. | | `json` | Structured reports for scripts and integrations. | | `markdown` | Review-ready reports for pull requests and issues. | | `sarif` | GitHub code scanning and security automation. | ## GitHub Action The [AI Plugin Scanner Action](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/ai-plugin-scanner-action) supports security gates, SARIF uploads, submission intake, and registry payloads. Its source lives in [`action/`](action/), and the [publication workflow](.github/workflows/publish-action-repo.yml) distributes the action bundle. The legacy [HOL Codex Plugin Scanner Action](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-codex-plugin-scanner-action) remains available for existing workflows. ### Plugin Author Submission Flow Use `submission_enabled: true` to open or reuse a submission issue when a plugin meets the configured threshold. `submission_token` must have permission to create issues in the target submission repository. The action emits submission status and issue URLs as outputs. See the [action's input reference](action/action.yml) for `submission_score_threshold`, `submission_token`, and the target repository options. ### Registry Payload For Plugin Ecosystem Automation Set `registry_payload_output` to write a machine-readable payload for a registry or badge pipeline. The action also exposes `score`, `grade`, `grade_label`, `max_severity`, and `findings_total` outputs and can write a job summary. The [HOL Registry Broker plugin](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/registry-broker-codex-plugin) is an example of an agent plugin in the [HOL Plugin Registry](https://hol.org/registry/plugins). Its [registry listing](https://hol.org/registry/plugins/hol%2Fregistry-broker-codex-plugin) provides current trust information. ## Why HOL Guard AI agents can run commands, install dependencies, read files, and call external tools within one session. HOL Guard reviews those actions at supported execution points and keeps the policy decision, approval request, and receipt together. Use it for AI agent security on a developer machine, MCP security around connected tools, and supply-chain checks for packages and plugins. Teams can add Guard Cloud for shared approvals and policy management while retaining local protection. ## Frequently Asked Questions ### What is HOL Guard? HOL Guard is open-source antivirus and runtime protection for AI agents. It reviews supported tool calls, shell commands, file access, and package operations for risks such as secret exposure, prompt injection, destructive actions, and malicious dependencies. ### Does HOL Guard work without a cloud account? Yes. Local protection, CLI commands, approvals, and receipts work without signing in. Guard Cloud is optional and adds synchronized evidence, team controls, and fleet visibility. See [Local Guard vs. Guard Cloud](docs/guard/local-vs-cloud.md) for the feature boundary. ### Which AI agents does HOL Guard support? Guard includes adapters for Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI, Grok, Hermes, Kimi Code, Pi, oh-my-pi, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Antigravity, ZCode, and Devin. [Paseo](docs/guard/paseo.md) is supported through these native provider integrations, with per-provider coverage. The [support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) explains which events and enforcement paths each adapter supports. ### What is the difference between HOL Guard and Plugin Scanner? Install `hol-guard` to protect agent activity on your machine. Install `plugin-scanner` to inspect plugin packages and enforce security and quality checks in CI. This repository builds and publishes both distributions. ### How does HOL Guard protect MCP servers? Guard inspects MCP server configuration and reviews supported MCP tool calls through agent hooks and managed proxies. Plugin Scanner checks MCP configuration and HTTP remote reachability; optional Cisco MCP analysis adds static security findings. ### Why did Guard pause my command? The action may need approval under your active policy, or its tools or artifacts may have changed. Start with `hol-guard approvals`, inspect the command with `hol-guard command explain ''`, and use `hol-guard receipts` to review the recorded decision. ## Documentation For enrollment or stale native authority errors, see [extension-control recovery](docs/guard/extension-control-recovery.md). | Guide | Contents | | :--- | :--- | | [Get started](docs/guard/get-started.md) | Installation, manual setup, package protection, and common commands. | | [Agent support](docs/guard/harness-support.md) | Integration coverage and approval behavior. | | [Architecture](docs/guard/architecture.md) | Runtime components and decision flow. | | [Policy specification](spec/guard-policy/v1alpha1/README.md) | GuardPolicy document format. | | [Policy recipes](docs/guard/policy-recipes.md) | Configuration examples for common workflows. | | [Extensions](docs/guard/extensions/README.md) | Built-in command rules and contribution guidance. | | [Native extension authoring](docs/guard/extension-builder/README.md) | Canonical JSON sources, the Rust compiler, portable fixtures, and review kits. | | [Contribute an extension](#contribute-a-new-extension) | Generate, review, integrate, and test a new extension with the CLI. | | [Local vs. cloud](docs/guard/local-vs-cloud.md) | Local capabilities and optional cloud services. | | [Troubleshooting](docs/guard/troubleshooting.md) | Diagnosis and recovery. | | [Security](SECURITY.md) | Vulnerability reporting and disclosure policy. | ## Contribute a New Extension To integrate a new AI coding agent or IDE, use the separate [harness adapter contribution guide](docs/guard/adapter-contributions.md). Harness adapters provide discovery, managed setup, and event integration. The command extensions below add policy coverage for CLI tools and do not install agent hooks. Command extensions are authored as **declarative JSON compiled and evaluated by Rust**. Add metadata, permissions, matcher trees, and safe variants in `contributions/command-sources/command..json`, then verify behavior with portable JSON fixtures. Most extensions compose existing native operations; a new Rust operation is needed only when the existing matcher contracts cannot express the behavior. | Contribution | Authoring input | Verification | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Command coverage | `contributions/command-sources/command..json` | Portable fixtures evaluated by `guard-command-source test`. | | MCP server knowledge | `contributions/mcp-servers/.json` | MCP contribution tests and native catalog validation. | | New matcher semantics | Reviewed Rust changes in `rust/crates/guard-command/` | Native contract, admission, evaluation, and regression tests. | The Rust compiler generates command descriptors, the catalog, and the native matcher program. Python remains part of the CLI, build orchestration, and tests; new command coverage does not require a Python detector or registry registration. See the [authoring guide](docs/guard/extension-builder/README.md) for direct source authoring and the [architecture](docs/guard/command-extension-architecture.md) for the runtime boundary. The **Extension Builder CLI** can create those command sources and portable fixtures from exported command metadata. It also supports MCP inventories. It works offline and reads the export without importing or running the target tool. Use the Builder's plan-and-apply flow to create the canonical source and fixture. Open a draft PR early for scope review. Before marking that PR ready for review, run `scripts/prepare_extension_contribution.py --source ... --fixture ...` to synchronize deterministic projections, then run `hol-guard extensions handoff --repo . --source ... --fixture ...`. The handoff check catches missing generated descriptors, catalog entries, and source bindings before final review. **1. Define the coverage in the PR.** Check the [Extension directory](docs/guard/extensions/README.md) and current [open pull requests](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/pulls) for existing or overlapping coverage. For a new capability, open a draft PR with the **Command extension** template and include the proposed `command.` ID, supported operations, destructive examples, safe counterparts, and upstream references. Scope review happens on the PR; a separate issue is not required. Extend an existing extension when it already owns the operation. Follow the [development setup](#development), then run the examples below from your HOL Guard checkout. `uv run --no-sync` uses that checkout's installed development version. **2. Generate a contribution kit.** This example uses the checked-in, synthetic `samplectl` inventory. For your own contribution, replace the input and metadata with your tool's export and public publisher details. ```bash uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions generate --from cli \ --input docs/guard/extension-builder/examples/cli-surface.json \ --slug samplectl --executable samplectl --name 'Sample CLI' \ --publisher community.example --publisher-name 'Example Maintainer' \ --homepage https://example.test/samplectl \ --upstream-version 1.0.0 --output samplectl-kit uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions validate samplectl-kit ``` The output directory must be new, with an existing parent directory. A command kit includes `discovery.json`, `review.json`, `report.json`, the canonical JSON source, a portable native fixture, a generated descriptor, and a file manifest. MCP kits contain their contribution metadata and generated Python tests. Other inputs: `--from help` reads saved command help; `--from click` reads a Click `Context.to_info_dict()` export; `--from oclif` reads `oclif.manifest.json`; `--from mcp` reads a complete exported `tools/list` result; and `--from snapshot` replays `discovery.json`. The `cli` example above uses normalized `guard.cli-surface.v1` JSON. For MCP contributions, the generator uses `--launcher` and `--package` instead of `--executable`. See the [MCP kit example](docs/guard/extension-builder/README.md#generate-an-mcp-kit) for a complete command and pagination requirements. **3. Review the operations and regenerate.** Read `report.json` and compare the discovered operations with the upstream implementation. Copy the review file before editing: ```bash cp samplectl-kit/review.json samplectl-review.json ``` Edit `samplectl-review.json`, keeping its discovery binding and operation IDs intact. CLI operations use `review` or `block`; the root operation stays `review`. Set `reviewed: true` for entries you have assessed, with rationale and a public HTTPS evidence reference. Add `safeArgv` only for exact, verified safe invocations. The [review format](docs/guard/extension-builder/README.md#review-and-recompile) includes a complete entry example. Recompile the saved snapshot after reviewing it: ```bash uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions generate --from snapshot \ --input samplectl-kit/discovery.json \ --review samplectl-review.json --output samplectl-reviewed uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions validate samplectl-reviewed uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions diff samplectl-kit samplectl-reviewed "$HOL_GUARD_NATIVE_SOURCE_COMPILER" test \ < samplectl-reviewed/artifacts/tests/fixtures/command-source-samplectl.v1.json ``` `diff` exits `0` for equal kits and `1` when valid kits differ. The Rust fixture runner evaluates command text without executing it. If the upstream export changes, generate and review a new snapshot. **4. Preview and apply the integration.** On your contribution branch, preview the changes to the current checkout: ```bash uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions apply samplectl-reviewed --repo . ``` Inspect the listed paths and generated files. Copy the printed plan digest into the following command before running it: ```bash uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions apply samplectl-reviewed --repo . \ --expected-plan THE_PRINTED_PLAN_DIGEST \ --write ``` The write integrates the canonical source, fixture, generated contribution descriptor, external trust map, packaging, and authoring ownership records. Regenerate the complete program and catalog in the next step. Existing IDs or conflicting files stop integration for review. **5. Test and submit a pull request.** Follow the [native validation sequence](docs/guard/extension-builder/VALIDATION.md) to regenerate the complete catalog, rebuild the compiler and runtime against that program, and run the contribution's fixtures against the integrated sources. This also covers updating an existing extension, where an addition to the packaged baseline would conflict with the existing ID. Then run the contribution checks and regenerate the public directory: ```bash uv run --no-sync python scripts/release/stage_guard_cloud_review_artifacts.py uv run --no-sync pytest -q \ tests/test_guard_extension_contribution.py \ tests/test_guard_extension_trust.py \ tests/test_native_source_program.py \ tests/test_guard_command_extension_registry.py uv run --no-sync python scripts/export_extension_directory.py uv run --no-sync python scripts/export_extension_directory.py --check uv run --no-sync python scripts/render_command_extension_directory.py uv run --no-sync python scripts/render_command_extension_directory.py --check git diff --check ``` Add fixture cases for destructive operations, safe previews, aliases, reordered flags, quoting, malformed input, and compound commands. Run the Rust checks when changing native semantics and the relevant Python checks when changing tooling. Inspect the final diff, commit the canonical inputs, generated projections, fixtures, and authoring records, and update the existing draft PR against `main` with the test results. Mark it ready for review after the handoff check passes. Keep scratch kit directories and raw upstrea

# 操作约定注入（dsh-ops-conventions）

把「操作约定」在**动手前**确定性注入上下文，解决「约定记了但干活时不提就不用」的问题。

## 它做什么

- **版本变化后下一轮就注入，不再等下一个操作轮**：不按「像不像要动手」过滤，闲聊轮也会注入；每会话每版本只注入一次（约 150 token）。
- **门铃自带 6 行常驻约定**：收尾三件（自检/记忆归并/`_tasks` 清空）、不列多方案、备份回滚、只改工具区、关会话提醒等直接写进门铃，不再依赖可能被 OpenViking 抽取重写的 `profile.md` 段。
- **同一会话同版本只注入一次**：不刷屏。
- **约定版本变化自动再提醒**：改 `VERSION` 后，下一轮（任何类型）会重新注入。
- **注入日志**：每次注入记一行（含选中的约定目录、索引是否存在），生效与否可核对。
- **硬拦截（默认开）**：操作类轮次里，本会话还没 `read` 过 `INDEX.md` 时，`write`/`edit` 等写类工具会被直接拒绝，并提示先读索引；读过后本会话放行。闲聊轮次不拦；shell 默认不拦（可配置）。
- **零配置可用**：包内自带 `skills/` 示例清单；也可以指向你自己的目录，或 OpenViking 里存的那份。

## 为什么会有这个插件

作者是一名 DSH 日常用户（学生，用 DSH + OpenViking 管理学习和工具工作流），遇到的问题很具体：

- 把「写脚本前先看清单」「改文件前先备份」这类操作约定写进了 OpenViking 技能和记忆；
- 但真正干活时，模型并不会稳定地主动去读它们——**约定记了，干活时不提就不用**，等于白记；
- 靠提示词或 `AGENTS.md` 也不稳：要么每轮全量注入太费 token，要么模型想起来才看。

于是和 AI 助手一起做了这个小插件：每会话每版本注入一条极短的门铃（入口清单路径 + 版本号），约定版本一改，下一轮就重新出现——不等到「像要动手」的那一轮。后来发现「注入了也可能不执行」，就补了硬拦截：操作类轮次里没读索引前，写操作直接过不去。

**关于代码**：需求、取舍、验证由作者决定；具体实现是与 AI 助手协作完成的。

**为什么公开**：相信「约定记了但干活不提就不用」不是个例，才把它整理出来上传，希望能帮到有同样需求的人。如果你遇到同样的问题，欢迎直接拿去用，也欢迎把你的场景告诉我，一起改进。

## 安装

### 方式一：安装脚本（推荐，跨平台、零依赖）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HeliosTangDev/dsh-ops-conventions.git
cd dsh-ops-conventions
node install.mjs                       # 默认装到 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop
node install.mjs /path/to/profile      # 指定 profile
node install.mjs /path/to/profile --uninstall   # 卸载
```

它会：复制到 `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-ops-conventions`、在 `package.json` 的 `dependencies` 登记、把包名加进 `dsh.profile.bundles`（不加不会被加载）。

### 方式二：手动

1. 把整个仓库复制到 `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-ops-conventions`；
2. 编辑 `<profile>/package.json`：
   ```json
   "dependencies": { "dsh-ops-conventions": "0.2.0" },
   "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ ..., "dsh-ops-conventions" ] } }
   ```

> 注意：`package.json` 里必须有 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向 `cordis.patch.yml`（本包已带）。缺了它，插件管理器会报「没有声明组合包」，且**不会被加载**。

### 装完

- **热重载**：DSH 插件页 → 找到 `dsh-ops-conventions` → 关掉再打开（改 `skills/` 或配置时不用重启）。
- 改的是**代码**（`index.mjs` / `rule.mjs`）时，关掉再打开不保证重新 import，**重启 DeepSeek Harness** 最稳。

## 配置

| 配置项 | 环境变量 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skillsDir` | `DSH_OPS_CONVENTIONS_DIR` | 包内 `skills/` | 约定目录，需含 `INDEX.md`；`VERSION` 可有可无 |
| `logFile` | `DSH_OPS_CONVENTIONS_LOG` | `~/.dsh/ops-conventions/ops-conventions.log` | 注入 / 拦截日志 |
| `enforce` | — | `true` | 是否启用硬拦截；`false` = 只注入门铃 |
| `blockedTools` | — | `write` `edit` `multi_edit` `apply_patch` `notebook_edit` | 拦截的写类工具名；要连 shell 一起拦就自行加 `bash` / `pwsh` |

解析顺序（会**逐个检查目录里真的有 `INDEX.md`**，取第一个有效的）：

1. 配置项 `skillsDir`
2. 环境变量 `DSH_OPS_CONVENTIONS_DIR`
3. **包内 `skills/`**（随包发布，开箱即用）
4. OpenViking 实际存储：`~/.openviking/data/viking/default/user/default/memories/ops-conventions`
5. `~/.dsh/ops-conventions/skills`

示例（写进 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`）：

```yaml
- id: dsh-ops-conventions
  name: "dsh-ops-conventions"
  config:
    skillsDir: "D:/my-conventions/skills"
    enforce: true
    # blockedTools: ["write", "edit", "bash"]
```

## 约定目录结构

```
skills/
├── INDEX.md          # 入口清单（注入文本里给的就是它的路径）
├── VERSION           # 版本号；改它 → 下一次操作轮重新注入
└── ops-scripts/
    └── SKILL.md      # 各类清单，INDEX.md 里引用
```

自带 6 类示例：`ops-scripts`（脚本/后台）、`ops-notes`（笔记）、`ops-files`（文件目录）、`ops-check`（自检）、`ops-longtask`（长任务）、`ops-dsh`（DSH/插件）。可以直接改成你自己的。

## 机制

- 监听 `agent/pre-step`（waterfall），在模型调用前判断最后一条用户消息像不像"要动手"（工具词 或 动作词+对象词）。
- 命中且该会话该版本未注入过 → 追加一条 `instructions` 来源的消息。
- **硬拦截**监听 `tools/pre-execute`（waterfall）：当轮用户消息像要动手、且本会话还没**成功** `read` 过 `INDEX.md` 时，对写类工具返回 `deny`（理由里带索引绝对路径），模型照做后重试即可通过；`tools/result` 观察成功的 INDEX 读取后放行。
- 钩子自身异常一律 **fail-open**（放行）并写日志；`skillsDir` 里没有 `INDEX.md` 时不拦。
- 任何异常都吞掉，不影响正常对话；多会话各自独立判断。
- 日志里可核对：`inject vN`、`guard deny`、`guard index-read`、`guard loaded enforce=...`。

## 常见问题

**Q：插件市场里搜不到？**
A：市场只索引 npm / GitHub 上的包，本地安装的不会出现在搜索结果里；在「已装」列表里能看到。

**Q：卡片显示「异常：这个包没有声明组合包」？**
A：`package.json` 缺 `dsh.bundle.patch`。本包已带；如果你自己改了包，记得保留。

**Q：模型说 `skill xxx is unknown`？**
A：那是会话启动时的技能目录快照导致的，与插件无关。直接用 `read` 读注入里给的那个 `INDEX.md` 路径即可。

**Q：写文件被拒绝，理由是「硬拦截」？**
A：本会话还没 `read` 过 `INDEX.md`。按理由里给的路径读一次（并执行对应清单），再重试原操作即可；不想要这个行为，把配置 `enforce` 设为 `false`。

**Q：注入的提醒会显示在对话里？**
A：会，作为一条来源为插件的消息。长度约 70 token，一个会话只出现一次（版本变了再一次）。

## License

MIT

## Star

如果这个插件对你有用，欢迎在 GitHub 上点个 ⭐ Star，让更多 DSH 用户看到。

# dsh-privacy-shield

Local-first privacy shield for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).

Keep plaintext on your machine. Send only placeholders to the model. See real values again
in your transcript.

**Version 1.0.0** · zero third-party runtime dependencies · pure ESM · Node.js 18+

---

## What it does

DSH keeps two different records of a conversation:

| Surface | What it is | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| **Model-visible surface** | the messages the request is built from | the model (outbound to the cloud) |
| **Human-record surface** | the original committed session events | the chat UI and local session logs |

`dsh-privacy-shield` replaces sensitive text **only in the model-visible copy**, with deterministic
placeholders of the form `<LABEL_8hexdigits>`. Your local session logs, the chat interface, and
tool execution keep the real values. When the model replies, the response stream is wrapped and
placeholders are restored — including placeholders split across stream chunks — so the assistant
message is persisted and displayed with real values.

```
What you type:      Call 张三 at 13800138000 about 京A12345.
What the model      Call <PERSON_1a2b3c4d> at <PHONE_9f8e7d6c> about <PLATE_0a1b2c3d>.
  sees:
What you see        Call 张三 at 13800138000 about 京A12345.
  in the UI:
```

## Features

- **Model-visible masking only** — a defensive patch over `Session.deriveEventMessage`
  rewrites the five surfaces (system, developer, user, assistant, tool result) as the
  model-visible copy is derived; the human-record surface is never rewritten.
- **HMAC placeholders (default)** — `<LABEL_8hex>` = first 4 bytes of
  HMAC-SHA256(label, value); the key lives in a local file (`$DSH_HOME/shield/.placeholder.key`)
  and cannot be enumerated. `placeholderHash: legacy` keeps the old FNV-1a format.
- **Response restoration** — wraps `llm/stream` and restores `text-delta`, `reasoning-delta`,
  `tool-call-delta`, and `block-end` chunks, with a carry-over buffer for split placeholders.
- **Three detection families** — 28 entity types of generic PII/credentials (including social
  insurance, housing fund, student ID, medical record, IMEI, MAC; bank cards pass Luhn), plus
  Chinese-entity rules (organization, project, system, ID number, address, person) and a user
  term list with literal and `re:` regex entries.
- **Smart vocabulary** — `/shield scan-doc <path>` extracts candidate proper nouns from local
  documents (txt/md/csv/json/code/docx); `/shield learn` mines frequent unmatched fragments from
  local session logs. Candidates enter the term list only after explicit confirmation
  (`terms adopt`). `termsFile` hot-reloads on change (fs.watch).
- **Rules-pack import/export** — `/shield export` / `/shield import` carry the term list and
  entity switches between machines (`schema: dsh-shield.rules/v1`); `--encrypt <passphrase>`
  protects a pack with AES-256-GCM + scrypt (`DSH-SHIELD-ENC/v1`), `--pass` decrypts on import.
  A pack never contains the restore table; import validation rejects `vault/values/secrets`-style
  fields outright.
- **Term file** — `termsFile` points at a line-based word list (`#`/`//` comments, `@category`
  tags); merged with inline `terms`.
- **In-memory vault** — the `placeholder → value` table never touches disk and is
  LRU-bounded; it can in principle be rebuilt by re-running the detectors over the local log.
- **Outbound audit** — per-request placeholder counts and label distribution, plus a
  detector re-run over the outbound text to flag plaintext leaks. JSONL sink on by default with
  retention cleanup; `/shield audit [days]` queries, `audit export` writes CSV.
  Counts and labels only — never plaintext.
- **Web UI** — a dock status bar plus an expandable panel (Settings / Terms / Test bench /
  Audit / Candidates). Settings groups the 28 entity types by sensitivity with a search box and
  shows an "enabled x/y" counter; Terms shows category chips and sorts entries by hit count;
  the Test bench can show an opt-in placeholder ↔ value table (off by default); the diagnostics
  badge is hidden unless enabled in Settings; an `⟳ host-version` pill plus a "restart DSH" hint
  appears when the loaded UI bundle is older than the host plugin. Sensitive actions need
  `confirm`. See `docs/CLIENT-RPC-NOTES.md` for the RPC contract (11 methods).
- **Ops commands** — `/shield pause <minutes>` temporarily passes plaintext and auto-resumes;
  `/shield doctor` runs a check-up with OK/warn lines.
- **`shield_scan` tool** — a model-callable tool that reports masking statistics (counts and
  labels only).
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** Toggleable via `/shield on|off` and `/shield enforce|observe`.

> **Image note.** This plugin does not inspect image content (no OCR); images pass through
> untouched — handle sensitive images yourself. Text-like file block contents are masked.

> **Plaintext note.** Real values in your local logs are a deliberate design choice — they are
> what makes restoration possible. Disk encryption, backup handling, and access control remain
> your responsibility. See [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md).

## How it differs from other masking plugins

Several DSH plugins mask PII before it reaches the model. The design choices here:

- **Only the model-visible copy is rewritten.** Local session logs, the chat transcript, and
  tool execution keep real values — which is what makes display-layer restoration possible.
  (Plugins that also rewrite the human-record surface trade away local readability.)
- **Placeholders are HMAC-derived** with a local key file (`$DSH_HOME/shield/.placeholder.key`),
  so they are stable across sessions but cannot be enumerated or reversed by someone who only
  sees the masked text.
- **Rules packs move between machines** — term lists and entity switches export/import as JSON,
  optionally AES-256-GCM encrypted, and a pack never contains the restore table.
- **Vocabulary mining** — `scan-doc` extracts candidate proper nouns from local documents and
  `learn` mines session history; candidates take effect only after explicit confirmation.
- **Outbound audit with plaintext re-check** — every request is re-scanned for leaks; the audit
  records counts and labels only, never plaintext.

## Quick start

1. **Install** the bundle (absolute path to this directory):
   `plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=<absolute path to dsh-privacy-shield>`
2. **Restart the DSH profile** — mandatory after install, upgrade, or uninstall
   (see *Known limitations*).
3. **Configure** in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (the shipped `cordis.patch.yml` is a
   working example; it already defaults to `mode: enforce`).
4. **Verify**:
   - `/shield status` — mode, surfaces, counts, derive-patch status.
   - `/shield verify 张三的手机号是13800138000` — trial masking (prints masked output only).

## Rules packs (import / export)

```
/shield export [path] [--encrypt <passphrase>]   # write terms + entity switches to a pack
/shield import <path> [--pass <passphrase>] [replace confirm]
                                                 # auto-detects encrypted packs; merge (default)
                                                 # or replace the term list
/shield rules                                    # show current pack summary (counts only)
```

- Pack schema: `dsh-shield.rules/v1` — `{ schema, exportedAt, plugin, entities, terms, notes }`.
- Packs contain **terms and entity switches only** — never the restore table. Still, a term
  list is itself sensitive; handle packs at the same classification level as your word list.
- Alternatively, set `rulesPack: "<path>"` in `cordis.patch.yml` to load a pack at startup,
  or `termsFile` for a line-based word list.

## Configuration

Full reference: [docs/CONFIG.md](docs/CONFIG.md). Summary:

| Field | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; `false` registers nothing. |
| `mode` | `enforce` | `enforce` rewrites the model-visible surface; `observe` counts only. |
| `entities` | 26 types | Enabled entity types (see *Entity types*). |
| `placeholderHash` | `hmac` | Placeholder hash: `hmac` (HMAC-SHA256, local key file) / `legacy` (FNV-1a, enumerable). |
| `minLevel` | `low` | Entity sensitivity floor (high/medium/low) when `entities` is not set explicitly. |
| `addressLevel` | `full` | Chinese address granularity: `full` to door number / `street` to street only. |
| `terms` | `[]` | Inline term list (`term`, `term @category`, `re:regex @category`). |
| `termsFile` | `null` | Line-based word list file (relative → `$DSH_HOME/shield/`); hot-reloads on change. |
| `disabledLabels` | `[]` | Disabled term labels (mirrors `terms label off`). |
| `rulesPack` | `null` | Rules-pack file loaded at startup. |
| `surfaces` | all `true` | Per-surface toggles: system / developer / user / assistant / tool. |
| `mediaPolicy` | `pass` | Media blocks pass; text-like file contents are still masked; no image OCR. |
| `audit.jsonl` / `audit.jsonlPath` | `true` / default | JSONL audit sink (counts only). |
| `audit.retentionDays` | `30` | Audit retention; older lines are purged at startup. |
| `audit.verifyOutbound` | `full` | Plaintext re-check over outbound text: `full`/`sample`/`off`. |
| `audit.maxVerifyChars` | 2000000 | Skip the re-check above this size. |
| `onUnmaskable` | `warn` | `block` throws instead of sending a frozen request with plaintext. |
| `registerProjections` | `true` | Core masking switch (the derive patch); `false` = audit only. |
| `registerCommand` / `registerTools` | `true` | `/shield` command / `shield_scan` tool. |
| `maxVaultEntries` | 5000 | Vault cap (100–200000), oldest evicted first. |

**Removed in 0.2.0:** `sessionFilter` — DSH's masking hooks are session-agnostic, so the
shield can only operate globally; a configured `sessionFilter` degrades to a notice. Use
`/shield off` for temporary exemption.

## Commands

```
/shield [status|on|off confirm|enforce|observe confirm|pause <minutes>|doctor
        |verify [text]|terms [label off|on LABEL|adopt <indices…|all>]
        |scan-doc <path>|learn|audit [days]|audit export <path>
        |vault|rules|export [path] [--encrypt <passphrase>]|import <path> [--pass <passphrase>] [replace confirm]|help]
```

All status output is counts and labels only — never your text. `on`/`off`,
`enforce`/`observe`, and `pause` are process-local and lost on restart.

## Entity types

28 entity names; 26 on by default, `ipv4`/`ipv6` opt-in. Full table and the Chinese-rule
heuristics: [docs/CONFIG.md](docs/CONFIG.md); rationale and DSH source evidence:
[docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md](docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md). Detection is rule- and list-driven (no NER
model): it will miss unusual names and over-match some technical text — use `terms`,
`scan-doc`, or `learn` for your own organizations, projects, systems, and codes.

## Known limitations

1. **Restart the profile after any install/upgrade/unload.** Masking rides on a defensive
   patch over `Session.deriveEventMessage`; unloading the plugin restores plain derivation,
   and sessions/logs are unaffected either way. (`termsFile` word-list changes hot-reload
   without a restart; every other config change still needs one.)
2. **No OCR** — images pass through untouched; avoid sending sensitive images or redact them
   first. Text-like file block contents are masked.
3. **Heuristic detection** — unmatched sensitive values leave in plaintext; watch the
   outbound-audit violation counter and extend `terms`.
4. **`observe` masks nothing** — it sends plaintext and reports `0` outbound placeholders.
5. **Label changes alter placeholders** — a value matched under a different label after a
   config change yields a different placeholder.
6. **Vault eviction is silent** — evicted mappings stay as placeholders in restored output.
7. **Runtime toggles do not persist** across restarts; edit `cordis.patch.yml` for durability.
8. **`mediaPolicy: 'strip'` is not implemented** — accepted by the config schema, no code
   removes media blocks.
9. **Hot reload overwrites in-process terms** — a `termsFile` change rebuilds the vocabulary
   from config sources, dropping terms added via the UI or commands (logged).

## Development and testing

```bash
node --test "test/*.test.mjs"     # 123 unit tests (engine, crypto, audit, RPC, runtime, UI render, locale sync)
node tools/build-dist.mjs         # release/ directory + .zip + .tgz
```

No dependencies to install. The browser half has an additional offline smoke harness
(React stub + loader stub); see `docs/CLIENT-RPC-NOTES.md`.

## Distribution

`dsh-privacy-shield` is a DSH bundle (`package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`); there is no build
step and no third-party dependency. Build the artifacts with `node tools/build-dist.mjs`, then
hand them to someone else in whichever of these ways fits:

1. **Local folder (offline, simplest).** Send `.zip`; the recipient unpacks it and asks their DSH
   agent to install the unpacked folder (absolute path, the directory that contains `package.json`):

   ```
   plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=<absolute path to the unpacked dsh-privacy-shield directory>
   ```

2. **Tarball URL.** Send `.tgz` (standard npm tarball, `package/` root; verified installable by
   npm/pnpm) or host it anywhere with a direct download link, then install by URL — either in the
   Plugins page install field or via the agent:

   ```
   plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=https://example.com/dsh-privacy-shield-1.0.0.tgz
   ```

3. **Git repository.** Push this directory as a repository and install by URL:

   ```
   plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=https://github.com/<you>/dsh-privacy-shield.git
   ```

4. **npm package (optional).** The unscoped name `dsh-privacy-shield` is available if you
   ever want `npm publish`; GitHub installs (above) do not need it.

After installing, the recipient restarts their DSH profile and reloads the page. Config is not part
of the package — send a config snippet (`cordis.patch.yml` keys), not your whole profile.

The recipient-facing walkthrough (Chinese and English) lives in `docs/DISTRIBUTE.md` and is also
copied into the release kit by `tools/build-dist.mjs`.

## Documentation

- [docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md](docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md) — why the implementation works this way, with DSH source evidence (Chinese).
- [docs/CLIENT-RPC-NOTES.md](docs/CLIENT-RPC-NOTES.md) — browser-half RPC contract and verified DSH mechanics.
- [docs/CONFIG.md](docs/CONFIG.md) — every config field, entity type, and heuristic.
- [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md) — threat model and boundaries.
- [docs/COMPLIANCE.md](docs/COMPLIANCE.md) — feature-to-principle mapping (not legal advice).
- [docs/CHANGELOG.md](docs/CHANGELOG.md) — release notes.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-session-delete-local

> 给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) 补一个**删除会话**的入口。
> Adds a **Delete conversation** action to DeepSeek Harness.

DeepSeek Harness 目前没有删除会话的界面入口。这个插件在**左侧会话列表每条的「…」菜单**里加一项 **「删除会话」**，点击确认后真正删除该会话的数据与投影缓存。

---

## 功能

- **会话行「…」菜单新增「删除会话」** —— 官方槽位 `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item`，带分隔线，排在插件区。
- 删除前弹原生确认框，避免误删。
- 删除成功后自动刷新页面，列表立即消失。
- 同时清理投影缓存，不会在列表里残留幽灵条目。
- 额外提供两个 agent 工具：`session_list` / `session_delete`（可选）。

## 安装

插件目录放到 profile 的 `node_modules` 下：

```
~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-session-delete-local/
```

并在该 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 追加：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-session-delete-local
      name: 'dsh-session-delete-local'
      inject: [tools]
```

然后**完全重启 DSH**（托盘图标 → 退出 → 重新打开），浏览器端刷新一次页面。

> 也可以把本目录 clone 到任意位置，再用 `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "file:<绝对路径>"` 安装。

## 使用

1. 左侧会话列表，鼠标悬停到某条会话；
2. 点右侧出现的 **「…」**；
3. 菜单里选 **「删除会话」**；
4. 确认 → 页面刷新，会话消失。

删除不可恢复。该会话的记录、统计会一并清除。

## 实现

| 层 | 文件 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 宿主 | `lib/index.js` | 注册 `POST /dsh-session-delete/api` + 两个 agent 工具 |
| 浏览器 | `client.js` | Module Loader（`factory(require)`）注册菜单项 |
| 清单 | `package.json` | `dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client` |

删除动作作用在：

```
$DSH_HOME/sessions/<workspaceKey>/session-<uuid>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd
$DSH_HOME/storages/session_projcache/sessions/session-<uuid>.json
$DSH_HOME/storages/workspace.json          # 清理该会话在侧栏索引里的 sessionIds
```

> 第三项很关键：会话数据与侧栏索引是两份文件。只删目录，`workspace.json` 里残留的 id 仍会让它挂在列表上，表现就是「删不掉」。

不依赖任何私有会话服务 API，因此对 DSH 版本变化更稳。

### 安全设计

- 会话 id 严格按 UUID 校验，防路径穿越；
- HTTP 路由只接受**回环地址**、只接受 `POST`；
- `apply()` 永不抛出异常，插件坏了也不会拖垮 profile 启动；
- 取不到 `webServer` 服务时静默降级（工具部分仍可用）；
- `MenuItemButton` 取不到时回退到原生 `role="menuitem"` 按钮。

## 兼容性

- 在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端（web platform）上开发与验证。
- 依赖的槽位与路由 API 均为 DSH 公开契约：
  - `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item`
  - `ctx.webServer.register({ kind, path, handler })`

## 本地自测

```powershell
node test-dry.mjs                       # 列出本机会话
node test-dry.mjs --delete <sessionId>  # 只做 dry-run，不删除
```

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # Agents Notch **`dsh-agents-notch`** — an always-on-top notch for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) that answers one question: **which of my sessions needs me right now?** ![the notch, unfolded](docs/screenshot.png) One bot per session; hover and the board unfolds: who is working, who is waiting on you, who failed, who finished and you have not looked yet. That strip is the whole visual language, and it is what the tab says at a glance: **working** has no ring (working is the quiet default), **needs you** wears an amber ring and a `?`, **failed** a red ring, and **host offline** means the harness stopped answering — not that everything is fine. ## Why If you run more than a couple of sessions, the answer to "is anything waiting on me?" is currently one of these, and all of them cost a context switch: | what you do today | what it costs | |---|---| | alt-tab between windows and read each sidebar | the thing you were doing, every time | | wait for a desktop notification | one per session, and none of them say which one is *blocked* | | leave the sidebar visible | it is only visible when the app is in front — which is when you do not need it | The notch is 220×30 px of always-on-top that never takes focus, hides under a full-screen app, and shows the one thing the sidebar cannot while you are in another window: **a session stuck on you**. With a single session it is a decoration; that is stated under *Limits* rather than glossed over. ## Requirements - **Windows 10/11, x64.** The window is WPF and Win32 (topmost, no-activate, fullscreen detection): there is no macOS or Linux build. `package.json` declares `"os": ["win32"]`. - **DeepSeek Harness.** Built and verified on **0.2.1-rc.2**. The host half reads `session/event` (`{ global: true }`), `ctx.webServer`, `ctx.agents` and `sessionQuery`; an older build may lack a field. Nothing is checked before mounting — see *Limits*. - **Node ≥ 22** for the plugin. **No .NET runtime**: the released window is self-contained. - Optional: the **`session-finished`** plugin, which is what retires a finished row (*What earns a row*). ## Install **One command**, like every other DSH plugin: ```powershell dsh plugin --profile add dsh-agents-notch # or the app's own plugin manager ``` That is the whole install. The plugin is ~30 KB of JavaScript; the 65 MB window does not ride in the tarball, because every version bump would re-upload it and every update re-download it. Instead the host **fetches the matching release asset itself** the first time it needs a window it cannot find: `v` of `repository` in the package manifest, hash verified against the `.sha256` published beside it, written to `$DSH_HOME\state\agents-notch\window\\`. You can watch it happen: ```jsonc {"event":"window-fetch","url":"https://github.com//dsh-agents-notch/releases/download/v0.1.1/AgentsNotch.exe"} {"event":"window-fetched","bytes":68276826,"verified":true} {"event":"window-started","pid":6704,"source":"installed"} ``` **What success looks like:** within a couple of seconds of the harness starting, the tab is at the top of the screen, and `$DSH_HOME\state\agents-notch\state.json` lists your sessions. If the tab does not appear, that directory holds `host-report.jsonl` — the newest line says which of the five places the host looked, whether it tried to fetch, and the command that fixes it. Offline, behind a firewall, or you just prefer to do it by hand? The installer does the same job: ```powershell pwsh -File "\node_modules\dsh-agents-notch\tools\install-window.ps1" ` -Url https://github.com//dsh-agents-notch/releases/download/v0.1.1/AgentsNotch.exe # or from a checkout you built yourself: pwsh -File tools\install-window.ps1 -FromPath dist\win-x64 ``` `autoDownload: false` in the plugin row turns the fetch off; `downloadUrl: ` points it at a mirror. The release is **one 65 MB file** with no prerequisites — no .NET runtime. Being one file, it unpacks its native libraries on first run, and the plugin points that unpack at `\bundle` rather than `%TEMP%`: measured on a normal Windows 11 box, the default unpack directory could not be created (error 5) and the app died before drawing anything, with no message a user would ever see. ## Configure **The notch has a pane of its own: Settings → Agents Notch.** Size, anchor, display, rows, opacity, motion and the three text switches live there, and a change lands on the notch immediately — the window re-reads its state on the next tick, so nothing restarts. Three layers decide a value, each beating the one above it: 1. the built-in defaults; 2. the plugin row's `config:` below — the file you edit, which nothing overwrites; 3. `$DSH_HOME/state/agents-notch/settings.json`, written by the pane, one click at a time. Both doors are clamped by the same rules, so a slider and a YAML line behave identically, and a value the pane writes is stored in its clamped form — the file always says what the window does. *Reset* in the pane clears that third layer and the row decides again. The pane keeps its own file because a browser cannot safely rewrite YAML: editing `cordis.patch.yml` from a UI would round-trip a file other sessions also edit. Defaults live in the package's own `cordis.patch.yml`. To change one, put a row **with the same id** in your profile's patch layer (`$DSH_HOME/profiles//cordis.patch.yml`) — a row without `insert:` is an override of a row that already exists: ```yaml - id: agents-notch config: contextBudget: 1000000 # your route's context window, in tokens anchor: top-right scale: 1.25 ``` | key | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `spawnWindow` | `true` | `false` runs the host without a window — useful for tests | | `pollMs` | `340` | how often the state file is rebuilt | | `maxRows` | `6` | 3–10, how many sessions the board may show | | `contextBudget` | `null` | your route's context window in tokens; `null` = unknown (see below) | | `contextHotAt` | `0.5` | the fraction where the bar turns amber — the route's compaction trigger | | `anchor` | `top-center` | `top-center` · `top-left` · `top-right` | | `screen` | `primary` | `primary` · `cursor` · `1` · `2` … (as Windows numbers them) | | `scale` | `1` | 0.75–2 | | `hideFullscreen` | `true` | hide under a full-screen app | | `opacity` | `1` | 0.35–1, how much of the desktop the notch sits in front of | | `motion` | `auto` | `auto` follows Windows' reduce-motion setting; `on` forces the animation, `off` draws the settled pose and nothing else | | `showProject` | `true` | the project name in the sub line (the colour chips at right stay) | | `showDone` | `true` | `false` keeps finished sessions off the board entirely (and out of the count) || `finishedFallbackMs` | `900000` | how long a settled row survives when `session-finished` is absent | | `stateDir` | `$DSH_HOME/state/agents-notch` | where the state file, the log and the window live | | `exePath` | — | force one window binary | | `autoDownload` | `true` | fetch the window from the release when it is missing | | `downloadUrl` | — | fetch from a mirror instead of the release | ### Honest numbers `contextBudget` is **not** guessed. The context window belongs to the model route, and nothing in the session feed carries it, so this plugin defaults it to `null` — and with `null` you get a token count and no percentage, no bar and no amber. A percentage against an invented denominator is a lie that looks like information, which is worse than a number with units. ![the same board with no budget: 412k and no bar](docs/screenshot-no-budget.png) Set it to your route's real window (this build's DeepSeek V4 routes: `1000000`) and the bar appears. ## What earns a row A session is on the board because **something happened to it**: it is working, it is blocked on an approval or a question, it failed, or it finished and you have not closed it out. Merely being open never earns a row, however many sessions are attached. Finished and failed rows do not expire on a timer. They leave when the harness's own close-out verdict says so — the ✓ that the **`session-finished`** plugin puts in the sidebar, read over that plugin's HTTP route. If it is not installed, this one notices after three failed probes and retires settled rows after 15 minutes instead, and says so in the tooltip. Nothing on a row decays on its own: a field that changed with nothing having happened would be the one untrustworthy thing on the board. When the host stops answering, the board stops pretending — the tab goes grey and the sub line dates the last heartbeat instead of repeating a summary nobody is updating: ![host offline: the tab says so, and the board says when it last saw the host](docs/screenshot-stale.png) ## Limits, stated plainly - **Windows only**, x64. No macOS or Linux build, and no partial one. - **No DSH version is declared in the manifest**, so nothing gates a wrong install. It was built and tested on `0.2.1-rc.2`; if a field is missing on your build, the host keeps serving and the log says what failed rather than the tab lying. - **`session-finished` is optional but recommended** — without it, closed-out sessions linger for the 15-minute fallback. - **The window is not draggable**, by design: it is a fixed surface at the top of the screen, and a draggable one got dragged by accident. Move it with `anchor` and `screen`. - **Two windows cannot coexist** — a named mutex makes the second instance exit. - **The binary is unsigned**, so SmartScreen warns the first time you run it. - **Quitting it from the tray is a one-hour dismissal, not forever**: the host brings the notch back, because a status board that can be lost by accident is worse than one that returns. ## Uninstall ```powershell dsh plugin --profile remove dsh-agents-notch # or the app's plugin manager Remove-Item -Recurse "$env:DSH_HOME\state\agents-notch" # state, log, window binary, unpack cache ``` ## Develop ```powershell npm test # 43 tests, node --test, no harness, no window, no network npm run window:build # dotnet build desktop/AgentsNotch.csproj -c Release npm run window:publish # self-contained single file + SHA256 into dist/win-x64 # a still of the board, from a fixture, without a harness: desktop/bin/Release/net9.0-windows/AgentsNotch.exe --state desktop/fixtures/working.json --open --shot dist/shots/working.png ``` The window takes `--shot`, `--open`, `--freeze`, `--log`, `--fps`, `--no-effects` and `--probe-rect`, and `desktop/fixtures/` holds schema-3 state files, so every state can be photographed with no harness running. - [`docs/CONTRACT.md`](docs/CONTRACT.md) — the interface between the two halves; frozen, and both halves and the tests are written against it. - [`docs/INTERNALS.md`](docs/INTERNALS.md) — the engineering record: every measurement that decided a shape, and the traps that cost a day each. The most useful file here if you change something. - [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) — what changed, per version. - [`docs/PUBLISHING.md`](docs/PUBLISHING.md) — the checklist for cutting a release. MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# dsh-opencli · 让你的 dsh 用**你的浏览器**办事 [![awesome-dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/awesome--dsh--plugin-listed-17695?logo=github&labelColor=555)](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/tree/main/data/plugins/IKEASven69__dsh-opencli.yml) [![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20topic-dsh--plugin-4D6BFE?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) > Let your DeepSeek Harness agent work in **your logged-in browser**: 知乎/B站/微博/GitHub 等 **180+ 站点一步式命令**,发帖点赞带审批门。 **dsh 自带的 web 工具是"搜索"——所有人拿到一样的匿名结果。这个插件给它补上"办事"的那一半:agent 操纵你自己日常使用的、带登录态的真实浏览器,以你的账号视角拿数据、替你动手(写操作先弹审批,你点了允许才执行)。** | 在对话里说 | 插件做的事 | |---|---| | "B站搜罗翔,总结播放量前 3" | `site bilibili search 罗翔` 一步拿到结构化结果 | | "知乎热榜前 10 摘要" | `site zhihu hot` | | "每天早 9 点自动跑热榜,有异常告诉我" | 面板建定时任务,持久化真执行,watch 关键词命中通知 | | "把这个转发到我的微博" | `site weibo post …` —— **先弹审批窗** | | "同时拉知乎/微博/B站热榜做对比" | `site_batch` 一条命令三站并行 | | "打开公司后台把审批单批了" | `browser_open/click` 通用原语,用你的登录态 | **实测效果(真实登录态,非演示数据):** | 对话里直接跑命令 | 定时采集 → 快照 → 时间线 → 带出处报告 | |---|---| | ![试试看](docs/assets/readme/demo-try-run.png) | ![真实数据时间线](docs/assets/readme/demo-timeline-realdata.png) | **没适配器的网站?** 180+ 站目录之外,`browser_*` 通用原语覆盖任意网页;agent 还能当场造适配器,越用越会浏览。完整命令目录: ![命令目录](docs/assets/readme/demo-catalog.png) ## 30 秒装完 ```sh # ① 装 opencli 并启动(已装过 opencli/OpenCLIApp?跳到 ③) npm i -g @jackwener/opencli && opencli daemon restart # ② 装 BrowserBridge 扩展(Chrome/Edge 都行),在浏览器里登录你的常用站点 # https://github.com/jackwener/OpenCLI/releases → opencli-extension-*.zip → 浏览器"加载解压缩的扩展" # ③ 装插件 dsh plugin add IKEASven69/dsh-opencli ``` **不想自己动手?把下面这句发给你的 dsh,它替你装完并自检:** > 请按 https://github.com/IKEASven69/dsh-opencli/blob/opencli-release/AGENT_INSTALL.md 里的步骤帮我安装 dsh-opencli,装完跑一次自检并告诉我结果。 装完打开 dsh 设置 →「浏览器代理」面板:四 tab(总览/命令/自动化/安全与设置)、180 站目录、登录态巡检、daemon 一键修复。
安装注意事项(3 条,遇到问题再展开) - ⚠️ 旧版 opencli(≤1.8.8)在插件目录内跑 `npm install` 会静默替换宿主链接([#2555](https://github.com/jackwener/opencli/issues/2555),**2.0 已修复**)——仍在 1.8.x 的用户请在仓库外装依赖。 - ⚠️ Windows:dsh shell 走 PowerShell,`DSH_OPENCLI_BIN` 需指向 `.cmd` 结尾的 shim(无扩展名会被静默忽略)。版本管理器(vfox/nvm)切 node 版本后插件会自动扫描各版本目录找回 opencli。 - ⚠️ 升级 dsh 到 0.2 前自查 profile `cordis.patch.yml` 有无引用未安装的 bundle——0.2 对此静默退出。
--- ## 登录态到底是怎么回事(重要澄清) **本插件不使用、也不需要 dsh 的内置浏览器。**它经 [OpenCLI](https://github.com/jackwener/OpenCLI) 的 daemon + BrowserBridge 扩展,驱动**你扩展装在哪个、就哪个浏览器的真实窗口**(Chrome/Edge 均可)——登录态来自你日常浏览器里的真实会话,和你在地址栏手打网址完全同源。你在哪登录了知乎,agent 就能用你的知乎;巡检面板会告诉你哪些站在线。 ## 两张牌:固定命令 × 任意网页原语 模型对每个站有两张牌,**先打第一张,失败自动换第二张**: 1. **固定命令**(`site <站> <命令>`):预编译站点知识,省 token、结果可验证、有失败签名恢复表; 2. **任意网页原语**(`browser_open/state/click/fill` + 只读脚本 + Playwright recipe):适配器没覆盖的页面用登录态自由组合。 动手前先让模型调 `site_knowledge <站>` 读知识卡:全部命令+已知坑+失败恢复表——不现场试错。知识卡可导出 markdown 分享(`~/.dsh/opencli-knowledge/`)。 ## 它回答的三个真实缺口 - *"browser agents re-learn every site on every session"*([browser-use#5841](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/5841))→ **180+ 站预置结构化命令**:站点知识预编译,不重学。 - *"想在当前打开的 Chrome 实例上做自动化"*([browser-use#4709](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/4709))→ **登录态原生**:所有命令跑在你已登录的浏览器里,不另起无头实例。 - *"求结构化动作证据:动作到底改没改页面"*([browser-use#5137](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/5137);同源 [BrowserSkill#242](https://github.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/issues/242))→ **执行真实性层**:采集结果经确定性规则+亚秒决策模型两层判定,`exit 0` 但内容无效会被标"疑似静默失败",无人值守定时任务按失败重试。 ## 已经自己装过 opencli,这插件还有什么用 | | 只装 opencli(agent 走 shell) | + 本插件 | |---|---|---| | 开局发现 | 模型得先跑 `opencli list`(数 MB 输出) | **蒸馏命令目录已注入 systemPrompt**,第一轮就选对命令 | | 权限模型 | 需要 shell 权限;写操作裸奔无门 | 一等公民工具 + **write 审批门**(工具层拦截) | | 只读/受限会话 | 无 shell 就没戏 | 无需 shell,工具照用 | | 定时采集 | 自己写 crontab + 脚本 + 通知 | 面板建定时任务,持久化 + 真执行 + 运行可见 | | 管理 | 敲命令 | dsh 设置页:诊断/一键启动/目录浏览/巡检/启停/模式切换 | 两不冲突:深度用法仍可配合官方 opencli 技能,本插件负责工具化、安全与面板。 ## 全功能面 | 模块 | 能力 | |---|---| | **site 适配器** | 180+ 站 / 200+ 命令,蒸馏目录注入 systemPrompt;`site_batch` 多站并行 | | **browser 原语** | open/click/type/fill/scroll/state/screenshot/extract/wait/crawl 全套(泛爬带限流) | | **定时任务** | cron,持久化真执行,重启不丢;失败重试 ×3 + 通知 + 运行历史 | | **采集快照/时间线** | 成功执行存结构化快照(50 份轮转);时间线趋势+历史;**带出处报告导出**(每节:命令+时间+快照路径,零模型改写) | | **watch 监控** | 关键词命中 → 通知事件(大小写不敏感) | | **执行轨迹** | 每条 browser/定时执行落盘 JSONL,面板「运行轨迹」复盘"上次为什么失败" | | **自动化模式** | read-only / standard / autonomous / unrestricted 四档,接入 `tools/pre-execute` 审批门 | | **站点健康度** | 上游 issue 实测数据驱动:受损站标注 + browser 兜底提示 | | **MCP Resources** | dsh 0.2 下站点知识经 `opencli://sites/{site}/knowledge` 暴露 | | **我的适配器** | 禁用/启用管理,禁用即从 systemPrompt 目录收缩 | | **登录态巡检** | 面板实时显示各站在线状态(cookie 级诊断) | | **登录态桥** | 探测 daemon 浏览器 CDP 端点,一键把 dsh 官方 Browser Use 接到你登录态的浏览器 | | **拦截审计** | 审批门拦截记录(近 7 天计数 + 明细) | | **限流与限域** | `usagePolicy` + 429/5xx 自动退避;`--authProfile` 限域登录,跨域拒绝 | | **站点品牌图标** | 48+ 站 simple-icons 官方标 + 品牌色 | | **中英双语** | 面板 EN / zh 一键切换 | ## 配置 零配置开箱即用;需要微调时: | 配置 | 方式 | 默认 | |---|---|---| | opencli 二进制路径 | 环境变量 `DSH_OPENCLI_BIN`,或插件自带本地依赖 | `opencli`(全局) | | 写审批开关 | 面板「审批门」一键开关 | 开 | | 自动化模式 | 面板四档 | standard | | 限流策略 | `usagePolicy`(minDelayMs 750 / maxConcurrency 2 / burst 3 / cooldown 30s / maxPagesPerRun 20) | 见左 | | 限域登录 | `authProfiles`(`allowedDomains`/`storageStatePath`),配 `site --authProfile` | 无 | ## 安全设计 - **write 审批门**(默认开):写命令经 dsh 原生审批——弹窗点"允许"才执行;权限不明按写处理(fail-closed)。 - 命令白名单与参数校验;`browser_do` 仅放行只读/创作类子命令。 - 全部输出经截断与噪声剥离,防上下文污染。 - 限流 + 自动退避;限域登录跨域拒绝。 ## 已验证的测试矩阵 | 层面 | 方式 | 结果 | |---|---|---| | 单元/回归 | vitest ×159(含 cron 回归/空参数护栏/trace/报告结构) | ✅ | | 全权审查套件 | 21 项真机逐项(渲染/真执行/状态对账/RPC 真值),`full-review.cjs` 一键复测;dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 与 0.2.1-rc.1 双版本通过 | ✅ | | 真模型 E2E | 会话调 `site zhihu hot`/写拒绝/browser 往返 | ✅ | | 登录态真数据 | 浏览器扩展桥 → try-run 真实热榜(判定 P=0.91)→ 定时采集 15s 回填 → 快照 → 时间线 → 带出处报告 | ✅ | ## 更新日志 完整版本历史见 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) 与 [Releases](https://github.com/IKEASven69/dsh-opencli/releases)。 ## 定位(不做什么) - 不替代 OpenCLIApp/daemon/扩展——那是引擎与管家,本插件是 **dsh 里的驾驶舱**; - 不替代 dsh 内置 web_search/web_fetch——内置管检索,本插件管办事; - 无头服务器(没有任何真实浏览器的机器)不适用。 MIT License.
