evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @jayyuen66/dsh-danger-guard [中文](./README.zh-CN.md) ### What it does - A pre-execution tool guard: the blocking decision lives in the synchronous predicate on `ctx.tools.guard` (host.ts), where returning a string physically rejects that call. It also subscribes to the two official waterfalls (`tools/pre-execute` / `tools/post-execute`) for the pre-edit preflight described below. - The host hands the reason back to the model as that tool call's error result, so the model gets "why it was blocked + what to change instead" rather than a silent failure. - Three defences: - Dangerous bash/pwsh commands (`bashVerdictOf` in lib/danger-rules.ts - git hook bypass, catastrophic rm, download-and-run, long-running dev server, the **git destruction family** (7 keys) and the **infrastructure destruction family** (5 keys)). - Secret/credential paths on edit/write tools (`secretPathDeny`). - The first-edit fact gate (state machine in lib/fact-gate.ts plus the evidence verdict in host.ts). - **The disposition forks on the permission preset: one rule key can resolve three different ways across the four presets** (the decision itself is `decideRule` in `lib/mode-policy.ts`; the preset × key matrix is pinned cell by cell in `test/mode-policy.test.ts`): - The preset facts are folded from the host's read-only service faces by `lib/policy-facts.ts`: the sandbox mode (`sandboxPolicy.resolve`), **whether asking is possible** (`approval.overrideOf ?? config.policy`), and **whether this is Auto review** (`permissionPresets.current`). None of them calls `approval.request()` - that appends a pair of audit events, i.e. asking once in order to learn whether asking is possible. - `deny` (hard refusal from the **synchronous** `ctx.tools.guard`): a hit physically rejects the call and the model gets `Error: `, composed of the base reason, the way out, and a **mode note** (`lib/policy-deny.ts`). - `ask` (`tools/pre-execute` → the host's `ApprovalService`): we hand over the official `{ kind: "ask", reason, displayReason }` and the host owns policy, audit logging, UI routing and fail-closed; only `allowed-once` passes. - `allow`: this layer stays out of it - the call goes to the downstream and the host sandbox. **The whole full-access preset is `allow`** (the user chose zero guardrails); hits only increment the stats (`noteAllowedHit`) and never interrupt the model. - One hard rule: **whether asking is possible decides whether `ask` can land.** The shipped presets bind `danger-full-access` to `approval: never`, and `never` returns `rejected` deterministically **before any answerer runs** (with the host swapping in its own fixed wording). So a rule that should ask is collapsed to `deny` by us in that preset, carrying a dedicated paragraph on "this preset cannot ask - switch to one that can" (`askBlockedGeneric`), so the model is not left with a bare "no". - The table's type makes two properties **structural**: a missing tier is a compile error, and one key belonging to both tiers is impossible (one cell cannot hold two values). The latter is a hard requirement: `tools.guard` is synchronous while approval is async, and the host **runs the guard again after approval passes** - so "both tiers claim one key" shows up as **the user pressing Allow and still being refused**. - Severity ordering: when one command holds both an `ask` segment and a `deny` segment, **the whole string resolves as `deny`** (the scan keeps going until it has a `deny`). Without it, the leading `ask` segment would end the scan early and the later catastrophe would never be judged at all. - **A repeat hit is not re-reported** (`AskDeduper` in `lib/confirm.ts`): the same session + same rule key + same command text no longer goes back to the lesson bus and its blast-radius rehearsal is not recomputed, but the **verdict and the prompt stay exactly as they were** (still `ask`, evidence still measured). What this suppresses is lesson-card fragmentation, not a user interruption - deduplication must never turn into a silent pass. - **Every refusal carries its way out**: `BashVerdict` holds a structured `Fix`; the git bypass names the offending flags, catastrophic rm names the offending targets (**excluding the safe ones**). So the model receives "change these words and it passes" rather than a verdict. - Preflight (evidence gathered before the edit, replacing "refuse first, let the model go look"). Two faces, one per waterfall, split by *when evidence actually becomes visible*: - Face A (read-only inspection: `read`/`view`/`str_replace_editor view`) on `tools/post-execute`: the reference surface the gate wants rides **this read's own result** (official `PostToolDecision.accept{additionalContexts}`; agent-loop accepts it at the next step boundary), so the model sees "who references it" before its next edit. - Face B (write calls) on `tools/pre-execute`: when the model edits **without having read** the target, the target content and reference surface are written into this call's denial reason (official `PreToolDecision.deny{reason}`, materialized as the call's error result), and an identical retry passes on the delivery watermark - the physical stop stays before dispatch, so "see it before you change it" is not negotiated away. The **layer evidence** a high-tier edit additionally requires (test/e2e/docs) comes from the same run: the conclusions are derived from that one reference scan (how many hits fall inside each layer directory), so no extra I/O is spent on them, and they are recorded on the delivery watermark together with read/refs. - Why not `agent.inject()`: that API queues context for the **next pre-step**, while context advances by steps - a decision made at step N only sees up to step N-1, so injected evidence would be read *after* the edit landed. Official docs also state a pending injection may be cancelled or discarded, while the watermark would already have recorded it as delivered. - Four yields (any one restores today's refusal path): a target the secret gate would block (its body must not leak through the preflight, and our deny would decide for that gate), a quota-released target (the anti-deadlock promise comes first), a run that earns nothing (content unreadable, or the scan truncated by its budgets), and **a layer gap this scan did not cover** (the walk was truncated by its budgets, that layer lies outside the scan root, or that layer is a symlink - the gate's layer probe follows links while the scan does not, per the official `lstat` contract). "Zero hits in this layer" is then no conclusion at all, and half an "I probed this layer" is worse than none. - Boundedness is a hard requirement, not an optimization: the platform never abandons a pending pre-execute promise, so the scan caps files (256), directories (256), per-file bytes (64KB, oversize files are **skipped**) and findings (40) while skipping dependency/build and dot directories; target content is read at **fixed length** (never slurped whole); cancellation merges with a 3-second wall clock. - **The traversal is layered** (fixed in 0.1.3): levels go **bottom-up** (the target's own directory → … → the project root) and each level is walked **breadth-first** (that level's own files before descending). It used to be one flat breadth-first pass from the root, which in a big repository spent the budget *before* the most useful files - `apps/a`, `apps/b`, … all came first, so the target's deep directory and its sibling `test/` layer were never reached. The traversal therefore always truncated, the credential was never granted, and the preflight did nothing in exactly the repositories that need it most. - **The credential criterion**: `the traversal was not truncated` **or** `references were found` (`refsCreditable`). The second clause is deliberate: the gate accepts the model's own **correctly scoped** search as a credential, and that search is **not exhaustive either** - demanding exhaustiveness from this scan would be stricter than the gate's own standard. But "**zero hits + truncated**" still grants **no** credential: every false negative lives there (a half "no referencers" lets the model delete a file that still has them, which is worse than giving no evidence at all - the "zero hits within the scanned range" wording exists for precisely that case). - One branch asks for confirmation instead of declaring danger (rule key `nestedShellUnconfirmed`): it hits when the `-c` body of a nested shell cannot be extracted reliably (unbalanced quotes) or the nesting goes past the drill-down limit (16 levels for `-c`/`eval` bodies, 16 for `$( )` substitutions). - The text sent back says "paste this to the user and run it only after they explicitly confirm", because it is neither "confirmed dangerous" nor "confirmed safe". #### What each permission preset blocks The host presets bundle a sandbox mode with an approval policy, and the official sandbox governs **file effects only** (network and process visibility are outside its vocabulary; even the tightest mode merely refuses writes and allows every read). This package covers those two faces - and yields the write-side rules whenever the sandbox genuinely governs them. | Rule family | Read-only | Workspace write | Full access | Auto review | |---|---|---|---|---| | `noVerify` (git hook bypass) | deny | deny | allow | allow | | `rmrf` (encloses a writable root / home / root) | allow¹ | deny | allow | **deny** | | `rmrf` (the sandbox fully covers this target) | allow | allow | allow | allow | | `pipeShell` (download-and-execute) | allow | **deny** | allow | **deny** | | `devServer` (long-running server) | allow² | allow² | allow² | allow² | | `nestedShellUnconfirmed` (cannot tell) | ask | allow | allow | allow | | git destruction family (7 keys) | ask | ask | allow | allow | | infrastructure family (5 keys) | ask | ask | allow | allow | ¹ Read-only refuses every write, so this whole family goes to the host (it returns the official denial marker plus the `sandbox_permissions` escalation path). ² The host's cooperative timeout and `promoteOnTimeout` already govern long-running commands, so this rule is no longer a safety property and goes to the host entirely. Two readings: - **Full access means zero guardrails - but only in the "cannot ask" arm.** The shipped preset pins this mode to `approval: never` (asking impossible), so choosing it means "do not block, do not ask": the whole preset allows, hits only increment the settings-card stats (one cell per rule key and per preset) and the model sees no change. `danger-full-access + ask` (a custom combination, or the default when the preset service is absent) **can still ask**, and that arm reuses the workspace-write column - silently allowing while the sandbox restricts nothing is the exact opposite direction from "collapse to deny only when asking is impossible". - **Auto review keeps exactly two deterministic hard stops** (`rmrf` and `pipeShell`). The reviewer is an LLM, its allow is not the user's approval, and this preset's sandbox restricts nothing; everything else goes to the reviewer so the same action is never asked about twice. ### Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @jayyuen66/dsh-danger-guard ``` - The packages are on the public npm registry, so installation needs no credentials. - No registry line is needed any more: the public npm registry is the default. To remove: `dsh plugin --profile web remove @jayyuen66/dsh-danger-guard`. - Requires host `dsh >= 0.2.1-rc.2`: the source of truth is the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` entry under `peerDependencies`, and the host **enforces** it - `evaluatePluginCompatibility` (`dsh-app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts`, called from `plugin-manager/src/operations.ts:344` and `:479`, byte-identical between alpha.1 and alpha.2) matches every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer against the running version with `includePrerelease: true` and refuses the install on a mismatch, pointing at the explicit risk grant `dsh plugin --profile

allow-version @ --dsh-version --accept-risk`. Because the `dsh-*` peers are pinned to one exact version (see the version-shape gates in `test/publish-manifest.test.ts`), a host **newer** than this floor mismatches the same way and needs that same grant: this plugin's types and nominal brands are coupled to the host ABI, and silently following it upward is exactly how a second copy of the host type surface ends up loaded. Measured against host `0.2.1-rc.2`: installing a probe whose peer says `@deepseek-ai/dsh: 0.1.0` comes back as `dsh: installation rejected: ... is incompatible with dsh 0.2.1-rc.2`, with `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `node_modules` rolled back. `engines.dsh` carries the same value but nothing reads it. - **Requires Node.js `>= 22.12`.** This is an ESM-only package: use `import { apply } from "@jayyuen66/dsh-danger-guard"` or `require("@jayyuen66/dsh-danger-guard")`. That Node floor is what makes `require()` of an ESM entry work at all, which is why `engines.node` is declared; on anything older the `require` form fails. - The published artifact holds `host.js` / `settings.js` / `client.js` / `cordis.patch.yml`, the `types/` declaration tree, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, both READMEs, `LICENSE` and `icon.svg`. Build artifacts are not committed; `prepack` rebuilds them, so what ships is always what the current source produces. - **TypeScript declarations ship** (`types/host.d.ts`, `types/settings-host.d.ts`, plus the `lib/` declarations they reference). The root and the `./settings` subpath each carry a `types` condition, so `tsc` resolves them under `node16`/`bundler`. `./client` and `./cordis.patch.yml` deliberately have none: the first is a browser UMD shell (`window is not defined` if you import it in Node), the second is read by the host loader as a file. - Four packages are imported for value at runtime: `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (the host's fork, `3.18.5-alpha.1`), `@jayyuen66/dsh-plugin-shared` (`^0.1.4`), `@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand` (`0.2.1-rc.2`) and `zod` (`^4.6.5`). `dependencies` carries only the last two: the two `@deepseek-ai/*` entries are **required peers** — they sit in `peerDependencies` and, so this repository's own typecheck/build/tests keep resolving them, in `devDependencies`. - The `shared` bump is not a version number for its own sake. `0.1.3` moved those host packages out of its own `dependencies` and into `peerDependencies`, which is what stops installing this plugin from materializing a second copy of the host type surface inside the profile; `0.1.4` then re-pins those peers to the same `0.2.1-rc.2` this package uses, so nothing downstream asks for `alpha.1` anymore. Measured against host `0.2.1-rc.2`: `dsh plugin --profile web add ` installs 3 packages, leaves **no** `@deepseek-ai/` directory under the profile's `node_modules`, and `pnpm peers check` in that profile now lists every host package at `0.2.1-rc.2` (`dsh-brand`, `dsh-output-retention`) or the host's own cordis-fork pins - whereas `@jayyuen66/dsh-danger-guard@0.1.1` from the registry writes `cosmokit`, `dsh-brand` and `schemastery` into the profile next to the copies the running host already loaded. - `zod` is imported for value by `lib/tool-ledger.ts` (its `stateSchema`), `@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand` by `host.ts` (`brandNumber`), `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` by `lib/settings-schema.ts` (`import Schema from …`), which is why that bare specifier lands in both `host.js` and `settings.js`. - **No `@deepseek-ai/*` under `dependencies` — this is not a style preference;** `test/publish-manifest.test.ts` enforces it. Consumers install this plugin into a profile whose pnpm settings are `nodeLinker: hoisted` with `autoInstallPeers: false`, so any host package listed under `dependencies` is written into that profile as a **real directory**, coexisting with the copy the running host already loaded. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` keys its `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER` with a plain `Symbol` (not `Symbol.for`), so symbol identity is per module instance: the host's `dsh-agent-loop` reads `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` on a `ToolRuntime` mounted from the profile copy, gets `undefined`, and **every native tool call throws** `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` — the whole profile loses its tools, while build, typecheck and coverage gates stay green right up to that. Peers are never installed into the profile and devDependencies belong to this repository only, so neither can materialize a second copy. - The brand package is the exception to "every `@deepseek-ai/*` **service surface** is type-only": phantom brands have no type-only way to be built, so this family of value imports must stay **externalized** — the externalization list in `build-host.mjs` reads `dependencies` ∪ `peerDependencies`, and a `devDependencies`-only entry lets rolldown inline the official function body into the artifact, giving each package its own copy of the official constructor. A required peer satisfies both halves: the specifier stays external in the artifact, and the consumer's profile installs nothing. - `test/build-host.test.ts` pins both bare specifiers in `host.js` (`from "zod"`, `from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand"`) together with the absence of the official function bodies; the settings half never imports brand, and the same test asserts the reverse for `settings.js`. This is also why the artifacts are **not** minified: minification removes the bare-specifier strings, which would turn those assertions permanently green and let an inlined copy ship undetected. - MIT, source at git+https://github.com/JayYuen666/dsh-danger-guard.git. - The fact gate and the command rules are **ported in mechanism** from ECC (MIT, © Affaan Mustafa) — [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) records the upstream files, what differs in this package, and the item-by-item comparison showing no upstream code, word list or message text was copied. ### Shared version floor If your profile pins `@jayyuen66/dsh-plugin-shared` with a pnpm `overrides` entry, that pin must be at least the `@jayyuen66/dsh-plugin-shared` version this package declares. A lower pin installs a copy without the names this package imports at runtime, and the host then reports `N entries did not activate` with `does not provide an export named ...` when it boots -- the package installs fine and never loads, and no per-repo CI run can see it. ### Enabling it in dsh - Bundle form: `dsh.bundle.patch` in package.json points at `cordis.patch.yml`, and `dsh plugin add/remove` maintains the assembly layer. - The package carries **two** lines (bulkhead): `- id: danger-guard` (guard half, **no Config**, name points at the package root) and `- id: danger-guard-settings` (settings half, strict schema, name points at the `./settings` subpath export). - Only the first line brings up the card: the host scans `dsh.client` on **bare package-name** entries only (`exactPackageSpecifier` in `dsh-client-modules` returns undefined for a subpath), so the settings line's subpath name is deliberate. - The card loads on the web platform only (`dsh.client = { platform: "web", immediately: true }`), as "danger-guard danger block" in the settings plugin list. - Deployment defaults sit on the **settings row's** `config:` (`- id: danger-guard-settings`): precedence is settings card runtime value > row config > `BUILTIN_BASE`. - An explicit `undefined` in the row does not override the base, and illegal numbers (e.g. `maxDenies: 0`) fall back to the built-in default - 0 would switch the fact gate off entirely. - Defaults belong on the `- id: danger-guard-settings` row: the guard half takes no `config` argument at all (`apply(ctx)` in `host.ts`), so a `config:` on the `- id: danger-guard` row is inert by design. - Failures go the conservative way: the settings surface lives on its own entry, `danger-guard-settings`, and only that entry carries the strict schema. - An out-of-range value (`maxDenies: 0`, `strictMode: "yes"`) fails **that** entry alone; the guard entry has no `Config`, so when it cannot read the value surface it falls back to `BUILTIN_BASE` and warns once - one mistyped line of configuration cannot switch the gate off. - `apply` only throws when the **settings surface** is missing: no `effect`, or a `settings` service without `describe`, raises `required services (settings/effect) missing` and that entry goes FAILED (the host-side service probe checks exactly those two). - ⚠ A missing `tools` service does **not** throw: `svc.tools?.guard(...)` yields no registration handle and the mount is skipped (optional chain plus the `dispose === undefined` branch in `host.ts`, pinned by `test/host.test.ts`); `apply` has no guard for it. - That is still not a silent pass in a real deployment: `tools` is in `inject`, so cordis never activates the entry without it, and the startup diagnostic prints `warning: N entry did not activate` with `pending (waiting for service: tools)`. What you see is "no gate mounted, and the host says so". ### Settings (namespace `danger-guard-settings` = the settings entry id; defaults are `BUILTIN_BASE` in lib/settings-schema.ts) | Field | Type | Default | Purpose | | ---------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Master switch; `false` silences all three verdicts (lesson reports included) | | `factGateEnabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns off only the first-edit fact gate; danger commands and secret paths still block | | `preflightEnabled` | boolean | `true` | Pre-edit preflight (see "Preflight" below): the plugin gathers the missing evidence itself, so an edit never gets refused twice. Off only restores "refuse, then the model gathers evidence" — no criterion is dropped | | `judgeStats` | boolean | `true` | Samples each verdict's duration and input size: a rolling summary line every 200 verdicts, plus one `judge-cost` pass per verdict when lesson-loop is installed (face / ms / character count only). Off = no visibility, every verdict identical. The card's judgement-stats readout (see "Exports and card") is **independent** of it: the readout reads the in-process counters, this switch governs only what leaves the process | | `maxDenies` | natural, 1–5 | `2` | Consecutive non-converging denials per target before the quota releases it with a warning | | `strictMode` | boolean | `false` | `true` ignores the risk tiers and runs the full probe on the first edit of every code file | | `smallEditChars` | natural, >=1 (card 1–2000) | `200` | A write of at most this many chars without signature keywords is small: only read is required | | `bigEditChars` | natural, >=2 (card 2–100000) | `2000` | A write above this size is a rewrite and escalates to the full probe | | `extraTestDirs` | string[] | `[]` | Appends test-layer directory names (built-in `test/tests/__tests__/spec/specs`); append-only | | `extraDevServerWords` | string[] | `[]` | Appends long-running command heads (built-in `vite/webpack/next/nuxt/cargo-watch/watchexec`); append-only | | `extraDevRunArgs` | string[] | `[]` | Appends run script names (built-in `dev/watch/serve/start/start:dev`); append-only | | `extraSecretPatterns` | string[] | `[]` | Appends secret path regex fragments (one per line on the card; invalid ones skipped with a warning); append-only, no allowlist | | `refSearchTools` | string[] | `["grep","glob","zg_search"]` | Which search tools count as reference evidence; clearing it means none count. **The instructions shown to the model only name tools actually registered on this host** (probed via the official `ctx.tools.get`; if the probe is unavailable the list is passed through as is) | | `refSearchStrictTools` | string[] | `["zg_search"]` | The subset of the above judged by the strict "root + query/fts/vector relative path" criterion; a name listed only here gets no credential | ### How blocking and exemptions are decided | Shared mechanics of the four command rules | Content | | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Scope and splitting | Only tool names `bash` and `pwsh` are judged (a non-string `command` passes, no guessing); the command is split at `;`, `&&`, `\|\|`, `\|`, newline, `&`, `(`, `)`, backtick and each segment judged, with no splitting inside quotes. Splitting, word lexing, the structure view and the unclosed-quote check are **four projections of one POSIX state machine** (`lib/command-segments.ts`): the machine that judges quote closure and the machine that splits words must not be two different ones, or the same string gets opposite verdicts in different predicates | | Wrapper words, bin prefixes, quotes, continuations | None of these are escape hatches: wrapper words (`sudo env time nice stdbuf timeout taskset watch setsid doas pkexec noglob nohup exec command xargs parallel` and leading `VAR=x`), bin path prefixes (`/bin/rm` - and the wrapper itself is matched by basename, so `/usr/bin/sudo` is no escape either), quoting and backslash line continuations. A **quoted flag or quoted command word is a working spelling**, not an escape: measured on real git 2.54, `git commit "--no-verify"` skips the hook and commits, and `"rm" -rf ~`, `rm "-rf" ~`, `\git` all judge like the unquoted form. Since a per-tool option table can never be complete, a wrapper-led segment also **treats every following word position as a candidate command head** (`sudo -p xrm rm -rf /` is closed that way, verified against real sudo) | | Principle and its one exception | "When unsure, let it through" - with one exception: **an execution face you cannot see**. A nested `-c`/`eval` body that cannot be extracted reliably, nesting past the drill-down limit (one 16-level cap for `-c`/`eval` bodies, another for `$( )` substitutions - the first holds down "how many bodies get extracted", the second "levels x text re-scanned per level", since a length cap only bounds a single scan), a segment head that is a non-shell interpreter running a code string (`python3 -c`, `node -e`, `perl -e`, `ruby -e`, `php -r`, `osascript -c`… - what that language does is invisible at the command-lexer level), or a command past the judgable length limit all become `nestedShellUnconfirmed`; the way out is explicit user confirmation, or rewriting it as one plain, quote-balanced layer | | The four command rules and secret path edits | Blocks | Passes / way out | | -------------------------------------------- | evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-uxexo

[![Listed on DSH Directory](https://dsh.directory/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh.directory/plugins/jiangnanquan/dsh-uxexo)

**中文** | [English](README_EN.md)

DeepSeek Harness(DSH)Web 界面增强插件,由**江南泉**个人开发并免费开源。它在设置面板里提供独立一页「界面增强」,所有开关即时生效;包含 25 套终端美学配色、文字墨色、中文优先字体、紧凑布局、折叠胶囊,以及账户余额 / 用量与官方峰谷提醒。

![dsh-uxexo](screenshot.png)

## 能力

| 类别 | 内容 |
|------|------|
| 设置页 | 设置面板左侧独立一页「界面增强」:每项功能即时生效,改完不用重启 |
| 配色主题 | 25 套,取自江南泉《终端美学》三部曲:经典 CRT、纸面浅色、现代双生、AI 品牌;深色主题自动带 `color-scheme: dark` |
| 文字墨色 | 深墨(默认, 推荐)/ 跟随配色 / 纯黑;只改文字 token,浅色主题生效 |
| 字体 | 中文优先的 0.5 窄体等宽方案(更纱黑体 Mono/Term、Noto Mono CJK、Maple Mono…);字重默认半粗(推荐) |
| 布局 | 加宽消息列、收紧对话间距、对齐新对话输入卡片与 / @ 候选菜单、禁用橡皮筋滚动 |
| 折叠胶囊 | 0.1.x:思考块聚合为 `Think ×N`、工具调用聚合为 `A → B → C` 链路胶囊。0.2.0:官方过程分组接管显隐,插件把胶囊摘要挂到「已完成,用时 X」行下方,点击联动官方展开/收起;长链路按可用宽度换行 |
| 账户用量 | 输入框下方显示官方账户余额、本轮 token 成本与近 30 天用量图表;官方 API/账号时附「峰 / 谷」计费徽标,点击查看官方峰谷规则与下一次切换 |
| 强调色 | 发送/停止按钮与侧栏「新会话」统一使用主题第三个锚点色(accent);按钮反白字按每套主题的 on-accent 自动取黑/白 |

长工具链会跟随消息列宽度自动重新分行,每个视觉行保持独立、完整的胶囊轮廓:

![工具链换行后每行独立胶囊](docs/images/tool-chain-multiline-capsules.png)

设置页顶部还有一枚 GitHub Star 入口:如果 dsh-uxexo 帮到了你,欢迎去仓库点个 Star。

## 配色主题:江南泉《终端美学》三部曲 25 套

设置页「外观 → 配色主题」用一个下拉切换,按来源分组——全部取自江南泉的《终端美学》三部曲。
命名统一为 **English · 中文**:英文保留官方原名与变体名(`Rosé` 的重音也保留),中文只做简短意译,
长名字在下拉里也不会断行。

| 分组 | 主题 |
|------|------|
| 官方 | Official · 官方配色 |
| 经典 CRT(第一部) | P1 Green Phosphor · 绿磷光、P3 Amber Phosphor · 琥珀光、Matrix Rain · 代码雨、Cyberpunk 2077 · 夜之城、Radar Red · 雷达血红、Weyland Corp · 维兰重工、NERV MAGI · 三贤者 |
| 纸面浅色(第二部) | P4 White · 纸白、Everforest Light · 绿色森林、Parchment Classic · 羊皮纸、Solarized Light · 暖羊皮纸、Catppuccin Latte · 拿铁 |
| 现代(第三部) | Tokyo Night · 东京夜、Tokyo Night Day · 东京白昼、Kanagawa Wave · 神奈川·浪、Kanagawa Lotus · 神奈川·莲、Rosé Pine · 玫瑰松木、Rosé Pine Dawn · 玫瑰晨光、Catppuccin Mocha · 摩卡 |
| AI 品牌(第三部) | Claude Light · 书斋浅、Claude Dark · 书斋深、OpenAI Light · 涌现浅、OpenAI Dark · 涌现深、Gemini Light · 极光浅、Gemini Dark · 极光深 |

每套主题只声明**底色、正文、强调、状态色**四个锚点,其余 surface / border / hover / 反白字
由同一套推导规则生成,所以 25 套的层级关系一致,加新配色只需补一行数据。深色主题会自动
设置 `color-scheme: dark`,并使用配色自带的墨色;「文字墨色」只对浅色主题生效。

0.2.x 起官方公共菜单改用玻璃材质 `--dsw-menu-surface-fill`(浅色 58% / 深色 45% + 背景模糊,
macOS 另铺一层 `bg-base` 做不透明 backing)。本层按「合成后等于本主题 layer-1」反解玻璃填充,
并接管配套的吸顶分组标题 `--dsw-alias-menu-group-header-fill`(94%)、菜单图标
`--dsw-alias-menu-icon` 与暗档文字 `--dsw-alias-label-primary-dimmed`;菜单面内的选中/悬停
底色则重绑到 layer-1 上(全局 hover 是 base + accent,直接落在 layer-1 上几乎同色)。
不接管这几个 token 时,深色主题会继承官方浅色玻璃,菜单就成了深色页面上的一块浅色板。

同一轮把官方 0.2.x 主题表新增的其余 token 也全部接管(共 49 个:文档预览、文件 diff、
状态色阶、遮罩、tooltip / toast、反白与 bluish 标签、轨迹品牌色等)。规则与官方同构:
状态三级色 = 底色混状态色,文件 diff 底/行号区 = 更淡的同色混合,反白标签取与主文字
对立的对比色,`link` 与深潜标签以 `accent` 为底做可读性兜底(不足 AA 时向黑/白收),
菜单材质与吸顶标题保持官方 58% / 45% / 94% 的透明度语义。Solarized 手写块保持官方
fallback(浅色主题下官方浅色值本就合规),观感不动。

主题的第三个锚点 `accent` 会统一应用到**发送/停止按钮**与侧栏**「新会话」**:前者总是跟随
accent;后者默认跟随,可在「外观 → 新会话按钮弱化」里改成只比侧栏底色略深的弱化样式。

所有非 Solarized 主题的正文在 `bg` 与 `layer-1` 上都过 WCAG AA(4.5:1);Solarized 保留
原手写 token 的观感,由墨色档位兜底。东京白昼的正文在原始 `#3760BF` 上对 layer-1 只有
4.08:1,已压深 4% 到 `#2F55B5`(4.74:1)。

## 文字墨色:深墨(默认)/ 跟随配色 / 纯黑

Solarized 的默认正文色是 base01 `#586e75`(青灰),在暖黄底上会显得「蒙了一层灰」:
基础面 `#fdf6e3` 上 4.99:1,落到 layer-1 `#eee8d5` 只剩 4.39:1(低于 WCAG AA 的 4.5)。
这一项只改文字 token,不动背景与品牌色,三档:

| 档位 | 效果 |
|------|------|
| 深墨(默认, 推荐) | 暖青黑 `#002b36`,比浅色主题的默认墨色深一档;Solarized 上对 layer-1 从 4.39:1 提到 12.2:1 |
| 跟随配色 | 继承配色自己的墨色(Solarized 即上面的青灰),最贴近原设计 |
| 纯黑 | `#000000`,19.5:1,强光/低视力更清楚,但大段正文会偏硬 |

只作用于浅色:深色配色各自定义 ink,不在这里强行覆盖;按钮主色上的反白字
(`--dsw-alias-label-primary-foreground`)也不受影响。

## 字体:中文优先 / 0.5 窄体西文

依据《终端排版哲学:中文优先与 0.5 窄体等宽工程实战》(本机实测数据见下表):

**汉字是不可妥协的 1.0 正方**。要让「2 个西文字符 = 1 个汉字」严格成立,西文就必须收窄到 **0.5**;
而以西文为基准的编程字体(Menlo、JetBrains Mono、Fira Code、Maple Mono……)西文宽 0.6~0.67,
汉字容器会被撑到 1.2 —— 汉字要么被横向拉宽 20%(矮胖、字怀塌陷),要么两边留白(中文词句涣散)。

本机 CoreText 实测(unitsPerEm=1000,字形前沿宽度):

| 字族 | 西文 `a` | 汉字 `中` | 比值 | `—` | `→` | `★` |
|------|---------|----------|------|-----|-----|-----|
| **Sarasa Mono SC** | 0.500 | 1.000 | **2.000** | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| **Sarasa Term SC** | 0.500 | 1.000 | **2.000** | 0.500 | 0.500 | 0.500 |
| Noto Sans Mono CJK SC | 0.500 | 1.000 | **2.000** | 0.894 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| Sarasa Gothic / UI SC | 0.562 | 1.000 | 1.78 | 1.000 | 0.954 | 1.045 |
| Maple Mono NF CN | 0.600 | **1.200** | 2.000 | 0.600 | 0.600 | — |
| Maple Mono(非 CN) | 0.600 | 无字形 | — | 0.600 | 0.600 | — |

更纱黑体的架构正是这一哲学的产物:西文用 Iosevka(严格 0.5),汉字用思源黑体(1.0),
基线、x 高度、字重曲线都被逐像素对齐过。**Mono 与 Term 的唯一差别是东亚歧义字符**
(—……→★■●):Mono 保持全角(适合读 Markdown、中文标点),Term 压成半角(适合密集网格、
跳格最稳)。Maple Mono NF CN 的汉字被拉到 1.2,正是文章里要避开的那一类。

设置页里可选:

| 方案 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| 自动(推荐) | 按可用性依次尝试:更纱黑体 Mono → Term → Noto Mono CJK → Maple Mono;一款都没装就落回官方字体栈 |
| Sarasa Mono SC | 0.5 窄体 + 全角歧义字符 |
| Sarasa Term SC | 0.5 窄体 + 半角歧义字符 |
| Noto Mono CJK | Noto Sans Mono CJK SC,同为 0.5/1.0 |
| Maple Mono | 旧观感(西文 0.6 / 汉字 1.2),保留兼容 |
| 关闭 | 完全不动官方字体栈 |

本机装了哪几款会实时探测并标在页面上(未装的方案置灰,装了字体回来即可,无需重启)。
**字重**另有「标准 / 半粗」两档,默认落在**半粗(推荐)**——把正文抬到 600、强调抬到 700,
用字族自带的矢量 SemiBold(文章 §3.2 的甜点位);两种模式都同时关掉 `font-synthesis`,
即文章 §3.1 的「不用算法级伪粗」——伪粗是光栅化阶段向外描边,会挤占字怀、让笔画黏连。

页面底部还带一块**对齐自检块**(文章 §5 的校验文本,已按 2:1 校齐列宽):
第 1 行 40 个半角字符必须与第 2 行 20 个汉字等宽,方框必须是矩形,一眼就能看出方案对不对。

选型依据、实测数据、加新字族的步骤见 [docs/字体方案-中文优先与0.5窄体.md](docs/字体方案-中文优先与0.5窄体.md)。

## 峰谷提醒(官方 API / 官方账号)

输入框下方那行「本轮 ¥x」后面会多一枚「峰 / 谷」徽标,只在**最近一次请求真实使用的
provider** 是 `deepseek-official` 或 `deepseek-account` 时出现:

| 状态 | 时段(北京时间) | 显示 |
|------|---------------|------|
| 峰 | 周一至周五(不含法定节假日)09:00–12:00、14:00–18:00 | 琥珀色「峰」,提示按峰时价计费 |
| 谷 | 其余时段,含**周末与法定节假日全天** | 绿色「谷」,提示空闲半价 |

判定口径按 DeepSeek 官方 2026-08-23 的调价公告与 2026-09-19 的节假日说明:

- 高峰仅落在**工作日**(周一至周五,不含中国法定节假日)的 9:00–12:00、14:00–18:00;
- 周六、周日全天按空闲价,调休上班的周末也算周末;
- 中国法定节假日全天按空闲价;空闲价为高峰价的一半。

### 节假日日历每年自动获取

放假安排每年由国务院办公厅发布,插件**不需要每年补表**:

- host 半按需拉取当年与次年的机读日历(来源:[holiday-cn](https://github.com/NateScarlet/holiday-cn),
  按国办通知维护,JSON 里保留原通知链接),解析出 `isOffDay` 的日期并缓存;
- 缓存位置 `~/.dsh/dsh-uxexo/calendar-<年份>.json`;往年日历视为不可变,当年/次年每 7 天刷新,
  客户端每 6 小时向 host 同步一次;
- 次年安排未发布时(数据源返回空列表)不会误判为「没有节假日」,仍按工作日口径兜底,发布后自动采纳;
- 断网时用内置的 2026 表兜底,不影响徽标与成本统计;
- 所以跨年是自动的:2027 年安排一发布,徽标与成本口径会自己切换,无需改代码。

**点击徽标**会弹出官方规则浮层:当前状态与原因(周末 / 法定节假日 / 工作日非高峰)、
下一次切换的具体时间与倒计时、官方定义与出处链接。悬停徽标同样能看到倒计时;「发送」与
「选择模型」两个按钮的 `title` 也会同步带上「官方 API 峰时计费 / 空闲半价」。状态每 30 秒
重算,跨过 12:00 / 18:00 或周末/节假日边界不用等下一次用量轮询。

判据是会话日志里的 `request/header.config.provider`,不是「余额能查」——余额走
API Key,用户完全可能刚切到 scnet / opencode2dsh,这时不显示峰谷,避免给出错误的计价提示。

## 设置(即时开关)

打开 **设置 → 界面增强**,这一页就是本插件的全部开关:

| 开关 | 关掉之后 |
|------|----------|
| 启用 dsh-uxexo 界面增强 | 总开关。整层增强立刻撤下、回到官方外观;各分项的选择保留,再打开时按原样回来 |
| 配色主题 | 下拉里选「Official · 官方配色」即回到官方主题;默认 Solarized;25 套主题与命名见上节 |
| 新会话按钮弱化 | 默认关闭(「新会话」跟随主题强调色);打开后左上角「新会话」只比侧栏底色略深一点,回到克制的弱化观感 |
| 字体方案 / 字重 | 回官方字体栈与官方字重;方案选「关闭」等价于只关字体层;默认半粗(推荐) |
| 文字墨色 | 三档单选:**深墨**(默认, 推荐)、**跟随配色**、**纯黑**;只影响浅色文字,不动背景与品牌色 |
| 紧凑布局微调 | 消息列宽、间距、输入卡片对齐都回官方几何 |
| 折叠胶囊 | 思考/工具调用恢复成官方逐条展开的样子,注入的胶囊节点同时被收回 |
| 账户余额与用量 | 输入框下方那行余额、本轮成本、峰谷徽标与图表消失,也不再轮询余额接口 |

**全部即时生效,不需要重启**:开关写在 `<html>` 的 `data-dsh-ux-*` 属性上(CSS 闸门,改属性立刻改变行为),
同时存进一枚 cookie,让宿主半在首帧渲染前就把状态恢复好(否则会先按官方配色画一帧再跳)。

唯一需要重启的情况是**插件本体更新**:客户端半随页面刷新/热重载换新,宿主半(几个 `/enh/*` 接口、
首帧注入脚本)由 dsh 进程在启动时加载,换不了。设置页顶部会比对两半的构建号,一旦对不上就直接写明
「重启 DeepSeek Harness 后生效」,并提供「重新检测」。这也是 `GET /enh/ping` 的用途。

## 安装

前置:已按 DSH 的 profile 机制运行(`dsh web`)。

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:jiangnanquan/dsh-uxexo#main
```

本包声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch` 与 `dsh.client`,`dsh plugin add` 会自动把它加入 profile 的 bundles,
**重启 dsh 后即生效**,无需手改任何配置。重复执行该命令是安全的(幂等);升级用
`dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-uxexo`。

> **官方桌面版不使用这条命令**:`desktop` profile 由 Electron 应用独占,
> `dsh plugin --profile desktop …` 会被直接拒绝。桌面版装法见
> [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)。

## 交给你的 AI

不想手动敲命令?把下面这段话粘贴给任意 AI agent(Claude Code、dsh、Gemini CLI……),让它读 INSTALL.md 并完成安装与自检:

> 请按照 https://github.com/jiangnanquan/dsh-uxexo/blob/main/INSTALL.md 里的步骤,在我的机器上安装并验证 dsh-uxexo 插件(profile 用 web),然后运行文档里的健康检查并告诉我结果。如果任何一步失败,按文档的回滚步骤恢复原状并说明原因。

## 依赖与前提

- **字体**:推荐安装**更纱黑体**(Sarasa Gothic 的 `Sarasa-SuperTTC`,或 `Sarasa Term/Mono SC` 单独字重)——
  它是唯一同时满足「西文 0.5 窄体 + 汉字 1.0 正方」且中西文字重曲线对齐过的免费字族。
  没有更纱时可用 [Noto Sans Mono CJK SC](https://github.com/notofonts/noto-cjk)(同为 0.5/1.0,但只有 Regular/Bold),
  或继续用 [Maple Mono](https://github.com/subframe7536/maple-font)(西文 0.6、汉字 1.2)。
  一款都没装时字体层自动落回官方字体栈,不影响其余功能。
- **余额 / 本轮成本 / 用量图表 / 峰谷提醒**:调用 DeepSeek 官方接口,需要当前 DSH 已配置
  `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 凭据;未配置时这些信息显示为查询失败/不可用,不影响其余功能。
- 计价表按官方峰谷价硬编码在 `lib/index.js` 的 `pricingFor` / `PRICE_TABLES`:高峰仅工作日
  9:00–12:00、14:00–18:00,周末与法定节假日全天空闲价(高峰价一半);历史成本按 2026-08-17
  (启用峰谷)、2026-08-23(周末全谷)、2026-09-10 12:00(Flash 调价)三个时间点分段。
- 中国法定节假日不再硬编码年份:`lib/calendar.js` 每年自动拉取、解析并缓存放假安排,跨年无需
  手工补录;`lib/index.js` 与 `lib/client.js` 里各保留一份 2026 内置表,只作离线/首启动兜底
  (冒烟测试核对两份兜底一致)。官方**调价**仍属事件驱动,需要人工更新价格表。

## 卸载

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-uxexo
```

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # rdsh-agent-ui エージェントが会話の途中で提示したUIを**DSHのWebチャット内**に表示し、人間の選択を **同じセッションへ返す**プラグインです。見本の展示ではなく、往復を目的としています。 ## 動き 1. エージェントが surface を公開する（`DSH_HOME/agent-ui/surface.json`、または認証付き POST） 2. チャットの各ターン末尾にパネルが表示され、グラフ・表・選択肢・差分・テスト結果を描画する 3. 人間が選択すると、選択内容が**通常のユーザーメッセージ**として同じセッションへ送信される 4. 選択内容は `DSH_HOME/agent-ui/actions.jsonl` にも記録される（送信に失敗した場合の控え） ## 出る場所 パネルは**会話の流れの中**に表示されます。エージェントがメッセージに記述した目印（anchor_text）の ターンへ固定され、目印がない場合は最初に表示されたターンで一度だけ固定されます（sessionStorage）。 新しい surface を最初に表示したターンの末尾がその surface を 引き取り、その位置に固定されます（`surface.turn`）。会話が進んでも末尾へ移動せず、 履歴と一緒にスクロールします。次の版を出せば、その時点のターンが新しく引き取ります。 送信後は「送信済み」と表示され、**選び直す**で同じ surface に対しもう一度答えられます。 surface を削除すればパネルも消えます。 ## ファイル - `store.js`：surface の検証と保存、操作の追記（重複は request_id で排除） - `index.js`：認証付きHTTPルート（`/api/rdsh-agent-ui/surface`、`/api/rdsh-agent-ui/action`） - `client.js`：チャットのターン末尾に表示するパネル（React、DSHのテーマ変数を使用） - `test/*.test.mjs`：検証・保存・追記と surface 置換の単体テスト surface は保存ごとの専用ファイルに書き出してから置換します。並行して公開した場合は、最後に置換が完了した surface が残ります。 ## 安全側の約束 - 値はテキストまたはSVG要素としてのみ描画し、**エージェント由来のHTML/JSは実行しない** - 未知の種別や破損したデータは描画せず、理由を表示する - 数値が未取得のときは `null` を使い、**0で埋めない** - ルートはDSHのGUIセッションとHost/Origin検証を通過した要求だけを受け付ける - ボタンは選択・入力の返送のみを行い、実行権限は発行しない（要求型は記録のみ） ## 使い方（配布先プロファイルへ） ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/rustdsh/plugins/rdsh-agent-ui ``` ## 検証 ```sh node --test plugins/rdsh-agent-ui/test/*.test.mjs ``` # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rdsh.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rdsh) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [日本語](README.ja.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond process launch**: `rdsh --version` starts in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak RSS, versus ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh --version`. This is process launch only: a booted agent profile still runs upstream Node.js, so conversation startup and session memory match upstream. See [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. The design rationale behind this hybrid split is documented in [docs/PHILOSOPHY.md](docs/PHILOSOPHY.md). ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` Or install the crate from crates.io (needs Rust 1.85+): ```sh cargo install rdsh ``` `cargo install` builds from source and installs the same binary as the release archives. Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL users can also install the release [`.deb`/`.rpm`](#native-packages-deb--rpm) with `apt`/`dnf`. ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG or an Ollama API key for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Native Packages (`.deb` / `.rpm`) Linux x86_64 users on Debian/Ubuntu (and WSL) or Fedora/RHEL can install the same release binary with the OS package manager. Download the `.deb` or `.rpm` from the [latest release](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest) and install that file directly; no extra repository is configured. ```sh sudo apt install ./rdsh__amd64.deb # Debian, Ubuntu, WSL sudo dnf install ./rdsh--1.x86_64.rpm # Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux ``` `` is the release tag without its leading `v` (`0.6.0` for `v0.6.0`). The package installs `/usr/bin/rdsh` together with the licence and README, so `rdsh --version` works right after installation: no Rust toolchain, no `install.sh`. Like `rdsh-linux-x64.tar.gz`, both packages carry the glibc build, so the musl archive and `install.sh` stay the fallback for older distributions. ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ### Package Managers (Homebrew / Scoop / winget) Advanced users on macOS and Windows can let a package manager own the installed `rdsh` binary. The manifests in [packaging/](packaging/README.md) pin the exact release archives and their SHA-256 values; [docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md](docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md) lists the install commands and the update procedure. **macOS (Homebrew)** — installs the Apple Silicon or Intel archive: ```sh brew install --formula ./packaging/homebrew/rdsh.rb ``` **Windows (Scoop)**: ```powershell scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/main/packaging/scoop/rdsh.json ``` **Windows (winget)** — winget 1.6 or newer reads the three manifests directly; submitting them to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` stays a manual step: ```powershell winget install --manifest .\packaging\winget ``` These channels track one release at a time, so a new tag is not served until `python3 scripts/update-packaging-manifests.py --version vX.Y.Z` refreshes them. ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh plugins status # essential plugins a profile is still missing rdsh plugins install --profile web # attach them after an upgrade rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Plugin provisioning (`rdsh plugins`) The essential plugin tier (the upstream tools absent from `dsh-base` plus the bundled rdsh plugins) only lived in `plugins/install.sh`, and nothing runs that script by itself: upgrading the binary leaves the profile manifest untouched, so an install can miss every essential package without any signal. The same catalog is compiled into the binary, so a release install can see and close the gap without the checkout: ```sh rdsh plugins status # read-only state per package, plus the fix rdsh plugins status --profile web --json # schema 1 for scripts and dashboards rdsh plugins install # attach what the profile is missing rdsh plugins install --profile web # web/desktop defaults also add the starter set rdsh plugins install --recommended=none # the essential tier only rdsh plugins install --no-bundled # no checkout: the upstream tools only rdsh plugins install --plugins-dir # or export RDSH_PLUGINS_DIR ``` Packages go through `dsh plugin --profile add ` (`RDSH_DSH_BIN` overrides the CLI), exactly as the checkout installer does. Bundled plugins are resolved from the checkout, and an absent checkout is reported instead of being skipped quietly. `rdsh doctor` prints the same gap for every initialized profile, and `--profile desktop` forwards to `rdsh desktop install`. See [plugins/recommended.md](plugins/recommended.md) for the tiers and the ids. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features and the privacy-sensitive switches (`discord`, `telemetry`) stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast, telemetry-free dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | SearXNG by default; `--provider ollama` uses `OLLAMA_API_KEY`; `--auto-start` starts the bundled local SearXNG compose service. See [Web search](docs/WEB-SEARCH.md). | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Command Code, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add commandcode --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash # key from COMMANDCODE_API_KEY rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact src/context.rs # direct/transitive dependents + affected tests ``` The extractor covers Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go and records imports, definitions, and static call sites per file. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are reused, so repeated runs stay fast. It is a static approximation: dynamic dispatch, indirect calls, macros, and generated code remain explicitly `unknown` and are reported as unresolved counts rather than guessed, and a missing index means "no information", never "no dependencies". When the index exists, `rdsh context build` and `rdsh context inject` also pull in the graph neighbours of the files their search matched, so a retrieved excerpt arrives with the files it actually depends on. Native execution overhead is ~1 ms per invocation. ## Low-end hosts Default profile: `RDSH_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, then `general.default_profile` in rdsh settings, then local `tui`, else a guided error. Set the saved default with `rdsh settings set general.default_profile web`; an explicit `--profile ` keeps its precedence. rdsh aims to remain useful on modest machines: older x86-64 CPUs, older Linux distributions, and hosts without Node.js installed. - **Faster Node startup.** When rdsh launches dsh, it sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to `~/.cache/rdsh-node-compile-cache`, letting Node reuse compiled code across launches (Node 22.1 or newer; older versions ignore it). An existing `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` value is preserved. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=0`, or use `--passthrough` / `RDSH_PASSTHROUGH=1`, to opt out. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=` to keep the cache at a fixed location instead of the default, for example on hosts where `$HOME` is volatile. - **Broad CPU support.** Prebuilt x86-64 binaries do not require AVX or BMI; the static musl build also runs on systems with older glibc. - **Session token estimates.** `sessions --tokens` reads a decompressed size from the zstd frame header when available. Most streaming frames need the `zstd -dc` fallback. Results are cached under `~/.cache/rdsh/sessions-tokens.json` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` takes precedence); set `RDSH_TOKENS_CACHE=0` to disable the cache. A `?` marks an estimate that could not be read, for example when the zstd CLI is unavailable. - **Bounded parallel work.** Search and session scans use at most eight worker threads. The zstd CLI fallback uses 8 to 32 parallel processes. - **Native commands without Node.** Commands such as `tokens`, `search`, and `sessions` keep working without Node. To delegate conversations, install `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or set `DSH_ORIG_BIN` (or `RDSH_ORIG_BIN`). - **Low-priority updates.** `sync-dsh.sh` updates dsh and rdsh, verifies archive bytes against that registry, and rolls back a failed update candidate. By default it uses the stable release selected by the reviewed repository digest registry; set `RDSH_SYNC_FROM_SOURCE=1` to build from `main` under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c3` when available. The systemd unit runs at low priority; adjust its `ExecStart` to your checkout. ## Web UI & Dashboard ### Lightweight Local Web UI (`rdsh serve`) A lightweight status and token estimation page running on localhost (default `:38080`, does not conflict with DSH `:3080`): ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # enable the server feature rdsh serve # launch (bound to localhost, protected with a one-time token) ``` ### Product language rdsh-owned CLI diagnostics and the native local page support English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese. Choose one run with `--language`, or persist it in `rdsh.json`; the default `auto` reads the first nonblank locale environment variable, falling back to English when it is absent or unsupported. ```sh rdsh --language ja settings show rdsh settings set general.language zh-CN ``` Precedence is `--language`, `RDSH_LANG`, `general.language`, then `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, and `LANG`. An explicitly invalid `general.language` stops the command without rewriting the settings file. Delegated `dsh` arguments, model output, JSON fields, files, and protocol identifiers are not translated. Interactive setup prompts and settings/policy validation use the selected language too. Authentication decisions and skipped-provider notes localize only the CLI presentation; their existing JSON strings remain unchanged, including malformed or oversized guard-input reasons. Native search continues to refuse unsupported non-Unix platforms before accessing the requested directory. `worker-scope validate` and `worker-scope policy` also localize their help and CLI diagnostics. These pure commands and their help ignore unrelated corrupt settings; ordinary commands and root help still report the settings error. Canonical JSON, policy codes and supplied paths stay unchanged. ### Protected delegated tools The opt-in agent tool sandbox supports Linux x86_64 with bubblewrap, prlimit, and unprivileged user namespaces. Its audited DSH/tool-runtime pairs are `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1`, and `0.2.1-alpha.3`, with matching versions in each pair. It verifies package metadata, runtime bytes and the loaded module, then limits in
