evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-colorlab **EN** · [中文](#中文) A colour theme plugin for the DeepSeek Harness chat UI. It ships Sublime Text's **Mariana** palette as its default preset, and adds a colour engine on top: 18 adjustable colour slots, 9 Markdown prose roles, saved presets, live WCAG contrast warnings and light/dark modes — all from a settings panel, persisted to your profile. ![Chat UI under dsh-colorlab](assets/screenshot-chat.png) > Process rows are colour-coded (green for tool calls, amber for summaries), > headings and inline code are tinted, and the surface sits on Mariana's > cool blue-grey rather than pure black. It does not patch `app.asar`, and it does not fork the host. It uses DSH's official theme extension point (`ctx.theme.overrideTokens`) and layers its tokens on top of whatever theme is active. --- ## Install ```sh dsh plugin add ruegg114514/dsh-colorlab ``` This installs from source, so DSH will ask you to approve the package's build step (`allowBuilds`) on first run. Restart DSH afterwards — the plugin is picked up by the loader at boot. ## Uninstall ```sh dsh plugin remove ruegg114514/dsh-colorlab ``` Or just turn **Enable** off in the plugin's settings panel: the theme reverts to the host default immediately, no restart needed, and your saved colours are kept. --- ## What it changes Mariana is the default colour scheme of Sublime Text 3.0 (2017) and Sublime Text 4. Its background is a cool blue-grey (`#343D46`) rather than pure black, and its foreground is a soft grey (`#D8DEE9`) rather than pure white — which is why it stays readable for long sessions on bright displays. | Area | Effect | |---|---| | Surfaces / cards / sidebar / menus | `#343D46` / `#2F3841` / `#23292E` | | Body / secondary / tertiary text | `#D8DEE9` / `#A7ADBA` / `#8792A2` | | Borders and dividers | low-opacity overlays of `#D8DEE9` | | Bubbles / input / code blocks | `#3B454F` / `#2E363F` | | Status colours | success `#99C794`, error `#EC5F67`, warning `#F9AE58` | | Code syntax highlighting | keywords `#C594C5`, strings `#99C794`, functions `#5FB3B3`, numbers `#F9AE58`, comments `#8792A2` | | Sidebar terminal | background and cursor follow the theme | ## The colour engine ### Settings panel Settings → **ColorLab**: | Option | What it does | |---|---| | **Enable** | Off reverts to the host palette immediately; your settings are kept | | **Apply to** | Dark appearance only (default) / both dark and light | | **Surface variant** | Standard `#343D46` / Deep `#252B32` (the early ST3 tmTheme) / Dim `#2B3336` | | **Accent** | Teal `#5FB3B3` / Orange `#F9AE58` / Blue `#6699CC` — affects business-state highlights only | | **Code palette** | Overrides Shiki's `--shiki-*` tokens used inside fenced code blocks | | **Prose highlight** | Adds colour hierarchy to Markdown body text (headings, bold, inline code, list markers, quote rules) | | **Prose brightness** | Original / Boosted (default) / Brighter — interpolates toward white without shifting hue | | **Prose preview** | Shows both states side by side, right under the toggle | | **Prose colours** | 9 independent slots: heading, bold, italic, inline code, list marker, quote text, quote rule, link, strikethrough | | **Process row highlight** | Colours process rows — tool rows one colour, summary rows another | | **File card colour** | Recolours the header band of "edited N files" cards and the whole card body of "delivered files" cards | | **Custom colours** | 18 slots (8 surfaces / 3 text / 7 syntax), each adjustable | | **Presets** | Save the current palette and load it back later, up to 12 | **LaTeX gets a dedicated highlighter.** Sublime's own `LaTeX.sublime-syntax` + `TeX.sublime-syntax` are ported wholesale and run through a small TextMate engine, then coloured with the rules from `Mariana.sublime-color-scheme` — so LaTeX matches Sublime character for character rather than approximately: the backslash is teal on its own, every brace is teal (including after user macros like `\zh{`), math builtins are purple while custom macros are blue, digits orange, `=` `+` `-` orange-red, identifiers white italic. See `docs/DESIGN.md` for why guessing at Shiki's tokens could never get there. Everything else keeps Shiki's tokens. Python built-ins (`print`, `len`, `open`) get Mariana's `var(blue)` (`#6699CC`) — the colour Sublime gives `support.function`. Shiki merges that scope with `entity.name.function` into a single token, so function *calls* match Sublime while function *definition names* are blue there too. Markdown gets Sublime's `markup.*` details: list markers in `var(green)`, blockquote text in `var(orange)`, and inline code on a tinted background. ### 18 custom colour slots | Group | Slots | |---|---| | Surfaces (8) | base, panel 1/2/3, overlay menu, sidebar, code block, bubble/input | | Text (3) | body, secondary, tertiary | | Syntax (7) | strings, functions/punctuation, links/calls, keywords, errors/constants, numbers/cursor, find highlight | Three ways to change a slot: click the swatch to open the system colour picker, type a hex value below it, or paste one in. **Resetting to default clears that override** — only the slots that actually differ from the default are written to your profile, so clicking around a bit does not pin all 18 down. **Live contrast warning**: when body text against the background drops below 4.5:1, the settings panel reports the measured ratio and suggests ≥ 7:1. The figure is computed as real WCAG contrast, not estimated. ### Presets Name it and press Save to store the current surface variant, accent and all custom slots. Each preset shows five swatches (surface / body / accent / keyword / string) so you can tell them apart at a glance. - Saving under an existing name overwrites it - 12 presets maximum — they live in your profile's YAML - Each carries a timestamp ("just now / N min ago / MM-DD HH:mm") - A preset matching your current palette is marked *in use* - **Resetting to defaults does not delete your presets** — they're your own work; reset only touches the live palette ### Three independent highlight toggles | Toggle | Scope | Mechanism | |---|---|---| | **Code palette** | Fenced code blocks only | Overrides `--shiki-*`, consumed by Shiki's inline `` styles | | **Prose highlight** | Markdown body text only | Injects a stylesheet targeting the host's markdown container | | **Process row highlight** | Process entries (write / edit / run command) only | Injects a stylesheet targeting `data-variant` rows | Turning one off does not affect the others. ### Prose brightness | Role | Original | Boosted (default) | Brighter | |---|---|---|---| | Heading | `#5FB3C3` 4.51:1 | `#7CC1C1` 5.39:1 | `#92CBCB` 6.11:1 | | Bold | `#F9AE58` 5.90:1 | `#FABD76` 6.63:1 | `#FBC88D` 7.23:1 | | Italic / quote | `#A7ADBA` 4.91:1 | `#B7BCC6` 5.80:1 | `#C3C7D0` 6.52:1 | | Inline code | `#99C794` 5.76:1 | `#ABD1A7` 6.52:1 | `#BAD9B6` 7.20:1 | | Link | `#80AAD5` 4.54:1 | `#97B9DD` 5.42:1 | `#A9C5E2` 6.19:1 | | Strikethrough | `#EC5F67` 3.36:1 | `#EF7C82` 4.14:1 | `#F29298` 4.91:1 | (Contrast measured against `#343D46`; darker surface variants score higher.) Only dark values are brightened — on the light appearance, interpolating toward white would *reduce* contrast. Code blocks and interface surfaces are never affected. ### Process row highlight Two colours, three targets. Summary and expanded content stay unchanged. | Target | Example | Default | |---|---|---| | Tool rows | write / edit / run command | Light green `#7EE787` | | Summary rows | ran a command, wrote files, analysing your request | Light amber `#FAC863` | | Turn summary | "Done, took 1m 20s" | Light amber `#FAC863` | 10 categories are selectable (grouped into summary rows and tool rows), 5 enabled by default. Both colours are independently adjustable. ### A status bar tells you what is actually happening At the top of the settings panel: - `channel override` — using the official extension point (normal) - `channel style` — fell back to the stylesheet channel (`ctx.theme` is unsupported in your build) - `channel none` — not active right now (switched off, or the appearance is light while the mode is dark-only) - `N tokens overridden`, `prose on/off`, `appearance dark/light`, `config connected / memory-only` > **The settings panel itself is currently in Chinese only.** The theme, the > preset names you type and everything else are language-independent. --- ## Known limitations - **Terminal ANSI 16 colours are not themed.** The host does not expose the xterm ANSI palette as design tokens and the plugin cannot reach the xterm instance, so only the terminal background, foreground, cursor and selection follow the theme. - **Prose highlighting depends on a host class-name prefix.** It matches `[class*="_markdown_"]`; the prefix comes from a host source filename and is stable across builds, but if the host **renames that CSS Module file** the rule stops matching — prose falls back to a single colour, without an error. - **Prose highlighting does not cover half-parsed Markdown.** During streaming the DOM structure is the same so rules still apply, but an unclosed `**` is not coloured while it is half-written. - **Corner radii and fonts are untouched.** Those belong to `ui-theme` and `dsh-font-probe`; this plugin only deals with colour. - **The light variant is not original Mariana.** Mariana itself is dark-only; the light values are same-hue lightened derivatives, there so that "apply to both" mode is not glaring. - **Custom colours only override the dark appearance.** There are no custom slots for light — deliberately, so colours picked against a dark background do not become invisible on a light one. - **Presets live as a YAML string in your profile.** The 12-preset cap keeps this bounded. If you hand-edit `cordis.patch.yml` and break the `presets` field, the plugin safely treats it as "no presets" — nothing throws and nothing is lost, the presets just stop showing until you fix the YAML. --- ## Design notes Implementation details — how the token override works, why the two channels exist, how host CSS specificity was matched rule by rule, how a write-race condition was found and fixed — are kept in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) (in Chinese). ## Tests ```sh npm test # 9 suites, offline npm run check # syntax check ``` ## License MIT. The Mariana palette originates from Sublime Text (`Sublime HQ Pty Ltd`, colour scheme by Dmitri Voronianski). This plugin is an independent reimplementation of the palette as DSH design tokens; it is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sublime HQ. --- # 中文 DeepSeek Harness 对话界面的配色主题插件。内置 Sublime Text 的 **Mariana** 配色作为默认预设，并在其上提供一套配色引擎：18 个可调颜色槽位、9 个正文 Markdown 角色色、配色方案存取、实时 WCAG 对比度提示、深浅两种模式 —— 全部在设置页里完成，配置持久化到 profile。 ![dsh-colorlab 下的对话界面](assets/screenshot-chat.png) > 过程条目按类型上色（工具行亮绿、汇总行亮黄），标题与行内代码着色， > 界面底色是 Mariana 的冷调蓝灰而不是纯黑。 它不改 `app.asar`，不补包，不 fork 宿主 —— 它走 DSH 官方的主题扩展点 （`ctx.theme.overrideTokens`），把令牌叠加在当前主题之上。 ## 安装 ```sh dsh plugin add ruegg114514/dsh-colorlab ``` 从源码安装，首次运行 DSH 会要求你授权该包的构建步骤（`allowBuilds`）。 装完重启 DSH —— loader 在启动时装载插件。 ## 卸载 ```sh dsh plugin remove ruegg114514/dsh-colorlab ``` 或者直接在设置页把「启用」关掉：立即回退到宿主默认配色，无需重启， 已保存的颜色不会丢。 ## 它改了什么 Mariana 是 Sublime Text 3.0（2017）起及 Sublime Text 4 的默认配色， 底色是冷调蓝灰 `#343D46` 而不是纯黑，前景是柔和的灰 `#D8DEE9` 而不是纯白 —— 长时间用下来没那么刺眼。 | 位置 | 效果 | |---|---| | 界面底色 / 卡片 / 侧栏 / 菜单 | `#343D46` / `#2F3841` / `#23292E` | | 正文 / 次级 / 三级文字 | `#D8DEE9` / `#A7ADBA` / `#8792A2` | | 边框与分隔线 | `#D8DEE9` 的低透明叠加 | | 气泡 / 输入 / 代码块 | `#3B454F` / `#2E363F` | | 状态色 | 成功 `#99C794`、错误 `#EC5F67`、警告 `#F9AE58` | | 代码语法高亮 | 关键字 `#C594C5`、字符串 `#99C794`、函数 `#5FB3B3`、数字 `#F9AE58`、注释 `#8792A2` | | 侧栏终端 | 底色与光标跟随主题 | ## 设置页 设置 → **ColorLab**： | 项 | 说明 | |---|---| | **启用** | 关掉立即回退宿主配色，设置保留 | | **套用范围** | 「仅深色外观」（默认）/「深浅都套用」 | | **背景变体** | 标准 `#343D46` / 深 `#252B32`（ST3 早期 tmTheme 那档）/ 中间 `#2B3336` | | **强调色** | 青 `#5FB3B3` / 橙 `#F9AE58` / 蓝 `#6699CC`，只影响业务态高亮 | | **代码高亮色板** | 覆盖代码块内 Shiki 的 `--shiki-*` 色板 | | **正文高亮** | 给 Markdown 正文加颜色层次（标题、加粗、行内代码、列表标记、引用竖线） | | **正文高亮亮度** | 原值 / 提亮（默认）/ 更亮。在原色基础上朝白插值，色相不动 | | **正文高亮预览** | 紧跟开关，直接展示开/关两种效果 | | **正文颜色** | 9 个独立槽位：标题、加粗、斜体、行内代码、列表标记、引用文字、引用竖线、链接、删除线 | | **过程行高亮** | 工具行一个颜色、汇总行另一个颜色 | | **文件卡片颜色** | 「已编辑 N 个文件」卡片的头部横带，以及「交付文件」卡片的整张底色 | | **自定义配色** | 18 个槽位（界面底色 8 / 文字 3 / 语法色 7），逐个调 | | **配色方案** | 把当前配色存成方案，随时载入，最多 12 套 | **LaTeX 走专门的高亮通道。** 直接把 Sublime 的 `LaTeX.sublime-syntax` 与 `TeX.sublime-syntax` **整份移植**过来，用一个小型 TextMate 引擎跑分词， 再套 `Mariana.sublime-color-scheme` 的规则上色 —— 所以 LaTeX 是**逐字符** 对齐 Sublime，而不是"近似"：反斜杠单独是青色、**所有**花括号都是青色 （`\zh{` 这类自定义宏后面也是）、数学内置命令紫而自定义宏蓝、数字橙、 `=` `+` `-` 橙红、标识符白斜体。为什么"猜 Shiki 的令牌"永远到不了这一步， 见 `docs/DESIGN.md`。 其余语言仍走 Shiki 的令牌。Python 内置函数（`print` `len` `open`）用 Mariana 的 `var(blue)`（`#6699CC`），与 Sublime 里 `support.function` 的颜色一致 —— Shiki 把 `support.function` 和 `entity.name.function` 合并成同一个令牌， 所以函数**调用**与 Sublime 一致，函数**定义名**则也是蓝色。 Markdown 会补上 Sublime 的 `markup.*` 细节：列表符号 `var(green)` 绿、 引用正文 `var(orange)` 橙、行内代码加淡色底。 ### 18 个自定义槽位 | 分组 | 槽位 | |---|---| | 界面底色（8） | 主背景、面板一/二/三层、浮层菜单、侧栏、代码块、气泡输入框 | | 文字（3） | 正文、次级文字、三级文字 | | 语法色（7） | 字符串、函数/标点、链接/调用、关键字、错误/常量、数字/光标、查找高亮 | 三种改法：点色块开系统取色面板、在下面直接输 hex、或粘贴色值。 **改回默认会自动清除该覆盖** —— 存进 profile 的只有「偏离默认」的那几项， 不会因为点过一圈就把 18 项全写进去。 **实时对比度提示**：正文与背景的对比度掉到 4.5:1 以下时，设置页会提示 「正文与背景对比度只有 x.xx:1（建议 ≥ 7:1），可能看不清」。这个数字是当场算的 WCAG 对比度，不是估算。 ### 配色方案 输入名字点「保存」，就把当前背景变体 + 强调色 + 全部自定义槽位存成一套。 列表里每套显示 5 个色点（背景/正文/强调/关键字/字符串）方便辨认。 - 同名保存 = 覆盖 - 上限 12 套（存在 profile 的 YAML 里） - 每套带保存时间：「刚刚 / N 分钟前 / MM-DD HH:mm」 - 与当前配色一致的方案显示「使用中」 - **「恢复默认配色」不会删掉已保存的方案** —— 那是你的资产 ### 三个高亮开关互不影响 | 开关 | 范围 | 机制 | |---|---|---| | **代码高亮色板** | 只有围栏代码块 | 覆盖 `--shiki-*` | | **正文高亮** | 只有 Markdown 正文 | 注入样式表，命中宿主 markdown 容器 | | **过程行高亮** | 只有过程条目 | 注入样式表，命中 `data-variant` 行 | ### 正文高亮亮度 | 角色 | 原值 | 提亮（默认） | 更亮 | |---|---|---|---| | 标题 | `#5FB3C3` 4.51:1 | `#7CC1C1` 5.39:1 | `#92CBCB` 6.11:1 | | 加粗 | `#F9AE58` 5.90:1 | `#FABD76` 6.63:1 | `#FBC88D` 7.23:1 | | 斜体 / 引用 | `#A7ADBA` 4.91:1 | `#B7BCC6` 5.80:1 | `#C3C7D0` 6.52:1 | | 行内代码 | `#99C794` 5.76:1 | `#ABD1A7` 6.52:1 | `#BAD9B6` 7.20:1 | | 链接 | `#80AAD5` 4.54:1 | `#97B9DD` 5.42:1 | `#A9C5E2` 6.19:1 | | 删除线 | `#EC5F67` 3.36:1 | `#EF7C82` 4.14:1 | `#F29298` 4.91:1 | （对比度在 `#343D46` 上算；背景越暗数字越高。） 只提亮深色值 —— 浅色外观是深字浅底，朝白插值会*降低*对比度。 代码块与界面底色完全不受影响。 ### 过程行高亮 两种颜色、三类目标，摘要与展开内容不变。 | 目标 | 例子 | 默认色 | |---|---|---| | 工具行 | 写入 / 编辑 / 运行命令 | 亮绿 `#7EE787` | | 汇总行 | 执行了命令、已写入文件 / 正在分析请求 | 亮黄 `#FAC863` | | 本轮汇总 | 已完成，用时 1 分 20 秒 | 亮黄 `#FAC863` | 10 个分类可勾选（分「汇总行」「工具行」两组），默认选中 5 项。 两个颜色各自独立可调。 ### 状态条 设置页顶部有一条状态条，把「到底有没有生效」摊开： - `主题通道 override` = 走官方扩展点（正常） - `主题通道 style` = 回退样式表通道（你的宿主版本不支持 `ctx.theme`） - `主题通道 none` = 当前没生效（开关关了，或浅色外观 + 仅深色模式） - `已覆盖 N 个令牌`、`正文高亮 开/关`、`外观 深色/浅色`、`配置 已连接/仅内存` > **设置页文案目前只有中文。** 主题本身、配色方案名称等与语言无关。 ## 已知限制 - **终端 ANSI 16 色不变。** 宿主没有把 xterm 的 ANSI 调色板暴露成设计令牌， 插件也拿不到 xterm 实例，只能保证底色 / 前景 / 光标 / 选区跟随主题。 - **正文高亮的选择器依赖宿主类名前缀。** 用 `[class*="_markdown_"]` 匹配， 前缀来自宿主源文件名，跨构建稳定；但宿主若**重命名那个 CSS Module 文件**， 规则会失配 —— 表现是正文退回同色，不会报错。 - **正文高亮不覆盖流式渲染中的半截 Markdown。** DOM 结构相同所以规则照常命中， 但未闭合的 `**` 在半截状态下不会被着色。 - **不改圆角与字体。** 那是 `ui-theme` 与 `dsh-font-probe` 的职责，本插件只碰颜色。 - **浅色变体不是 Mariana 原版。** Mariana 本身只有深色版，浅色值是同色相提亮的 自制品，只为「深浅都套用」模式下不刺眼。 - **自定义配色只覆盖深色。** 浅色没有对应槽位 —— 刻意的，避免把深色下挑的颜色 搬到浅色底上变成看不见的字。 - **配色方案存在 profile 的 YAML 字符串里。** 12 套上限是为了不让它无限膨胀。 如果手改 `cordis.patch.yml` 把 `presets` 写坏，插件会安全地当成「没有方案」， 不抛错也不丢数据，只是界面上看不到 —— 修好 YAML 即可恢复。 ## 实现说明 实现细节 —— 令牌覆盖的原理、两条通道的存在理由、宿主 CSS 特异性的逐条对齐、 一个写盘竞态的发现与修复 —— 放在 [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md)。 ## 校验 ```sh npm test # 11 个套件，离线可跑 npm run check # 语法检查 ``` ## 许可 MIT。Mariana 配色来自 Sublime Text（`Sublime HQ Pty Ltd`，配色方案作者 Dmitri Voronianski）。本插件是把该配色重新实现为 DSH 设计令牌的独立实现， 与 Sublime HQ 无隶属或背书关系。

decision.reason: Held for versioned DSH compatibility, package or companion artifact mapping. MIT and native modules exist, but no versioned DSH contract was found. The client capture is truncated and the host invokes subprocesses, so the full shipped client/helper surface is not established. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# 联合视图（dsh-union-view）

> 把好几个对话并排摊在屏幕上一起看；需要的话，还能把它们的历史焊成一个新对话接着聊。

## 先说这东西解决什么

假设你最近在干一件事，但聊得很散：

- 上周定需求，在 **A** 对话里
- 中间反复试错，在 **B** 对话里
- 最后结论和踩过的坑，记在 **C** 对话里

现在你想回顾整件事。怎么办？点开 A 翻一遍，退出来，点开 B 翻一遍，退出来，点开 C 翻一遍。翻到 C 的时候，A 里说的什么已经忘了一半。

**联合视图就是为这个做的**：勾上 A、B、C，三份对话同时摊在同一个屏幕上，左右对照着看。

```
┌ 对话   GAL视窗   [联合视图]   轨迹 ┐
│ 联合视图  3 个会话 · 1500 条消息 · 只读                    │
│ ─── 定需求 ───┬─── 试错 ───┬─── 结论 ─── │
│ 你 14:02      │ AI 15:31   │ AI 23:44    │
│ 我想做…       │ 报错了：…  │ 所以最终…   │
└───────────────┴────────────┴─────────────┘
```

## 三种摆法

浏览器里点一下就能换，随时切：

| 摆法 | 什么时候用 |
| --- | --- |
| **时间线** | 想知道"当时到底先发生什么、后发生什么" |
| **分栏** | 想知道"同一时间，两边各自在干嘛" |
| **轮次对齐** | 想知道"同一个问题，两边分别怎么回答的" |

![时间线](docs/screenshots/timeline.png)
![分栏](docs/screenshots/columns.png)
![轮次对齐](docs/screenshots/turns.png)

## 最重要的一件事：它只是"看"

用联合视图的时候，它**只读不写**：

- 原对话里一个字都不会被改
- 不会把几份对话合并、搬来搬去
- **AI 完全不知道你在这么看** —— 就像你把三份打印稿摊在桌上比对，桌上那台电脑（AI）并不知道

所以它很安全，随便试：看完关掉，世界和之前一模一样。

消息太多时它也不会卡死——每个视角只摆最近一段，上面会提示"更早的 N 条已折叠"。

### 它只显示你和 AI 说的话

对话记录里其实混着三种你不关心的东西，联合视图全部滤掉：

| 滤掉的 | 长什么样 | 为什么要滤 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI 的思考过程 | 一大段"我需要先……所以我打算……" | 又长又碎，把真正的结论淹了 |
| 工具调用 | `[调用 read_image]`、`[调用 pwsh]` | 一行一条，几十条连着刷屏 |
| 系统注入 | `Time sampled while preparing turn 12…`、`<AEGIS_DSH_ROUTING_BOOTSTRAP>`、`Current working directory…` | 这些是宿主塞给 AI 的，不是你说的话，混在你的对话框里看着莫名其妙 |

所以一屏看下去只剩干净的对话。代价是：如果那个对话里 AI 光在调工具没怎么说话，会显得内容很少——它本来就没说几句话。

## 如果你想让 AI 真的看见：`/weld`

> **实验功能**。见下方「已知限制」——生成的新对话有可能打不开。只是并排看的话不需要它。

上面说了，联合视图 AI 是看不见的。要让它真的看见，用 **`/weld`**。

**最省事的用法**：在联合视图里勾几个对话，工具栏右边填「每个取最近 N 轮」，点**「合并为新会话」**。它替你把这些填进输入框并提交，下面那行提示写着结果。等一两秒，左边对话列表最上面会多出一个「未命名」，点开就是合并好的新对话。

也可以手打：

```
/weld 3f2a1b 9c8d7e --turns 20
```

（`3f2a1b`、`9c8d7e` 是两个对话的编号前缀，`--turns 20` 表示每个对话只取最近 20 轮）

不打参数直接 `/weld` 回车，会列出最近 12 个对话的编号、时间和第一句话，照着抄就行。

它会真的**造出一个新对话**，把这两个对话的历史装进去。这个新对话：

- 出现在你的对话列表里，点开就能看
- **可以接着聊** —— 这时候 AI 是真的看得见这些历史了
- 原对话一个字没改（只是被读了一遍）
- 思考过程和工具调用也不带进去，只装你和 AI 说过的话

⚠️ 但这条路上有个坑：dsh 打开新对话时会校验日志结构，拼接出来的不一定过。所以「合并为新会话」按钮上标了**（实验）**。视图那部分是稳的，这个不是。

打个比方：

| | 联合视图 | `/weld` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 类比 | 把几份文件摊在桌上，自己比对 | 把几份文件装订成一本新的，递给 AI |
| AI 看得见吗 | 看不见 | 看得见 |
| 会多出一个对话吗 | 不会 | 会 |
| 原对话会变吗 | 不会 | 不会 |

**为什么一定要 `--turns`**：两个几百条消息的对话，加起来一万多条，AI 一次吃不下。所以必须截断，只取最近若干轮。

新对话的标题会显示「未命名」，因为原来的标题带引用关系，截断后对不上，干脆不要了。改个名字就行。

### 怎么知道对话的编号

通常在联合视图里点按钮就够了，不用记编号。真要手打，`/weld` 不带参数回车会列出来；也可以去 `.dsh/sessions/` 目录下看，每个对话是一个以 `session-` 开头的文件夹，文件夹名就是编号。

## 安装

用插件管理器：

```bash
dsh plugin install dsh-union-view
```

装完重启 DSH Web（或刷新页面），对话页面的标签栏会多出一个「联合视图」。

### 从源码装

`pnpm` 用不了的时候走这条路：

```bash
node scripts/build-client.mjs     # 把界面代码打包成 .dsh-plugin/client.js
node scripts/install-local.mjs    # 装进 DSH
```

第二行脚本做三件事：把整个项目复制到 `~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-union-view`、在 DSH 的 `node_modules` 里建一个目录联接（不需要管理员权限）、把插件名登记进配置。会先备份配置文件，可以反复跑。

## 用法

1. 打开任意对话，点顶部的「联合视图」标签
2. 点「选择会话」，勾上你想看的对话（可以多选，下次会自动记住）
3. 换摆法看
4. 「系统事件」开关：打开后能看到更细的过程（工具调用、轮次边界），平时关着更清爽

## 它不做什么

列清楚，免得误会：

- **不能在里面发消息**：它是只读窗口。要接着聊，切回原对话，或者用 `/weld` 造一个新对话
- **不会自动更新**：新开的对话不会自己冒出来，点一下「刷新」
- **不显示思考过程**：只显示你和 AI 的正式发言，AI 的推理过程不带
- **看不到已折叠的历史**：如果某个对话之前被压缩过（上下文太长时 DSH 会折叠旧内容），联合视图看到的也是折叠后的样子
- **不做对比和评分**：它只是并排显示，不计算差异、不判断谁对谁错

## 给想改代码的人

<details>
<summary>展开技术细节</summary>

### 界面部分怎么挂上去

注册在 DSH 的 `conversation.view` 槽位（`id: 'union'`，`order: 6`），和官方 `gal-view` 是同一个位置。

关键点：`src/client.js` 里必须写

```js
export const inject = ['slots', 'sessions', 'uiConversation']
```

少写一个，DSH 就不会把对应服务挂到插件身上，`ctx.sessions` 永远是 `undefined`（插件会显示"宿主未暴露 sessions 服务"）。`package.json` 里的 `dsh.client.inject: ["slots"]` 只负责让界面代码被加载，两回事。

### 数据从哪来

```js
const ref = ctx.sessions.retain(sessionId, { source: 'unionView' })
await ref.ready
const chat = ctx.uiConversation.binding(ref.binding).target('chat')
const nodes = chat.getSnapshot().legacy.nodes   // 对话节点数组
```

纯客户端读取，只用 `retain` 的引用计数，不调 `activate`、不 `prompt`、不 `fork`。

### 怎么铺满整个对话区

根节点加 `data-union-view`，`useEffect` 往上找第一个 `position !== 'static'` 的祖先（实测是 `.wSkVaW_body`），给它加上 `data-union-fill`，定位规则写在注入的 CSS 里。

**踩过的坑**：定位一定要写在 CSS 里，不能写内联 `style`——内联的 `position: relative` 会盖掉 CSS 里的 `absolute`，面板会按内容高度一路涨到十几万像素。

### `/weld` 为什么要自己写文件

DSH 有个 `ctx.sessions.create()`，但它只准备内存里的会话对象，**不落盘、不进侧栏账本**（源码注释写得很直白：persistence is a plugin concern）。所以 `/weld` 只能自己造文件：

1. **文件格式**：header 必须独占第一个 zstd frame 且以单个 `\n` 结尾，之后每条事件各自成一个 frame。全塞进一个 frame 会被判 corrupt，而扫描目录的代码对这类文件是**静默跳过**的——不报错，就是看不到。
2. **侧栏账本**：对话列表不是扫目录得来的，是读 `~/.dsh/storages/workspace.json` 里的 `sessionIds` 数组。不在数组里，文件再正确也不显示。

所以流程是：自己写文件 → 调 `workspaceRegistry.attachSession(newId)` → 它会校验 header 里的 `cwd` 和真实路径一致，通过后才把编号插进数组。

**改 `workspace.json` 只能用 JSON 解析器改**。用正则删数组元素会留下孤立逗号，JSON 一坏，整个界面会变成"暂无会话"。

</details>

## 目录结构

```
src/client.js       界面（联合会话视图，~1300 行）
src/merge.mjs       合并逻辑（纯函数，不碰磁盘）
.dsh-plugin/index.mjs   Node 半边（注册 /weld 命令）
scripts/build-client.mjs   打包界面代码
scripts/install-local.mjs  本机安装
scripts/merge-sessions.mjs 命令行合并（调试用）
scripts/cleanup-test.mjs   清理测试会话
scripts/e2e-verify.mjs     自动验收（需要浏览器调试端口）
```

## 已知限制

- 只读视图最多渲染最近 400 条消息（分栏每列独立计算）；轮次对齐最多 120 轮
- 消息正文按纯文本显示，保留 `**`、反引号原样——这是有意的，转录要保真
- 没有跨对话搜索、没有导出
- `/weld` 生成的新对话，第一批请求的缓存要从零建立（新对话全新前缀，这个省不掉）
- **`/weld` 目前是实验性的**：它能生成会话、能登记进侧栏，但 dsh 打开时会报
  `SessionFormatError: turn/start does not open the expected turn`。原因是宿主对从磁盘
  读回的日志有一套很严的结构校验（turn 必须连续、turn/start 必须跟在上一轮收尾之后、
  `sourceEventSeqs` 不能重复也不能指向后面的行），跨会话拼接出来的事件流很难同时满足。
  已试过的四种修法（顺序重编号 turn、末轮补齐收尾、保留首组初始化事件、引用去重）
  都没过。要做稳，得改成走宿主自己的 `ctx.sessions.create()` 那条路，让内核自己写日志。
- 视图（多选会话、三种摆法、只显示正文）不依赖上面这条，是稳的

## 许可

MIT

# DeepSeek × Codex：DSH 协作桥接 0.2.1

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

在 DSH 中把 DeepSeek 当前会话的公开内容带入 Codex 持久线程，查看双方公开回复、token 用量和账户额度。此仓库提供源码和 Windows 本机安装脚本。

在 DSH 的原会话中调用本机 Codex App Server，并在右侧「协作」面板查看双方公开消息、token 用量和账户额度。当前实现针对 Windows 上的 DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 与桌面附带的 Codex App Server；其它版本尚未确认兼容。

## 使用

1. 安装 [Node.js 22 或更新版本](https://nodejs.org/)，克隆或下载本仓库，在项目目录运行 `node install.mjs`，再完全退出并重开 DSH（包括托盘）。
2. 在会话右上角点击 **⇄ 协作**。也可从原生右侧面板选择协作页签。
3. 在主聊天里对 DeepSeek 说：「问 Codex：……，然后说说你的看法。」
4. 下一条「继续讨论……」延续该 DSH 会话绑定的 Codex 上下文。面板和 DSH 原停止按钮均可停止正在进行的 Codex 调用。

面板不另开输入框，也不会自动发起讨论。每条用户消息最多调用一次 ask，180 秒超时。讨论会使用双方模型额度；查看消息、读取用量和刷新额度不发起模型生成请求。

## 面板数据

- **消息**：发起讨论的用户消息、DeepSeek 提问、Codex 回答和 DeepSeek 后续公开回复。处理中逐步显示 Codex 返回的正文。不展示思考过程。
- **DeepSeek 最近协作轮**：DSH 记录的整个相关 turn（可包含多次模型请求）；展开可看 DeepSeek 原会话累计。
- **Codex 最近请求**：App Server 返回的最近一次请求；展开可看绑定 Codex 会话累计。与 DeepSeek 整轮统计范围不同。
- **输入**包含缓存命中，推理 token 已包含在输出中，不能再次相加。缺失数据为 `—`，不猜成 0。DSH 输入归一化按当前 DeepSeek 适配器的定义处理。
- **账户**：DeepSeek 显示宿主账户充值/赠送余额；Codex 显示账户配额窗口剩余百分比。均为账户共享数据，不是当前聊天独享额度，也不根据 token 推算金额。读取失败明确显示不可获取。
- 面板本地快照在讨论中每 0.8 秒更新，空闲时每 5 秒更新；窗口不可见时暂停读取。账户信息在打开面板/手动刷新时读取，缓存 60 秒；新 Codex 配额通知也会更新显示。
- 面板默认显示最近 100 条，可加载到 2000 条；完整公开消息仍在 DSH 原会话。旧版未保存的 Codex 用量不会伪造，下一轮收到事件后才有数据。

## 上下文和连接

每个 DSH Session 独立绑定一个持久 Codex Thread，重启后继续。它不是 Codex 桌面原聊天的克隆，不会自动获得桌面聊天历史。

首轮最多附带最近 6000 字符的用户/DeepSeek 公开文字，后续仅同步新增文字。附件、工具输出和思考过程不自动转发；必要内容由 DeepSeek 放入提问。旧绑定线程已经收到的上下文不会因升级被清空。

成功调用后的连接空闲 5 分钟内复用，最多保留 4 个连接（包括额度读取连接）。中断、失败和卸载都会关闭相应进程；失败不静默换新会话。UI 展示连接、恢复上下文、等待回复、回复中等状态以及耗时。减少上下文与复用连接只减少可控开销，不保证服务端回复时间。

讨论使用只读沙箱、拒绝交互审批。仅在桥接线程中关闭 shell、网页搜索及配置中列出的 MCP/插件；不更改用户全局 Codex 配置。插件不给双方自动施工或无限互聊的授权。

## 配置和存储

使用本机 Codex 已有登录。插件不读取、复制或保存认证令牌，不要求 API Key。

可选配置 `%USERPROFILE%/.dsh/codex-bridge/settings.json`：

```json
{
  "maxContextChars": 6000
}
```

还支持 `codexCommand`（可执行文件绝对路径）、`model`、`effort`、`instructions`（讨论附加指令，最多 8000 字符）。未填时沿用 Codex 模型配置并自动发现 Windows 桌面附带的 Codex。更改配置后重启 DSH。

绑定、最近用量和运行状态位于 `%USERPROFILE%/.dsh/codex-bridge/sessions/`，真实 Codex 历史由 Codex 自己持久保存。面板从 DSH 公开事件增量整理记录，不建立第二套聊天数据库。前后端走宿主原生 Typert 通道和 Session 查找，不启动额外 HTTP 服务。

## 安装和卸载

安装脚本将运行文件复制到 `%USERPROFILE%/Documents/Codex/plugins/dsh-lucy-codex-bridge`，在 DSH desktop profile 添加 `link:` 依赖和 bundle，原 profile package.json 保存时间戳备份。遇到其它同名目录或并发配置改动会停止，避免覆盖。

卸载运行 `node install.mjs --uninstall`，然后重启 DSH。仅移除本插件的依赖和 bundle，保留文件、绑定和历史；不会用旧配置覆盖其它插件变更。

源码以 MIT 许可证发布，详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。当前已验证的环境是 Windows 上的 DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 与其附带的 Codex App Server；其它 DSH 版本、操作系统和 Codex 安装方式尚未确认兼容。安装脚本会备份 DSH profile 配置，并在发现意外同名目录或并发修改时停止。升级前建议先备份该 profile。

0.2.0 错用了 `conversation.session.header.corner` 单一插槽，它已由 DSH 原生侧栏按钮占用，会使前端插件进入 failed 并阻止桌面启动。0.2.1 将按钮放进 `conversation.session.header.utilities` 列表插槽，保留原生侧栏按钮。

同时用 `remote.$mount` 挂载前端 Remote namespace，并提供前端要求的 strict 参数 codec。只向 Typert 注册描述不会生成可调用的 `remote.lucyCodex` 服务。

本机开发诊断脚本依赖特定 DSH 安装路径和构建，因此未包含在公开仓库中。

保留 DSH 插件添加的后端 `module-loaded.txt` / `activate-error.txt` 诊断；前端激活异常另以 `[lucy-codex-bridge] Client activation failed` 写入浏览器控制台，方便启动报告保留具体原因。

# dsh-hello

The smallest possible bundle: one row, no client half, no services, no state.

## Behaviour

Logs `[dsh-hello] loaded` once at boot and does nothing else.

Its job is to answer one question — *does this Harness installation load a linked local plugin at all?* — before you debug a real plugin. A host-only plugin exercises the patch row, the Loader import, and TypeScript source loading, and nothing more, so when it works the remaining variables are your plugin's.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dev add ./plugins/hello
```

If boot prints nothing, the row never mounted: start with `dsh --profile dev --dump-config` and check that `hello` is in the composed tree.

## Limits

It proves loading, not rendering. A client half is a different path — the bundle protocol, the slot registry, and the boot graph can all fail while this plugin stays quiet. For that, use a client plugin with a test that drives its bundle.

## Tests

None, by design. There is no logic to drive; the only assertion is the log line, which you read at boot.

# dsh-su

A monorepo of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins. The Harness itself is installed globally; this repo holds plugin sources only, and links them into a profile.

## Getting started

```sh
git clone https://github.com/serhaturtis/dsh-su && cd dsh-su
./setup.sh                             # Node, then the Harness, then the plugins
dsh --profile web web                  # boot the GUI
```

`./setup.sh` is a shell script for one reason: it may need to run *before Node
exists*, and `bootstrap.mjs` is a Node program. It uses an existing nvm to
provision Node 24 (see [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc)) if Node is missing, and
installs nvm — `curl … | bash`, a bigger decision than installing a CLI — only
when passed `--install-node`. Its one limitation is shell-shaped: a script
cannot change the PATH of the shell you are standing in, so if it installs nvm
it prints the two lines to add to your shell rc.

With Node already on PATH, `./setup.sh`, `pnpm setup`, and
`node scripts/bootstrap.mjs` are the same thing. `bootstrap` takes it from
there:

1. **installs the Harness** globally at the version pinned in `package.json`, if `dsh` is missing (`--no-harness-install` refuses and prints the command instead);
2. checks pnpm, which `dsh plugin` forwards to;
3. installs workspace dependencies;
4. **creates the profile from the shipped `web` template** if it doesn't exist;
5. links every plugin in the repo into it.

It never *upgrades* an installed Harness — a version mismatch is reported with the exact command, because a global upgrade mid-project is your call. Re-running is safe: it is the repair command as much as the setup one.

Flags: `--dry-run` reports without changing anything, `--profile <name>` targets another profile, `--no-install` skips workspace deps, `--no-harness-install` leaves the global Harness alone.

## Plugins

| Plugin | Shows up as | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`status-widget`](plugins/status-widget/README.md) | bottom-right card | Account balance and rate class cached 60s, eight-state cat mascot, [character packs](plugins/status-widget/docs/character-packs.md) |
| [`rate-hours`](plugins/rate-hours/README.md) | composer row | Peak/off-peak rate badge with a countdown; weekday schedule, public holidays not tracked |
| [`hello`](plugins/hello/README.md) | boot log | Smoke test that a linked plugin loads at all |

Add a row when you add a plugin. The table is the index; each plugin's README is the detail.

What is next, and what is deliberately parked, is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Layout

```
setup.sh                 shell entry point: provisions Node, then runs bootstrap
.nvmrc                   the Node version this repo is developed on
plugins/<name>/          one bundle per directory; <name> is the short name
  package.json           dsh.bundle.patch, dsh.client, exports
  cordis.patch.yml       the row this bundle inserts
  src/index.ts           host half: export name / inject / apply(ctx)
  src/client.js          client half (optional): a client-module bundle
  test/*.test.mjs        node tests, no Harness runtime
  README.md              behaviour, install, limits, tests
scripts/                 workspace tooling: bootstrap, sync, scaffold, test runner
docs/plugin-contract.md  what the Harness requires, and its sharp edges
ROADMAP.md               what is next, with effort and reasoning
```

## Conventions

- **Directory name is the short name; package name is `dsh-<short>`.** One plugin, one directory, one package, one row.
- **The exported Cordis `name` equals the package name**, so boot logs and the composed tree agree with the directory.
- **Every plugin has a README** with four sections, in order: behaviour, install, limits, tests. The limits section is not optional — it is where a plugin admits what it cannot know.
- **Tests are plain `node`,** no framework, no dependencies. `node scripts/test-all.mjs` (also `pnpm test`) finds `plugins/*/test/*.test.mjs` and runs each in its own process.
- **No build step** while plugins are plain JavaScript. A TypeScript client half would need one; nothing here has that yet.
- **`private: true` and `0.x`** until a plugin is worth publishing.
- **Two-space JSON/YAML/Markdown, tabs in source.**

Start a plugin with the scaffold rather than copying a neighbour:

```sh
pnpm new <name>            # host-only
pnpm new <name> --client   # host + browser half
```

## Dev loop

```sh
node scripts/new-plugin.mjs <name> --client   # scaffold a conforming plugin
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile dev   # link + enable it
pnpm dev                                      # boot the Web UI on the dev profile
```

`sync-profile` is the only step that touches a profile. It is idempotent — it links what's missing, adds the bundle row, and reports stale links left by deleted plugins (`--prune` removes them) — so run it after adding, renaming, or deleting a plugin instead of remembering `dsh plugin add` per package:

```sh
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --dry-run   # report, change nothing
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web             # apply
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --except rate-hours  # keep one out for good
```

- `bootstrap` is `sync-profile` plus the version checks and workspace install, i.e. the same thing for a machine that has never run this repo.
- A profile that doesn't exist yet is **seeded from the shipped `web` template** (`--template` changes that), so a fresh machine needs no manual profile creation. An existing profile that lacks `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` gets a warning with the repair command instead of being rewritten — seeding replaces profile-local settings, so that stays your call.
- Profiles live at `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>` (`~/.dsh` by default); `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` prints the composed tree without booting. `pnpm dev` uses the default port, so stop the running GUI first or pass `--port` to `dsh` directly.
- **Client code is composed at boot**: restart the Host after editing `src/client.js`. The Harness is a global install here, not a checkout, so there is no client HMR.
- Plugins are linked, so source edits need only a restart. Published plugins should ship built JS instead of raw `src/*.ts`.
- Bump the Harness with `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>`, update `dsh.harness.version` in `package.json`, and re-read [`docs/plugin-contract.md`](docs/plugin-contract.md) — the bundle contract is version-sensitive.

## Verifying

```sh
node scripts/test-all.mjs                  # every plugin's suite; no install needed
dsh --profile dev --dump-config            # composition, no boot
pnpm sync --profile dev --dry-run          # what the profile is missing
```

`pnpm test` runs the same script, but pnpm re-checks the workspace install first — reach for the direct command when `node_modules` is stale or absent.

A throwaway Harness home keeps experiments out of `~/.dsh`:

```sh
DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-dev dsh plugin --profile dev add ./plugins/<name>
```

`.dsh-dev/` is gitignored.

# dsh-rate-hours

> **Status: reference implementation, excluded from the `web` profile.** `status-widget` also shows the rate in the corner, so this composer-row badge is optional. It stays because it is the schedule implementation the parity test drives, and because a composer-row variant is a reasonable thing to re-enable with `sync-profile --include rate-hours`.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that shows whether DeepSeek is billing you at **peak** or **off-peak** rates right now, and when that changes.

```
● Peak pricing · off-peak in 2h 30m
● Off-peak · peak in 13h 39m
● Weekend off-peak · peak in 1d 22h
```

It sits in the composer row (`conversation.input.left`), just before the model selector. Only the dot carries colour — the text inherits the theme — so it reads as part of the row rather than a widget on top of it.

| Dot | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 🔴 Red | Peak — full rate |
| 🟡 Amber | Weekday off-peak — half rate |
| 🟢 Green | Off-peak all day (weekend) |

Hover for the schedule, the next boundary in UTC, and the caveats.

## The schedule

Peak is **01:00–04:00** and **06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday**. Everything else is off-peak — including weekends, and Chinese public holidays, which DeepSeek bills off-peak in full (this badge does not track those; see below). Off-peak is billed at half the peak rate.

Source: [DeepSeek Models & Pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing).

Older write-ups describe a single `16:30–00:30 UTC` off-peak window. That is out of date; DeepSeek split peak into the two weekday blocks above.

### Chinese public holidays are not tracked

The badge runs the weekday rule year-round. DeepSeek's official holiday spans are republished by the State Council every year, and carrying that table was yearly maintenance with a bad failure mode: a late or forecast year could silently mis-price days. The table has been removed, so a holiday weekday shows as **peak** here even though the API bills it off-peak. The tooltip says so. On a holiday, check the pricing page before relying on the badge.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dev add ./plugins/rate-hours   # from the repo root
```

That links the package into the profile and adds the `dsh-rate-hours` bundle. Restart the Host afterwards: the client-module graph is composed at boot, so a running page will not pick the plugin up.

The bundle is plain JavaScript served straight from `exports["./client"]`, so there is **no build step** — edit `src/client.js`, restart, reload.

## How it works

- **Host half** (`src/index.ts`) exists only to give the Loader a row: client bundles are discovered by scanning enabled Loader entries for a `dsh.client` declaration. It registers no service, no route, and no RPC.
- **Client half** (`src/client.js`) is a client-module bundle in the required shape: it calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` once and does everything else inside the factory closure. It requires only `react`, which is a platform seed module, so it declares no externals.
- **The clock is the browser's.** Computing locally avoids a Host round-trip, an RPC surface, and a route registration. The cost is that a badly skewed browser clock gives a wrong answer; the tooltip says the figure is browser-derived rather than presenting it as authoritative.

## Limits

- **An indicator, not a bill.** It reports the published schedule. It cannot know about account credits, negotiated discounts, or a schedule change DeepSeek makes without updating this file.
- **Chinese public holidays are not tracked.** A holiday weekday is shown as peak. The tooltip states the limitation; the table was removed rather than maintained by hand every year.
- **No cost estimate.** Deliberately out of scope; the session usage projection is a separate concern and a harder claim to make honestly.

## Tests

```sh
node test/schedule.test.mjs
```

The tests need no dependencies, so they run straight from a checkout. (`pnpm --filter dsh-rate-hours test` also works once the workspace has been installed; the plugin's only dependency is a `cordis` devDependency for editor typings, and `import type` is erased at runtime.)

22 checks, no Harness runtime needed: the loader handshake (bundle registers under the right id, exports `apply`/`inject` rather than a factory, registers into `conversation.input.left`), every peak edge, the gap between blocks, weekends, the public-holiday limitation, transition correctness across a full week, and the component's element tree.

The component is rendered against a React stub, not real React: the browser shell ships its own React bundle, so there is no React on disk for an SSR render in this workspace.

# dsh-status-widget

A speech bubble in the bottom-right corner, in which the **account balance** and the **DeepSeek rate class** appear as her dialogue — with a tail that points down at the character speaking them.

```
● ¥110.00 · Off-peak · peak in 13h 39m
```

She also **drifts slowly along a docked edge when left alone**, does something occasionally while quiet (stretches, taps the fuselage), **announces the peak boundary** the moment it flips, warns once an hour when the balance falls under your threshold, and **purrs if you pat her head** — press the top third rather than the body. Menu and dialogue text follow the browser language (English or Chinese); rate labels are still English.

While a turn runs, a thin bar under the bubble shows how full the context window is — green, amber at 70%, red at 90% — from the `contextPressure` projection. It hides itself when no provider has reported capacity, because an unknown window is not an empty one.

When a turn finishes, the bubble adds a third line: **`Last turn $0.0042`**. That is the delta between two readings of the `tokenUsage` projection — the four provider-reported buckets — priced with the published list rates at whatever rate class was in force. Off-peak is exactly half, and a test holds that relationship rather than hard-coding both columns.

Each finished turn also feeds **`Today $0.123`**, a running estimate for your local day kept in this browser's storage. It resets at local midnight. This is not account spend: it counts model tokens for turns this page watched, priced the same way as `Last turn`.

When a turn is blocked waiting for your approval, she leans in, the line becomes **"Waiting for your approval"**, the dot turns red and pulses, and a cue plays if sound is on. That signal comes from `uiSession.sessionStatus.pendingInteraction` — a push-based store, so it costs one subscription and no polling.

A black Norwegian Forest cat with a white mask stands under it, in one of eight drawings: **idle**, **happy** (a turn just finished), **busy** (a turn is running), **worried** (the balance read failed), **sleepy** (ten quiet minutes), **wave** (first sighting), **pat** (a head pat) and **party** (the balance went up). She bobs while idle, hops when happy and leans in while busy. **Drag her anywhere (the bubble comes along)** — she snaps to the nearer edge and flips to face into the page. Click her to collapse the card to the balance alone.

The art is raster, one PNG per state. There is no vector fallback: a second drawing of the same character drifts away from the generated one, and a missing image is better reported than silently replaced by a different animal.

Hover for the full picture: the schedule and its next boundary, the granted/topped-up split, and how fresh the reading is.

This is the feature set of the popular whale widget, built as an ordinary DSH plugin rather than a 22,000-line script injected into the page.

## Behaviour

- **Balance** comes from [`GET /user/balance`](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/get-user-balance), read by the host half with the key from the credential store and served to the browser as amounts only. The key never reaches the page. Amounts pass through as the decimal strings the API returns — no float arithmetic on money.
- **The reading is cached for 60 seconds** in the host, so a page left open for an hour costs one request per minute, and concurrent tabs share one read.
- **Failures are named, not blank**: `no API key`, or `balance ?` for a rejected key or a network problem, each explained in the tooltip. Polling continues once a minute, so a fixed key recovers without a reload.
- **The rate line** follows the same rule as [`rate-hours`](../rate-hours/README.md): peak `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00` UTC, Monday–Friday. Chinese public holidays are **not tracked**; DeepSeek bills them off-peak, so a holiday weekday shows as peak here. The tooltip states that limitation.

The mascot — a cat in the corner that reacts to turns, rate changes and a low balance — is replaceable; the format is in [`docs/character-packs.md`](docs/character-packs.md).

## Install

```sh
node scripts/bootstrap.mjs      # links every plugin in the repo
```

or this plugin alone:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/status-widget
```

Needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the credential store — Settings → Models, or the environment when the Host starts.

### The artwork

Four drawings, one per state: `assets/mascot-{idle,happy,busy,worried}.png`, all 432×788. They come from a single generated 2×2 expression sheet, cut apart with **one shared canvas, one scale, and alignment on her stance** — the horizontal centroid of the lowest 12% of each figure. Centring on the bounding box was wrong: a raised arm moves the box centre, which left two poses looking off-centre by up to 25px.

`assets/mascot.png` is a byte copy of the idle drawing: it is the URL an already-cached page asks for, and the fallback for an unknown state.

The design is deliberately alluring — harness-style crop top, fishnets, thigh-highs, peace sign — and deliberately clothed. Nudity and see-through fabric are out of scope for this artwork, whatever the prompt. The host serves them at `/dsh-status-widget/mascot.png?state=<state>`, because a client bundle cannot require a relative asset and inlining ~300 KB of base64 would ride in every page load. Responses carry an ETag and revalidate, so a redrawn face is not pinned by a stale cache.

An inline SVG is the fallback: if the route 404s or the file is missing, the corner still has a character in four expressions instead of a hole. `test/character.test.mjs` pins the properties that matter — PNG signature, alpha channel, at least 2× display size, under 400 KB.

### Preferences

Size and position are stored in `$DSH_HOME/status-widget.json`, written by a `PUT /dsh-status-widget/prefs` route and read back on load. That is deliberate: the web GUI and the desktop client do not share `localStorage`, so browser-only state would disagree between them. `localStorage` remains the offline fallback.

The same choice is available in **Settings → Status widget**, which shares the widget's live size store rather than keeping a copy — pick a size there and the mascot changes immediately.

### Placement modes

| Mode | Anchor | Bubble |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Docked** | side edge + 32px margin, moving the whole frame | identical shape in every mode |
| **Free** | left/top where you dropped her | identical shape in every mode |

**Two invariants.**

1. She is always centred in the bubble.
2. The widget is one fixed-width frame (**220px, equal to the bubble's cap**). The character is centred in it, the bubble is centred on her, and docking *moves the frame*. Nothing inside reflows because of docking, so the bubble keeps one shape and she keeps one place in it. Because the frame equals the cap, the bubble can never stick out past the frame.

The frame is a constant rather than derived from the bubble's text on purpose: a layout that adapts to its content is what made her drift in the first place.

**Centring is done by the flow, never by transforms.** The frame is a flex column with `alignItems: center`, so the bubble and the character are centred by layout. This matters: the idle animation animates `transform`, and CSS animations outrank inline styles — centring with `translateX(-50%)` was being cancelled by the bob animation, which is what made her sit off-centre. The left-edge flip uses the standalone `scale` property for the same reason.

Dragging within 48px of a side docks; anywhere else is free. Both modes are persisted (host-side preferences, `localStorage` as the fallback) and both are repaired on resize rather than stranded off-screen.

The root element is exactly the character's box — the bubble is absolutely positioned around it. That is what makes the text unable to move her: the layout no longer depends on the bubble's width at all.

### Sound

Synthesised with WebAudio — two short tones, no audio files to ship or license. A chime when a turn finishes, a lower tone when the balance read fails. **Off until switched on**, in Settings or by preference; the choice is stored host-side with the rest.

### Cost, honestly

The figure covers **model tokens only**, priced at list rates for the model chosen in Settings (Flash by default). It cannot see account credits, negotiated discounts, retries billed elsewhere, or a mid-turn model switch. Cache writes are priced as ordinary input, because DeepSeek publishes a cache read discount but no separate write premium. A delta that goes negative — possible if compaction resets the fold — is clamped to zero rather than reported as a refund. `Today` is the sum of these same estimates, so it inherits every one of those limits.

## Limits

- **The balance is the account's, not the session's.** It says what is left, not what this conversation has cost.
- **No usage history beyond today.** The `Today` estimate keeps only the current local day; the whale derives full spend from session logs, which is a much larger claim than this widget makes.
- **One product assumption:** the credential is the DeepSeek API key. A profile signed in through the DeepSeek *account* provider has no `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, so the card says so instead of reading nothing.
- **The art is generated, not drawn to the grid.** Judge it at 180 px wide — the size it actually ships. The four states are one generation, so continuity between poses is only as good as the sheet was.
- **Chinese public holidays are not tracked.** The badge runs the weekday peak rule year-round. DeepSeek bills holidays off-peak, so a holiday weekday is shown as peak; the tooltip says so rather than shipping a table that needs a State Council notice every November.
- **`Today` is an estimate, not a bill.** It lives in this browser's storage, counts only turns the page watched, resets at local midnight, and two tabs watching one turn can each add it. It cannot see account credits, discounts, or turns that happened while the page was closed.
- **The schedule is duplicated** from `rate-hours` rather than imported: client bundles cannot require each other without a cross-plugin dependency, and either plugin should work alone. [`test/schedule-parity.test.mjs`](test/schedule-parity.test.mjs) drives both copies over every 15-minute sample of 2026-2027 and fails if they diverge.

## Feature catalogue

[`docs/feature-catalogue.md`](docs/feature-catalogue.md) lists **166 candidate features** with effort and value, drawn from the three DSH widgets plus Shimeji, Desktop Goose, Tamagotchi-style pets and VS Code Pets. 26 are shipped; the rest are scored and IDed (`E03`, `F07`, …) so commits and issues can reference them.

## Character packs

A standard for replacing the mascot: a directory (`pack.json` + images) or a single shareable `.dshchar` file, with the same manifest in both. Nobody's character art ships with this repository: the format is public, the art is personal. [`examples/README.md`](examples/README.md) walks through authoring one — the smallest valid pack, motion, and the mistakes that produce drifting or cropped frames.

Import, export, activate, delete and **Rescan** are live in Settings → Status widget → Character and over the host routes; the right-click Character submenu offers the same switch and import. The format, its refusals, the storage layout, routes, import/export and versioning rules are specified in [`docs/character-packs.md`](docs/character-packs.md); the rules themselves live in [`src/pack.js`](../src/pack.js) with 16 tests, deliberately free of Node and DOM so the format can be checked without a running Harness.

Packs may carry **animated characters** — an animated GIF/WebP, or a sprite sheet with `frames`/`fps` in horizontal, vertical or grid layout — and **their own sounds** per event (`done`, `error`, `alert`, `pat`), which win over the built-in cues. The renderer, the per-state routes and the Settings controls are implemented and tested end to end.

## Research

Which client-side signals a root-scope widget can read, and what they unlock: [`docs/client-data-sources.md`](docs/client-data-sources.md) — including the finding that pending approvals come from `sessionStatus.pendingInteraction`, not from the `permissions` projection.


What the three most-installed character widgets in this ecosystem actually ship, which of their features are worth copying, and which ones are a configuration product wearing a mascot: [`docs/widget-research.md`](docs/widget-research.md).

## Todo

Every known gap in this plugin — layout, dialogue, a11y, tests, packaging — is listed in [`TODO.md`](TODO.md), with the shipped items marked.

## Tests

```sh
node test/balance.test.mjs          # normalization, the request, the cache
node test/host.test.mjs             # route, missing key, throwing store
node test/client.test.mjs           # bundle handshake, slot, rendered tree
node test/interaction.test.mjs      # drag, click/pat, menu focus and submenus
node test/character.test.mjs        # four state drawings, placement maths
node test/pack.test.mjs             # character-pack format and refusals
node test/schedule-parity.test.mjs  # this widget's schedule == rate-hours'
```

No Harness runtime and no network: the balance fetch is injected, and the component renders against a React stub — the browser shell ships its own React, so there is none on disk here.

# dsh-su

A monorepo of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins. The Harness itself is installed globally; this repo holds plugin sources only, and links them into a profile.

## Getting started

```sh
git clone https://github.com/serhaturtis/dsh-su && cd dsh-su
./setup.sh                             # Node, then the Harness, then the plugins
dsh --profile web web                  # boot the GUI
```

`./setup.sh` is a shell script for one reason: it may need to run *before Node
exists*, and `bootstrap.mjs` is a Node program. It uses an existing nvm to
provision Node 24 (see [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc)) if Node is missing, and
installs nvm — `curl … | bash`, a bigger decision than installing a CLI — only
when passed `--install-node`. Its one limitation is shell-shaped: a script
cannot change the PATH of the shell you are standing in, so if it installs nvm
it prints the two lines to add to your shell rc.

With Node already on PATH, `./setup.sh`, `pnpm setup`, and
`node scripts/bootstrap.mjs` are the same thing. `bootstrap` takes it from
there:

1. **installs the Harness** globally at the version pinned in `package.json`, if `dsh` is missing (`--no-harness-install` refuses and prints the command instead);
2. checks pnpm, which `dsh plugin` forwards to;
3. installs workspace dependencies;
4. **creates the profile from the shipped `web` template** if it doesn't exist;
5. links every plugin in the repo into it.

It never *upgrades* an installed Harness — a version mismatch is reported with the exact command, because a global upgrade mid-project is your call. Re-running is safe: it is the repair command as much as the setup one.

Flags: `--dry-run` reports without changing anything, `--profile <name>` targets another profile, `--no-install` skips workspace deps, `--no-harness-install` leaves the global Harness alone.

## Plugins

| Plugin | Shows up as | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`status-widget`](plugins/status-widget/README.md) | bottom-right card | Account balance and rate class cached 60s, eight-state cat mascot, [character packs](plugins/status-widget/docs/character-packs.md) |
| [`rate-hours`](plugins/rate-hours/README.md) | composer row | Peak/off-peak rate badge with a countdown; weekday schedule, public holidays not tracked |
| [`hello`](plugins/hello/README.md) | boot log | Smoke test that a linked plugin loads at all |

Add a row when you add a plugin. The table is the index; each plugin's README is the detail.

What is next, and what is deliberately parked, is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Layout

```
setup.sh                 shell entry point: provisions Node, then runs bootstrap
.nvmrc                   the Node version this repo is developed on
plugins/<name>/          one bundle per directory; <name> is the short name
  package.json           dsh.bundle.patch, dsh.client, exports
  cordis.patch.yml       the row this bundle inserts
  src/index.ts           host half: export name / inject / apply(ctx)
  src/client.js          client half (optional): a client-module bundle
  test/*.test.mjs        node tests, no Harness runtime
  README.md              behaviour, install, limits, tests
scripts/                 workspace tooling: bootstrap, sync, scaffold, test runner
docs/plugin-contract.md  what the Harness requires, and its sharp edges
ROADMAP.md               what is next, with effort and reasoning
```

## Conventions

- **Directory name is the short name; package name is `dsh-<short>`.** One plugin, one directory, one package, one row.
- **The exported Cordis `name` equals the package name**, so boot logs and the composed tree agree with the directory.
- **Every plugin has a README** with four sections, in order: behaviour, install, limits, tests. The limits section is not optional — it is where a plugin admits what it cannot know.
- **Tests are plain `node`,** no framework, no dependencies. `node scripts/test-all.mjs` (also `pnpm test`) finds `plugins/*/test/*.test.mjs` and runs each in its own process.
- **No build step** while plugins are plain JavaScript. A TypeScript client half would need one; nothing here has that yet.
- **`private: true` and `0.x`** until a plugin is worth publishing.
- **Two-space JSON/YAML/Markdown, tabs in source.**

Start a plugin with the scaffold rather than copying a neighbour:

```sh
pnpm new <name>            # host-only
pnpm new <name> --client   # host + browser half
```

## Dev loop

```sh
node scripts/new-plugin.mjs <name> --client   # scaffold a conforming plugin
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile dev   # link + enable it
pnpm dev                                      # boot the Web UI on the dev profile
```

`sync-profile` is the only step that touches a profile. It is idempotent — it links what's missing, adds the bundle row, and reports stale links left by deleted plugins (`--prune` removes them) — so run it after adding, renaming, or deleting a plugin instead of remembering `dsh plugin add` per package:

```sh
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --dry-run   # report, change nothing
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web             # apply
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --except rate-hours  # keep one out for good
```

- `bootstrap` is `sync-profile` plus the version checks and workspace install, i.e. the same thing for a machine that has never run this repo.
- A profile that doesn't exist yet is **seeded from the shipped `web` template** (`--template` changes that), so a fresh machine needs no manual profile creation. An existing profile that lacks `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` gets a warning with the repair command instead of being rewritten — seeding replaces profile-local settings, so that stays your call.
- Profiles live at `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>` (`~/.dsh` by default); `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` prints the composed tree without booting. `pnpm dev` uses the default port, so stop the running GUI first or pass `--port` to `dsh` directly.
- **Client code is composed at boot**: restart the Host after editing `src/client.js`. The Harness is a global install here, not a checkout, so there is no client HMR.
- Plugins are linked, so source edits need only a restart. Published plugins should ship built JS instead of raw `src/*.ts`.
- Bump the Harness with `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>`, update `dsh.harness.version` in `package.json`, and re-read [`docs/plugin-contract.md`](docs/plugin-contract.md) — the bundle contract is version-sensitive.

## Verifying

```sh
node scripts/test-all.mjs                  # every plugin's suite; no install needed
dsh --profile dev --dump-config            # composition, no boot
pnpm sync --profile dev --dry-run          # what the profile is missing
```

`pnpm test` runs the same script, but pnpm re-checks the workspace install first — reach for the direct command when `node_modules` is stale or absent.

A throwaway Harness home keeps experiments out of `~/.dsh`:

```sh
DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-dev dsh plugin --profile dev add ./plugins/<name>
```

`.dsh-dev/` is gitignored.

--- ## Supported hosts The latest plugin supports **dsh 0.2** only — do not apply it to 0.1.x. - **dsh 0.2** (official desktop **0.2.1-rc.2** / 0.2.0-rc.2 / official `dsh web`): use **1.2.0** or newer. This page installs that line. - **dsh 0.1.7** (incl. rc.1 / rc.2): use **1.1.39** or older — pick the tag on [Releases](https://github.com/ShadowCat2233/dsh-purge-plus/releases). Unmatched patches stay pending or skipped; nothing is rewritten blindly. --- ## Install Web and the official desktop EXE are the two maintained hosts. **Install both. Apply each separately.** A Web install does not reach the desktop app, and a desktop install does not reach Web. **Web (official `dsh web`)** ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-purge ``` **Desktop (official EXE)** ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-purge ``` If this directory is already a clone, use `add .` instead of the package name. If `dsh` is not on PATH, use [Manual install](#manual). Registry blocked: add `https://github.com/ShadowCat2233/dsh-purge-plus/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz` with the same `--profile`. Hub one-click on [dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/yujunzhixue/dsh-purge) searches npm for this repository and installs `dsh-purge`. The catalog line may still show `github:` — use the command above if the button falls back to git. For the desktop client you can also click the button (`dsh://` deep link):

Install in desktop client

### After the command: three steps Adding the plugin to a profile does **not** patch `@deepseek-ai` by itself. 1. **Quit and reopen** the host you installed into — stop and restart `dsh web`, or quit the desktop tray and reopen that app. 2. On **that host**, click **dsh-purge** beside the session title, then **Apply** on the **Clean** page. It is not on the host Settings page. 3. A successful **Apply** restarts once so patches load. It does not restart if it did not finish. Web controls affect Web only; desktop controls affect the desktop app only. Do not Apply one host from the other. ### How to tell it installed - **dsh-purge** sits beside the session title, with **Apply** on its Clean page. - `/purge status` in chat prints `DSH_HOME` and the patch list — the path should be the home you actually run. - Optional packages that are not installed (liangshen) show as skipped and do not block Apply. ### Hand this to an assistant Paste the block below to a local assistant. It should only run the install command — no disk scan, no other edits, no Apply, no restart.
For AI assistants (install only) Install the DeepSeek Harness plugin `dsh-purge` into both the Web profile and the official desktop profile. Do not scan the whole disk, do not read or edit other files, do not apply settings, and do not restart the app. If `dsh` is not on PATH, tell the user and stop. If this directory is already a clone, use `.` instead of the package name in both commands. If the npm registry is blocked, use `https://github.com/ShadowCat2233/dsh-purge-plus/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz`. If one profile is missing, skip that command and still install the other. **Web (official `dsh web`)** ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-purge ``` **Desktop (official EXE)** ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-purge ``` After the commands finish, tell the user to fully quit and restart `dsh web`, and to quit the desktop tray then reopen the EXE. On each host, open **dsh-purge** beside the session title and **Apply** on **Clean**. Then stop.
### Manual install Use this when the command fails or `dsh` is not on PATH. Edit **only the profile for the host you run** — do not touch the other, and do not delete existing bundles.
Full manual steps **1. Find the `$DSH_HOME` this host uses.** A real home is named `.dsh` (official EXE sometimes `dsh-home`), contains `profiles`, and has at least one `profiles//package.json`. Check in order: `DSH_HOME` env → `.dsh` next to the install root (portable) → `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh` or `~/.dsh` → `%APPDATA%` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepSeek Harness\dsh-home`. Confirm: `profiles/web/package.json` has `"name": "dsh-profile-web"` (or `dsh-profile-desktop`). Machines often have two homes — use the one that belongs to the host you actually start. PowerShell to list candidates: ```powershell $cands = @() if ($env:DSH_HOME) { $cands += $env:DSH_HOME } $cands += "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh" $dsh = Get-Command dsh -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue if ($dsh) { $dir = Split-Path $dsh.Source $cands += @((Join-Path $dir ".dsh"), (Join-Path (Split-Path $dir) ".dsh"), (Join-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $dir)) ".dsh")) } $cands += @("$env:APPDATA\DeepSeek Harness\dsh-home", "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\DeepSeek Harness\dsh-home") $cands | Select-Object -Unique | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $_ "profiles")) } ``` **2. Put the plugin at `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-purge`** (folder must be named `dsh-purge`, with a `package.json` whose `"name"` is `dsh-purge`). ```sh git clone https://github.com/ShadowCat2233/dsh-purge-plus.git "$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-purge" ``` Without git: download [main.tar.gz](https://github.com/ShadowCat2233/dsh-purge-plus/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz), extract, rename `dsh-purge-main` → `dsh-purge`, and place it under `plugins`. If you already have a clone, copy the whole tree — not a few `.js` files. **3. Edit only that profile's `package.json` — back it up first.** Web → `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/package.json`; desktop → `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/package.json`. Add **only two things**, keeping every existing dependency and bundle: 1. In `dependencies`, add `"dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge"` 2. At the **end** of `dsh.profile.bundles`, append `"dsh-purge"` (skip if already there) ```json { "name": "dsh-profile-web", "private": true, "dependencies": { "dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge" }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-purge" ], "patchReload": "live" } } } ``` Keep JSON valid (comma before the new item, none after the last). Do not switch `file:../../plugins/dsh-purge` to an absolute path, do not touch `patchReload` or other plugins, and do not list `"dsh-purge"` twice. On desktop, if there is no `dsh-web-app` row, do not add one. **4. Run `pnpm install` in that profile only** (`cd` into the profile dir, not the repo root or `$DSH_HOME`): ```sh cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" # or profiles/desktop pnpm install ``` Success: `profiles//node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json` exists. If `pnpm` is missing, use the Node / pnpm shipped with official `dsh`; on `Could not resolve`, re-check the `file:` path; on a JSON error, fix commas or restore the backup. **5. Fully quit that host, reopen it, then Apply** — same three steps as above. The card appears beside the session title; click **Apply** (or `/purge apply`) on that host only. If the card is missing, you likely edited the other `.dsh` — go back to step 1.
### Uninstall **dsh-purge** beside the session title → **Clean** → **Uninstall**. Confirm the dialog: it reverts any applied patches, restores the original Harness, and restarts the current host. ```sh # or from a terminal / chat dsh-purge --uninstall # /purge uninstall ``` Plugin config lives in `cordis.patch.yml` (`postPrompt` is empty by default): ```yaml - insert: - id: dsh-purge name: 'dsh-purge' config: enabled: true autoApplyOnStart: true autoUpdateOnStart: false autoRevertOnMissing: false verbose: false postPromptOrder: 5100 postPrompt: "" ``` --- ## Preview **Settings is the only surface**: the last row of the settings rail, Purge, opens the full panel. It is drawn on the harness's own design tokens — a 720px column, card rows with a 0.5px stroke, 36px buttons and 32px inputs, the same visual grammar as Models and General. ![Settings page](docs/preview/settings-1.3.1.png) In the real app (Settings → Purge, v1.3.1, Windows desktop): ![Settings page in the app](docs/preview/app-settings-1.3.1.png) The dark theme follows the host; there is no separate switch: ![Settings page, dark](docs/preview/settings-1.3.1-dark.png) There is no in-conversation button any more: Settings is the only surface. The page has four segments: **Armor** (patches, prompt, own servers), **Rules**, **Skills**, **Drill**. Patches are grouped; the count only includes items that actually applied. Rule sets sit in a list above the editor, with Enable and Delete on each row. The first time you open Drill you read the notice, wait out the countdown, scroll to the end, and check three boxes. Clean does not need that step. Drill is only for a host you manage, an offline target, or an exercise that already has written authorization. **Clean (dock)** ![Clean](docs/preview/dock-clean.png) **Drill authorization** ![Drill authorization](docs/preview/dock-auth.png) **Drill** ![Drill](docs/preview/dock-drill.png) **Own servers** On the Clean page, under Prompt. One host per line, then Save list. Steps are in [Own servers](#own-servers). ![Own servers](docs/preview/own-servers-en.png) | Area | What it shows | |---|---| | Settings → Purge | the only surface: patches, prompt, rule sets, skills, and the drill console | | Clean | the old Rules page: patches, prompt, rule sets, skills | | Drill | assets, skills, and environment after authorization. The tab says Unauthorized until then | | Patches | grouped status, Apply, Restore, or Uninstall | | Prompt | edit `prompt-inject.md` as the session override | | Own servers | one IP or exact hostname per line, saved to `$DSH_HOME/net-scope-allow.txt` | | Rule sets | multiple `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`; Enable writes under `$DSH_HOME`, Delete removes the row | | Skills | import a zip or folder into this host’s official `$DSH_HOME/skills//SKILL.md` (web and desktop each use their own home; no drive letter is hardcoded); DSH owns match, load, and `/name`. You can also delete that folder yourself | --- ## Layout `bin/` is the CLI, `lib/` is patches and the drill console, `presets/redteam/` is the red-team preset, `skills/redteam/` is the bundled skills, and `client.js` is the dock. Runtime files live under `$DSH_HOME`: `prompt-inject.md`, `rules/`, `skills/`, `net-scope-allow.txt`, `redteam/`. If `DSH_HOME` is unset, the launcher-adjacent `.dsh` wins over `~/.dsh`. Web and the desktop app each use their own home. Skills are not part of the inject section and do not replace the prompt. --- ## Usage ```sh dsh-purge --status dsh-purge --apply dsh-purge --revert dsh-purge --uninstall dsh-purge --edit /purge status | apply | revert | uninstall | edit | help /rules list | use | create | delete | reset | help /skills list | import | create [description] | delete | help /rewind purge_status purge_apply purge_revert ``` After a successful Apply, the host restarts so patched packages load; you can also click **Restart** manually. Under the patch title are the stable release and the test release. The test release follows the `beta` branch. **Switch to stable** installs `master` and clears any pin. Picking an older stable version pins it; click **Update** to return to the latest. Old test tags are not listed. The composer **Undo once** and **Undo last round** follow official DSH `session.fork({ atSeq })`: the withdrawn turn is cut off, a new session keeps the earlier context, the old session is archived, and the line returns to the input so **send again** re-injects. `/rewind` does the same. If the **same task works in standard but fails in minimal or PTC**, preset `run_code`, sandbox, or plan intercept text is often still uncleared, or built-in minimal is missing `agent-instructions`. Use **1.1.61+**, then **quit the host fully → Apply in Clean → restart → start a new chat**. Switching preset alone does not reload patches in the running process. ### Response speed DSH runs Bash calls in a tool batch one at a time. Older dsh-purge releases raised the default foreground wait from 60 seconds to 10 minutes, so one slow command could hold up later calls for that long. Patch #21 now restores marked plugin values to the official 60-second default. Unmarked timeouts and other custom values are preserved; an unmarked 10-minute value cannot reliably be distinguished from a user setting. For a shorter wait in `dsh web` on macOS/Linux, add this entry to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (normally `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`). Edit an existing entry with the same id instead of adding a duplicate. This profile layer is applied after the bundled configuration, so future plugin applies keep the override. ```yaml - id: bash-sandbox config: timeoutMs: 10000 ``` With the standard jobs service and `promoteOnTimeout: true`, an unfinished command returns a background job id after 10 seconds and keeps running. Read it with `job_output` or stop it with `job_kill`. This changes the foreground wait, not the command's speed. Without that service or with promotion disabled, the timeout kills the command. A per-call `timeoutMs` overrides this default; `run_in_background: true` returns a job id immediately. For routine tasks, you can also opt into Low reasoning for new sessions: ```yaml - id: agent-default-model config: provider: deepseek-official model: deepseek-flash reasoningEffort: low ``` Restart `dsh web` to load the profile. The model and reasoning defaults apply to newly created sessions; select Low in the composer for an existing session. The plugin does not change these model preferences automatically. Keep High when the task needs deeper reasoning, and narrow file searches rather than recursively scanning every application directory. ### Own servers Addresses in mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macau stay forbidden unless that one host was registered first. Saying “this is my server” in chat does not allow it. A key or a password does not allow it either. The box sits under Prompt. If the dock does not show it yet, quit DeepSeek Harness completely and open it again. 1. Click **dsh-purge** beside the session title and stay on **Clean**. 2. Scroll past **Prompt**. **Own servers** is the next block. 3. Put one host on each line, in one of these forms: - `203.0.113.10` — one IP. - `my-vps.example.com` — one exact hostname. After you save, the addresses that hostname resolves to at lookup time are allowed too. - `alice@my-vps.example.com` — the account only identifies this form. It does not prove the machine is yours. 4. Click **Save list**. The list is written to `$DSH_HOME/net-scope-allow.txt`. 5. Keys, passwords, ranges, and wildcards are dropped on save. Unlisted mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macau addresses stay forbidden. `203.0.113.10` and `example.com` above are only examples of the form. Replace them with your own host before you save. --- ## Local checks ```sh node --check lib/index.js node --check lib/core.js node --check lib/surface.js node --check lib/web.js node --check lib/desktop.js node --check lib/host.js node --check lib/rewind.js node --check lib/skills.js node --check cli

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Whale Trail · 鲸迹 **让每一次探索，都留下一枚值得收藏的徽章。** Whale Trail for DeepSeek Harness 是一款以小鲸鱼为主题的成就徽章插件。它把日常的使用天数、连续使用、Token 用量与对话轮次，变成一册会逐渐点亮的航海收藏。达到条件就自动获得，不需要打卡、领取或确认完成，让成长记录自然发生在工作之中。 *Whale Trail is a local-first achievement badge collection for DeepSeek Harness. Earn whale-themed badges automatically as you explore, build, and talk with your agent.* > **非官方社区项目，由社区成员独立开发与维护，未获 DeepSeek 官方背书。** 当前版本 **0.2.4**，已验证 **macOS / DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2**。 [下载与安装](#安装) · [徽章示例](#徽章示例) · [备份与迁移](#备份与迁移) · [反馈与建议](https://github.com/ShawnRen57/dsh-whale-trail/issues) ## 你的使用足迹，值得被看见 - **自动点亮**：正常使用 Harness，满足条件即获得；首次安装时同步可读取的历史记录。 - **有进阶的收藏**：圆形印章与贴纸风格，统一数值牌；小鲸鱼的装备、角色与航海场景随等级变化。 - **一眼看见成长**：六项成就统计，包括徽章数、累计天数、最长连续、当前连续、Token 与对话轮次。 - **有惊喜的探索**：节日限定与隐藏徽章；未获得的隐藏徽章只展示名称和问号占位，保留发现的乐趣。 - **本地记录**：不新增模型调用，不上传聊天内容；支持导出备份，在自己的设备间迁移。 点击 Harness 左下角 **用户信息 → 我的徽章**，打开你的收藏册。 *账户菜单入口：点击带奖章图标的「我的徽章」。* ![Whale Trail 我的徽章：两行成就统计、亮金叶枝与印章风徽章](docs/images/my-badges.png) *截图为独立测试档案的演示进度。已获得徽章按获得时间倒排；未获得徽章分类展示，普通徽章为灰色，悬浮可查看获得方式。* ## 徽章示例 目前包含 **28 枚徽章、6 个系列**：累计使用、连续使用、Token 回响、累计对话、节日限定与隐藏典藏。

初次下潜
累计使用 · 1 天
三日同游
连续使用 · 3 天
深海回响
Token 回响 · 1M

初声相遇
累计对话 · 1 轮
月下鲸歌
节日限定 · 中秋
还有未被发现的航迹
隐藏典藏 · 等你探索
| 系列 | 当前内容 | | --- | --- | | 累计使用 | 1 / 7 / 30 / 100 天 | | 连续使用 | 3 / 7 / 30 / 100 天 | | Token 回响 | 10K / 100K / 1M / 10M | | 累计对话 | 1 / 10 / 50 / 200 轮 | | 节日限定 | 2026 元旦、春节、端午、中秋、国庆、程序员节 | | 隐藏典藏 | 6 枚设计，4 枚可自动识别；另外 2 枚等待宿主行为证据适配后启用 | **徽章会持续更新。** 后续将继续带来新的主题、进阶设计、节日限定与隐藏惊喜，并随 Harness 的能力演进完善识别规则。欢迎在 [Issues](https://github.com/ShawnRen57/dsh-whale-trail/issues) 提交喜欢的主题或新的成就点子，关注 [Releases](https://github.com/ShawnRen57/dsh-whale-trail/releases) 获取更新。 ## 安装 当前发布预构建安装包，无需自行编译，也不需要配置额外模型或 API Key。 1. 确认使用 **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2**。其他宿主版本尚未验证。 2. 从 [v0.2.4 Release](https://github.com/ShawnRen57/dsh-whale-trail/releases/tag/v0.2.4) 下载 `dsh-whale-trail-0.2.4.tgz`。 3. 在终端执行以下命令，将文件路径替换为实际下载位置： ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add 'file:/绝对路径/dsh-whale-trail-0.2.4.tgz' --ignore-scripts ``` macOS 上如果没有安装全局 `dsh` 命令，可以调用应用自带的 CLI： ```sh '/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh' plugin --profile desktop add 'file:/绝对路径/dsh-whale-trail-0.2.4.tgz' --ignore-scripts ``` 4. 重新启动 Harness，打开左下角 **用户信息 → 我的徽章**。 升级时安装新的 `.tgz` 并重启，原有本地进度会保留。若需禁用，可在 Harness 插件页操作；卸载插件可使用 `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-whale-trail --ignore-scripts`，本地徽章账本仍保留。 ## 怎么统计 **自动统计，历史数据会在初次安装徽章插件时同步。** 只统计能够核实的历史，重复扫描或重复导入不会叠加进度。 - **使用天数**：按固定时区中的自然日累计，一天多次使用只计一天。默认时区为 `Asia/Shanghai`。 - **连续使用**：同时记录最长连续和当前连续，当前连续允许从昨天接续到今天。 - **Token**：累计 Harness 正式记录的模型用量，不估算缺失记录。 - **对话轮次**：一次用户输入得到可见的 Agent 回复，并正常结束，计 1 轮；一条聊天可以累计多轮。多条排队输入合并为同一回合时只计 1 轮，工具调用、重试、失败、中止和后台自动续跑不单独计轮。 - **节日限定**：按文化日期判断，不按调休假期；当前内置 2026 年日历。 归档会话、手动确认和主动领取均不参与计数。更详细的事件规则和兼容边界见 [开发与实现说明](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)。 ## 备份与迁移 在“我的徽章”弹窗底部点击 **导出备份**，换设备时带走生成的 **`.dshbadge` 文件**。新设备安装插件后，使用相同档案和时区，选择 **导入备份**；先预览新增与重复记录，再确认合并。 默认数据保存在： ```text ~/.dsh-whale-trail/profiles/personal/whale-trail.sqlite ``` 插件只保存成就所需的最小事件特征，不保存提示词、回复正文、附件、API 密钥或登录凭据。备份为明文元数据文件；当前提供手动迁移，不提供自动云同步。日常迁移请使用 `.dshbadge`，不要直接同步运行中的 SQLite 文件。 ## 开发与反馈 插件包含 Host 统计服务、账户菜单入口与徽章弹窗。原始 PNG、256px PNG 和 WebP 分别保存在 `assets/badges/`、`assets/png-256/` 与 `assets/web/`。 构建、测试、配置和已知边界见 [开发说明](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)。发现问题或想投稿徽章主题，请提交 [Issue](https://github.com/ShawnRen57/dsh-whale-trail/issues)，附上 Harness 版本、插件版本与复现方式。 源代码与原创 AI 辅助生成物料一并公开；当前包的许可声明为 `UNLICENSED`，尚未授予开源许可证。
