evidence.readmeExcerpt:
Your coding agents stop re-debugging what you already fixed.

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 39 more agents already save every session to disk. deja indexes all of it, months back, and hands the part that matters to whichever agent is working now.

English | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Español | Português | Français | Deutsch | Русский | Türkçe | हिन्दी

Nobody searched anything — the agent called deja itself. Two real runs against a synthetic corpus: nobody's history is published.

```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/main/install.sh | sh deja install --auto ```

macOS and Linux; ten seconds to install, about ten to index · Windows, Homebrew, npm and the rest

Recall
97.2% R@5 on LongMemEval-S
MemPalace publishes 96.6%, agentmemory 95.2%		 Tokens
half the tokens of agentmemory
on a task this machine had already solved		 Index time
17.6 s to index 19,195 sessions
the next of seven tools takes 72 s

I maintain deja-vu, so every driver, the corpus and the scoring rule are in this repository · the head-to-head, and how to re-run a row you doubt · every run

Docs · Benchmarks · How it compares · Building it into your tool

Found it useful? Star deja-vu on GitHub.

## Search it yourself `deja` with no arguments in a terminal opens a search over every agent's history. It starts on the sessions behind your uncommitted change, then the recent ones in this project, and the list narrows as you type.

- `↑↓` picks a session, `↵` opens it at the match, `n` and `N` step through the matches, `esc` goes back. Inside a session, `/` finds a word and `]` `[` jump between the turns you asked. - The box takes filters: an agent with a colon (`codex:`), `today`, `yesterday`, `week`, `month`, and `in:`. - `r` resumes the session in the agent that wrote it. `o` continues it in any other agent, which starts with what the session asked, decided and left open. - `tab` switches between this project, all projects and Deleted, the sessions their agent deleted that deja still holds; `R` puts one back. - `D` erases a session from its agent and from deja, after asking (`deja delete ` from a script). - `?` lists every key, `^k` has the rest (copy the session id or project path, forget a session), `q` quits from the list; `esc` steps back and quits from an empty search box. With `DEJA_TUI=0` it prints the text summary instead, which is also `deja brief`. Piped, it prints what is indexed and which command to run next. ## Highlights - **Starts full.** Months of history from before you installed it are searchable on day one: `deja "connection pool exhausted"` over gigabytes. - **One memory, every agent.** A fix found in Codex comes back in Claude Code, Cursor or opencode; all [forty-two agents](#supported-harnesses) read the same index. - **Nobody has to ask.** Recall arrives at session start, before a file is edited or a command runs, and after a command fails. - **Survives compaction.** Over 43 measured compactions the summary kept 77% of the decisions and 0.2% of the commands; deja hands back the rest ([how](docs/compaction.md)). - **Indexes the work, not just the talk.** The files each turn opened, the commands with their exit status, the exact spans an edit replaced. - **Knows what held.** `deja promote --state rejected` marks a reverted decision, and every later hit says it was tried and why it was dropped; `--state accepted` takes the mark back. - **Says when the ground moved.** A hit reports *4 files this session touched have changed since*, and stays quiet when it cannot tell. - **Local and private.** No model and no server; embeddings only if you turn on [semantic recall](#semantic-recall-optional). Keys and tokens are stripped as the index is built ([privacy](#privacy)). - **Moves with you.** `deja sync ssh laptop` between machines, no cloud in between; `deja handoff --to codex` to continue in another agent. - **One Go binary.** macOS, Linux and Windows, through Homebrew, Scoop, winget, npm or `go install`. ### Your own work, wrapped `deja stats --card` draws it in the terminal; give it a filename and it writes an SVG for a profile README. To post it anywhere else, [turn it into a PNG](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/card/) — that page converts it in your own browser.

The full feature reference lives in the [docs](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/). ## Install The two commands at the top are the whole install on macOS and Linux: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/main/install.sh | sh deja install --auto ``` The script puts the binary in `~/.local/bin`. If that directory is not on your `PATH` yet, the second command is not found in the same shell: run the `next:` line the script prints, which has the full path, or open a new shell once the `PATH` line is added.

Ten seconds to install, about ten to index, and it is useful. The second command wires MCP recall into every agent it finds, turns on session-start recall where the agent supports it, and builds the first index so the next session does not pay for it. Start a new agent session and ask it something you worked on months ago: > have we dealt with jwt refresh rotation before? check your memory It does not have to be asked, either — with auto-recall the agent already knows what you solved in that project when the session opens. To look for yourself, run `deja`.
Other ways to install, and what to do if you want less than all of it `brew install deja-vu`, `go install github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/cmd/deja@latest`, or `npx @vshulcz/deja-vu "query"` to try it without installing anything. Desktop apps that take MCP servers as bundles can open the `.mcpb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/releases/latest); it carries the binary. Claude Code, Cursor, Qwen and OpenClaw can take the same plugin bundle from their own marketplaces instead (Codex has a bundle of its own, in the table under [Harnesses with a package of their own](#harnesses-with-a-package-of-their-own)). Copilot CLI installs it too but takes only the skill, so use `deja install copilot-auto` there: ```sh claude plugin marketplace add vshulcz/deja-vu && claude plugin install deja-vu@deja-vu ``` On Windows the install script exits with `unsupported OS` — it is a shell script. Use Scoop, from the main bucket every Scoop install already has, or winget, which ships with Windows: ```powershell scoop install deja-vu winget install vshulcz.deja-vu ``` Or take `deja-vu__windows_amd64.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/releases/latest) and put `deja.exe` on your `PATH`, e.g. in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`. The binary alone is a complete install for searching: index, search, `show`, `ctx`, `blame`, `--json` and redaction need nothing else. `deja install` is what wires MCP into your agents and turns on session-start recall — worth having, and optional. On a binary-only setup `deja doctor` reports every MCP target as `config missing`, or `not-wired` where the agent is installed, which is that setup working as intended. `deja warmup` also leaves a skill at `~/.agents/skills/deja-search/SKILL.md` that teaches an agent the CLI contract — `deja search --json`, `ctx`, `blame`, how to read `tier` and `total` — so it knows history is searchable without MCP. The copy in the repo is [`skills/deja-search/SKILL.md`](skills/deja-search/SKILL.md). `deja install --all` is `--auto` without the session-start recall: agents answer from memory when they decide to call it, rather than starting each session with it. The [agent setup guide](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/agents.html) covers what each harness supports, aider's read-only context file, and the Windows `cmd /c deja mcp` wrapper.
What gets written into each agent's own guidance file Install also writes user-level guidance for the harnesses it detects: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Qwen, Kimi Code, pi, Senpi, Copilot, VS Code Copilot Chat, Goose, OpenClaw, Hermes, Roo Code, omp, Amp, prime-agent, DeepSeek Harness, Continue, Crush, CodeBuddy Code, WorkBuddy, Zed, TRAE CLI, TRAE IDE, Muse Code, CodeWhale, ZCode and Junie each get it in their own guidance file (or under the configured `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). Re-run rewrites deja's skill or marked block without changing surrounding user content. Use `deja install --all --no-guidance` to opt out; Grok Build and Devin CLI get the shared skill in `~/.agents/skills`, which is what they read; the `~/.grok/GROK.md` written beside it is for the unrelated community CLI that shares that directory. Cursor has no user-level instructions file, so it gets the shared skill in `~/.agents/skills` — one of the four places Cursor reads skills from — read only when something looks relevant rather than every session. Kilo Code, gajae-code, Kimchi, Command Code, Cherry Studio and Reasonix get the skill, and Kiro the skill and a steering file, from their own install target.
## Privacy Indexing and search are local. The network is used only by `deja update`, `deja sync ssh`, the version check in `deja doctor`, `deja embed` against an endpoint you configure (and, once it has built the semantic sidecar, each search, which sends the query to that endpoint), and a once-a-day look at the latest release from an interactive command. That look sends no session data; `DEJA_OFFLINE=1` turns it off, and so does `DEJA_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE` set to any value, which also hides the note a new version prints on its first run. Credentials are stripped as the index is built: cloud and provider keys, tokens and JWTs, PEM blocks, passwords in URLs or stated in prose. Each becomes `[redacted:]` and the text around it stays searchable. The source transcripts still hold them ([one machine had 84 in 42 sessions](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/credentials-in-transcripts.html)): `deja secrets` names those sessions without printing a value, and `deja secrets --scrub` rewrites the ones it can, keeping the original beside the file. `deja forget` drops sessions and keeps them dropped across rebuilds. `~/.config/deja/exclude` skips a project per line, or a whole store with `harness:opencode`. The [security model](docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md) has the data flows and what redaction cannot catch. ## CLI Bare `deja` in a terminal opens [the search screen](#search-it-yourself). With a query, or any command below, it prints and exits: ```text $ deja "jwt refresh token" [claude] api · Jul 8 · 8f31c0a9 — 2 matches login started failing after refresh token rotation; jwt kid mismatch in tests fixed by reloading jwks cache after rotateKey and adding a clock-skew test [codex] web · Jul 1 · b77d91e2 — 1 match refresh token cookie needed SameSite=Lax in local callback flow ``` **Ask your history** | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `deja ` | Search every history. Multi-word is AND and quoted phrases require contiguous text; a query with no exact match then tries word forms and close spellings, which is where a substring reaches its word (`code` finds `opencode`). | | `deja` | In a terminal, the full-screen search above. `deja brief` prints the text summary instead: today's sessions, what deja served, recent work and a search to try. | | `deja wip` | What the last session in this directory was doing: the task, what it settled, the files in flight, the last command and whether it failed — derived from the transcript, not from a note someone remembered to write. | | `deja blame [:line]` | Which sessions discussed a file, what was decided, and why. With a line: the commit that last changed it, and the session that wrote that line or the text the commit replaced. `--attribution` prints the line answer alone, as JSON with `--json`, and `--git-note` records it in `refs/notes/deja`. | | `deja files ` | The other direction: which files the work on a subject actually touched. | | `deja how ` | How this machine actually runs a thing, with the real flags, from what agents ran before. | | `deja fix ` | What this machine ran after that same error before, when the error did not come back. Never a merge, a force push or a deletion. | | `deja friction` | Errors that hit three or more separate sessions, with the harnesses named. | When the first word of a bare query has at least four characters and is one edit from a command name, deja names that command on stderr and then searches as usual. `deja search ` skips the suggestion.
Using what it finds, and moving it between machines **Use what it finds** | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `deja ctx ` | Markdown digest of the best match, with the code it changed, ready to pipe into a prompt. | | `deja recall ` | The page the MCP recall tool gives an agent: about 4 KB, this project first. For skills and scripts that run deja through the shell. | | `deja resume ` | Reopen a found session in its native harness. `--app` opens a Codex session in the ChatGPT desktop app. | | `deja restore ` | Hand back a span an agent replaced, from the `old_string` its edit recorded. Never writes over the original. | | `deja promote ` | Distill a session into a curated note with provenance, tags and a lifecycle state. Notes outrank raw transcripts. | | `deja share ` | A sanitized session digest for a colleague, with secrets already scrubbed. | **Move it and check it** | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `deja sync export/import/ssh` | Move memory between machines. Watermarked, append-only, idempotent. | | `deja view` | Your whole memory as one local HTML file. No server, and the file never leaves the machine. | | `deja stats` | Your agent work, wrapped. `--card` draws it in the terminal, `--card .svg` writes one for a profile, `--html` a browsable timeline. | | `deja secrets [--scrub]` | Which sessions' source transcripts carry credentials, and what kind. Never prints a value. `--scrub` rewrites the ones it can, original kept beside the file. | | `deja rules [sync]` | Keep your standing rules in `~/.config/deja/rules.md`; `sync` copies them as a marked block into every installed agent's global rules file. | | `deja rules candidates [--json] [--limit n] [--since 90d]` | The turns where you corrected an agent, across every tool, numbered with their session. Ask your agent to suggest rules and it groups them; nothing is written until you pick. | | `deja doctor [--deep]` | Self-diagnosis, and with `--deep`, proof of the index against the sources. | | `deja mcp` | The stdio MCP server, which is what `deja install` wires in. |
Full reference: [commands](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/commands.html) and [JSON output](docs/json-output.md). ### MCP tools The server exposes one tool, `deja`, with a `mode`; `deja install` wires it in. One tool costs 477 tokens of definitions a turn, against 8,283 for the largest of the seven servers measured in [day zero](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/day-zero.html). The six older tool names (`recall`, `recall_context`, `blame`, `fix`, `how`, `remember`) still answer.
Arguments and return shapes | Tool | Arguments | Returns | | --- | --- | --- | | `deja` | `mode`, `q`, `harness?`, `project?`, `limit?` | Depends on the mode, below. | `q` carries whatever the mode asks about. The per-mode names below are still accepted; they are no longer declared, because the schema is read every turn whether or not the tool is called. | Mode | `q` is | Also reads | Returns | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `recall` | the question, or an exact error string, name or flag | `harness?`, `limit?`, `offset?` | Dense matching snippets, capped at 4KB. | | `context` | the same as recall | `harness?` | Markdown digest of the best-matching session, with the code it changed. | | `blame` | a file path | `harness?`, `project?`, `since?`, `limit?`, `all?` | Sessions that discussed a file. | | `fix` | the failing output, verbatim | `limit?` | What this machine ran, or changed, after that same error before. | | `how` | the tool or target, e.g. `go test` | `project?`, `limit?` | The real invocation, from what agents ran here. | | `orient` | nothing — it asks about the project | `project?`, `limit?` | The commands past sessions ran here and the files they worked in. | | `remember` | one durable fact or decision | `project?`, `tags?` | Stores a durable decision for later recall. | | `handoff` | a session id or harness name; empty for the newest session here | `harness?` | Another session's goal, standing instructions, latest conclusions, passed checks and where it stopped, to continue it. |

TRAE IDE is wired, not read: its chats are in an encrypted database. `deja install trae-ide` adds the MCP server and the skill, and `trae-ide-auto` adds hooks, which TRAE IDE runs only after you turn them on in Settings > Hooks. Custom store locations go through `DEJA_*_ROOT` variables, and each agent's own relocation variable is honored too. The [session format registry](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/registry/README.html) documents the observed paths, record schemas and role mapping per harness, with synthetic fixtures keeping those descriptions checked against the parsers. ### Harnesses with a package of their own `deja install --auto` wires every one of these like every other harness, and that stays the shortest path. They also have a package in their own ecosystem, for people who install extensions there rather than from a CLI: | Harness | Package | Install | | --- | --- | --- | | opencode | npm `opencode-deja` | `opencode plugin opencode-deja` | | DeepSeek Harness | npm `dsh-deja` | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-deja` | | Zed | `deja-context-server` | Zed → Extensions → deja | | Kimi Code | plugin `deja` | `/plugins install https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu` | | Codex CLI | plugin `deja-vu` | `codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu` then `codex plugin add deja-vu@deja-vu` | | Grok Build | plugin `deja` | `grok plugin marketplace add vshulcz/deja-vu` then `grok plugin install deja` | | OpenClaw | ClawHub and npm `@vshulcz/openclaw-deja` | `openclaw plugins install clawhub:@vshulcz/openclaw-deja` | | pi (and omp) | npm `@vshulcz/pi-deja` | `pi install npm:@vshulcz/pi-deja` | | Hermes | memory provider `deja-memory`, in the Hermes plugin catalog | `hermes plugins install deja-vu`, or from GitHub: `hermes plugins install vshulcz/deja-vu/extensions/hermes` | Either path works alone, and both together double nothing: each package reads what `deja install` already wrote and uses the deja you already have. In a [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) project, an extension adds `/speckit.deja-vu.recall`, which searches past sessions for the feature before you implement it: ```sh specify extension add deja-vu --from https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/releases/latest/download/deja-spec-kit.zip ``` The same search is also a skill, for any agent that loads a `SKILL.md`: ```sh npx skills add https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu --skill deja-search # skills CLI: Claude Code, Cursor, Goose, Copilot… openclaw skills install @vshulcz/deja-search # ClawHub hermes skills install vshulcz/deja-vu/skills/deja-search # Hermes ``` The skill drives the `deja` binary from the install step above; it does not bundle one. ## Semantic recall (optional) Point `deja embed` at a local Ollama, LM Studio or OpenAI-compatible endpoint with `DEJA_EMBED_URL` and rephrased queries still hit. Without a reachable runtime, lexical search and MCP recall continue unchanged. OpenAI Platform works with its standard key: ```sh export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...' export DEJA_EMBED_URL='https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings' export DEJA_EMBED_MODEL='text-embedding-3-small' deja embed ```
Local runtimes, other endpoints, and what vectors cost With no `DEJA_EMBED_URL` set, deja probes `localhost:11434` and `localhost:1234`, so a machine already running Ollama or LM Studio is picked up without being asked. `DEJA_EMBED_OFF=1`, or `DEJA_EMBED_URL=off`, turns that probe off — any other configured `DEJA_EMBED_URL` still wins. For another authenticated OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set `DEJA_EMBED_KEY` explicitly: ```sh export DEJA_EMBED_URL='https://example.com/v1/embeddings' export DEJA_EMBED_MODEL='embedding-model' export DEJA_EMBED_KEY='...' deja embed ``` `DEJA_EMBED_KEY` takes precedence. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is used automatically only for an HTTPS `api.openai.com` URL; it is never implicitly sent to local or third-party endpoints. Models trained with instruction prefixes, such as the multilingual E5 family, need them on both sides. `DEJA_EMBED_QUERY_PREFIX` goes in front of every search query and `DEJA_EMBED_PASSAGE_PREFIX` in front of every indexed text; both are empty by default: ```sh export DEJA_EMBED_MODEL='multilingual-e5-small' export DEJA_EMBED_QUERY_PREFIX='query: ' export DEJA_EMBED_PASSAGE_PREFIX='passage: ' deja embed ``` The passage prefix is part of the sidecar's model name, so changing it embeds everything again, and search ignores vectors made with another model or prefix (it says so once). The sidecar sits beside the index as `.vectors.bin`, not inside `index.db`. Float32 vectors cost roughly 4 MB per 1k messages for a 1,024 dimension model. A remote endpoint receives the redacted indexed text, truncated to about 2k characters, but never raw source files. With Ollama or LM Studio, embedding stays local and needs no key.
## Proof Millisecond lookups, and on LongMemEval-S 88.1% hit@1 (470-question cleaned set) and 87.4% hit@1 on all 500 questions; on LoCoMo retrieval, 70.5% hit@1. On a task this machine had already solved, 58% fewer tokens: eleven runs an arm, 53,558 against 126,222 with nothing wired, and 52,815 against 103,443 on a later build with the arms alternated. Both retrieval harnesses ship in this repo and run on the public datasets in minutes: [benchmarks](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/benchmarks.html) · [what one task costs](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/day-zero.html). The rest is measured by `deja bench`: ```sh deja bench recall # ranking floor: 100 queries, half Russian, CI fails if recall drops deja bench context # 30 seeded task chains plus five negative controls deja bench block # does the answer survive into what deja hands over deja bench prompt # what the per-prompt hook fires on, and what it fires on wrongly deja bench ingest # what an update costs: unchanged, a turn, a new transcript, a rename, a rewrite deja bench read # what it costs to read a database-backed store, and what one long value does to it ```
What the in-repo benches measure, and lookup cost on a real store `bench block` asks the question the others cannot: with the right session in hand, does the block carry wh

# dsh-mcp-expose **Turn your DeepSeek Harness into an MCP server** — hand another agent (Codex, WorkBuddy, Claude Code, Cursor, n8n, anything that speaks MCP) either the whole Harness or exactly **one conversation you pick in the UI**. A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) plugin. No extra process, no extra port, no bridge: it registers routes on the Harness Web server and speaks **MCP Streamable HTTP** on the same origin as the GUI. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-mcp-expose)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-mcp-expose) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](./LICENSE) ![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.19-blue) **English | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md)** --- ## Why DeepSeek Harness already is a full agent runtime: model routing, shell, filesystem, web, skills, subagents, MCP clients, sandbox and approval policy. If you also run Codex or WorkBuddy, you end up with two agents that cannot see each other's work. This plugin closes that gap in the smallest possible way: - **Runtime endpoint** — `/mcp/dsh` exposes the whole Harness. The caller passes a `session_id` to continue an existing conversation or omits it to start a new one. - **Session endpoints** — `/mcp/dsh/` exposes *one* session. It is a different MCP server per session, and there is no way to reach any other session through it. Use it when you want to give a client a narrowly scoped capability instead of the keys to the whole machine. Both surfaces are the same code path an ordinary DSH session uses, so the delegated agent gets your model, tools, workspace, sandbox mode and permission policy. ## Requirements - DeepSeek Harness `0.2.x` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`), desktop app or `dsh web`. - Node.js `>= 22.19` (the version the Harness itself runs on). - An MCP client that supports **Streamable HTTP** (sometimes called "HTTP" or "streamable" transport). stdio-only clients can bridge with `mcp-remote`. ## Install ```bash # add it to the profile that should host it (the desktop app's profile is "desktop") npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-mcp-expose ``` Then restart the Harness (close the desktop app and reopen it, or restart `dsh web`). The plugin registers its routes on startup, so a restart is what makes them live.
No npm registry? Install straight from GitHub Installing by path works without any registry account, and is also how you work on the plugin itself: ```bash git clone https://github.com/wangpeng123-ux/dsh-mcp-expose.git npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-mcp-expose ``` `dsh` resolves plugin specs through npm/pnpm, so a GitHub spec usually works too: ```bash npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:wangpeng123-ux/dsh-mcp-expose ``` Or run it without touching any profile at all: ```bash npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web --patch /path/to/dsh-mcp-expose/cordis.patch.yml ``` To update a clone-based install later: `git pull` in the checkout and restart.
### Verify With the Harness running, open the URL it printed and go to **Settings → Plugins → 「MCP 服务器」** (the "MCP server" tab). The page lists every visible session, exports the ones you choose, and shows the endpoint each one gets. Prefer curl? The same data comes from the control API: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh/api ``` The port is whatever the Harness Web UI uses — take it from the URL the Harness printed, or from the settings page. ## Use ### 1. Pick what to expose | What you want | What to do | Endpoint | |---|---|---| | The whole Harness | nothing — it is on by default | `http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh` | | One specific conversation | Settings page → 「导出」, or the 「导出 MCP」 button in that session's header | `http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh/` | Exporting is instant and reversible: 「取消导出」 makes the URL answer `404` immediately, without deleting the session or its transcript. Exports persist across restarts in `~/.dsh/mcp-expose/exports.json`. ### 2. Connect an MCP client **Codex** (`~/.codex/config.toml`) — whole Harness: ```toml [mcp_servers.dsh] url = "http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh" startup_timeout_sec = 30 tool_timeout_sec = 900 ``` **Codex** — just one conversation: ```toml [mcp_servers.dsh_web_project] url = "http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh/session-49def6c7-d76f-429c-8871-dfdea254a481" tool_timeout_sec = 900 ``` **Claude Code / any `mcp.json` client:** ```json { "mcpServers": { "dsh": { "type": "http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh" } } } ``` **WorkBuddy / stdio-only clients** — bridge the same endpoint: ```bash npx -y mcp-remote http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh ``` If you configured a `token`, add `Authorization: Bearer ` (or `?token=`); the Codex equivalent is `bearer_token_env_var = "DSH_MCP_TOKEN"`. ### 3. Delegate ``` dsh_run prompt="in this repo, add a CHANGELOG entry for 1.2.0 and run the tests" dsh_run prompt="what did we decide about the retry policy?" session_id="session-49de…" ``` `dsh_run` blocks until the turn ends and returns the assistant's final answer. The repository, shell and tools it uses are all inside your Harness workspace, so the result is real work, not a suggestion. ## Tools The **runtime endpoint** exposes seven tools: | Tool | Arguments | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `dsh_run` | `prompt`, `session_id?`, `cwd?`, `timeout_ms?`, `provider?`, `model?` | Delegate one task; continue a session or start a new one. | | `dsh_sessions` | `limit?` | List sessions, newest activity first. | | `dsh_history` | `session_id`, `limit?`, `max_text_chars?` | Read a transcript: user prompts, answers, tool calls and results. | | `dsh_tools` | `query?` | List the tools a delegated agent can call, from its preset scope. | | `dsh_models` | — | Routable providers/models and the deployment default. | | `dsh_cancel` | `session_id` | Cancel the running turn, keeping the history. | | `dsh_status` | — | Endpoint, process, model, presets, capability and auth summary. | A **session endpoint** exposes four: | Tool | Arguments | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `dsh_run` | `prompt`, `timeout_ms?` | Always drives *that* session — there is no `session_id` parameter. | | `dsh_history` | `limit?`, `max_text_chars?` | That session's transcript only. | | `dsh_cancel` | — | Cancel that session's running turn. | | `dsh_info` | — | Title, workspace, liveness and turn state of that session. | Resources and prompts are advertised as empty; tools are the exposed surface. ## The plugin UI The plugin ships a browser half (no build step, two slots): - **Settings → Plugins → 「MCP 服务器」** — the full page: runtime endpoint with a copy button, the list of exported sessions with their URLs, and every visible session with a filter box and an 「导出」/「取消导出」 toggle. - **Session header → 「导出 MCP」** — one-click export/revoke for the conversation you are reading, plus 「复制地址」 once it is exported. A green dot marks exported sessions. Both talk to the same-origin control API below; the page never constructs MCP traffic itself. ## Control API Not MCP — a small JSON API for the UI (and for scripts). It follows the same auth rule as the MCP routes. ```http GET /mcp/dsh/api ``` ```json { "ok": true, "origin": "http://127.0.0.1:57787", "runtimeEndpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh", "auth": "loopback-only", "sessions": [ { "session_id": "session-49def6c7-…", "title": "MCP plugin", "running": true, "live": true, "blank": false, "cwd": "C:\\Users\\me\\Documents\\project", "updatedAt": 1792407838229, "exported": false, "endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:57787/mcp/dsh/session-49def6c7-…" } ] } ``` ```http POST /mcp/dsh/api { "action": "export" | "revoke" | "refresh", "sessionId": "session-49def6c7-…" } ``` → `{ "ok": true, "state": }` `sessions[].endpoint` is always the URL that session *would* use, so you can write a client config before exporting anything; `exported` says whether it currently answers. ## Configuration | Field | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `path` | `/mcp/dsh` | Base route on the Harness Web server. Session endpoints live under it. | | `token` | `''` | Bearer token. Empty means **loopback callers only**. | | `defaultCwd` | `''` | Working directory for new sessions; empty uses the Harness default directory. | | `defaultPreset` | `''` | Agent preset for new sessions; empty uses the registry default (see `dsh_status`). | | `maxPromptWaitMs` | `600000` | Default `dsh_run` budget when the caller sends no `timeout_ms`. | Override them in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (usually `~/.dsh/profiles//cordis.patch.yml`): ```yaml - id: dsh-mcp-expose config: token: 'your-long-random-token' defaultPreset: standard ``` The plugin ships no settings form, so this file is the configuration surface. ## How it works ``` MCP client (Codex / WorkBuddy / …) │ POST /mcp/dsh POST /mcp/dsh/ ▼ ▼ dsh-mcp-expose ── JSON-RPC over Streamable HTTP ──┐ │ exports registry (~/.dsh/mcp-expose/exports.json) │ │ └──────────────► ctx.agents / session log ◄─────┘ │ ▼ DSH agent loop → model, tools, sandbox, approvals ``` - One `exact` route (runtime), one `prefix` route (session endpoints), one `exact` route for the control API. - The transport is **stateless**: no `Mcp-Session-Id`, notification-only POSTs answer `202`, `GET`/`DELETE` answer `405`, batches and request-scoped SSE are supported. - `dsh_run` admits a real user message into the session log, waits for the turn to start, then waits for the agent to go idle (or for `timeout_ms`). ## Security - **Loopback by default.** With no `token`, every route accepts only `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, so a hostile page cannot reach it through DNS rebinding. Set `token` before exposing the Harness on a non-loopback interface. - **The caller acts as you.** `dsh_run` can read and write files and run commands under your Harness permission policy. Point a client here only if you would give it the same access to a DSH terminal. - **`dsh_run` cannot approve itself.** An approval prompt still goes to the Harness UI, exactly as for a human turn. - **A session endpoint is a capability URL.** Anyone who can reach the route and knows the session id can continue that conversation. Revoke the export when you are done. ## Limitations - Stateless transport: a client that insists on a server-initiated SSE session cannot use it (request-scoped SSE is fine). - `dsh_run` waits for idleness, so a long turn can exceed a client-side tool timeout. Raise the client timeout or pass a smaller `timeout_ms`. - No sampling, elicitation, resources or prompts. - Session endpoints are single-session by construction. For a second conversation, export that session too — or use the runtime endpoint. ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint

**Session-aware task checkpoints for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).**
Go back to a milestone and both halves come back: the files *and* the agent
context that produced them.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **What it is** | an MCP server (nine tools) plus a small browser badge, installed as one DSH plugin bundle |
| **What a checkpoint holds** | the exact working tree (as a git tree object) **and** a digest of the DSH session — plan, recent messages, tool usage |
| **File storage** | native `git` CLI, in your own repository; the plugin invents no new file format |
| **Context storage** | JSON sidecars under `.dsh-checkpoint/` in the workspace |
| **Destructive operations** | always two-phase: a human-confirmed, single-use token is required |
| **Network** | none. Local only, no telemetry, no push/pull/fetch |
| **Requires** | Node.js ≥ 20, `git` ≥ 2.23 (recommended), a DSH build with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` |

Contents: [The problem](#the-problem) · [Feature tour](#feature-tour) ·
[How it works](#how-it-works) · [Quick start](#quick-start) ·
[Using it in a session](#using-it-in-a-session) · [The commit badge](#the-commit-badge-in-the-web-ui) ·
[Tool reference](#tool-reference) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Storage](#storage-layout) ·
[Safety model](#safety-model) · [Rollback](#rollback-semantics) ·
[Context capture](#agent-context-capture) · [Errors](#error-reference) ·
[Development](#development) · [Limitations](#limitations-and-roadmap)

---

## The problem

A coding session is not just a pile of files. It is files **plus** a direction:
the plan the agent is following, the decisions it just made, the command output
that justified them.

Snapshot tools that only copy files lose the second half. Roll back to “before
the refactor” and the files return, but the conversation has moved on — the agent
starts the milestone from a blank slate and re-discovers what it already knew.

`dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint` treats the pair as one unit:

```
checkpoint = { git tree of the working directory } + { digest of the DSH session }
                    ↑                                        ↑
          restored by git                     handed back to the agent in the tool
          (files, exactly as they were)       result, and kept on disk as a sidecar
```

## Feature tour

### 1. Draft snapshots that never touch your branch

`create_draft_checkpoint` captures the whole working tree into a git tree object
and a **dangling commit**, anchored under `refs/dsh-checkpoint/drafts/<id>` so
garbage collection cannot prune it. `HEAD` never moves, nothing is staged in your
real index, and `git status` looks exactly as it did a moment before.

Each draft records the changed files with their status, a diff (inline, or a
`.patch` sidecar when huge), a byte-capped context digest, the workspace, the
branch, the base commit, and an id such as `draft-1792582824171-fb62938a`.

### 2. Preview before you commit to it

`preview_checkpoint` shows one checkpoint in full — title, remark, tags,
timestamps, file list, unified diff, context digest (plan progress, last user
request, tools used) and the bound commit hash (empty for drafts).
`list_checkpoints` gives the newest-first index, filterable by tags, by free-text
query, or restricted to confirmed snapshots.

### 3. Confirmation turns a draft into a real commit

`confirm_checkpoint` is the only code path in the plugin that commits:

```
git add --all
git commit --no-verify -m "<message>"
```

The commit hash is written back into the checkpoint record, the draft is retired,
and its `draft-…` id keeps resolving to the confirmed record. If the working tree
or `HEAD` drifted since the draft was taken, the confirm is **refused** with a
conflict report instead of quietly committing a mixture.

### 4. Rollback restores files *and* re-hands the context to the agent

`rollback_checkpoint` first refuses to run on a dirty working tree — uncommitted
work is never discarded. On a clean tree it restores a confirmed checkpoint with
`git reset --hard <commit>`, or a draft with `git read-tree --reset -u` (files
only; the branch does not move, because a draft was never a commit). The result
carries the stored context digest and the restored plan, and tells the agent to
treat it as authoritative and to re-read files from disk.

### 5. Branch off a checkpoint instead of losing work

`create_branch` starts a branch at a checkpoint commit (or at `HEAD`) so an
alternative can be explored without disturbing the current one; `switch_branch`
moves between them. Both are plain local git operations with validation —
nothing is pushed anywhere.

### 6. The commit badge — and enabling checkpoints from the UI

Every finalized reply in the DSH web UI gets a quiet pill showing the workspace
HEAD (`⎇ main 4e850e7`), a `*` when the tree is dirty, and a `⚑` when that commit
is a confirmed checkpoint. In a project that is not a git repository yet, the pill
becomes a dashed **⚙ Enable checkpoints** control that initialises the project —
behind a second click and a server-side `confirm=1` check.
[Details below.](#the-commit-badge-in-the-web-ui)

### Why not just `git stash` / `git commit` / tags?

| Plain git | This plugin |
| --- | --- |
| You must remember to commit, or stash and forget | Drafts are cheap, anchored, and never disturb `HEAD` |
| A stash has no plan, no conversation, no rationale | Each draft carries a session digest: plan, recent messages, tool usage |
| Restoring files leaves the agent amnesiac | Rollback returns the context digest into the agent's context window |
| `git reset --hard` discards uncommitted work | Rollback refuses on a dirty tree and reports the files instead |
| Committing is one keystroke away for an agent | Committing needs a payload-bound, single-use token the operator approved |
| Nothing links git history to “which milestone” | Confirmed checkpoints annotate the history the badge reads |

## How it works

One npm package, two halves, mounted by a profile bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`):

```
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  Agent ──────────────▶ │  MCP stdio server            │
  (nine tools)          │  dist/index.js               │
                        └───────┬──────────┬───────────┘
                                │          │
                     ┌──────────┘          └───────────┐
                     ▼                                 ▼
            system git CLI                    .dsh-checkpoint/
            (trees, commits,                  (records, context
             refs, branches)                   sidecars, tokens)
                     ▲                                 ▲
                     │                                 │
  Browser badge ─────┴──── host plugin  ◀──────────────┘
  (client.js)              dist/host.js
        │                        │
        └── GET /api/agent-checkpoint/git ──────┐
            POST /api/agent-checkpoint/init ────┘

  DSH session log (read-only) ──▶ context capture ──▶ .dsh-checkpoint/contexts/
```

- **The MCP server owns writes.** Nine tools, spawned over stdio by
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`, exposed to the agent as
  `mcp__agent-checkpoint__<tool>`.
- **The host plugin owns two loopback routes.** The browser cannot run git, so
  the badge asks the host half; the git route never commits, stages or resets,
  and both routes are loopback-only.
- **The browser half is a slot registration**, not a separate app: a
  `__ModuleLoader__` bundle that renders into
  `conversation.chat.assistant-actions`.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone git@github.com:wiley7/dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint.git
cd dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint
pnpm install
pnpm run build                 # emits dist/ (host half + MCP server)
node dist/index.js --help      # sanity check the server half
```

`git` must already be on `PATH`; the plugin never installs or bundles it.

### Register with DSH

| Half | Composited entry | What it contributes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP server | `agent-checkpoint-mcp` → `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` | the nine tools, spawned over stdio |
| Host plugin | `agent-checkpoint` → `dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint` | the loopback routes the badge reads |

**Option A — install as a bundle (recommended).** A profile's user layer can only
patch entries that already exist, so a bundle is the supported path:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint
# or, once published:  add dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so DSH records it in
`dsh.profile.bundles` and applies `cordis.patch.yml` on the next boot. Restart
DSH: the tools appear as `mcp__agent-checkpoint__*` and the badge appears under
every finalized assistant reply.

Workspace resolution, highest priority first: an explicit tool argument →
`?workspace=` on the route → the **cwd of the session being viewed** (read from
its log header) → the entry config → `$DSH_AGENT_CHECKPOINT_WORKSPACE` →
`$DSH_WORKSPACE` → the directory DSH was launched from. To pin both halves:

```bash
export DSH_AGENT_CHECKPOINT_WORKSPACE=/absolute/path/to/your/project
```

Or override the entries in the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` — note that an
override **replaces** the whole `config` object, so repeat every key:

```yaml
- id: agent-checkpoint
  config:
    workspace: /absolute/path/to/your/project

- id: agent-checkpoint-mcp
  config:
    transport: stdio
    serverName: agent-checkpoint
    command: node
    args:
      - !!js decodeURIComponent(new URL('node_modules/dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint/dist/index.js', baseUrl).pathname)
      - "--workspace"
      - /absolute/path/to/your/project
    cwd: /absolute/path/to/your/project
    toolCallTimeoutMs: 120000
    failOnStartupError: true
```

`baseUrl` inside `!!js` is the profile directory, so the first argument resolves
to the installed copy of the server.

**Option B — insert the entries by hand** (without installing the package into
the profile):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: agent-checkpoint
      name: dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint
      config:
        workspace: /absolute/path/to/your/project
    - id: agent-checkpoint-mcp
      name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client"
      config:
        transport: stdio
        serverName: agent-checkpoint
        command: node
        args:
          - "/absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint/dist/index.js"
          - "--workspace"
          - "/absolute/path/to/your/project"
        cwd: "/absolute/path/to/your/project"
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 120000
        failOnStartupError: true
```

A bare `- id: …` entry at the top level does **not** work: entries without
`insert:` only override entries that already exist. Drop the host entry if you
want the tools without the badge — the MCP half works on its own, including in
`headless` profiles where no web server exists.

### Verify the registration

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A 12 agent-checkpoint   # both entries present
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/agent-checkpoint/git' | head -c 400
```

If the MCP server fails to start, DSH reports the spawn error at boot; run it by
hand (`node dist/index.js --workspace <project>`) to read its own diagnostics.

## Using it in a session

A milestone looks like this. The operator (or the agent, at a milestone boundary)
takes a draft; the operator reviews it; confirming produces a real commit.

```
init_workspace                                  # once per project
  └─ create_draft_checkpoint "login flow done"  # cheap, does not commit
       └─ preview_checkpoint <draft-id>         # operator reviews diff + context
            └─ confirm_checkpoint <draft-id> "feat: login flow"   # needs a token
                 └─ … next milestone …
                      └─ rollback_checkpoint <ckpt-id>            # needs a token
```

Two-phase confirmation, seen from the agent's side:

```jsonc
// 1st call — never destructive; it mints a token and returns a summary
{"draft_id": "draft-1792582824171-fb62938a", "commit_message": "feat: login flow"}
// → isError: true, status: "confirmation_required",
//   confirmation_id: "cfm-4f0c…", summary: "…", details: {…}, expires_at: "…"

// 2nd call — the same payload plus the token the operator approved
{"draft_id": "draft-1792582824171-fb62938a", "commit_message": "feat: login flow",
 "confirmation_id": "cfm-4f0c…"}
// → isError: false, status: "confirmed", commit_hash: "4e850e71be0a…",
//   checkpoint_id: "ckpt-1792582824171-9b2c9d71"
```

The token is bound to the exact payload by SHA-256: changing the draft id or the
message invalidates it (`confirmation_mismatch`), it expires after
`confirmation_ttl_seconds` (default 600 s), and it is consumed on use.

Every tool also accepts an optional absolute `workspace` argument, so one stdio
server can snapshot, roll back and branch several projects without a restart.

## The commit badge in the web UI

```
⎇ main 4e850e7 *    ⚑
```

- `4e850e7` — short hash of the workspace HEAD; **click copies the full hash**;
  the tooltip carries branch, subject, commit time, checkpoint id and workspace.
- `*` — the working tree has uncommitted changes, so the badge never implies the
  files match that commit.
- `⚑` — that commit is a **confirmed checkpoint**; hover for its title.

### Enabling checkpoints from the UI

In a project that is not a git repository yet, the pill becomes a dashed
**⚙ Enable checkpoints** control instead of disappearing:

1. **First click arms it** — nothing is written; it becomes an amber
   `Confirm setup` button plus a `✕` cancel, so a stray click initialises nothing.
2. **Second click** posts `POST /api/agent-checkpoint/init?session=<id>&confirm=1`.
3. The host half runs the same path as `init_workspace`: `git init
   --initial-branch=main` when needed, `.gitignore` defaults appended, the managed
   block written to `.git/info/exclude`, the `.dsh-checkpoint/` store created. The
   control then re-fetches and becomes the normal commit pill — no reload.

The control is only offered when the workspace came from the session being viewed
(`source: "session"`); for the `cwd` fallback DSH merely launched from, nothing is
shown — the plugin never offers to `git init` a directory the user did not point
at. A folder that lives inside another repository answers
`409 workspace_not_repository_root` and is left untouched.

### Route reference

| Aspect | `GET /api/agent-checkpoint/git` | `POST /api/agent-checkpoint/init` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose | read the badge snapshot | enable checkpoints for a project |
| Access | loopback only (`127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, `::ffff:` forms); else `403` | same |
| Methods | `GET`, `HEAD`; else `405` | `POST`; else `405` |
| Guard | none | `confirm=1` required, else `400 confirmation_required` and **no write** |
| Response | `{ ok, workspace, source, isRepo, branch, head, isDirty, commits[], capturedAt, error, warnings }` | `{ ok, workspace, created, gitVersion, branch, head, gitignoreUpdated, excludeUpdated, storePath, configPath, warnings, nextSteps }` |
| Caching | `cache-control: no-store` | same |
| Writes | none — never commits, stages or resets | working tree and `.git` (init, ignore rules, store) |
| Errors | `not_a_git_repo`, `invalid_workspace` | `confirmation_required`, `workspace_not_repository_root` (409) |

`GET` also accepts `?workspace=<path>` and `?limit=<n>`; the badge polls every
20 s (paused while the tab is hidden), shares one request per session, and
memoizes snapshots for 8 s. The route is read-only on purpose: a UI that could
move `HEAD` would make the “no destructive operation without confirmation”
guarantee meaningless.

The badge reports the *current* HEAD, not the commit that existed when each reply
was written. Per-reply attribution needs the per-turn timeline the route already
returns; it is a roadmap item, not a promise.

Badge configuration (entry config of the host half): `workspace` (fallback when a
request carries no `?session=`) and `maxCommits` (default `120`; requests clamp at
`500`). The browser half itself has no configuration — it registers into the
`conversation.chat.assistant-actions` list slot with id `agent-checkpoint-commit`
and order `60`, so it coexists with the built-in feedback buttons rather than
competing for the single `turnTail` chain slot.

## Tool reference

All nine tools are exposed as `mcp__agent-checkpoint__<name>`. Every one accepts
an optional `workspace` (absolute path of the project) in addition to the
arguments below. **Destructive** tools require the two-phase confirmation
described above.

### `init_workspace`
Prepares a project: checks git, initialises a repository when needed, appends the
plugin's `.gitignore` defaults, writes the managed `.git/info/exclude` block,
creates the store, and returns repository state plus next steps.
Arguments: `workspace_path?`. Idempotent.

### `create_draft_checkpoint`
Captures files **and** agent context without committing. Returns `draft_id`,
`files`, `diff_stat`, `diff`, `context_summary`, plus warnings. Refuses with
`nothing_to_checkpoint` when nothing changed and no context was captured.
Arguments: `title`, `tags?`, `remark?`.

### `preview_checkpoint`
Full view of one checkpoint: metadata, file list, diff, context digest, and the
commit hash it is bound to (`null` for drafts). Arguments: `checkpoint_id` (a
unique fragment is accepted), `include_diff?` (default `true`), `max_diff_chars?`
(default 12000, max 200000).

### `confirm_checkpoint` **(destructive)**
The first call returns a confirmation token and a summary; the second call
commits and returns `commit_hash` plus the confirmed `checkpoint_id`. Refuses with
a conflict report when `HEAD` moved or the working tree changed since the draft.
Arguments: `draft_id`, `commit_message`, `confirmation_id?`.

### `rollback_checkpoint` **(destructive)**
The first call returns a token and a summary; the second call restores files and
returns the context digest, the restored plan and rehydration instructions. Aborts
with `status: "conflict"` when the working tree is dirty.
Arguments: `checkpoint_id`, `confirmation_id?`.

### `list_checkpoints`
Newest-first index. Arguments: `tags_filter?` (all listed tags must match),
`limit?` (default 20, max 200), `include_drafts?` (default `true`), `query?`
(substring over title, remark, tags and context digest).

### `create_branch` / `switch_branch`
Local-only branch management. `create_branch` takes `branch_name` (validated with
`git check-ref-format`) and an optional `checkpoint_id` to start from;
`switch_branch` takes `branch_name`. `git switch` is used when available and
`git checkout` otherwise.

### `get_status`
Read-only report: repository status, branch, `HEAD`, dirty and untracked files,
draft/confirmed counts, effective policy, newest checkpoint, pending
confirmations, and hints. Takes no arguments besides `workspace`.

### Checkpoint ids

Stable, human-readable strings such as `draft-1792582824171-fb62938a` and
`ckpt-1792582824171-9b2c9d71`. Any unique fragment is accepted. After a draft is
confirmed, its `draft-…` id keeps resolving to the confirmed record through an
alias.

### CLI options

`node dist/index.js` is the MCP server half (normally spawned by DSH; useful
standalone for debugging):

```
dsh-plugin-agent-checkpoint [options]

  -C, --workspace <path>     workspace (git repository root) to manage
                             (default: $DSH_WORKSPACE or the current directory)
      --session-file <path>  read agent context from an explicit DSH session log
  -v, --version              print the version and exit
  -h, --help                 print this help and exit
```

`--session-file` is a testing/automation escape hatch: normally the plugin
discovers the session log from `$DSH_HOME` and `$DSH_SESSION_ID` itself.

## Configuration

Optional `checkpoint.config.json` in the workspace root. Missing fields fall back
to the defaults; invalid values produce warnings but never abort a tool call.

```json
{
  "auto_draft_on_milestone": true,
  "ignore_patterns": ["node_modules", ".venv", "dist", "build"],
  "max_draft_count": 10
}
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto_draft_on_milestone` | `true` | policy hint for the agent: draft at a milestone instead of every turn |
| `ignore_patterns` | `["node_modules", ".venv", "dist", "build"]` | extra patterns written to `.git/info/exclude`; `.dsh-checkpoint/` is always ignored |
| `max_draft_count` | `10` | drafts kept per workspace; the oldest is dropped beyond this (confirmed checkpoints are never dropped) |
| `max_context_message_chars` | `1200` | per-message truncation limit in the context snapshot |
| `max_context_messages` | `40` | messages kept per context snapshot |
| `max_context_bytes` | `524288` | hard cap per serialized context; oldest messages are dropped first |
| `max_diff_chars` | `100000` | inline diff cap; longer diffs go to `.dsh-checkpoint/diffs/` |
| `confirmation_ttl_seconds` | `600` | lifetime of a confirmation token |

Trigger policy: a user command such as `/checkpoint` always wins, an agent
marking a subtask complete comes second, and snapshotting every conversational
turn is **off** by default.

## Storage layout

```
<workspace>/
├── .dsh-checkpoint/                 # plugin store (git-ignored)
│   ├── drafts/<id>.json             # draft records
│   ├── checkpoints/<id>.json        # confirmed records
│   ├── contexts/<id>.json           # serialized agent context sidecars
│   ├── diffs/<id>.patch             # diffs too large to inline
│   ├── confirmations/<token>.json   # pending single-use tokens
│   ├── aliases/<draft-id>.json      # draft id → confirmed id
│   └── tmp-index                    # scratch index, deleted after each draft
└── .git/                            # file versions live in git, not here
    ├── info/exclude                 # managed ignore block
    └── refs/dsh-checkpoint/         # anchors keeping draft objects alive
```

File history is git's job. The plugin stores only what git cannot represent: the
context sidecars, the metadata, and the anchors that keep draft objects from being
pruned.

A record carries: `id`, `status` (`draft`/`confirmed`), `title`, `tags`, `remark`,
timestamps, workspace, branch, `base_commit`, `tree_hash`, `draft_commit`,
`commit_hash`, `parent_commit`, `files`, `diff_stat`, `diff` (or `diff_path`),
`context_path`, `context_summary`, `session_id` and `anchor_ref`.

## Safety model

- **Two-phase destructive operations.** `confirm_checkpoint` and
  `rollback_checkpoint` never act on the first call. They mint a single-use token
  (`cfm-<hex>`, TTL 600 s) bound to the exact payload via SHA-256, return a
  human-readable summary, and execute only when called again with that token.
- **No automatic conflict resolution.** Drifted working tree, moved `HEAD`, dirty
  rollback target — each returns a conflict list (`status: "conflict"`) with the
  affected files for the operator to resolve manually.
- **Uncommitted work is never discarded.** Rollback refuses on a dirty tree.
- **Drafts never touch `HEAD`.** Capture uses a scratch index
  (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=.dsh-checkpoint/tmp-index`) plus a dangling commit anchored by
  a ref, so the branch and the real index are untouched.
- **Built-in ignore defaults** live in a managed, clearly delimited block inside
  `.git/info/exclude`; existing user content is preserved.
- **No deletion of confirmed checkpoints** in this release; only the oldest drafts
  beyond `max_draft_count` are trimmed.
- **Loopback-only UI routes**, POST-only initialisation behind `confirm=1`.
- **Local only.** No network calls, no telemetry, no remote operations. Push,
  pull, fetch, pull requests and multi-user collaboration are out of scope.

## Rollback semantics

1. A confirmation token is required (see above).
2. The working tree must be clean. Otherwise the rollback aborts with
   `status: "conflict"`, `reason: "worktree_dirty"`, the modified and untracked
   files, and instructions.
3. Confirmed checkpoint → `git reset --hard <commit>` (the branch moves).
4. Draft checkpoint → `git read-tree --reset -u <draft commit>` (files return; the
   branch does **not** move, because a draft was never a commit).
5. The stored context sidecar is attached as a digest: plan progress, the last
   user request, captured message count and tool usage. The agent is told to treat
   that digest as the authoritative post-rollback state and to re-read files from
   disk before assuming their contents.

The plugin deliberately does **not** rewrite DSH's live session log
(`session.v4.jsonl.zstd`). That file is the harness's source of truth; rewriting it
while DSH has it mapped in memory would corrupt the session. Rehydration happens
through the tool result (which the agent sees in its own context window) plus the
sidecar on disk for later sessions.

## Agent context capture

`create_draft_checkpoint` reads the current DSH session log:

```
$DSH_HOME/sessions/<bucket>/session-<id>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd
```

Selection order: explicit `--session-file` → `$DSH_SESSION_ID` directory match
(validated against the log header) → the most recent log whose header `cwd`
matches the workspace. The log is zstd-compressed JSONL; records are parsed
defensively and unknown shapes are skipped with a warning. Decompression prefers
`node:zlib`'s zstd support and falls back to the `zstd` CLI.

Only meaningful context is kept:

- user messages with `source.kind === "user"` (runtime/time/model-selection
  injections and `<system-reminder>` blocks are dropped);
- assistant text and the names of the tools it called;
- the most recent `todo/write` plan;
- tool call/error counts.

Streaming payloads (`assistant/message` → `data.stream`), base64 blobs and data
URIs are never stored. Very long messages are truncated; when a payload exceeds
`max_context_bytes`, the oldest messages are dropped first. A missing session log
is not an error — the checkpoint still captures files and records a warning.

## Error reference

Tool failures return `isError: true` with a structured payload instead of crashing
the server:

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "code": "checkpoint_not_found", "message": "…", "details": {} } }
```

Confirmation challenges and conflicts are also `isError: true`, with
`status: "confirmation_required"` or `status: "conflict"` at the top level, so an
agent cannot mistake them for success.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `git_unavailable` | no `git` binary on `PATH` |
| `git_init_failed` | `git init` (or the ignore-rule scaffolding) failed |
| `not_a_git_repo` / `nested_repository` | workspace is not a repository / lives inside another one |
| `workspace_not_repository_root` | the target is a subdirectory of a repository |
| `nothing_to_checkpoint` | no file changes and no context to capture |
| `checkpoint_not_found` / `checkpoint_incomplete` | unknown id / record missing its tree |
| `already_confirmed` | the draft was already turned into a commit |
| `invalid_confirmation` / `confirmation_expired` / `confirmation_mismatch` | token unknown, expired, or bound to a different payload |
| `invalid_branch_name` / `branch_exists` / `branch_not_found` / `no_commits` / `switch_failed` | branch management failures |
| `internal_error` | an unexpected failure; the message carries the detail |

## Development

```bash
pnpm run typecheck   # tsc over src + tests, no emit
pnpm run build       # dist/ without tests
pnpm test            # builds, compiles tests, runs node:test
```

The suite covers the service against real temporary git repositories, the config
loader, the session-log reader (including zstd fixtures), the MCP transport itself
(it spawns `dist/index.js` and talks to it as a client), both loopback routes
(workspace resolution, timeline, method and loopback fences, the init guard) and
the browser bundle (loaded in a `node:vm` sandbox with a React shim, so slot wiring,
the display model and the init control are exercised without a DOM).
**73 tests, no network access, no writes outside the OS temp dir.**

```
src/index.ts      MCP stdio server (nine tools)
src/checkpoint.ts service: drafts, confirmation, rollback
src/host.ts       web host half: loopback git + init routes
src/session.ts    DSH session-log discovery and digest
src/git.ts        system git wrapper
src/store.ts      .dsh-checkpoint storage and confirmation tokens
client/client.js  browser half: commit badge (no build step)
```

## Limitations and roadmap

| Area | Today | Next |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Destructive ops | two-phase token | same, plus approving from the badge |
| Context rehydration | tool result digest + sidecar | survive a DSH restart by re-reading sidecars into a fresh session |
| Badge | current `HEAD` per reply | per-reply attribution from the per-turn timeline the route already returns |
| Branching | local create/switch | store export/backup, timeline UI, cross-workspace index |
| Out of scope | push/pull/fetch, remotes, collaboration, automatic conflict resolution, binary large-object handling, background scheduling, checkpoint deletion | — |

Known maintenance surfaces:

- **DSH session schema drift.** `session.v4` is a DSH implementation detail. If DSH
  bumps the version or reshapes records, context capture degrades to warnings
  (never to corrupted checkpoints) and the reader must be updated. This is the
  plugin's deliberate maintenance surface.
- **Draft staleness.** A draft captures a tree, not a promise. If files change or
  `HEAD` moves before confirmation, the confirm is refused — take a new draft.
- **Repository identity.** Without `user.name`/`user.email`, the plugin writes a
  repository-local placeholder identity so commits do not fail; set a real identity
  for real commits.
- **Client bundle contract.** `client/client.js` targets the DSH web slot API
  (`conversation.chat.assistant-actions`, `ctx.slots`

# @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy) [![GitHub Releases](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/wingsky-1/dsh-plugin-hub)](https://github.com/wingsky-1/dsh-plugin-hub/releases) 局域网访问 dsh web UI：在 `0.0.0.0:` 监听，把 HTTP/HTTPS 与 WebSocket/wss 转发到回环 web 服务器（默认 `127.0.0.1:3080`）。 **简体中文** | [English](README.en.md) ## 一键安装 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy ``` > 安装 / 卸载 / 更新后都需**重启一次** `dsh web`（bundle 层只在启动时组合）生效。 ## 快速导航 [使用前须知](#使用前须知) · [安全模型](#安全模型) · [最短上手](#最短上手) · [常用配置](#常用配置) · [验证与排障](#验证与排障) · [详细参考](#详细参考) · [开发与架构](#开发与架构) ## 使用前须知 前提：已安装 DeepSeek Harness 且 `dsh web` 可正常启动（未全局安装 dsh 见下方「未全局安装 dsh」）。 - 重写 Host/Origin 以通过 /api 浏览器信任围栏 - 仅接受 IP 字面量或 localhost 的 Host 头（**DNS 重绑定防护**） - HTTPS 默认并存（3443），证书可配置或自动生成自签名 ## 安全模型 - **出站目标白名单（L1）**：`targetHost` 仅允许回环地址（localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1），配置层与运行时入口双重校验——**防止开放转发/SSRF** - **DNS 重绑定防护**：只接受 Host 为 IP 字面量或 `localhost` 的请求，域名一律 403/断开；IP 字面量在任何端口都安全 - **凭据面**：dsh settings RPC 仅回环可读写；通过本插件访问的远程设备在 浏览器信任围栏内可读写服务器 settings（**含凭据类数据**）——确保你的局域网 可信，或禁用该插件 - **桥接头透传**：WS 桥接的上游连接透传入站头（Cookie 等认证凭据——dsh 0.1.2 起 `/api/remote.mux` 升级需 Cookie 认证，丢弃即 401 连不上），仅覆盖 Host/Origin 为回环目标、剥离 hop-by-hop 与 WS 握手专有头；上游被 `targetHost` 强制约束为回环，凭据只发往本机回环上游（不承诺跨进程隔离）。**压缩炸弹面**：桥接浏览器段 permessage-deflate 解压存在放大点（LAN 内恶意客户端高压缩比帧 → 代理进程 解压）——在「LAN 信任」威胁模型内可接受（与 injectToken 同一信任边界） - **私钥权限**：自动生成的自签名私钥落盘 0600；一键 CA 的 CA 私钥 + 叶子私钥 + .bak 一律 0600（write + chmodSync 双保险），certs/ 目录 0700 - **证书下发面（issue #911）**：下发路由只读给公钥（loopback 围栏 + 仅 GET + 无 Cookie 要求）。只伺服首个 CERTIFICATE 块，误指私钥一律 404；响应禁缓存。无 CA 时一律 404（自签/孤叶子装了建不起信任，不下发） - **一键 CA 动作面（issue #930）**：POST 只写（loopback 围栏 + POST 白名单 + settings 可写才可用）。CA 私钥文件名固定（ca-key.pem），永不进下发源；失败响应只出固定码（ca-generate-failed 等），路径与私钥原文只进服务端日志。默认轮换仅换叶子（CA 续用，已装设备零操作）；轮换 CA 为独立危险动作（已装设备信任全部失效，需逐台重装）。旧材料搬时间戳 .bak 只留最近 1 个 - **开放端口提醒**：0.0.0.0 监听对局域网所有设备可见 - **HTTP 响应压缩**：压缩在转发层完成，只作用于「本插件与局域网客户端之间」 的链路，不触碰 dsh web 的响应生成；不新增可达数据面，仅增加少量 CPU 开销 （可经 `httpCompressEnabled: false` 关闭）。health/标记路由的 loopback 围栏 对**直连回环 web** 的请求生效；经本插件转发的请求按设计视为受信（见凭据面）。 注意：health 响应携带的诊断元数据——`configDir` 绝对路径与压缩协商计数—— 会随转发原样到达局域网设备，对其可见 ### injectToken 自动注入（issue #380） dsh web 的浏览器会话认证（launch token + 持久签名 cookie）无法关闭，token 每次重启变化且只打印在本机终端——固定 局域网设备拿不到实时 token。本插件经官方 connection 服务的**公开 API** `authenticatedUrl()` 动态读取当前 token，仅在铸造入口（`GET /`、无会话 cookie） 自动补上：LAN 设备零操作进入。安全取舍与缓解： - **等效「信任整个局域网」**：开启后任何能网络到达本端口的客户端都免 token 获得完整 dsh 控制权（bash 直通宿主机）。仅在可信家庭/办公内网开启； 不可信网段务必关闭（设置卡片开关）。 - **默认开启（维护者决策）**：业界同类先例（Home Assistant `trusted_networks` 认证 provider、qBittorrent WebUI 「Bypass authentication for clients」）默认 需显式配置；本插件按家用固定内网场景默认开启，以「启动横幅警示行 + 设置 卡片常驻警示 + 本节说明」作缓解。 - **关闭不吊销已发 cookie**：会话 cookie 有效期内（默认 30 天）已登录设备 在关闭后仍可直接进入；需立即收回访问时清空 dsh credentials 存储。 - **失效 cookie 自愈**：cookie 失效（credentials 重置等）的设备原本会陷入 401 死锁（Max-Age 内浏览器不删 cookie、又拿不到新 token）；转发层在检测到 上游 401 后自动带 token 重放一次，上游直接重铸 cookie，设备无感恢复。 - **cross-site 残余面**：公网恶意页面对 `http://:3081/` 发起的跨站 GET 可被白铸 cookie，但读不到响应（CORS opaque）、后续请求因 `SameSite=Strict` 不携带 cookie、`POST /api` 被 sec-fetch-site 围栏拒绝—— 链条闭合；token 与 cookie 均不出现在浏览器地址栏/历史。 - **不注入范围**：仅 `GET /` 且无 token 参数的请求；WebSocket、非根路径、 已带 token 的请求、provider 不可用时全部原样透传（行为与未开启一致）。 自建口令页（信任收窄为「知道口令」）为后续演进方向。 ### ownsHostCompat 兼容注入（issue #856，默认关） 经官方 webServer 注入钩子向**非回环**页面声明 `ownsHost`，恢复 Host 设置持久化面与 「打开配置文件」动作。它伪造的是页面侧拓扑事实，不是服务端授权变化：`/api` 围栏、 launch token 与会话 cookie 认证保持不变；兼容开启后，LAN 页面与回环页面在界面上不再可区分。 - **配置入口**：Plugin Manager → dsh-lan-proxy → Configure。canonical row id 为 `dsh-lan-proxy`，keyed row 为 `@wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy#dsh-lan-proxy`， 官方 settings namespace 使用 `dsh-lan-proxy`。 - **挂载边界**：配置页由 `plugins.row.config` 渲染，仅在 Host 服务 canonical settings 条目时 注册。`compat-off` 或上游契约漂移时，非回环页面可能无法进入配置行。 - **可见性**：启动横幅与 `/api/dsh-lan-proxy/health` 显示宿主侧开关；页面加载时若兼容未生效 或契约漂移，浏览器控制台给出独立告警，不依赖配置页。 - **恢复旁路（仅在行详情不可达时）**：可直接编辑 DSH 当前设置文档中的 `dsh-lan-proxy.ownsHostCompat`（宿主使用 `settings.yaml` 时，以「打开配置文件」显示的 路径为准），或执行 `ssh -L 3080:127.0.0.1:3080 <主机>` 后访问 `http://127.0.0.1:3080/`。两者都是恢复旁路，不是常规配置路径。 ## 最短上手 > **安装即开端口**：本插件会在 `0.0.0.0:3081`（HTTP）与 `0.0.0.0:3443`（HTTPS）监听，局域网内所有设备都可访问你的 dsh web。不需要时请卸载（见后文卸载）。 ### 安装插件（add） ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy ``` > 安装 / 卸载 / 更新后都需**重启一次** `dsh web`（bundle 层只在启动时组合）生效。 ### 访问 在可信局域网设备打开 `https://<服务器IP>:3443/`（或 `http://<服务器IP>:3081/`）。自签名证书首次访问需手动「继续访问」，详见 HTTPS 支持。 ### 验证 在宿主机检查健康端点： ```sh curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3081/api/dsh-lan-proxy/health ``` ## 配置 | 键 | 默认 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `true` | 总开关（关闭后转发器停止监听） | | `host` | `0.0.0.0` | 监听地址 | | `port` | `3081` | HTTP 监听端口 | | `httpsPort` | `3443` | HTTPS 监听端口 | | `targetHost` | `127.0.0.1` | 回环上游主机（**仅允许回环地址**） | | `targetPort` | 自动 | 上游端口（默认取 web 服务器实际绑定端口） | | `httpsEnabled` | `true` | 是否并存 HTTPS | | `tlsCertFile` / `tlsKeyFile` | 无 | 自定义证书（mkcert 等） | | `tlsCaCertFile` | 无 | 自建 LAN CA 公钥（PEM，仅读） | | `printBanner` | `true` | 启动时是否在终端打印监听横幅（LAN 访问地址等） | | `wsBridgeEnabled` | `true` | 桥接总开关；关闭会失去保活与压缩。 | | `wsCompressEnabled` | `true` | 是否对命中 `wsCompressPaths` 的 WebSocket 做压缩桥接（仅控制压缩，不影响桥接保活） | | `wsCompressPaths` | `/api/remote.mux` | 参与 WebSocket 压缩的路径白名单（清空 = 桥接不压缩，保活不受影响） | | `wsDeflatePolicy` | `{browser:true, uaDeny:[iPhone…]}` | 浏览器压缩策略与 UA 排除规则。 | | `httpCompressEnabled` | `true` | 转发层 gzip/Brotli 压缩开关。 | | `httpCompressLevel` | `1` | gzip 与 Brotli 共用的 0..3 档位。 | | `injectToken` | `true` | LAN 免 token 直入，默认开；见安全模型。 | | `ownsHostCompat` | `false` | 伪造页面侧宿主事实位，默认关；见安全模型。 | 配置页入口：**Plugin Manager → dsh-lan-proxy → Configure**（保存即热更新）。 > 非回环 LAN 地址默认不提供持久化设置面，Configure 按钮按 DSH 安全策略隐藏；请从 `127.0.0.1:3080` / `127.0.0.1:3081` 或 SSH 回环隧道管理。只有在可信 LAN、明确接受共享控制面风险时，才开启 `ownsHostCompat` 恢复远程设置入口。 ### 配置存储（单一通道） - 全部配置存于 dsh 官方 settings 存储；settings namespace 为 `dsh-lan-proxy`， 落盘位置由宿主统一管理。组合层 `cordis.patch.yml` 的 config 作为 base 层生效； 热更新由官方 `settings/document-updated` 事件驱动，无需重启。 #### Settings namespace DSH 官方 importer 会按同名 section 直接导入 `dsh-lan-proxy`；本插件不再运行第二套 namespace migration。`settings.yaml.imported` 仅为已消费文档的审计副本，不应整体复制。
旧 config.json 迁移 - 本插件不再维护自建 `~/.dsh/lan-proxy/config.json`。升级后首次启动会自动把 存量 config.json 一次性迁移进官方存储：原文件原子改名保留为 `config.json.migrated.bak` 备份；若写入官方存储失败会自动还原改名、下次 启动重试；若进程在写入完成前退出（中断），下次启动检测到备份残留会自动 从备份重放写入并以日志提示。确认运行正常后可手动删除该备份。 此后手改 config.json **不再生效**。
### 配置项细则 #### `wsBridgeEnabled` WebSocket 桥接总开关（issue #552）：`true` = 所有 WS 升级一律走「终结 + 桥接」（保活基座：ws 库自动代答上游 Ping + 半开探活）；`false` = TCP 字节透传（显式放弃保活与压缩，移动端切后台可能被上游心跳判死而频繁断连重连，见「WebSocket 压缩」节） #### `wsDeflatePolicy` WS 压缩协商策略：`browser` 为 false 全局关压缩；`uaDeny` 为不协商压缩的 UA 片段列表（iOS Safari 默认拦截，见「WebSocket 压缩」节） #### `httpCompressEnabled` HTTP 响应压缩总开关（转发层对可压缩响应协商 gzip/Brotli；Brotli 生效条件见「HTTP 响应压缩」节，合并自 dsh-gzip） #### `httpCompressLevel` 压缩档位预设 0..3：`0` 默认 / `1` 低（gzip 1 / br 2，最快）· `2` 中（gzip 5 / br 5，均衡）/ `3` 高（gzip 9 / br 9，最高压缩比），gzip 与 Brotli 两侧参数同时按下发；旧配置整数 4..9 自动迁移为 3 #### `injectToken` 自动注入启动令牌（issue #380）：LAN 设备首次访问 `GET /` 由转发层自动补当前 token 铸造会话 cookie，固定设备免手工拿 token；带失效 cookie 的请求在上游 401 后自动重放自愈。安全语义见「安全模型」 #### `ownsHostCompat` 向非回环页面声明 `ownsHost`（issue #856）：恢复 Host 设置持久化面与「打开配置文件」动作；远程页与本机页在界面上不再可区分。默认关，配置入口与恢复旁路见「安全模型」 ## 验证与排障 ```sh # 健康检查（回环；含压缩配置与生效状态/协商计数） curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3081/api/dsh-lan-proxy/health # 合并版压缩标记路由（回环） curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3081/api/dsh-lan-proxy/compression # 局域网访问（在另一台设备上） curl http://<本机局域网IP>:3081/api/dsh-lan-proxy/health ``` ### 已知限制 - HTTPS 自签名证书由内置库生成，无外部命令依赖（未配置证书文件且生成失败时，HTTPS 通道自动降级关闭） - 换网段导致 IP 变化时，自签名证书需重新生成或更新设置（证书文件路径） - WS 桥接默认对所有 WebSocket 生效（保活基座）；压缩仅对命中 `wsCompressPaths` 的路径生效（多一跳、额外压缩 CPU）。桥接为代理解析终结：子协议与 close 码 不向另一端保真（dsh 客户端不依赖，实测零影响） - `wsBridgeEnabled=false` 时全部 WS 走透传（省一跳 CPU），但移动端切后台 >4~6s 会被上游心跳判死而频繁断连重连——仅建议无移动端场景使用 ## 详细参考 ### WebSocket 桥接与压缩（wss 事件流） - **桥接是默认基座（issue #552）**：`wsBridgeEnabled` 开启（默认）时，**所有** WebSocket 升级一律走「终结 + 桥接」——lan-proxy 用 ws 库分别连接浏览器段与 DSH 段、双向转发帧。桥接提供两项**与压缩无关**的基础能力： - **上游 Ping 自动代答**：dsh 上游（api-gateway）对 remote.mux 每 2s 发一帧 WS Ping、连续 2 周期（约 4~6s）无 Pong 即 `terminate()`。桥接的上游连接由 ws 库自动回 Pong——手机切后台/息屏/短暂冻结不再触发上游判死，连接在亮屏后 继续可用（不再「频繁断开→重连」）。 - **半开探活（issue #268）**：桥接对两端各自独立每 30s 发一帧 WS ping；一帧 ping 在下一个周期内未收到 pong（即约 30~60s 无响应）即判定半开连接并强拆 该端——close/error 语义由此在半开下也能成立。判定强拆时输出 warn 日志 `ws-bridge half-open detected, terminating (intervalMs=…)`。 - **压缩是桥接上的可选增强**：命中 `wsCompressPaths`（默认 `/api/remote.mux` ——dsh 0.1.2 起 api-gateway 拥有的 Remote 流 mux 端点，取代旧 `/api/events.mux`、`/api/events.host`）且 `wsCompressEnabled` 开启时，浏览器段 协商 permessage-deflate（浏览器自动解压）、DSH 段明文，再双向桥接转发。 收益：remote.mux 承载大流量帧，permessage-deflate 实测约省 **75~79%**。 - **清空压缩白名单 / 关闭压缩开关不再丢保活**（issue #552）：`wsCompressPaths=[]` 或 `wsCompressEnabled=false` 仅关闭压缩，桥接（Pong 代答 + 探活）保持生效。 - DSH 服务端即使未来自身开启 permessage-deflate，这里 DSH 段固定不协商压缩， 两段各自独立，**不会双重压缩、不冲突**。 - **桥接非字节透明**：桥接是代理解析终结（非 TCP 透传），子协议 （Sec-WebSocket-Protocol）协商与 close 码不向另一端保真（dsh 客户端当前 不依赖这两者，实测零影响）；对通用 WS/未来端点以此语义为准。 - **显式关闭桥接**（`wsBridgeEnabled=false`）：全部 WS 走 TCP 字节透传 （省一跳 CPU），但失去 Pong 代答与探活——移动端切后台 >4~6s 会被上游心跳 判死断开重连，仅建议在无需移动端的场景使用。 ### HTTP 响应压缩（Brotli/gzip 自适应，合并自 dsh-gzip） - v0.1.10 起，原独立插件 dsh-gzip（源码已自本仓移除）的 HTTP 响应压缩能力已合并进本插件， 在**转发层**实现（成熟开源库 [compression](https://www.npmjs.com/package/compression) 中间件，构建期内联进产物）：经本插件访问时，对 `/api`（RPC）、 `/plugins`（客户端 bundle）与静态资源/index.html 等可压缩响应（JSON / 文本） 自动协商压缩；SSE（text/event-stream）、zip 导出、已编码响应、HEAD、 带 Range 的请求、小于 1KB 的响应原样透传。 - **Brotli 的实际生效条件（实测口径）**：dsh 自身的 web 服务器自带 gzip 压缩 （`compression: gzip`），且只协商 gzip。因此这条链路上有两种情形： | 客户端声明 `Accept-Encoding` | 上游行为 | 经本插件最终返回 | |---|---|---| | `br, gzip`（主流浏览器） | gzip | gzip（响应已编码，本层让位不重压） | | `gzip` | gzip | gzip（同上） | | `br`（仅声明 br） | 原文 | **br** | 即：只有当上游未压缩且客户端只声明 br 时，本层的 Brotli 才真正生效。主流浏览器 都同时声明 gzip，故这条链路上拿到的是上游 gzip、**拿不到 Brotli 的额外压缩率**； 该情形仍远优于不压缩（同一响应实测 322900 → 5065 字节）。两层不会重复压缩。 - 收益：会话历史等大 JSON 响应（4~13MB 未压缩）经远程/慢链路访问时常触发 浏览器 RPC 30s 超时「历史加载失败」；压缩后约 ~1.2MB，隔离环境实测由 ~36s 降到 ~3s。 - 实现位置在转发器自己的监听链上，不修改 dsh web 与任何其他插件的运行时行为； `httpCompressEnabled: false` 关闭本层压缩（当客户端同时接受 gzip 时，上游自带 gzip 仍会压缩响应，故该开关不改变这类响应的线上体积）。注意：直连回环 web （本机浏览器访问 `127.0.0.1:3080`，不经本插件）的流量不在压缩面内——回环链路 无需压缩。 - **从 dsh-gzip 迁移**：升级本插件并确认压缩生效后，卸载独立 gzip 包： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web update @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy # 需 >= 0.1.10 curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3081/api/dsh-lan-proxy/health # 回环校验：httpCompressMounted 为 true 再继续 dsh plugin --profile web remove @wingsky-1/dsh-gzip # 重启 dsh web 生效 ``` - 存量 gzip@0.1.9（无检测逻辑）与本插件双装时，因 content-encoding 检查只会 压缩一次（已实测任意装配顺序均单层），不会损坏响应；建议尽快卸载以免 health 诊断口径混淆。 ### HTTPS 支持 - **证书来源（两级）**：① 配置 `tlsCertFile`/`tlsKeyFile`（正式证书或 mkcert 本地 CA，浏览器零警告）；② 自动生成自签名证书（内置 selfsigned 库生成并缓存到 `/@wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy/`（旧 lan-proxy 目录首次启动自动迁入），私钥权限 0600，无需宿主机 openssl） - 自签名证书首次访问需手动"继续访问"；内网设备零警告推荐自建 LAN CA（一台设备装一次 CA，见下） - **一键生成本地 CA（issue #930）**：设置页“局域网访问”卡片点“一键生成本地 CA”，即签发 10 年 CA + 398 天叶子并写入托管目录 `/@wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy/certs/`（CA 公钥 `ca-cert.pem` / 私钥 `ca-key.pem` / 叶子 `leaf-cert.pem` + `leaf-key.pem`），三键自动回填。默认“轮换叶子证书”仅换叶子（CA 不变，已装设备零操作）；“轮换 CA”为危险动作。不想走 UI 时可用 mkcert 自建 CA（零代码并存路径，hint 同上） - **移动设备安装证书（issue #911，#930 Phase 1 无 CA 不下发）**：配 tlsCaCertFile（CA 公钥）后，设置页下载直链即下发 CA（须用浏览器直接点开链接）。无 CA 时下载链接一律 404（自签模式与自定义孤叶子都不下发：装了建不起信任）：先在设置页一键生成本地 CA，或配置 CA 公钥后重试。iPhone 装描述文件后去证书信任设置打开信任；Android 在设置安全项安装 CA 证书；Windows 双击装进受信任的根证书颁发机构 ### 卸载插件（remove） ```sh dsh plugin --profile web remove @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy ``` ### 更新插件（update） ```sh dsh plugin --profile web update @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy ``` > 安装 / 卸载 / 更新后都需**重启一次** `dsh web`（bundle 层只在启动时组合）生效。
低频安装变体：指定版本与 npx ### 指定版本号（@version） 省略 `@版本号` 即安装默认 latest（推荐）。仅当 registry 尚未同步到最新、或最新版在你的环境有问题时，在包名后追加 `@版本号`： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy@<版本号> ``` ### 未全局安装 dsh 若本机没有全局 `dsh` 命令，用 `npx` 临时拉起（底层调用 `pnpm`，仍需本机装好 `pnpm` 与 `Node.js`）： ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web update @wingsky-1/dsh-lan-proxy ```
