evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-wechat-media

**Personal WeChat for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`)** — scan a QR
code once, then talk to your agent from WeChat: one DSH conversation per contact or group, and two-way
text, images, video, documents and archives. Several WeChat accounts can be paired side by side.

**给 DeepSeek Harness 的个人微信桥**：扫一次码，之后就能在微信里和 agent 对话 —— 每个联系人/群各自
一个独立会话，文字、图片、视频、文档、压缩包**双向**互通，支持**多个微信号同时在线**（小号 + 大号）。

---

## What it gives you / 它能做什么

| Capability | Detail |
|---|---|
| QR pairing | Cards in the Plugins panel. The login token is stored under `$DSH_HOME`, so **restarting dsh does not need a new scan**; re-pairing is one click. |
| One conversation per chat | Every WeChat contact (and group) gets its own DSH session with its own context, created or resumed automatically. |
| Text both ways | Your message becomes a turn; the answer is chunked back to WeChat. |
| Media both ways | Images, video, documents and archives. Inbound files are downloaded and decrypted to `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/<date>/<chat>/`; the agent gets the path, so a text model can read images through `read_image`. Outbound files are uploaded and sent by the agent through its tools. |
| Multiple accounts | Pair a spare account and your main account; each keeps its own token, cursor and session map. |
| Persistence | Accounts, receive cursor, per-peer context tokens, chat→session routes, allowlist and preferences all live under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-wechat-media/`. |

## Requirements / 环境要求

- **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer** with the standard agent loop and tools (the shipped `dsh web` / desktop
  profiles qualify), Node.js >= 22 (Node 24 tested), Windows / macOS / Linux.
- **A WeChat account that can scan a QR code.** A spare account is strongly recommended: personal WeChat
  automation is against WeChat's terms of service and carries a ban risk, whichever library you use.
- Outbound access to `ilinkai.weixin.qq.com` and `novac2c.cdn.weixin.qq.com`.

## Install / 安装

```sh
# from GitHub
dsh plugin --profile web add github:wjh-ux/dsh-wechat-media

# or from a checkout
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-wechat-media
```

Restart `dsh`, then open **Plugins → `dsh-wechat-media`** and press **Add an account (QR code)**.

重启 dsh，然后在 **插件 → `dsh-wechat-media`** 点「**添加账号（扫码）**」。

## Pairing / 配对

1. The card shows a QR code (it polls its own status and refreshes an expired code automatically).
2. Scan it with WeChat on the phone, confirm on the phone.
3. If WeChat asks for digits, type them into the card and submit.
4. The account appears with a status dot: `monitoring` means the long poll is running.
5. **Add an account (QR code)** stays available at all times — scanning a *different* WeChat account
   adds it as another account, so a spare and your main account can run side by side. Scanning the account
   you already have simply refreshes its login. Each row also has **Pair again** and **Unpair**.
6. Opened the QR by mistake? Press **Cancel** — the attempt disappears immediately instead of waiting for
   the code to expire. (A QR lives five minutes; an attempt gives up after eight, and at most three QR codes
   are issued per attempt.)

The QR encodes the landing-page URL the platform hands out — scanning it is what completes the binding.
Each account is stored under its normalized `ilink_bot_id` (`b0f5860fdecb@im.bot` → `b0f5860fdecb-im-bot`),
with `0600` permissions on the files that hold a token; accounts, cursors and conversation routes are keyed
per account, so several can poll at the same time.

## Where inbound files go / 收件目录

By default inbound media is decrypted into `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/<date>/<chat>/`. That directory is
configurable, and the change takes effect without a restart:

1. **From the card** - the field under *Inbound files are saved in* submits a plain GET form (a navigation, not a
   fetch), so it works even in browsers where the card's requests never reach the plugin.
2. **From the control panel** - `/dsh-wechat-media/panel` has the same field and a *restore default* button.
3. **With the system folder dialog** - *Browse… / 浏览…* (card and control panel) or
   `GET /dsh-wechat-media/pick-folder` opens Windows' own picker on the desktop and saves the choice. A browser
   cannot hand over an absolute path (a directory input only exposes relative names), which is why the dialog is
   opened by the host (`powershell -STA`) rather than in the page.
4. **From the plugin config** - `inboxDir: "D:\\wechat-files"` in the plugin options, used when no runtime
   preference is set.

The order is preference (card/panel) → config → `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox`. Only an absolute path is accepted: a
relative one is refused with a message instead of being resolved against the process working directory, because a
silently different directory is worse than the documented default. `GET /dsh-wechat-media/state` reports the
effective value as `inboxRoot`, with `inboxRootDefault` and `inboxRootConfig` for comparison.
## Using it / 使用

Just message the bot from WeChat. A few things the agent can do from inside the conversation:

- answer through the normal reply channel (the bridge relays its final text automatically);
- send **extra** messages or **files** with its tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wechat_send_text` | An extra text message, or a message to a different chat (`to`), pre-empting the automatic relay for that turn. |
| `wechat_send_file` | Send a local file back to WeChat. Images (`.jpg/.png/.webp/.gif`) travel as pictures, videos (`.mp4/.mov`) as videos, everything else (pdf, docx, xlsx, zip, 7z, …) as a file attachment. |
| `wechat_status` | Which accounts are paired and which conversations exist. |

Every incoming message is prefixed with `[微信 <name> <wxid>]` so the agent can pass the right `to` when it
answers a specific chat. Group ids look like `12345678@chatroom`.

## Remote approval / 微信里远程审批

When a WeChat-driven session asks for approval — a tool call the permission preset wants confirmed — the prompt
goes to the same WeChat chat, not only to the GUI:

```
⚠️ 需要你批准一次操作（远程审批）
工具：pwsh
原因：write outside the workspace

回 1 = 批准一次 · 回 2 = 拒绝
```

Answer `1` / `y` / `同意` / `批准` / `/approve` to allow that one call, or `2` / `n` / `拒绝` / `/reject` to
refuse it. The answer is **consumed** — it never becomes a new turn. If nothing arrives within
`approvalTimeoutSec` (default 120 s), or the prompt cannot be delivered, or the turn is aborted, the request is
handed back to the GUI, so an approval is never silently dropped. Set `approval: "ignore"` in the plugin config
to keep approvals in the GUI only.

## Contact allowlist / 联系人白名单

Every chat that writes to the bot is remembered, and the card lists them under **Contacts & groups / 联系人 /
群**, with **Allow / Ignore / Clear** per row and an **Only accept allowlisted chats** switch.

- The switch is **off by default** — otherwise a freshly paired account would look broken to everyone who writes.
- With it on, only chats marked *Allow* reach the agent; *Ignore* and undecided chats are dropped and logged.
- A decision takes effect immediately (no restart) and is stored in `peers.json` beside the accounts.

## Friends only / 只处理好友私聊

**Only answer friends (1:1 chats)** — the card's second checkbox, or `/friends on` from a chat. The protocol
carries no "is a friend" flag, so *friends* means **1:1 chats**: when the switch is on, every **group** message
is dropped, whatever the allowlist says about that group. Direct chats are unaffected.

- **Off by default**: an upgrade must not change who the bot answers.
- Group messages are **ignored silently** (that is the point) but never invisibly: each one bumps
  `counters.groupsSkipped`, `/status` prints `已静默忽略群消息 N 条`, and the card shows the same number.
- It is one preference (`prefs.json`), so the checkbox and `/friends` can never disagree, and it applies to
  personal WeChat and WeCom alike.
- Switching it on **while a group is waiting** answers once in that group to explain the coming silence. Turning
  it off works from a 1:1 chat or the card — a group message is skipped before it could be read as a command,
  which is the honest consequence of "silent".

## WeCom (企业微信) / 企业微信

WeCom works alongside the personal-WeChat bridge, outbound through two paths and **inbound through a third**:

| Path | What you need | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| **Group robot webhook** | one webhook URL from a WeCom group (*群设置 → 群机器人 → 添加*) | out: text, markdown, images |
| **Self-built app** | corpid + corpsecret + agentid of an app (*应用管理 → 自建*) | out: text, markdown, image, file, voice, video |
| **Intelligent robot, long connection** | the robot's BotID + Secret (*智能机器人 → API 模式 → 长连接*) | **both**: messages in, answers back in the same chat |

Configure any of them on the plain page `http://127.0.0.1:19387/dsh-wechat-media/wecom` (also linked from the card
and the control panel), which is where you send a test message from as well. The long connection needs no public
address: the plugin opens a WebSocket to `wss://openws.work.weixin.qq.com` and answers each message through the
frame the platform sent, so a WeCom chat becomes an ordinary DSH conversation - the same session machinery,
allowlist, approvals and reply relay as personal WeChat. Approval requests reach a WeCom chat as a proactive
long-connection message and are answered there with `1` (allow once) or `2` (reject); anything else stays in the GUI,
exactly as on the personal-WeChat side. The agent gets two extra tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wecom_send_text` | Send text or markdown through the configured robot, long connection or app (`to` overrides the recipients). |
| `wecom_send_file` | Send a local file as image / file / voice / video. Over the long connection (or through a self-built app) any type works; with only a group-robot webhook, images do. |

Files travel the other way too: a file sent to the robot is uploaded as a temporary WeCom asset over the long
connection (init -> 512 KiB chunks -> finish -> `media_id`) and then sent, so no app credentials are needed. Uploads
are capped at 100 chunks (~50 MB) and each chunk is retried twice, which is what the platform tolerates; a failure is
reported back instead of being swallowed.

Settings live in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-wechat-media/wecom.json` with mode `0600` - they contain a webhook key, a corpsecret
and the robot secret, so they never go into `prefs.json` or a cordis patch. `GET /dsh-wechat-media/state` reports
whether a secret is set, never its value.

**What stays impossible is the callback API.** It insists on a public HTTPS URL that the enterprise registers, so a
bridge running on your own machine cannot receive that way; the long connection above is what makes two-way WeCom
possible without one.

**Media arrives too.** Images, files and videos sent to the robot are downloaded, decrypted and written to the same
inbox the WeChat side uses (`$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/<date>/<chat>/`), then handed to the model as a path plus a
`[企业微信图片] …用 read_image 查看` hint, so a text-only model with a vision plugin can actually look at them. The
scheme is the official one for the long connection (`@wecom/aibot-node-sdk`): `aeskey` is base64 of a 32-byte AES-256
key, the bytes are AES-256-CBC with the `iv` taken from the key's first 16 bytes, PKCS#7 padded to 32 bytes, and the
file name comes from `Content-Disposition` because the payload carries none. Note this is *not* the personal-WeChat CDN
scheme (AES-128-ECB). A download that fails says so in the chat instead of dropping the attachment silently, and
`/state` counts both outcomes (`counters.mediaDownloaded` / `counters.mediaFailed`).

## Feishu (飞书 / Lark) / 飞书机器人

Two kinds of Feishu bot exist, and both are supported, because they solve different problems.

| | Custom webhook bot | App bot |
|---|---|---|
| Credentials | the webhook URL (and its signing secret, if set) | `app_id` + `app_secret` |
| Can send | text and rich text | text, rich text, images, files, audio |
| Can receive | no | yes - over the **long connection**, with no public URL |
| Config | `feishu.webhookUrl`, `feishu.secret` | `feishu.appId`, `feishu.appSecret` |

### Configuring it from the panel / 在面板里配置（不用 setx，不用重启）

The Web UI panel has a **Feishu** block: App ID, App Secret, the custom-webhook URL and its signing secret, the
platform (`feishu` / `lark`), a default receive id, and the long-connection switch. **Saving reconnects immediately** -
there is no `setx` and no DSH restart, which used to be the only way in.

Values are resolved in this order, so a field the panel leaves alone keeps whatever config or environment provides:

1. what the panel saved (`prefs.feishu`),
2. `config.feishu` in the plugin config,
3. the environment: `FEISHU_APP_ID` / `FEISHU_APP_SECRET` / `FEISHU_WEBHOOK_URL` / `FEISHU_WEBHOOK_SECRET` /
   `FEISHU_DOMAIN` / `FEISHU_TO` / `FEISHU_LONG_CONNECTION` / `FEISHU_VERIFICATION_TOKEN` / `FEISHU_ENCRYPT_KEY`.

Two rules make that safe:

- **A blank field is never sent** by the panel's Save button, so saving something else cannot wipe a stored secret.
  Clearing is a separate, deliberate action (the Clear button sends explicit empties).
- **Secrets never come back.** `/state` and `/prefs` report *whether* a secret is set, never its value - one redaction
  helper covers every response that carries prefs (a test found the leak that made this rule necessary).

`feishu.domain` is `feishu` (mainland China) or `lark` (international); an explicit URL also works. `/state` reports
`savedFields` and, per field, whether the value in force came from the panel, the config or the environment.

Tools: `feishu_send_text` (text or markdown, `to` + `toType` optional - `chat_id` by default, `open_id`/`user_id`/`email`
also accepted) and `feishu_send_file` (`path`, `kind` = file/image/audio/video). The reply always says which channel it
used and gives the `message_id`, so "sent" is not a guess.

**A webhook-only setup cannot send files, and says exactly that** rather than reporting a success that never arrived -
the custom bot API has no file message at all. Configure `appId`/`appSecret` for that.

`/feishu` (`/飞书`, `/lark`) reports what is configured - **never the secret itself, only whether one is set** - and
`/feishu test [id] [type]` sends a self-test.

Every endpoint and algorithm here was read from the official `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk` 1.75.0 source, not recalled:
messages are `POST /open-apis/im/v1/messages?receive_id_type=…`, the token is
`POST /open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal`, media is `POST /open-apis/im/v1/images` and `/files`, an event's
AES key is `sha256(encryptKey)` with the **first 16 bytes of the ciphertext as the IV**, and the event signature is
`sha256(timestamp + nonce + encryptKey + body)` in hex (`sha1` with the verification token when the event is
unencrypted). The custom-webhook signature is the trap of that API - `HMAC-SHA256(key = timestamp + "\n" + secret,
data = "")`, base64 - and it is checked against an independent implementation's published test vector.

### Receiving: the long connection / 用长连接接收（不需要公网地址）

An app bot receives events over Feishu's **long connection** - a WebSocket the bot opens itself - so **no public URL,
no tunnel and no port forwarding are needed**. The event route (POSTing events to a URL Feishu calls) is deliberately
*not* implemented: it is the option that requires a public address.

**Turn it on in the Feishu console, then restart DSH:**

| Step | Where |
|---|---|
| Enable the bot | 开发者后台 → 你的应用 → **应用功能 → 机器人 → 启用** |
| Subscribe over the long connection | 开发者后台 → **事件与回调 → 订阅方式 → 使用长连接接收事件** |
| Permissions | at least `im:message` (send and receive); add the receive scopes the console asks for |
| Publish | 创建版本并发布 - **changes do not take effect until a version is published** |

Configuration: `feishu.longConnection` (default **on**; `feishu.longConnection = false` or `FEISHU_LONG_CONNECTION=false`
turns it off). It only connects when `feishu.appId` and `feishu.appSecret` are configured - a webhook-only setup has
nothing to connect with, and says so.

What happens to an inbound message: text and rich-text messages become a prompt for the model, prefixed like the other
channels; the answer is **posted as a reply under the question** (`message_id`), falling back to an ordinary send if the
reply is refused, and long answers are chunked. Two things are refused on purpose: the bot **ignores its own messages**
(`sender_type: "app"`), because answering them would wake itself in a loop, and a **re-delivered event is answered only
once**.

The protocol facts were read from the official SDK, not recalled - the handshake is `POST {domain}/callback/ws/endpoint`
(request `{AppID, AppSecret}`, response `{code, data:{URL, ClientConfig}}`, whose keys are capitalised and whose
intervals are in **seconds**), the frames are protobuf in the `pbbp2` namespace (`Frame` 1 `SeqID` / 2 `LogID` /
3 `service` / 4 `method` / 5 `headers` / 6 `payloadEncoding` / 7 `payloadType` / 8 `payload` / 9 `LogIDNew`, `Header`
1 `key` / 2 `value`), an event is acknowledged by **sending the received frame back** with a `biz_rt` header and
`{"code":200}`, and a fragmented event is reassembled from `message_id`/`sum`/`seq`/`trace_id` with malformed metadata
**rejected** rather than silently corrupting the payload.

`GET /state` carries a `feishu` block (configuration, connection state, `lastError`, `lastEventAt` and the counters
`feishuEvents` / `feishuAnswered` / `feishuIgnored` / `feishuErrors`), and `/feishu` shows the same in a chat, including
*why* the long connection is not up when it is not.

## Scheduled tasks / 定时任务

A task is a sentence plus a chat: it fires on its own and sends its result there. Three actions, four triggers, and
one switch for the dangerous action:

```text
/task                                   # list, with next run time and last result
/task rm t3k9m2                         # delete
/task off t3k9m2                        # pause     (/task on ... resumes)
/task command on                        # allow `command` tasks to run locally (default off)
```

| Action | What happens at the fire time |
| --- | --- |
| `message` | sends fixed text - no model call, no tokens |
| `prompt` | runs one ordinary agent turn in that chat and delivers the answer |
| `command` | runs a local command and sends its output (needs `/task command on`) |

Triggers accept English and Chinese interchangeably: `daily 08:30` / `每天 08:30`, `weekly mon 09:00` / `每周一 09:00`,
`every 30m` / `每 30 分钟`, `monthly 15 09:00` / `每月15日 09:00` (clamped to short months), `once 2026-10-20 09:00`. Tasks live in `tasks.json` under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-wechat-media/`,
separate from prefs; a task that has run once never fires again for the same window, and a `once` task switches
itself off afterwards.

Ask for one in a chat - "每天 8 点提醒我喝水" - and the agent creates it with `task_add`, targeting the chat that
asked; `/state` reports `tasks: { count, enabled, nextAt, commandEnabled, ran, failed, items }`.

### What people actually schedule / 实际用法

| You want | The schedule | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A weather line before work | `每天 07:30` | `prompt`: "用一句话说今天厦门天气，再给一句提醒" |
| A digest of a group at noon | `daily 12:00` | `prompt`: "总结今天群里值得看的消息，五条以内" |
| A weekly report on Monday | `每周一 09:00` | `prompt`: "汇总上周完成的事，写成三条" |
| A monthly reminder | `每月1日 10:00` | `message`: "该交房租了" |
| A one-off, then again next week | `once 2026-10-20 09:00` + `[+1周] [再次运行]` | any |
| Watch a folder every half hour | `every 30m` | `command` (needs `/task command on`) |

`prompt` is the interesting one: it runs a **normal agent turn**, so every tool the agent has is available to it -
web search, files, Feishu. A scheduled prompt is therefore "ask me this every morning and do the work", not a
canned message.

### The card / 面板

The Web UI card is the management half; creation works both there and in a chat.

| Control | When it appears | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| time + action + text + `添加` | always | create a task targeting the chat that last wrote |
| `[暂停]` / `[恢复]` | recurring tasks | stop and restart the schedule |
| `[+1 天 ▾] [再次运行]` | finished one-offs | move it forward one day / week / month and re-enable |
| `☐ 完成后再排一次` | one-offs | re-arm automatically after each run (same clock time, next day) |
| `[删除]` | always | remove it |
| `☐ 允许 command 任务执行本机命令` | always | the switch behind `command` tasks (default off) |

A finished one-off shows `✅ 已跑完（一次性任务，不能暂停）` rather than a pause button that would do nothing: `dueTasks`
compares the last run against **that occurrence's** `atMs`, so re-arming is meaningful and a plain resume is not.

Two more behaviours worth knowing:

- **Missed runs are skipped, not replayed.** A task more than 60 minutes late (a laptop that slept, a bridge that was
  stopped) is recorded as missed and the schedule moves on - the alternative is every missed `prompt` task firing in
  the same second when the machine wakes. `taskGraceMinutes` in prefs tunes it; `0` means "always run, however late".
  `/state` shows `tasks.skipped` next to `ran` and `failed`.
- **Any chat can be targeted.** `task_add` takes `transport` (`wechat` / `wecom` / `feishu`) with `to`, so a task can
  be created for a group you have not just spoken to; without it, the default is still "the chat that asked".

## Office documents / 办公文档

Four tools read, create and convert `.docx` / `.xlsx` / `.pptx`, and export PDF or page images. They are a thin,
honest surface over two programs already on this machine - the runtime's own Python (`python-docx`, `openpyxl`,
`python-pptx`) and the LibreOffice Kit CLI - so nothing is bundled here and nothing is installed at run time:

| Tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `office_read` | text and structure: paragraphs, tables, sheets with rows, slide texts |
| `office_write` | create from a JSON spec (below) |
| `office_convert` | `.docx/.xlsx/.pptx` → PDF, source untouched |
| `office_render` | pages (or a sheet range) → PNG, for a visual check or to send as a picture |

```jsonc
// .docx
{"title": "季度报告", "blocks": [
  {"type": "heading", "level": 1, "text": "一、概述"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正文"},
  {"type": "bullets", "items": ["要点一", "要点二"]},
  {"type": "table", "rows": [["项目", "数值"], ["收入", "120"]], "header": true}
]}

// .xlsx
{"sheets": [{"name": "报表", "rows": [["月份", "收入"], ["1月", 120]], "widths": [12, 10], "header": true}]}

// .pptx
{"slides": [{"title": "第一页", "bullets": ["背景", "结论"]}]}
```

`/office` prints which program each capability needs and whether it was found; `/state.office` carries the same
answer for a script. A missing program is named (`找不到 Python（设置 officePython…）`) rather than reported as a
broken document - the toolchain and the file are different problems and must not look alike.

Create a file, then send it: the bridge already has `send_file` for WeChat, WeCom and Feishu, so "做个 Excel 发我"
is `office_write` then `send_file`.

Relative paths land in **`officeDir`**, printed by `/office`:

```text
/office                      # toolchain + the directory relative paths use
/office dir D:\报表\2026     # set it (also /prefs?officeDir=…, or DSH_OFFICE_DIR)
```

Empty means "the bridge's working directory" - workable, but forgettable, which is why `/office` always prints the
effective path instead of expecting anyone to remember it.

## Desktop control (mouse, keyboard, screen) / 桌面控制

Seven tools can drive this machine's own mouse and keyboard, read the screen and manage windows. They are
**off by default** and every one of them refuses until you arm the switch, because they are the only tools here
that act on your screen instead of on the bridge:

```text
/desktop on        # arm  (also: POST /dsh-wechat-media/prefs?desktopControl=true)
/desktop off       # disarm
/desktop           # toggle
```

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `desktop_screen` | virtual screen origin/size in physical pixels, monitor count, pointer position - call it first so coordinates are real pixels |
| `desktop_windows` | visible top-level windows: title, pid, rectangle, minimised |
| `desktop_focus` | bring the first window whose title contains a string to the front, restoring it if minimised |
| `desktop_screenshot` | PNG of the whole screen or a region into the shared inbox, path returned so it can be sent to the chat |
| `desktop_mouse` | `move` / `click` / `double_click` / `right_click` / `middle_click` / `drag` / `scroll` at physical pixels |
| `desktop_type` | type literal text (Unicode scan codes, so Chinese arrives as typed) |
| `desktop_key` | press a chord such as `ctrl+s`, `alt+tab`, `up` |

Three things are deliberate:

- **Off unless armed.** The switch is checked in one wrapper (`desktopTool`) that is the only way to define one
  of these tools, so a new desktop tool cannot forget it. `/state` reports
  `desktop: { enabled, supported, reason }`.
- **Nothing is interpolated into PowerShell.** Coordinates are integers; text and window titles travel as
  base64 and are decoded by PowerShell, so a window title containing `'; Remove-Item …` is data, not code.
- **Windows only, for now.** The scripts use `user32.dll`, `System.Windows.Forms` and `System.Drawing`;
  on any other platform the tools refuse and say which platform they found.

`desktop_screen` also reports the size of the `INPUT` struct the C# compiled, so a wrong layout (which makes
`SendInput` silently do nothing) is visible rather than guessed at.

## Web search (Tavily) / 联网搜索

A `tavily_search` tool lets a WeChat, WeCom or Feishu conversation ask about something current and get real titles,
links and snippets. The shapes were copied from the user's own working plugin (`wjh-ux/dsh-mcp-tavily`, cited line by
line in `tavily.js`) rather than guessed, and the live API was called to check them: with a key, three results came
back in about three seconds - and **keyless mode works too**, so search functions before a key is configured.

The key is set in the panel's Tavily block and takes effect on the next search with no restart, because the tool
re-reads the saved settings before every call. It is never echoed back: `/state` reports `keySet` and nothing more,
including for the case that used to leak - a Tavily-only prefs object with no Feishu block. A failure states its
reason (`Tavily 搜索失败：…`) instead of returning an empty answer.

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `query` | what to search for (required) |
| `maxResults` | 1-20; defaults to the configured value |
| `searchDepth` | `basic` (default), `advanced` or `fast` |
| `includeDomains` / `excludeDomains` | comma-separated domains to restrict to, or leave out |

## Browser automation / 浏览器自动化

Nine tools drive a **real browser** - the Chrome or Edge already on the machine, over the Chrome DevTools
Protocol - with **no third-party dependency**: Node's own global `WebSocket` carries CDP. There is nothing to
install: no npx, no npm install, no config file. The panel chooses the channel, the debugging port and whether it
runs headless.

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `browser_open` | open a URL and return the page title |
| `browser_text` | the page's title, URL and visible text |
| `browser_click` | click an element by CSS selector (a real mouse event) |
| `browser_type` | type into an element by CSS selector (real key input) |
| `browser_screenshot` | PNG of the page into the shared inbox, path returned so it can be sent to the chat |
| `browser_eval` | run JavaScript in the page and return its value (the escape hatch when selectors are not enough) |
| `browser_flow` | replay a list of steps and return the rows they collected (see below) |
| `browser_record` | record the person's own clicks/typing/Enter into a replayable flow |
| `browser_close` | close the browser this plugin started |

It starts its own instance with a profile under `$DSH_HOME/browser-profile`, so **the browser a person actually
browses with is never touched**; a browser already listening on the port is attached to instead of duplicated.
The "自动测试软件正在控制 Chrome" bar is **hidden by default**: `--enable-automation` is passed only when the
panel's `browserHideAutomationBar` box is unticked, and the single CDP call that required the flag
(`Browser.getBrowserCommandLine`) is no longer used - a leftover browser is found by port, not by its command line.
Verified live against Chrome 155: a page received typed input (17 and 25) and a real mouse click and computed 42 by
itself, and a screenshot came back as a 68,561-byte PNG and was delivered to Feishu. Every failure states its reason
(`browser_click 失败：nothing on the page matches the selector "…"`).

**Which browser? (`会话` / `browserProfileMode`)** - four answers, because "same Chrome as mine" has four readings:

- `own` (default) - the plugin's own profile above;
- `chrome` - import bookmarks and preferences from the real Chrome. Cookies and saved passwords **cannot** be brought
  across: Chrome 127+ encrypts them with an app-bound key that dies with the profile (measured: 114 cookie rows in, 29
  after one start). Kept for the files that do survive;
- `attach` - drive a Chrome **you** started with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` and never close it. `/browser launch`
  starts such a Chrome on its own profile and switches to this mode;
- `extension` - **the one that reaches your real Chrome.** Load `extension/` as an unpacked extension
  (chrome://extensions → developer mode), put the address and token from the panel (or `/browser ext`) into its
  options, and every `browser_*` tool runs through `chrome.debugger` inside your own browser - your logins, your tabs,
  no debugging port.

Why not simply drive the real profile? Chrome 136+ silently ignores `--remote-debugging-port` when `--user-data-dir` is
the default one - measured on Chrome 155: process up, window visible, port never listening. That is also why the

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-auto-update 给 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）CLI 装一个**能安全升级自己**的插件：检查 `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 新版本、后台安装到独立目录、切换启动指针、健康检查失败自动回滚。网页端设置页里点按钮就行，安装目录（版本装在哪块盘）也能在同一个卡片里改。 > **English TL;DR** — a DSH plugin that checks the npm dist-tag for `@deepseek-ai/dsh`, installs the new version **side by side** (never in place), smoke-tests the composed config, repoints a launcher pointer, restarts the web host from a process outside the host's job object, and rolls back automatically if the new version does not come up healthy. It also moves the side-by-side install base to another drive (copy → verify → repoint → restart), rolling back both the pointer and the base if that fails. Windows only (PowerShell 5.1 + cmd). MIT. > **维护者当前状态（2026-10-22）**：这台机器上的 web 实例**故意停在 `0.2.0-rc.2`**。`0.2.1-rc.2` 本体能启动，但带 `dsh-vision-router` 的 profile 起不来（`connection` 等 `webRuntime` 超时，见下文「实战记录」），已两次真实切换验证并自动回滚。等 vision-router 出兼容版本后再升；`autoApply` 保持关闭，升级器会继续如实报告「有新版」。 ## 为什么需要它 DSH CLI 没有 `update` 子命令——`dsh plugin` 只是把参数转发给 pnpm，装插件用；升级主程序得自己 `npm install`。而在**服务正在运行**时原地覆盖安装，结果是：旧进程还握着旧模块，新版本起不来时你也回不去了。 这个插件的前提只有一条：**永不原地升级正在运行的实例**。 ## 设计原则 1. **旁路安装**：新版本装到 `\dsh-install-`，和当前实例完全隔离。 2. **先验证再切换**：`node bin.js --profile web --dump-config` 能组合出配置树（且退出码 0）才算装成功；装好才动启动指针。 3. **重启必须来自宿主之外**：进程内做不到原地复活。切换指针后由一个通过 WMI 拉起的进程接手（父进程是 `WmiPrvSE.exe`，不在任何 job 树里），宿主死掉不会连坐。 4. **起不来就退回去**：健康检查失败 → 指针切回旧版本 → 重启旧版本 → 写 `last-result.json`（`status: "rolled-back"`）。 5. **安装目录是配置项，不是常量**：换目录 = 复制 → 自检 → 改 `install-base.txt` → 切指针 → 重启；失败时指针和目录一起回滚（否则指针会指向新目录里不存在的版本）。 ## 组成 | 文件 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `lib/index.js` | 宿主插件：`/status` `/check` `/apply` `/rollback` `/config` `/install-base` `/migrate` 接口 + 后台定时检查 + 自动应用 | | `lib/client.js` | 设置页「载具更新」卡片（当前/最新版本、检查、安装、回滚、安装目录、自动更新开关） | | `apply-update.ps1` | 真正干活的脚本：npm 安装 → 冒烟 → 切指针 → 停旧起新 → 健康检查 → 失败回滚 | | `cordis.patch.yml` | 把插件本体插进 loader | | `examples/start-dsh-web.cmd` | **重启命令的模板**（插件不猜你怎么启动服务，见下文） | | `test/handler.test.mjs` | 离线测试：临时目录里造一个假安装，直接驱动 HTTP handler，不碰真服务、不重启 | ## 安装 ```powershell # 从 GitHub 装（推荐；先 fork/clone 到本地也行，用 link: 指向本地目录） dsh plugin --profile web add github:Wonderow666/dsh-auto-update # 或从本地目录装 dsh plugin --profile web add link:C:\path\to\dsh-auto-update ``` 然后把它加进 profile 的 bundles（`%DSH_HOME%\profiles\web\package.json`）： ```json { "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "...", "dsh-auto-update" ] } } } ``` 最后重启一次 web 宿主让插件加载（**这一步重启会掐掉当前对话的传输，页面上稍等重连**）。之后的升级就不用再手动重启了。 装之前先确认你的启动链就位（见下面「启动脚本契约」），否则插件会拒绝切换版本——这是刻意的：它宁可不动，也不把你留在一个起不来的版本上。 ## 配置 ### 环境变量（重启命令与指针目录） 插件不去猜你的目录结构，三件事全部可配置： | 变量 | 默认 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | `DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_LAUNCH_CMD` | *（空）* | 切换版本后用来重启 web 宿主的脚本。**没配置就不允许升级** | | `DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_LAUNCHER_DIR` | `%DSH_HOME%\auto-update\launcher` | 启动指针 `current-root.txt` 所在目录 | | `DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_BOOT_LOG` | *（空）* | 启动日志路径；配了才能把"起不来"的具体原因显示在卡片上 | | `DSH_HOME` | `~/.dsh` | DSH 数据根；安装目录默认在它旁边 | | `DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_INSTALL_BASE` | *（空）* | 安装目录的兜底默认值，会被 `install-base.txt` 覆盖（见「安装目录」） | ```powershell setx DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_LAUNCH_CMD "C:\tools\start-dsh-web.cmd" setx DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_LAUNCHER_DIR "C:\tools\dsh-launcher" setx DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_BOOT_LOG "C:\tools\start-dsh-web.log" ``` ### profile 配置（`cordis.patch.yml`） ```yaml - id: dsh-auto-update name: dsh-auto-update config: enabled: true channel: latest # latest | next | alpha intervalHours: 6 autoApply: false # true = 定时检查到新版本就自动装 registry: "" # 空 = npm 默认源；可填镜像，例如 https://registry.npmmirror.com ``` 运行时修改（设置页开关、接口调用）落到 `%DSH_HOME%\auto-update\config.json`，优先级高于 patch 里的默认值。 ## 启动脚本契约 插件只负责**切换指针**，起进程这一步交给你自己的脚本。`examples/start-dsh-web.cmd` 是一份可直接改的模板，要点： 1. **指针只写版本号**（如 `0.2.1-rc.2`），脚本自己拼出安装目录。原因：`current-root.txt` 由 cmd.exe 按 OEM 代码页读取，写完整路径时，**用户名含非 ASCII 字符的机器**（如 `C:\Users\张三\...`）会读成乱码，然后静默判成"安装不存在"。只存 ASCII 版本号则任何代码页都安全。 2. 脚本读不到指针时，按 `dsh-install-*` 目录名倒序回退到最新的完整安装。 3. 一定要把 stdout/stderr 落盘（模板写同目录 `web-run.out.log`，并自行轮转）——否则"90 秒没起来"这种故障无从查起。 4. 用了自定义安装目录时，脚本还要读同目录的 `install-base.txt` 决定去哪个目录找 `dsh-install-<版本>`（见下一节）。 ## 安装目录（可改） 默认安装目录是 `%DSH_HOME%` 的上一级（这台机器上是 `...\w`），每个版本装在 `<安装目录>\dsh-install-<版本>` 里。设置页的「安装目录」区块可以把它换到别的盘： - **改到这里**：只写配置，不动正在跑的安装；之后 `/apply` 装的新版本会落在新目录。 - **把当前安装迁过去**：整体复制（robocopy）→ 自检（版本号 + `--dump-config` 冒烟）→ 写 `install-base.txt` → 切指针 → 重启 → 健康检查 + 版本核对。任何一步失败，**指针和 `install-base.txt` 会一起回滚**——只回滚指针会让启动脚本去新目录里找一个根本不存在的版本。 - **恢复默认位置**：删掉 `install-base.txt`。 契约（`<指针目录>\install-base.txt`，默认 `%DSH_HOME%\auto-update\launcher\`）： ``` D:\dsh-installs ``` - 只有一行、**纯 ASCII 绝对路径**、无 BOM。启动脚本是 cmd 批处理，按 OEM 代码页读文件；`C:\Users\张三\...` 这种路径会读成乱码，然后静默指向空目录。 - 文件不存在 = 用默认安装目录，**不需要**这个文件。 - 迁移后旧目录不会自动删（它就是回滚路径），确认新版稳定后自己清理。 - 指针存的是版本号而不是路径，所以"同一版本在两个目录里都有"时按 `install-base.txt` → 默认目录的顺序找，再退到该目录下最新的完整安装。 限制：自定义目录必须在 ASCII 路径下（空格可以、中文不行），磁盘剩余空间需 ≥ 安装体积的 1.2 倍（0.2.x 每个版本约 300–700 MB）。 ## 接口 全部在 `/dsh-auto-update/api` 下。**写操作**必须带 `x-dsh-auto-update: 1` 头（挡跨站表单/图片式 CSRF；浏览器跨站发不出自定义头）。 | 方法 | 路径 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | GET | `/status` | 当前/最新版本、通道、可用更新、上次结果、挂起任务、`canRestart` | | GET | `/health` | 存活探针 | | POST | `/check` | 查 registry 的 `latest`/`next`/`alpha`，写 `state.json` | | POST | `/apply` | 后台安装，body 可带 `{"version":"x.y.z"}`，默认最新版 | | POST | `/rollback` | 回到 `previous-root.txt` 记录的版本 | | POST | `/config` | 改 `autoApply` / `intervalHours` / `channel` / `registry`，落 `config.json` | | POST | `/install-base` | 设置安装目录，body `{"base":"D:\\dsh-installs"}`；传 `""` 恢复默认位置（只影响以后的新版本） | | POST | `/migrate` | 把当前安装复制到新目录并重启过去，body `{"base":"..."}`；失败自动回滚指针与目录 | ```powershell $base = "http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-auto-update/api" curl.exe -s "$base/status" curl.exe -s -X POST "$base/check" -H "x-dsh-auto-update: 1" curl.exe -s -X POST "$base/apply" -H "x-dsh-auto-update: 1" -H "content-type: application/json" -d "{}" curl.exe -s -X POST "$base/rollback" -H "x-dsh-auto-update: 1" curl.exe -s -X POST "$base/install-base" -H "x-dsh-auto-update: 1" -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"base":"D:\\dsh-installs"}' curl.exe -s -X POST "$base/migrate" -H "x-dsh-auto-update: 1" -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"base":"D:\\dsh-installs"}' ``` ## 升级流程（`apply-update.ps1`） 1. 抢锁（`apply.lock`，超过 120 分钟的陈旧锁自动接管） 2. `npm install @deepseek-ai/dsh@` 到 `\dsh-install-`（可与已装版本复用） 3. `node bin.js --profile web --dump-config` 冒烟：组合出配置树才算装成功 4. 记录旧根到 `previous-root.txt`，把指针指向新版本 5. **交接**：WMI 拉起 stage-2 进程，本进程立刻退出 6. stage-2 停旧实例：只杀监听端口的 PID，再补一轮命令行含 `--profile web` 的 node 7. 用你的重启命令拉起新实例 8. 轮询 `/api/pair/status` 最多 150 秒（20 秒后放宽为端口可连） 9. 失败 → 指针切回旧版本 → 重启 → `last-result.json` 记 `rolled-back` 手动排障（不下载、不切指针、不重启）： ```powershell $ps = 'C:\path\to\dsh-auto-update\apply-update.ps1' # 纯计划 powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $ps -Mode apply -Version 0.2.1-rc.2 -CurrentRoot C:\path\to\dsh-install-0.2.0-rc.2 -DryRun # 只安装 + 冒烟，不激活 powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $ps -Mode apply -Version 0.2.1-rc.2 -CurrentRoot C:\path\to\dsh-install-0.2.0-rc.2 -StageOnly ``` `-DryRun` 的早退发生在 `npm install` **之前**——不存在"dry run 也真装了"的情况。 ## 迁移流程（`-Mode migrate`） 1. 校验目标目录：ASCII 绝对路径、不是某个 `dsh-install-*` 本身、盘存在、剩余空间 ≥ 1.2× 安装体积（"已经在那个目录"这个判断放在最前面，所以它给出的原因永远准确） 2. `robocopy <当前根> <新目录>\dsh-install-<版本> /E /R:1 /W:1 /MT:8`（退出码 ≥ 8 视为失败） 3. 自检：`package.json` 版本 == 当前版本，且 `--dump-config` 能组合出配置树 4. 备份旧指针与旧 `install-base.txt`（`previous-root.txt` / `previous-base.txt`，`-` 表示原本没有） 5. 写新 `install-base.txt` → 切指针 → WMI 交接到 stage-2，由它停旧实例并用重启命令拉起 6. 健康检查 + 版本核对；失败则指针和 `install-base.txt` 一起回滚，重启回原目录 ```powershell # 只打印计划，不复制、不改任何文件 powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $ps -Mode migrate -Version 0.2.0-rc.2 -CurrentRoot C:\...\dsh-install-0.2.0-rc.2 -InstallBase D:\dsh-installs -DryRun ``` ## 为什么重启要绕道 WMI 宿主只能被**不在它 job 树里**的进程重启。插件拉起的 `apply-update.ps1` 是 web 宿主的子进程，而 DSH 的 `subprocess-local` 会给工具树套 job object：宿主一死，job 关闭，整棵树一起没了。实践中表现出来的样子是——重启脚本日志停在 `stopped pid ...` 那行，后面重启的几行**永远不执行**（这类脚本我写过三个，三个都这样死掉）。 所以指针一切换就立刻 relinquish 控制权：`Win32_Process.Create` 让新进程的父进程变成 `WmiPrvSE.exe`，没有任何 job 覆盖它，stage-2 一定活到把新宿主拉起来。 失败恢复也不放在 `catch` 里：会抛异常的地方都在指针切换**之前**，那时旧实例还在正常服务，什么都不用做；切换之后的健康检查与回滚由 stage-2 独占。 ## 安全边界 - **安装目录白名单**：只安装到 `\dsh-install-`，不会把 `npm install` 引向任意目录；改安装目录同样受限——只接受 ASCII 绝对路径，且不能指向某个 `dsh-install-*` 目录本身 - **版本串校验**：`^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$`，且必须比当前版本新（想降级请走 `/rollback`） - **写操作要护栏头**：见上，非凭证、只为挡 CSRF - **没配重启命令就拒绝升级**：`apply` / `rollback` 会在动指针前失败，不会留下起不来的 profile - **默认只查不装**：`autoApply: false`，自动更新必须用户在设置页显式打开 ## 状态文件 `%DSH_HOME%\auto-update\` | 文件 | 内容 | | --- | --- | | `config.json` | 用户在网页上改过的配置 | | `state.json` | 最新 tag 表、上次检查时间、上次结果、进行中的任务 | | `last-result.json` | 脚本结论：`pending` / `ok` / `rolled-back` / `failed` / `staged` / `dry-run` | | `update.log` | 每次升级的完整日志（含 npm 输出） | | `apply.lock` | 单实例锁 | | `launcher/current-root.txt` | 启动指针（只存版本号；目录可由 `DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_LAUNCHER_DIR` 改变） | | `launcher/install-base.txt` | 安装目录（唯一一行 ASCII 路径；文件不存在 = 默认目录） | | `previous-base.txt` | 迁移前的 `install-base.txt` 内容，供回滚恢复（`-` 表示原本没有这个文件） | ## 排障 - **升级后起不来**：先看 `last-result.json`，卡片上也会带 `Cause:`（取自启动日志的首条错误行）。手动 `-Mode rollback -TargetRoot <旧根>` 可立刻回退。 - **registry 太慢**（某些网络下 `npm install` 要几分钟）：把 `registry` 指到镜像，插件的查询和 `npm install --registry` 都会跟着走。 - **新版拒绝 `host: '0.0.0.0'`**：`dsh-host-webserver` 的较新版本不再允许通配地址绑定（"binding every interface would expose remote code execution to the network"）。如果你的 profile patch 里留着 lan-bind 的 `host: '0.0.0.0'`，升级后会在 webserver 处启动失败并自动回滚。改成 `127.0.0.1`（远程访问交给隧道/中继）或某个具体网卡地址，再升级。 - **网页升级中途断开**：正常现象，宿主被重启了；页面重连后卡片会显示结果。 ## 实战记录：0.2.1-rc.2 在带 vision-router 的 profile 上起不来 `0.2.0-rc.2 → 0.2.1-rc.2` 在这台机器上做过两次真实切换，两次都是「新版启动失败 → 自动回滚到 0.2.0」，结论稳定且**与升级器无关**： - 全新 `DSH_HOME` + 真实 profile 配置逐插件二分：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app` 能起；再加 `dsh-vision-router` 立刻起不来；移除它、其余六个插件全留着，能起。 - 失败形态固定为 `StartupError: dsh: startup failed: 1 required plugin did not activate`，诊断表首行是 `connection (required) webRuntime`（即 `webRuntime` 一直没被提供，`connection` 卡在等待），日志里没有更具体的插件异常。 - 机理线索：`dsh-vision-router` 的 `dsh.client.inject` 声明了 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`，而 0.2.1-rc.2 不再发布这个包（0.2.0 有、0.2.1 没有）；它的 bundle patch 又给 `modules` / `connection` 两行追加了 `webServer` / `webRuntime` 依赖。3.0.0 与最新的 3.0.5 声明的 inject 完全一致，`engines` 虽写着支持 `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`，实测起不来。 - 结论：**想上 0.2.1 就得先等 vision-router 发布兼容版本**，或者在升级前把它从 profile 摘掉（会失去自动识图/视觉工具）。升级器该做的是照原样失败并回滚，这点它做对了。 ## 测试 ```powershell node test/handler.test.mjs # 全部（含一次 registry 查询） $env:DSH_AUTO_UPDATE_OFFLINE=1; node test/handler.test.mjs # 跳过网络 ``` 测试在系统临时目录里造一个假安装（含 `bin.js`、`package.json`、指针文件）并把 `DSH_HOME` 指过去，所以**在没装过 dsh 的机器上也能全绿**，也不会碰你的真实 profile。 ## 已知限制 - 只更新 `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 主包，不动 profile 里的插件（插件各自更新） - Windows 专用：重启链依赖 PowerShell 5.1 + cmd.exe 的实例语义 - 自定义安装目录必须是纯 ASCII 路径（cmd.exe 代码页限制）：空格可以，中文/日文目录名会被拒绝 - 迁移是整个目录复制，不保留硬链接；同一版本在两个目录各占一份空间，直到你手动删掉旧目录 - `next` / `alpha` 是预发布通道，别在生产开 - 升级期间网页会短暂断连（服务确实被重启了） - 成功判定不只看「端口有人应答」：重启后会再确认**实际在跑的是哪个版本**（先问插件自己的 `/api/status`，再退回查端口属主进程的安装目录）。这条是踩出来的——曾经有一个老启动器残留进程占着端口，健康检查返回 200、卡片显示成功，而新版其实根本没起来。同时 `Stop-WebHost` 现在也会结束启动脚本包装进程（`start-web.cmd`），避免它把旧版本重新拉起来抢端口。 ## License MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-client-ui-alice-skin
#最近新出的游戏爱丽丝与彼岸，画风不错也挺好玩的就做了个界面插件，大家对画风感兴趣可以去steam下一个玩

Alice Nation 主题皮肤 —— 给 DeepSeek Harness 的 Web 界面换上一层「爱丽丝」风格的配色与装饰,
并带一个右下角的角色面板:点一下头像,整个界面就跟着换成那位角色的配色和立绘。

![浅色主题](docs/light.png)

![深色主题](docs/dark.png)

拖到任意位置:

![拖动](docs/dragged.png)

换一位角色:

![换角色](docs/character-xiaoli.png)

## 它做了什么

**整站配色重绘** —— 不去改 DSH 的组件,而是重写它本来就读取的那层设计令牌
（`--dsw-alias-bg-*`、`--dsw-alias-label-*`、`--dsw-alias-border-*`、`--dsw-alias-brand-*`、
`--dsw-specific-*` 等 60 多个变量）。所以侧栏、输入框、气泡、按钮、代码块、滚动条、
设置卡片会一起变色,深浅两种主题都适配。

**角色氛围图** —— 右侧一层低透明度的角色立绘,用径向遮罩融进背景,不影响阅读。

**角色面板** —— 右下角常驻卡片:立绘 + 名字 + 一句台词。上面是 12 个圆形头像的
选择器,点谁换谁:

| 角色 | 来源 | 主题色 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 爱丽丝 / 爱丽丝·蓝 / 爱丽丝·夜 / 爱丽丝·礼 | `Player`, `Player2..4` | 玫瑰 / 天蓝 / 紫罗兰 / 鎏金 |
| 梅莉 | `RMeili` | 蜜桃 |
| 女王 | `Rqueen` | 淡紫 |
| 兔执事 / 雪兔 | `Rrabbit`, `Rrabbit2` | 薄荷 / 冰蓝 |
| 小璃 | `XiaoLi` | 樱粉 |
| 主管 / 熊掌柜 / 猫女仆 | `Supervisor`, `RKuma`, `Cat` | 蜜色 / 钢灰 / 藕荷 |

**交互**

- 点头像 → 换角色:主题色、氛围立绘、卡片立绘一起以 0.4 秒交叉淡入切换
- **拖动卡片或头像栏的空白处 → 整个面板跟着走**(鼠标/触屏都行),松手即记住位置,刷新不丢;
  不会被拖出窗口(贴边自动夹住),窗口变小时也会自动收回可见区域
- 点卡片 → 收起 / 展开头像选择器(拖动过的那一下不会被误判成点击)
- 卡片右上角 ✦ → **开关背景氛围图**:就是右侧那张大立绘淡出/淡入(见下方说明)
- 选择、位置、开关状态都记在 `localStorage`,刷新后还在

### ✦ 氛围图开关到底是什么效果

它只控制**右侧那张大面积的角色立绘**(默认约 12% 不透明度、径向遮罩融进背景)。
关掉之后右侧恢复成纯渐变底色,其余东西一个都不变 —— 主题色、头像栏、卡片、文字都不受影响。
觉得大图干扰阅读就关掉,想要氛围就打开。开着时 ✦ 是实心、关掉是空心 ✧,鼠标悬停会浮出「氛围图」标签。

| 开着(默认) | 关掉 |
| --- | --- |
| ![](docs/light.png) | ![](docs/aura-off.png) |

## 安装

插件已作为 bundle 装进 desktop profile。重新安装:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:E:/chajian/alice-skin
```

它在 profile 里注册为一个 bundle(`dsh.bundle.patch`),加载器条目 id 是
`ui-alice-skin`;要临时关掉,在 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml` 里加:

```yaml
- id: ui-alice-skin
  disabled: true
```

装好后刷新一次页面即可看到（DSH 的 client HMR 一般会自己推送,没动静就 F5）。

## 结构

```
alice-skin/
├─ package.json        # dsh.bundle(profile 层) + dsh.client(浏览器半边)
├─ cordis.patch.yml    # 唯一的 insert 行:id: ui-alice-skin
├─ lib/index.js        # 宿主半边:注册 /dsh-alice-skin 静态资源路由
├─ lib/client.js       # 浏览器半边:注入 CSS + 角色面板(手写 __ModuleLoader__ bundle)
├─ assets/
│  ├─ manifest.json    # 角色名 / 台词 / 主题色
│  ├─ portraits/*.webp # 560px 立绘卡(12 张,约 440 KiB)
│  └─ avatars/*.webp   # 128px 圆形头像(12 张,约 75 KiB)
├─ tools/
│  ├─ extract_unity.py # 用 UnityPy 从 AssetBundle 里导出 Sprite/Texture2D
│  └─ build_assets.py  # 按角色表裁立绘 + 圆头像,输出 webp 和 manifest
└─ docs/               # README 用的截图
```

`tools/` 里两个脚本顶部的路径常量指向本机位置,换机器时改那两行即可
(依赖 `UnityPy` + `Pillow`:`pip install UnityPy Pillow`)。

宿主半边只做一件事:把 `assets/` 通过 `/dsh-alice-skin/…` 发出去（带目录穿越防护、
只发 GET/HEAD、10 分钟缓存）。浏览器半边是手写的 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load`
工厂模块,不复用任何 DSH 内部组件,所以 DSH 升级时不会因为组件改名而崩掉 ——
它只依赖公开的设计令牌和 `document.body[data-ds-dark-theme]`。

拖拽用 Pointer Events 实现:按下后移动超过 4px 才算拖,否则仍按点击处理;位置以
**左下角**为锚点(`left` + `bottom`),这样上方头像栏展开/收起时卡片本身不会跳。
`localStorage` 键:`dsh-alice-skin:character` / `:dock` / `:aura` / `:position`。

## 换成你自己的图

1. 把新立绘放进 `assets/portraits/<id>.webp`(竖版,建议 372×512 或等比),
   头像放 `assets/avatars/<id>.webp`(正方形)。
2. 在 `lib/client.js` 顶部的 `CHARACTERS` 里加一行:`{ id, name, tagline, accent }`,
   `accent` 就是整站主题色。
3. 同步一下 `assets/manifest.json`(可选,仅供查阅),刷新页面。

要重新从游戏里抽图:`tools/extract_unity.py` 先把 AssetBundle 里的图导出成 PNG,
再用 `tools/build_assets.py` 按角色表裁立绘和头像(两者都依赖 `UnityPy` + `Pillow`)。

## 说明

- 立绘、头像来自本地游戏 **Alice Nation** 的 AssetBundle,仅供本机个人界面美化使用;
  角色名与台词是本插件为界面配的,与游戏原剧情无关。
- 只读取了角色卡与小图标,没有导出任何剧情 CG。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @jieai/dsh-malong-bridge

Official DSH (DeepSeek Harness) plugin for LiuHe / malong. One command puts the
**Six-He line** (13 `malong__*` MCP tools) into dsh web, and **malong's workspace
automatically follows the current conversation's workspace** — no need to pass a path
manually.
(Since 0.5.22 the bridge defaults to `graph` + state layer = 13 tools — the recommended
daily entry. The classic full catalog (44) and the diagnostic tier (18) are still one
env away: export `MALONG_INTERFACE=classic|diagnostic` on the dsh host.)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @jieai/dsh-malong-bridge
pkill -f "dsh web"
dsh web --port 3456 --host 0.0.0.0
```

Works out of the box for the MCP server itself: the bridge locates the bundled
`server/mcp-server.js` (complete toolset backend; better-sqlite3 ships
cross-platform precompiled binaries, with a vendored sql.js WASM fallback).

**Parser prerequisite (one-time per machine)**: the Rust parsing service
`malong-parse` is NOT bundled in this tarball. Install it yourself or point
`MALONG_PARSE_BIN` at a binary (see Platform support below). If it cannot be
resolved, tool calls that need parsing fail with an explicit resolution error
listing the searched locations.

> **pnpm 10 warns `Ignored build scripts: better-sqlite3`**: that is pnpm's
> default security policy (blocks dependency postinstall scripts). Run
> `pnpm approve-builds` and check `better-sqlite3` in the list (or edit
> `~/.dsh/profiles/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml` and add `better-sqlite3` under
> `onlyBuiltDependencies`, then `pnpm rebuild better-sqlite3`).
> Without this, better-sqlite3 has no native binary and tool calls will fail.
>
> **Native build fallback**: better-sqlite3 ships prebuilt binaries for common
> platforms (Node 20+); if your platform lacks a prebuilt and you have no build
> toolchain (Windows: Visual Studio Build Tools for node-gyp), the server
> automatically falls back to the vendored sql.js WASM backend
> (`malong/vendor/`, zero native deps) — the startup log shows which backend is
> active. Both backends use SQLite with compatible data files.

## Uninstall

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove @jieai/dsh-malong-bridge
pkill -f "dsh web"
dsh web --port 3456 --host 0.0.0.0
```

## Configuration (optional, zero-config by default)

| Env var | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MALONG_SERVER_PATH` | bundled `server/mcp-server.js` | Override the mcp-server entry (e.g. point at your own LiuHe dev copy) |
| `MALONG_STATE_DIR` | `~/.local/state/malong-dsh` | Index/state storage dir (all workspaces isolated under it by hash) |
| `MALONG_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000` | Per tool call timeout |

You can also write a `config:` override on the `malong-dsh-bridge` entry in the
profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (user layer, applied later).

## How It Works

```
DSH Agent → malong__read_symbol(...) (no workspace_dir)
         → dsh-bridge injects workspace_dir = current session workspace
         → malong mcp-server (spawned subprocess) → per-path-hash isolated indexes
```

- **Dynamic workspace follow**: every tool invocation carries the session
  workspace (`exec.agent.session.header.cwd`); the bridge injects it
  automatically; explicit paths from the model are respected (cross-workspace
  management).
- **State isolation**: indexes are hash-isolated by workspace path under
  `MALONG_STATE_DIR`, unrelated to any project directory.
- **Zero intrusion**: does not touch dsh's node_modules; dsh upgrades are safe.

> **Platform support**: `malong-parse` (the Rust parsing service) is NOT bundled
> with this tarball. It is resolved at runtime by `parse-bin.js`, in this order:
> `MALONG_PARSE_BIN` / `MALONG_PARSE_BIN_ALT` env → an installed
> `@jieai/malong-parse-<platform>-<arch>` package (only if you installed one;
> this bundle no longer declares such optionalDependencies) → the bundled
> `server/bin/malong-parse` (legacy layout; absent in this tarball) →
> `~/.local/bin/malong-parse` → a sibling `../malong-parse/target/{release,debug}`
> dev build.
>
> Point it explicitly when installing by hand, e.g.
> `MALONG_PARSE_BIN=/opt/malong-parse/malong-parse` (Linux) or
> `MALONG_PARSE_BIN=C:\tools\malong-parse\malong-parse.exe` (Windows).
>
> **0.5.13 note**: this bundle no longer declares `optionalDependencies` for the
> platform packages. They were pinned to `0.5.9`, a version that was never
> published (npm tops out at `0.4.8`), so they could never install and only
> produced a silent `catch {}` miss on every resolution. Install the binary
> yourself (`~/.local/bin/malong-parse`) or point `MALONG_PARSE_BIN` at one.

On Windows, replacing an existing source file uses the inbox Windows PowerShell
and .NET `File.Replace` with a hidden process to preserve the target's ACL.
Edits, undo and rollback use this path; new files inherit their directory's
permissions. If Windows PowerShell is blocked or replacement is denied, the
write fails explicitly instead of falling back to a rename that resets the ACL.
This adds Windows-only process startup overhead to existing-file writes.

## Differences vs. the official dsh-mcp-client

The official `dsh-mcp-client` bridges a single MCP server; this plugin's bridge
adds **dynamic workspace injection** (fills `workspace_dir` per invocation from
the session workspace, so the model never needs to know the path) — a
capability unique to LiuHe.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Log shows `mcp tools/list timeout` | Verify the install is complete (`dsh plugin` reports no node_modules errors); restart dsh |
| No `malong__*` tools in the conversation | Confirm the bundle layer is attached (`dsh web --dump-config \| grep malong`); hard-refresh the browser |
| Call fails with `missing_parameter: workspace_dir` | The conversation has no workspace (no cwd) to inject; pass a path in the prompt |
| Plugin stops working after a dsh upgrade | The plugin lives at the profile layer, upgrades do not affect it; if the cordis interface changes, reinstall the plugin |

## Index Rules (Transparency)

- **Default ignored**: `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, `target`,
  `coverage`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `.malong`, `.ai-transactions`, `vendor`, etc.
- **md/json not indexed**: only code files are indexed; use a read tool for documents
- **`.malongignore` customization**: a `.malongignore` file at the project root
  excludes directories allowlist-style (one per line; `*` wildcards supported; max 100 entries)

## License

MIT

# Malong LiuHe（码龙·六合工具）

**LLM-Native Code Operations Toolkit** — Code tooling reinvented for the LLM that has no hands, no eyes, and no memory.

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [Docs](https://wulun811.github.io/LiuHe) | [GitHub](https://github.com/wulun811/LiuHe)

[![wulun811/LiuHe MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/wulun811/LiuHe/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/wulun811/LiuHe)
![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-166%20files%20%C2%B7%200%20failed-brightgreen)
![tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/tools-44%20classic%20%2F%2013%20graph%20%2F%2018%20diagnostic-blue)
![languages](https://img.shields.io/badge/parsers-10%20languages-brightgreen)
![read](https://img.shields.io/badge/read%20P95-1ms-brightgreen)
![write](https://img.shields.io/badge/write%20P95-7ms-blue)
![memory](https://img.shields.io/badge/512MB%20limit-RSS%20134MB-brightgreen)
![concurrency](https://img.shields.io/badge/128%20concurrent%20requests-zero%20OOM-brightgreen)
![throughput](https://img.shields.io/badge/throughput-588%20calls%2Fs-blue)
![token](https://img.shields.io/badge/token%20est%20(fixed--path)-65%25-blue)
![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)
![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.5.27-blue)
![commits](https://img.shields.io/github/commit-count/wulun811/LiuHe)

**Malong LiuHe** is a toolkit built for LLMs rather than humans. It ships two components:
- **`malong/`** — an MCP toolset whose **default tier is the Six-He line** (13 tools: `code_task → code_read → code_patch / code_batch → code_check → code_control`, with task state, evidence and structured `next_action` hand-back built in); the classic full catalog (44) and the diagnostic tier (18) are one env away — `MALONG_INTERFACE=classic` / `MALONG_INTERFACE=diagnostic`. The catalog spans symbol read/write, indexing, impact analysis, reference tracing, call graphs, dead-code detection, code review, security scanning, atomic batch editing, test orchestration, pipeline verification, plus capability discovery (`code_query` mode=capabilities/capability) and the ADR-018 full-call outlet (`invoke_capability`) — served to the LLM over MCP (JSON-RPC over stdio). Since 0.5.24 the Six-He line is the default; classic remains the full catalog.
- **`malong-parse/`** — a Rust parsing service: a tree-sitter-based multi-language symbol extraction engine (JavaScript/TypeScript/TSX/Python/Go/Rust/C/C++/Java/Bash), talking to the toolset over a Unix socket, with an LRU tree cache and batched parallel extraction.

## Core Idea

Traditional tools (git, sed, IDE) assume a user with hands, eyes, and memory. An LLM has none of these. Malong LiuHe is redesigned around that fact:

| Missing | Design Consequence |
|---------|--------------------|
| **No hands** | Operations must be atomic, undoable, retryable (`edit_transaction` with rollback and undo journal) |
| **No eyes** | Output must be structured and self-explanatory (JSON for direct consumption; errors carry `suggestion`/`next_action`) |
| **No memory** | Every call is self-contained (takes `workspace_dir`); optimistic concurrency with version anchors (`read_symbol` → `write_symbol(base_version)` conflict state machine) |

## Performance (Measured)

| Metric | Value | Note |
|--------|-------|------|
| Small-file read P95 | **1ms** | 50 runs, warmed |
| Small-file write P95 | **7ms** | 30 runs, incl. post-write re-index |
| `repo_map` | **98ms** | down from tens of seconds (SQLite index + Rust parsing) |
| Memory | **RSS 134MB / 26%** | under a real docker `--memory=512m` cgroup limit |
| Concurrency | **128 concurrent / 256 in-flight requests, zero OOM** | 32-way mixed read+write on one hot file, no tearing, DB `integrity_check` PASS |
| Throughput | **~588 calls/s** | single-threaded ceiling — 60–600× real LLM demand |
| Token estimate (fixed-path) | **↓65.3%** | scripted `measure-trail.js`: 6-step legacy chain → 3-call primitives, 7673 → 2662 chars/4 est. **Fixed editor path only — not a host-vs-malong nor an agentic-conversation result.** |
| Call reduction (fixed-path) | **↓50.0%** | 6 calls (legacy chain) → 3 calls (primitives); same scripted path |
| Tool-description compression | **44 classic tools ≈ 1.33k tokens** | tiered: core kept, low-freq ≤70 chars, verbose ≤230; detail flows via next_step hints |
| Default-tier catalog tax (per turn) | **13 tools = 16.5 KB ≈ 4.86k tokens** | descriptions 2.0 KB (≈0.60k) + inputSchema 14.5 KB (≈4.26k) — the schema is 88% of it; to shrink the catalog, cut the parameter surface, not the prose |
| Index throughput | **538 files / 7s** | scoped reindex, measured |
| dry_run fidelity | **47/47** | golden-hash comparison across 3 languages, 100% |
| Concurrent writes to same symbol | **16/16** | exactly one winner + one conflict, zero silent overwrites |

## Language Support

| Language | Symbol Extraction | Reference Extraction |
|----------|:---:|:---:|
| JavaScript / TypeScript / TSX / JSX / MTS / CTS | ✓ | ✓ |
| Python | ✓ | ✓ |
| Go | ✓ | ✓ |
| Rust (impl blocks / trait / enum semantics) | ✓ | ✓ |
| C / C++ (incl. headers) | ✓ | ✓ |
| Java | ✓ | ✓ |
| Bash | ✓ | ✓ |

## Tool Overview

| Category | Tools |
|----------|-------|
| **Six-He line** (graph + stateful — recommended daily entry) | `code_task` (resolve + plan) → `code_read` (materials + `read_ref`) → `code_patch` / `code_batch` / `code_maintain` (journaled writes) → `code_check` (evidence) → `code_control` (status / resume / expand / reopen / job); plus `code_status`, `code_audit`, `code_worktree`, `edit_transaction` — 11 tools, env-gated |
| **I/O primitives** | `read_symbol` (symbol read + version), `write_symbol` / `write_symbols` (safe write: conflict state machine + atomic write + undo) |
| **Index & search** | `reindex`, `symbol_search`, `code_search` (keyword + regex intent patterns — NOT semantic search), `repo_map` (98ms file map; skeleton pagination: `page`/`page_size`/`prefix` — truncated output always carries the full top-level skeleton with page numbers)
| **Analysis** | `impact_analysis` (blast radius + risk), `call_chain`, `references`, `dep_graph`, `inspect` (outline + refs + call chain in one), `trace_symbol` (constant tracing + hardcoded copies) |
| **Editing** | `edit_batch`, `edit_transaction` (atomic txn + rollback + cross-session lock + dry-run preview + create), `edit_collision_guard` (write conflict detection), `sandbox_validate` (pre-write validation), `diff_facts` (symbol changes + test sync), `rename_symbol` (atomic cross-file rename), `git_worktree` (isolated branch + verify + merge) |
| **Quality gates** | `code_review`, `security_review` (regex security patterns), `code_quality` (5-dim probe), `style_sniffer`, `guard_patterns`, `naming_consistency`, `exception_guard`, `config_drift`, `dependency_gatekeeper`, `fix_imports`, `sweep_dead_code`, `mock_sync` — all pure regex/AST, zero LLM calls, deterministic |
| **Engineering** | `test_bridge` (run/suggest/discover), `find_tests`, `verify_pipeline` (lint/test/typecheck stages), `debug_runner` (error analysis), `patch_parser` (SEARCH/REPLACE), `tsc_check`, `spec_gen`, `active_todos` |
| **System** | `health`, `gc`, `feedback` |

> **Long test suites must run in the background.** The MCP request has a hard 120s ceiling and a foreground stage is capped at 110s, so a suite that takes minutes is reported as `failed` — that is a request-budget truncation, **not** a code defect. Run it as a background job instead: `code_check` with `run: true, async: true` (600s cap), then poll with `code_control(action="job")`.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│  LLM Client (MCP)       │     │  malong-parse (Rust daemon)  │
│  malong/ 13 six-he      │◄───►│  tree-sitter, 10 languages   │
│  (+44/18 gated)         │     │  LRU tree cache 50MB / batch │
│  Unix socket client     │     │  catch_unwind crash recovery │
└─────────────────────────┘     └──────────────────────────────┘
```

- All parsing is done by the Rust service (zero tree-sitter bindings on the Node side)
- Index is SQLite (WAL mode, multi-process safe), isolated per workspace
- LRU tree cache (50MB / 5min TTL), batched extraction 50 files/batch
- Daemon multi-session safety: circuit breaker + liveness probe + cross-session coordinated restart (O_EXCL lock) — a slow request in one session never stalls others

## Self-Hosting (Dogfooding)

30+ rounds of "Malong reviews Malong": the toolset audits and fixes its **own** code, with dozens of real bugs fixed and locked by tests — including directory-scope filtering gaps, false dead-code reports for registration patterns, lost constant read-sites, and SQL parameterization cleanup. Every round grew the suite (now 166 JS test files, full chain 0 failures). Latest round (r5): cross-file reference resolution is now import-aware — member calls such as `path.join` no longer bind to same-named local symbols (216 false bindings in this repo alone), cross-language (Python↔JS) links are blocked by a language-family filter, and aliases resolve through the import graph (ESM specifier scanning added on the JS side) — locked by `test-crossfile-resolve` (14 assertions, red→green); the DSH bridge also now pins `MALONG_STATE_DIR` when spawning the server, locked by `test-dsh-bridge`.

## Scan Boundaries (limits acknowledged; committed within)

Deterministic scanners only — regex pattern matching and reference graphs. **No control-flow, data-flow, or cross-module semantic coverage.** 0 findings ≠ clean; high scores ≠ healthy.

- `security_review` scans: injection (eval/Function-ctor, exec/spawn string building, template `${}`, `$()` substitution, SQL concat), XSS, hardcoded secrets, CORS *, timing/insecure compare, dotenv. **Not scanned**: SSRF, XXE, deserialization, auth/logic flaws, control-flow defects.
- `sweep_dead_code` reference scope: import graph + fixed text-ref fallback (.sh/.json/.md etc.); CLI-string references count as alive (miss-over-delete). **Not scanned**: dynamic/reflection wiring.
- Commitment: issues in scope get fixed; covered patterns are test-locked; new rules must stay within committed categories.

## Quick Start

### Standard install (default — recommended)

`npm ci` installs `better-sqlite3` (the full SQLite backend); this is the default recommended path:

```bash
# 1) Get the parsing daemon — download a prebuilt binary from releases/, or build:
cd malong-parse && cargo build --release && cp target/release/malong-parse ~/.local/bin
malong-parse &                                   # start the daemon (Unix socket)

# 2) Install the toolset (npm ci installs the full better-sqlite3 backend)
cd ../malong && npm ci

# 3) Register the MCP server (works with any MCP client, e.g. opencode / Claude Desktop)
#    opencode (project-root opencode.json; Windows paths use double backslashes, Linux/macOS forward slashes):
#    {
#      "mcp": {                                    # opencode V2 native: servers grouping (V1 used direct mcp.<name>)
#        "servers": {
#          "malong": {
#            "type": "local",
#            "command": ["node", "--max-old-space-size=512", "N:\\repo\\liuhe\\malong\\mcp-server.js", "--workspace", "N:\\repo\\liuhe"],
#            # default since 0.5.24 = Six-He line (13 tools); this block is optional now — delete it for the classic 44 catalog
#            "environment": { "MALONG_INTERFACE": "graph", "MALONG_ENTRY_STATE": "1" }
#          }
#        }
#      }
#    }
#    Claude Desktop (verified on Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json):
#    {
#      "mcpServers": {
#        "malong": { "command": "node", "args": ["/path/to/malong/mcp-server.js"], "env": { "MALONG_INTERFACE": "graph", "MALONG_ENTRY_STATE": "1" } }
#      }
#    }

# 4) Ask your LLM: "search for the symbol 'handle' in my workspace"

#    DeepSeek Harness (dsh web) — auto session-workspace convenience (extra, optional):
#    Run once on the dsh host (Linux/macOS):
#      Option A (npm, one line — full backend + platform binary included):
#        dsh plugin --profile web add @jieai/dsh-malong-bridge
#        pkill -f "dsh web"; dsh web --port 3456 --host 0.0.0.0 --trusted-host <LAN IP>
#      Option B (script, points at a checkout of this repo):
#        bash malong/dsh/install-dsh.sh         # idempotent; edits ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml with backup
#    The bridge exposes the Six-He line (13 tools: code_task/code_read/code_patch/...) as malong__* and auto-fills workspace_dir from the
#    current conversation's workspace (no per-call path needed; explicit paths still win).
#    Need the classic full catalog (44) or the diagnostic tier (18)? export MALONG_INTERFACE=classic|diagnostic on the dsh host.
#    Full guide incl. index rules: malong/dsh/DSH-INTEGRATION.md
#    Troubleshooting: if EVERY malong__* call hangs until timeout, the bridge's
#    mcp-server subprocess is gone. The bridge now auto-restarts it (exponential
#    backoff, pending calls fail fast with "restarting — retry shortly"); if that
#    keeps failing, restart dsh web: kill <dsh web pid> && dsh web --port 3456 ...
```

> **SQL backend note:** the default is the full `better-sqlite3` backend. If `npm install` fails (offline / no build toolchain / Node < 20), the server automatically degrades to the **vendored sql.js WASM sandbox backend** (`malong/vendor/`, zero-dependency, no network) — the startup log shows which backend is active and the upgrade command. Data files are fully compatible between backends (both are SQLite).

### Zero-build deployment (degraded path: sandbox / offline environments)

For environments with **Node >= 20 and no npm access** (no `npm ci`, no native
compilation), everything runs from the repo files as-is (Linux/Windows — the
prebuilt binaries are `linux-x86_64` and `windows-x86_64`). On this path SQLite
runs on the sql.js sandbox backend (degraded):

```bash
# 0) Clone, then enter the toolset directory:
git clone <repo-url> liuhe && cd liuhe/malong

# 1) Parse daemon — prebuilt binary from releases/ (no cargo needed):
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
tar -xzf ../releases/malong-liuhe-0.5.27-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cp malong-parse/target/release/malong-parse ~/.local/bin
malong-parse &                                   # start the daemon (socket: /tmp/malong-parse-$UID.sock)

# 2) Run the toolset — zero npm install:
node --max-old-space-size=4096 mcp-server.js --workspace /path/to/project
# vendored SQLite (sql.js WASM) auto-enabled when better-sqlite3 is unavailable

# 3) Self-check (30s, optional):
node tests/test-db-adapter.js   # 22 assertions: sql.js backend + persistence
node tests/test-mcp-server.js   # 37 assertions: MCP stdio + daemon round-trip
```

> **Windows users:** use `malong-liuhe-0.5.27-windows-x86_64.tar.gz` from GitHub Releases (contains `malong-parse.exe`), extract and put it on PATH; the MCP server auto-starts the daemon, so step 1's `malong-parse &` is not required. The `mkdir -p`/`tar -xzf` above are Unix syntax — on Windows use any extractor (`tar -xzf` works on Win10+).

> Note: if the daemon is not running, parse-dependent tools (symbol extraction
> etc.) degrade; the SQLite-backed tools (repo-map / code-index / health-check)
> still work.

- See `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` for the vendored component.

What the LLM sees back:

```json
{
  "results": [
    { "name": "handle", "type": "function", "start_line": 6, "end_line": 12, "file": "app.js" },
    { "name": "handle_login", "type": "function", "start_line": 5, "end_line": 9, "file": "src/auth.py" }
  ],
  "count": 2,
  "next_step": "Before modifying found symbols, check blast radius: impact_analysis(...)"
}
```

### Build the Rust parsing service

```bash
cd malong-parse
cargo build --release
cp target/release/malong-parse ~/.local/bin/   # or add to PATH
malong-parse &                                   # daemon (Unix socket: /tmp/malong-parse-$(id -u).sock)
```

Prebuilt binaries for Linux x86_64 are committed under
[`releases/`](releases/) (with `.sha256` checksums) — pick one up instead of building if you prefer.

**Platforms:** Linux and macOS use the Unix socket; on **Windows** the daemon listens on TCP `127.0.0.1:31001` (set `MALONG_PORT` to override) — the MCP server probes and auto-starts `malong-parse.exe` on startup, so no manual launch is needed (if you use the parse-client API directly outside MCP, start it manually). Set `MALONG_SOCKET` to override the Unix socket path.

### Install the toolset

```bash
cd malong
npm ci
npm test          # 166 test files (daemon must be running)
```

### Start the MCP server

```bash
cd malong
node --max-old-space-size=512 mcp-server.js --workspace /path/to/project
```

Register the MCP server with any MCP-capable LLM client and the tools become available. For **opencode**, register in the project root `opencode.json` (the `environment` block is **optional since 0.5.24** — the default tier already is the Six-He line, 13 tools; set `MALONG_INTERFACE=classic` for the classic 44-tool catalog):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "malong": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["node", "--max-old-space-size=512", "malong/mcp-server.js", "--workspace", "."],
        "environment": { "MALONG_INTERFACE": "graph", "MALONG_ENTRY_STATE": "1" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> Windows note: relative paths in `--workspace` and `malong/mcp-server.js` resolve against the directory where opencode is launched; pass absolute paths (escape backslashes as `\\` in JSON) if you start it elsewhere. The daemon is auto-started by the MCP server — no need to launch `malong-parse.exe` manually.

For opencode V2 details — config shape, tool visibility (`codemode`), and troubleshooting — see [`malong/opencode/OPENCODE-V2.md`](malong/opencode/OPENCODE-V2.md).

### Configuration (environment variables)

All optional — sensible defaults apply when unset.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MALONG_STATE_DIR` | `~/.config/malong` | Root of MCP state since 0.5.0: workspace indexes (`workspaces/<hash>/code-index.db`) plus usage / feedback / edit-stats. Legacy per-repo `data/malong-mcp` (seeded via `--workspace`) is migrated on first launch in an isolated child process (copy→verify→delete; fail-soft, source kept on failure); pre-0.3.37 `~/.config/opencode/` reads still fall back. |
| `MALONG_SKIP_STATE_MIGRATION` | unset | Set to `1` to skip legacy-state migration at startup (emergency escape; old directory left untouched). |
| `MALONG_SOCKET` | `/tmp/malong-parse-$(id -u).sock` | Unix socket path to the parse daemon (Linux / macOS). |
| `MALONG_PORT` | `31001` | TCP port for the parse daemon (Windows). |
| `MALONG_PARSE_BIN` | npm platform pkg / `~/.local/bin` | Binary used when the client auto-starts the daemon. Resolution order: this env → `@jieai/malong-parse-<os>-<arch>` npm platform package (installed as an optional dependency of `@jieai/dsh-malong-bridge`) → `~/.local/bin/malong-parse` → `malong-parse/target/release` (dev tree). |
| `MALONG_PARSE_MODE` | rust-service | Parse transport. Only `rust-service` is supported (`builtin` / `shadow` are rejected). |
| `MALONG_WS_GC_DAYS` | `14` | Days a workspace index cache may sit untouched before `health cleanup` prunes it; `0` disables. |
| `MALONG_INTERFACE` | `graph` | Tool tier. Default (unset) = the **Six-He line** (13 tools: `code_task`/`code_read`/`code_status`/`code_query` + 8 stateful entries + `edit_transaction`). `classic` = the full 44-tool catalog; `diagnostic` = 18 (Six-He line + 5 analyzers). |
| `MALONG_ENTRY_STATE` | on | The state layer (S1–S5 task state machine + ADR-018 `invoke_capability`) is allowed by default; set `0` for the read-only 5-tool tier. |
| `MALONG_PYTHON` | unset | Explicit interpreter for Python test runs (`test_bridge` / `verify_pipeline`); overrides the auto-detected project venv (`.venv`/`venv`/`env` next to the project root). |

### Suppressing security false positives

`security_review` is deliberately conservative, so benign patterns (a hash used as a cache key, `process.exit` in a CLI entry) can trip it. Two explicit, auditable suppression mechanisms exist — neither ever auto-suppresses injection rules.

**Inline** — append `malong-ignore` to a line to suppress all findings on it, or `malong-ignore[eval,exec-cmd]` for specific rules (a reason after `:` is encouraged):

```js
const id = crypto.createHash('md5').update(p).digest('hex') // malong-ignore: cache-dir name, not security
```

**Config** — add a `securityIgnore` array to `.ai-patterns.json` (the same file `guard_patterns` reads). Each entry takes `files` (`*` / `**` globs) and/or `rules`; omit one side to match all:

```json
{ "securityIgnore": [ { "files": ["**/mcp-server.js"], "rules": ["process-exit"] } ] }
```

Suppressed findings are dropped from the score but counted in the summary's `suppressed` field, so nothing is hidden silently. Injection rules (eval / exec / SQL / spawn) are only ever suppressed by an explicit marker or entry you authored — never heuristically.

### Journal auto-cleanup

Every safe write (`write_symbol` / `write_symbols` / `edit_batch`) leaves an undo journal under `.malong/journal/`. Terminal transactions (`committed` / `rolled_back` / `abandoned` / `failed`) older than a TTL (default **24h**, configurable) are pruned automatically — throttled to at most one scan per hour per workspace, so it costs nothing. In-flight (`created` / `staged`) and `needs_review` (external change awaiting human review) journals are **never** auto-deleted. This only ever touches the tool's own rollback backups — never your source files.

### Using with Claude Code

Verified end-to-end with Claude Code 2.x. The MCP layer is standard JSON-RPC over
stdio, so any MCP client (Claude Code, codex, opencode, Claude Desktop…) connects
the same way.

**1) Prerequisites** — Node >= 20 and the parsing daemon running (see the
*Zero-build deployment* or *Build the Rust parsing service* sections above).

**2) Install Claude Code**

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

**3) Point Claude Code at an Anthropic-compatible provider**

Claude Code needs an LLM backend. Any Anthropic-compatible endpoint works — set the
variables below (or manage them with [`cc-switch`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cc-switch/cli)):

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://your-provider/anthropic"   # any Anthropic-compatible endpoint
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="your-api-key"                     # never commit this
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="your-model"                            # a model your provider serves
```

> With [`cc-switch`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cc-switch/cli): `npm i -g @cc-switch/cli`,
> `cc-switch new my-provider` (fill in the same `ANTHROPIC_*` keys under `env`),
> `cc-switch switch my-provider`, then `eval $(cc-switch export)`.

**4) Register the MCP server**

```bash
claude mcp add liuhe -- node /path/to/malong/mcp-server.js --workspace /path/to/project
claude mcp list        # → "liuhe … ✔ Connected"
```

**5) Use it** — start `claude` in your project and ask, or run headless:

```bash
claude -p "index the workspace with reindex, then find createDb with symbol_search" \
  --allowedTools "mcp__liuhe__reindex" "mcp__liuhe__symbol_search"
```

Tools are exposed as `mcp__liuhe__<tool>` (e.g. `mcp__liuhe__health`,
`mcp__liuhe__symbol_search`, `mcp__liuhe__repo_map`). Run `reindex` (optionally
`blocking=true`) once per workspace first, so symbol search / impact analysis have
an index to query.

### U
